"Go, sanctify them, let garments be clean, Be ready by the third day, my power will be seen. Set bounds on the mount, don't touch or climb, For touching the mountain is death's chime."
Moses came down, told the people the plan, "Be pure, wash up, don't touch woman or man." On the third morning, thunder roared, lightning flashed, A trumpet's blast, in the camp their hearts thrashed.
Moses led them out to meet God face to face, Mount Sinai quaked, smoke filled the place. Trumpet grew louder, Moses spoke out strong, God's voice answered, like a powerful song.
Yahweh called Moses up, but warned him tight, "Tell the people, don't come near my sight. Even priests must cleanse, or face my flame, Keep them back, hold them in my name."

Moses replied, "Boundaries are set, none can breach," Yahweh said, "Bring Aaron, but the rest must not reach." Moses descended, shared Yahweh's command, Ensuring God's word was spread through the land.
God spoke to the crowd, laying down the line, "I am Yahweh, your God, the one who freed you just in time.
No other gods before me, keep your worship pure, No idols, no images, let your faith be sure.
Don't bow, don't serve them, I'm a jealous type, Punishing fathers' sins till the fourth, but to the loved, kind ripe.
Don't misuse my name, it's sacred, keep it tight, Respect the Sabbath day, rest in holy light.
Six days you labor, but the seventh's for rest, Everyone's included, give your servants your best.
For in six days, heaven, earth, sea were made, On the seventh, I rested, so the Sabbath I laid.
Honor your parents, so your days will stretch long, In the land I give, keep your spirit strong.
No murder, no adultery, don't steal or lie, Don't covet what's your neighbor's, let desires pass by.
The people saw thunder, lightning, mountain smoke, Trembling from the power, they felt the divine yoke.
They said to Moses, "Speak, let it be your voice, But don't let God speak, or we won't have a choice."
Moses calmed them, "Don't fear, it's a test, So you'll hold his fear, and live your life blessed."
People kept their distance, Moses stepped near, Into thick darkness, where God's words were clear.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Tell them what you’ve seen, No gods of silver or gold, let the worship stay clean.
Build me an altar of earth, offer peace and fire, In places I name, my blessings will inspire.
If stone you choose, use no tool that pollutes, Keep the altar simple, no steps that reveal the roots."
Ordinances set, here's what to know, A Hebrew servant's time, six years to show. Year seven comes, he walks out free, Alone or with his family, as it should be.
If a master's gifts bring family ties, He goes alone if kids arise. But if he loves them, chooses to stay, To the doorpost they go, an awl in play.
A daughter sold, not the same plan, If he’s deceitful, redeeming’s at hand. Married to his son, treat her right, Food, clothing, rights, don’t slight.
Kill a man, death’s the fate, Unintentional though, God’s plan’s straight. Scheming murder, take him from the altar, To die, no chance for him to falter.
Hit mom or dad, or curse, it’s death, Kidnap and sell? Face the last breath. Men quarrel, stones or fists in the fray, If walking again, debt he must pay.
Servant struck, dies from the rod, Punishment comes, but wait for the nod. Pregnant woman hurt? Fine in demand, Harm follows? Life for life, God’s command.
Eye or tooth struck, servant goes free, Bull’s rage known, owner’s penalty. Open pit traps, pay the cost, Divide the dead, nothing’s lost.
Bull injures bull, split the price, Known danger? Pay for the vice. These are the rules, the laws to heed, Justice served for every deed.
If a man steals an ox, or a sheep, makes the sale, He owes five oxen, four sheep, a costly tale.
Break into a house, and if he falls, No guilt for blood if within the walls.
But if by morning he's caught in crime, He's guilty and must pay in time.
If he’s got nothing, he'll be sold, To pay his debt, as laws unfold.
If the stolen beast he still retains, Double the debt, that’s how it remains.
If you let your beast stray to graze, Pay back with fields of the finest praise.
Fire in the field, blazing, wild, and broad, The one who sparked it pays to God.
Give your neighbor goods, they get nicked, Find the thief, pay double quick.
If no thief, the owner swears, Before God, to settle affairs.
In trespass matters, ox or sheep, To God they go, the verdict to keep.
If you lend a beast and it's injured or dead, If the owner’s not there, pay what's said.
But if the owner stands by its side, No need for payment, just abide.
Entice a virgin, you must pay, A dowry for marriage in the proper way.
Sorceress or beast with lust, Judgment comes, return to dust.
Sacrifice to gods that aren’t Yahweh, Utter destruction, the law’s way.
Treat strangers well, remember your plight, In Egypt, you were strangers in the night.
Widows or orphans, don’t oppress or wrong, Cry to God, His wrath comes strong.
Lend to the poor without a fee, Don’t charge interest, let them be.
If you take a cloak for a debt unpaid, Return it by sunset, don’t be swayed.
He cries to Me, I'll hear the plea, For I am gracious, hear and see.
Don’t blaspheme God, respect the throne, Don’t curse leaders, it’s in the tone.
Offer your first, both crop and son, Seven days with mother, then the duty’s done.
Holy men, no torn meat to eat, Cast it to dogs, walk in God’s beat.
Don't spread lies, don't join with the wicked crew, In court, keep justice, don't let the lies break through.
Your enemy's ox lost, bring it back, don't stall, Help the donkey that's burdened, even if you don't like him at all.
Justice for the poor, in court, it must stay, Avoid false charges, let innocence light the way.
No bribes, they blind the eye, twist what's right, Don't oppress the outsider, remember Egypt's night.
For six years work the land, the seventh let it rest, For the poor and beasts, that year is best.
Six days of labor, then a day of rest, Refresh the weary, let the tired be blessed.
Observe my words, don't speak of other gods, Keep your feasts as I said, in your holy squads.
Unleavened bread for seven days, as I command, Harvest and ingather, the fruits of your land.
Three times a year, before Yahweh appear, Bring your first fruits, get your blessings clear.
"An angel leads you, hear his voice, Obey, and I’ll make your enemies no choice."
Drive out the nations, but not all at once, Little by little, to avoid nature's response.
Borders wide, from sea to river wide, No deals with their gods, let none abide.
Serve Yahweh alone, and blessings will flow, Your enemy's terror, God's might will show.
Don't let them dwell, don't let them in, Serve their gods, and you'll fall to sin.
"Come up to Yahweh," He spoke so clear, Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, draw near. Seventy elders, but keep your distance, Moses alone will enter God's presence.

Moses shared Yahweh's word, the people's choice, "We'll do all Yahweh's words," they said in one voice. Moses wrote down every word Yahweh declared, At dawn, he built an altar, twelve pillars prepared.
Young men brought offerings, peace and burn, Half the blood in basins, half on the altar, discern. He read the covenant, the people vowed again, "We'll do what Yahweh says," they proclaimed, amen.
Moses sprinkled blood, "This covenant's sign," By Yahweh's word, this bond we define. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu ascended the height, Seventy elders saw God, beneath His feet, sapphire light.
No hand on nobles, they saw God, they dined, Yahweh said to Moses, "Stone tablets you'll find. Come to the mountain, learn law and command, Teach them to people, as I have planned."
Moses with Joshua climbed God's domain, Told the elders, "Wait, we'll return again. Aaron and Hur will judge disputes wide, While upon God's mountain, I'll abide."
Clouds covered Sinai, glory did bestow, Six days it lingered, then Yahweh's call did flow. To the people, His glory, like fire it blazed, Moses in the cloud, forty days did he praise.
Moses heard Yahweh's voice, so clear, "Tell Israel to bring offerings, draw near.
Gold, silver, bronze, the list goes on, Scarlet, linen, with the finest yarns drawn.
Rams' skins, acacia, oil for light, Spices sweet, onyx stones shining bright.
A sanctuary's what they will create, For there I’ll dwell, with them relate.
Show them the plan, from furniture to tent, Build it exactly, every detail meant.
An ark of wood, two and a half cubits long, Overlaid with gold, both inside and strong.
Four gold rings, placed on its feet, Poles of acacia, gold complete.
Carry it carefully, covenant placed within, A mercy seat of pure gold, where it begins.
Two cherubim, with wings spread wide, On either end, looking side by side.
"Here I'll meet, from the seat I’ll speak, To guide them all, the words I’ll seek.
A table of wood, gold over it laid, With rings for poles, craftsmanship displayed.
Its dishes, spoons, and bowls of gold, Bread of presence always foretold.
A lamp stand of gold, with branches six, Almond blossom cups, crafted with a fix.
Seven lamps shall shine, brightly in view, All made as shown, in the pattern true."
From the mountaintop came the grand design, For Israel’s journey, the sacred sign.
Craft the tabernacle, curtains wide and tall, Fine linen, blue, purple, scarlet, cherubs on the wall.
Ten curtains long, each twenty-eight cubits stand, Four cubits wide, they fit the plan.
Five curtains together, coupled side by side, Loops of blue on the edge, where they abide.
Fifty loops here, fifty loops there, Golden clasps unite them, floating in the air.
Make the goats' hair curtains, eleven in line, Thirty cubits each, four wide, all divine.
Five and six, a double of the sixth, Loops on edges, nothing missed.
Clasps of bronze, tents unite as one, Overhangs drape when the work's done.
Rams' skins dyed red, sea cow hides on top, Acacia wood boards, upright they prop.
Ten cubits high, each board stands, With two tenons, for steady hands.
Twenty boards south, sockets silver bright, Two per board, holding tight.
North side the same, west with six and two, Corners doubled, whole and true.
Eight boards total, sockets plenty made, Acacia bars, this tabernacle's parade.
Five bars here, five bars there, Middle bar runs through, everywhere.
Overlay in gold, rings shining bold, Set it up just as you were told.
A veil of blue, purple, scarlet twined, With cherubim by skill designed.
Four pillars hold it, hooks of gold they bear, Separate the holy from most holy, a sacred pair.
The mercy seat on the ark, in the most holy place, Table outside the veil, lamp stand keeps its grace.
Screen the door with color, blue and purple bright, Five gold pillars, bronze sockets, all in sight.
Make the altar of acacia wood, precise and square, Five by five cubits, three cubits in the air.
Four corners with horns, one piece it's got, Overlay it all with bronze, make it hot.
Pots for ashes, and shovels too, Basins, hooks, fire pans, all in bronze hue.
A bronze net grating, with rings on the four, Underneath the ledge, halfway up, but no more.
Acacia poles, overlaid with bronze sheen, Slide them in the rings, keep it mobile and clean.
Hollow with planks as on the mountain shown, Crafted with care, the details are known.
The tabernacle court, stretch wide and long, South side hangs linen, hundred cubits strong.
Twenty pillars stand, sockets bronze and bright, Hooks and fillets silver, gleaming in the light.
North side matches, hundred cubits grand, Bronze holds the pillars, silver hooks in hand.
West side's fifty, pillars ten will stand, East mirrors west, a courtyard well spanned.
Gate hangings fifteen, three pillars in line, On each side they stand, in sockets they shine.
Gate screen of twenty, blue, purple, scarlet blend, Embroidered work, four pillars at each end.
Silver-filleted pillars, bronze sockets all round, Court's a hundred long, fifty wide, tightly bound.
All instruments and pins, bronze-crafted to serve, Every detail precise, nothing left to swerve.
Command the children, bring oil pure and bright, Keep the lamp burning, through the long night.
In the Tent of Meeting, Aaron stands tall, Evening till morning, he serves the call.
A lasting statute, generations to hold, For Israel's children, the story unfolds.
"Bring Aaron and his sons to serve me, yo, In the priest's office, let glory show. Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar, they’ll stand, In holy garments, made by wise hands.
“Speak to the wise, with wisdom filled, To craft the garments, as I have willed. A breastplate, ephod, robe shining bright, Turban, sash, in gold, blue, and scarlet light.
Gold threads woven fine, purple and red, Holy garments for the priesthood ahead. Ephod with straps, joined like a chain, Gold and linen, skillfully made, again and again.
Two onyx stones, names engraved bold, Six on each, in birth order told. Set in gold, on shoulders they’ll stay, Memorial stones for Israel, day by day.
Chains of gold, braided and pure, On the ephod for Aaron, to serve secure. Breastplate of judgment, skillfully wrought, In gold and linen, its purpose taught.
Four stone rows on the breastplate shine, Ruby, sapphire, emerald align. Twelve tribes’ names, engraved in array, On Aaron’s heart, always to stay.
Blue lace binds, ephod and breastplate unite, For Aaron before Yahweh, shining bright. Urim and Thummim, in judgment they guide, On Aaron’s heart, they’ll never hide.
“Robe of blue, with a hole in the top, Woven strong, so it won’t tear or flop. Pomegranates and golden bells around the hem, Sounding when Aaron enters, a holy gem.
A plate of pure gold, ‘HOLY TO YAHWEH,’ On Aaron’s forehead, always to stay. A tunic of linen, a turban so fine, For glory and beauty, divine design.
Anoint, consecrate, make them stand firm, In the priest’s office, for all time to affirm. Linen pants to cover, from waist to thigh, A lasting statute, under Yahweh’s eye."

"Here's the way to make them holy," said with a true voice, "One bull, two rams, without defect, that's the choice. Unleavened bread, cakes, and wafers with oil, Fine wheat flour, all set for the toil.
Put it all in one basket, neat and grand, Bring it with the bull and rams in your hand. Bring Aaron and his sons to the Tent’s door, Wash them with water, pure to the core.
Dress Aaron with tunic, ephod, and band, Crown on the turban, as the plan's been planned. Pour oil on his head, anoint with grace, Bring his sons, dress them for their place.
Bind belts, headbands, the priesthood’s theirs, Consecrate them with careful prayers. Bring the bull before the Tent now, Aaron and his sons will lay hands, they know how.
Slaughter the bull at the Tent’s door, Blood on the altar's horns, pour it on the floor. Burn the fat and kidneys on the fire, The rest of the bull is burned outside, higher.
Take one ram, lay your hands on its head, Kill it and sprinkle the blood, just as was said. Cut the ram, wash it, head and feet, Burn it whole on the altar, smoke rising sweet.
Take the other ram, hands on its crown, Kill it, blood on ears, thumbs, toes, pass it down. Sprinkle blood and oil on Aaron’s vest, He, his sons, their garments, now all are blessed.
Fat of the ram, bread from the basket, wave in hand, Burn it on the altar, by Yahweh’s command. Wave the breast, it’s for you, take your share, An eternal portion, a holy affair.
Seven days they wear the sacred attire, Consecrate the altar, cleanse with fire. Offer lambs day by day, morning and night, With flour, oil, and wine, a pleasing sight.
At the Tent of Meeting, I'll be there, Speak to you, children, the place made fair. I’ll dwell among you, be your God, From Egypt, you were freed, upon this holy sod."
Make an altar, acacia wood's the call, Square and tall, gold over it all.
"Overlay it pure, with gold so bright, Molding around, shining in the light.
"Two golden rings, beneath the frame, Poles of acacia, gold just the same.
"Place it before the veil, by the sacred seat, Where I'm gonna meet you, where we will meet.
"Every morning, Aaron burns the spice, Tending lamps, making it precise.
"Evening comes, the incense burns again, A sweet scent rising, like a holy refrain.
"No strange incense, nor offering here, Only atonement, once a year.
"Blood on the horns, for the sin's release, It’s sacred to Yahweh, it won't cease."
Then God spoke, with a census plan, "Each man's ransom, show where you stand.
"Half a shekel, sanctuary's rate, Each soul's offering, don't debate.
"Rich and poor, equal, face to face, To make atonement, for your soul's place.
"Use that silver, for the Tent's affair, Memorial for Israel, in Yahweh's care."
"Make a bronze basin, for washing clean, Set between tent and altar seen.
"Aaron and sons, wash hands and feet, Before they come near, or their lives will deplete.
"Statute forever, through generations, Purity required for holy ministrations."
Then more words from God’s own voice, "Gather fine spices, but make the right choice.
"Liquid myrrh, and cinnamon sweet, Cane and cassia, for the mix complete.
"A holy oil, anointing all, Tent and altar, large or small.
"Make it holy, set apart, Nothing like it, in your heart.
"Anoint Aaron, sons sanctify, They serve as priests, pure and high.
"To Israel, this oil is mine, No imitations, none entwine.
"Compounds like this, for common use, Cut off that one, there's no excuse."
"Take sweet spices, frankincense pure, Create incense, holy and sure.
"Seasoned fine, pure, and holy made, In the Tent of Meeting, let it be laid.
"This incense sacred, none for your pleasure, For Yahweh alone, it’s my treasure.
"Whoever makes it for himself to smell, Cut him off, there he shall dwell."
Yahweh spoke to Moses, His chosen one, "Behold, Bezalel, skilled and wise as the sun.
Filled with My Spirit, to craft and to build, Gold, silver, bronze, with his hands he's skilled.
Stones he will cut, wood he will carve, All kinds of workmanship his mind will starve.
Oholiab too, from Dan’s great line, With wisdom in hearts, for My plan divine.
The Tent of Meeting, with each sacred piece, The ark, the mercy seat, their works won't cease.
Tables, lampstands, incense to arise, Garments for priests, holy in their eyes.
Anointing oil, sweet incense to smell, According to My commands they'll do well."
Yahweh continued, His voice strong, "Tell Israel of the Sabbath, where they belong.
A sign between us, through your line it shall stay, I am Yahweh, who sanctifies in this way.
Keep it holy, set apart and blessed, Profane it, you'll face eternal rest.
Six days for labor, the seventh you rest, Who works on Sabbath, won't be blessed.
A covenant perpetual, for generations to hold, In six days I made all, on the seventh, I'm told,
I rested, refreshed, a sign to see, Between Me and Israel, eternally."
When words were finished on Sinai’s peak, Moses received tablets, God's words to speak. Stone tablets written with finger divine, A covenant of stone, for all of time.
Moses was delayed, and the people grew wild, "Make us gods," they said, voices defiled. Aaron nodded, "Bring me your gold," Earrings, rings, treasures untold.
They brought him the gold, from ears it came, He molded a calf, they shouted its name. "These are your gods," they cried with glee, "That brought you out of Egypt, set you free."
Aaron built an altar, "A feast we’ll raise," Early they gathered, with offerings and praise. God saw from the mountain, spoke to Moses in flame, "Your people have turned, corrupted my name."
"They’ve made a calf, worshiped and bowed, Said it's their god, voices loud and proud. I see they're stiff-necked, wrath burns hot, Leave me alone, consume them on the spot."
But Moses pleaded, "God, calm your fire, Remember your promise, your holy desire. Abraham, Isaac, Israel you swore, Their children would grow, like stars evermore."
God relented, his anger subdued, Moses descended, with God's tablets imbued. Joshua heard noise, thought war was near, But Moses knew it was dancing and cheer.
He saw the calf, and his anger did spark, Threw down the tablets, shattered in the ark. Burned the calf, scattered it on the stream, Made Israel drink, to erase the dream.
"What have you done?" Moses asked with a glare, Aaron shrugged, "You know their evil stare. They gave me gold, I threw it in flame, Out came this calf, I'm not to blame."
Moses called, "Who stands with Yahweh, arise!" Levites gathered, swords ready, eyes wise. "Go through the camp," was the divine command, Three thousand fell by their hand.
"Consecrate yourselves," Moses announced, "On Yahweh's side, your loyalty pronounced." Next day Moses climbed, to plead once more, "For this great sin, mercy implore."
"Oh, they've sinned, made gods of gold, Forgive them, blot me out if I’m too bold." God replied, "Each sinner I'll judge, Lead them on, my angel won’t budge."
God struck the people, a lesson told, For sins with the calf, their actions bold.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Time to depart, You and your people, make a new start. To the land I promised, flowin' milk and honey, An angel leads, but I'll keep my distance, sonny.
You're a stiff-necked people, and I'd consume, So strip off your jewels, don't meet your doom." The news hit hard, they mourned in tears, Jewels abandoned, facing their fears.
Moses pitched the Tent, far from the crowd, Seeking Yahweh, where no one's allowed. People stood up as Moses went in, The cloud descended, where the talks begin.
Face to face, like friends, they spoke, Moses turned back, as the people awoke. Joshua stayed, never left the Tent, Moses asked Yahweh, "Show me what you meant.
You said, 'I know you, you've found my favor,' Show me your way, let me savor." "My presence goes with you," Yahweh did rest, "Without you, we can't leave, won't pass the test."
"How will they know? We're your chosen crew," Yahweh replied, "I'll go with you too. You've found favor, I know your name, Ask what you will, I'll do the same."
"Show me your glory," Moses did plea, "My goodness will pass, but you can't see me. I'll be gracious, show mercy where I choose, My face unseen, it'll mean your lose."
"Stand on the rock, here's where you'll stay, My glory passes, my hand will sway. I'll cover you first, then the vision will lack, Remove my hand, you'll see my back."
Moses on a mountain, tablets to renew, Yahweh's words to write, for the people true. "Chisel them like the first, be ready at dawn, Come to Sinai's top, where my glory's drawn.
Alone you must come, no one else can see, Not even the flocks should be grazing near me." Moses rose early with two tablets of stone, To the peak of Sinai, where he'd meet God alone.
Yahweh in the cloud, His presence came near, Proclaiming His name, His voice we could hear. "Merciful and gracious, slow to anger," He said, "Lovingkindness and truth, from God they are spread.
Forgiving the sin, but justice is sure, From fathers to sons, the guilt will endure." Moses bowed low, worshiped, and then, "Have mercy," he asked, "on this stiff-necked men.
Make us yours, forgive our sin, Let your presence with us begin." "I'll make a covenant, marvels I'll show, Nations before you, their strength I'll throw.
Break down their altars, shatter their stone, Worship no other, worship me alone." "Keep the feasts, remember the days, Rest on the seventh, in plowing and blaze.
Bring me your first, the fruits of the ground, My covenant stands, in these words found." Moses on the mountain, forty nights and days, The covenant written, in God's holy ways.
When Moses came down, his face full of light, The people saw glory, shining so bright. He shared God's commands, with veiled face, But before Yahweh, the veil had no place.
The people stood back, but they came near, To hear the commandments, their hearts to steer. Moses' face shining, the veil would return, Until once more to God, his face would turn.
Moses gathered the crowd, he had words to convey, "This is what Yahweh commands, follow His way.
Work six days, but take the seventh to rest, A holy Sabbath for Yahweh, it's truly blessed.
No fire in your homes on that Sabbath day, Break this rule, and there's a price to pay."
Then Moses declared to the congregation wide, "Yahweh's command, let it be your guide.
Bring an offering, from hearts that are free, Gold, silver, bronze—bring it willingly.
Blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, Rams' skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood to share.
Oil for the light, spices sweet and rare, Onyx stones for the ephod, breastplate with care.
Wise-hearted folks, come and make what's planned, The tabernacle, the coverings, all by Yahweh's command.
The ark and its poles, the mercy seat of gold, The veil, the table with vessels, the stories of old.
Lampstand for light, the altar's incense sweet, Doors of the tabernacle, every detail neat.
Altar of burnt offering, bronze grating and base, Court hangings, gate screens, pins in their place.
Garments for Aaron, the priest's holy attire, All these are needed, as Yahweh did require."
The people left, their hearts moved and inspired, Men and women came, with gifts they were fired.
With brooches, earrings, rings, and gold, All who had treasures, their offerings told.
Blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen brought near, Goats' hair spun by women with wisdom clear.
Rulers brought stones, for ephod and breastplate, Spices and oil, their offerings were great.
Israel brought offerings, their heartstrings played, For all that Yahweh had Moses say.
"Behold," said Moses, "Yahweh's chosen by name, Bezalel, son of Uri, steps into fame.
Filled with God's Spirit, wisdom and skill, To craft in gold, silver, with craftsmanship's thrill.
Stones to be set, wood carved with grace, Bezalel and Oholiab, teaching their place.
Wisdom of heart, for every artful hand, To weave, embroider, create as planned."
Bezalel and Oholiab, their skills divine, Crafting the sanctuary, every line. God gave wisdom, hearts stirred to create, Each wise worker, their hands wouldn't wait.
Morning offerings, the people did bring, More than enough, so the craftsmen could sing. Moses said, “Stop! No more needs to come, The work is complete, and then some.”
Fine twined linens, blue, purple, and red, Curtains with cherubim skillfully spread. Twenty-eight cubits long, four cubits wide, Five curtains together, seamlessly tied.
Loops of blue, fifty each side, Golden clasps, the curtains unify and abide. Curtains of goat hair to cover the tent, Eleven pieces with purpose bent.
Covers of ram skins, dyed deep red, Sea cow hides placed up overhead. Boards of acacia, tall and grand, Standing upright, by wisdom's hand.
Sockets of silver, holding strong, Every board in place, where they belong. Bars of acacia, overlaid with gold, Holding the structure, mighty and bold.
Veil of blue, purple, scarlet hue, Cherubim dancing, skillful and true. Pillars of acacia, overlaid with gold, Silver sockets, the structure controlled.
Screen for the entrance, colors displayed, Embroidered with care, each stitch carefully laid. Five golden pillars stand in a row, Bronze sockets anchoring, steady and slow.
The work complete, each detail precise, A tabernacle worthy, a holy device.
Bezalel got to work, with acacia wood in hand, Building the ark, the finest in the land. Two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, Pure gold inside and out, molding gleaming with pride.
Four golden rings he cast, at the ark's four feet, Poles of acacia wood, with gold complete. In those rings, he slid the poles to bear, A mercy seat of gold, shining fair.
Two cherubim of gold, wings spread wide, Faces toward each other, by the mercy seat they abide. Crafted from one piece, at each end they stand, Guardians of glory, crafted by skilled hand.
Next, he made a table, acacia wood its base, Two cubits long, a cubit wide, a cubit and a half in space. Overlaid with gold, a border around, Four rings on the corners, to carry it when bound.
Dishes, spoons, bowls, pitchers, all gold shining bright, Golden vessels for the table, a marvelous sight. The lamp stand next, of gold so pure, Beaten work of beauty, every detail sure.
Six branches out each side, cups like almond blooms, Buds and flowers crafted, filling the room. Four cups on the stand, buds beneath each pair, A masterpiece of gold, crafted with such care.
Seven lamps, snuffers, all of gold's embrace, A talent's worth of pure gold, in every place. The altar of incense, acacia wood and gold, Square and splendid, a sight to behold.
Rings on its sides, poles to carry there, Anointing oil and incense, scents fill the air. Bezalel made it all, with hands skilled and true, Every piece was crafted, in gold's radiant hue.
Acacia wood crafted into an altar square, Five by five by three, standing tall with care.
Horns at the corners, bronzed and bold, With vessels of bronze, the story's retold.
A grating of bronze, network designed, Four rings cast, perfectly aligned.
Poles of wood, bronzed in display, Fit in the rings to carry away.
Bronze basin from mirrors, polished and clean, Where ministering women once were seen.
Court of linen, south side's long, Twenty pillars standing strong.
North side matches, a hundred feet wide, Pillars and sockets, harmony abide.
West side, fifty cubits of grace, Silver hooks on pillars in place.
East side's entry, fifty cubits long, Each gate adorned, a beautiful song.
Screen embroidered with colors so grand, Blue, purple, and scarlet, all at hand.
Materials counted, the Tabernacle's weight, Moses directed, Ithamar's state.
Bezalel and Oholiab, skillful and true, Crafting all that the Lord had them do.
Gold, silver, and bronze measured right, Sanctuary's beauty, a glorious sight.
Sockets and hooks, each in their spot, Under the Tabernacle, every lot.
Bronze altar, grating, and vessels all, Pins of the Tabernacle, standing tall.
With blue, purple, scarlet thread, the garments they made, For the holy place, finely crafted, as Yahweh bade.
Ephod of gold, colors that shine, Woven with skill, a work divine.
Gold plates beaten, cut into wire, Mixed with fabrics to inspire.
Shoulder straps joined at two ends, A woven band, where skill and gold blend.
Onyx stones set in gold to shine, Names engraved, a memorial sign.
Breastplate crafted, square and bold, Gold, blue, purple like stories told.
Double its span, rows of stones set tight, Ruby, turquoise, sapphire, a color delight.
Chains of gold, braided and strong, Rings and settings where they belong.
On ephod’s front, chains do cling, Bound with blue, like a king's ring.
Robe woven all in blue, Opening bound, work they knew.
Pomegranates and bells interlace, A rhythmic dance, in holy place.
Tunics fine, for Aaron’s sons, Linen headbands when service runs.
Holy crown of gold inscribed, "HOLY TO YAHWEH," it described.
Tabernacle work now complete, Every piece brought to Moses’ feet.
Tent and furniture, all arrayed, As Yahweh commanded, each part laid.
Moses saw, and to them he said, “You've done as Yahweh's words were led.”
And with a blessing, he closed the day, As they followed what Yahweh did say.
"First day, first month, raise it tall," The tabernacle's up, where He'll call.
Ark inside, wrapped in the veil, Table next, order prevail.
"Bring the lamp, let it shine bright, Set the incense, make it right."
Altar's there, near the tent door, Basin's filled, water's pour.
"Anoint it all, make it holy, Every piece, sanctify solely."
Aaron's sons, wash them clean, Holy garments, priestly scene.
"Anoint them, serve in this space, Everlasting priesthood, their place."
Moses acted as commanded, all was done, Tabernacle raised under the sun.
Sockets laid, boards set wide, Pillars high, coverings tied.
Ark inside, mercy seat on top, Veil set up, there won't be a stop.
Table and bread, on the north side, Lamp stand south, light won't hide.
Golden altar, incense burns sweet, Screen at the door, the work's complete.
Offerings given, as Moses was told, Basin there, water cold.
Hands and feet washed, pure and clean, Priests prepared, seen and unseen.
Cloud descends, glory fills that space, Moses steps back, can't show his face.
When cloud lifted, they moved ahead, But stayed put, if it still spread.
By day a cloud, by night fire's glow, Israel watched, ready to go.
Yahweh called Moses, His voice clear and loud, From the Tent of Meeting, amidst the gathered crowd.
"Speak to Israel's kin, let this message ring, When offering to Yahweh, bring the best you can bring.
From your livestock, your herds, your flock's finest, A sacrifice to the Lord, make sure it's the rightness.
For a burnt offering from the herd, bring a male, no defect, At the Tent's entrance, for Yahweh to accept.
Lay your hand on its head, find atonement in its stead, Slay the bull for the Lord, where the sacrifice is led.
Aaron's sons, the priests, handle the blood with care, Sprinkle it on the altar, let it purify the air.
Skin the offering, cut it piece by piece, Fire on the altar, the fragrance released.
Put the head, the fat, on wood in a row, Wash the innards, let the pure water flow.
Priests burn it all up, a pleasing aroma it brings, A burnt offering to Yahweh, where the fire sings.
If it's from the flock, sheep or goats you bring, A male without defect, let the ritual swing.
On the north side, before Yahweh, let its life go, Blood sprinkled round the altar, let the purity flow.
Cut in pieces, head and fat laid on wood, Wash innards with water, offer it good.
Burn the whole on the altar, let the smoke rise high, A pleasant aroma for Yahweh, reaching to the sky.
For birds as an offering, turtledoves or young pigeons are fair, Bring them to the altar, the priest will prepare.
Wring off the head, let the blood be drained, Feathers cast aside, in ashes they’re contained.
Tear it by wings, but keep it as one, Burn it on the altar, to Yahweh, it is done.
A burnt offering, a fire that pleases Yahweh's sight, Sacrifices burning, in the day and in the night."
When you bring a meal to Yahweh’s domain, Fine flour’s the ticket, don’t forget the grain. Pour oil on top, with frankincense, Bring it to Aaron’s sons, commence.
A handful taken by the priest's own hand, Burned on the altar, sweet aroma so grand. What remains is for Aaron and his kin, It's sacred, from the fire, let the feast begin.
Unleavened cakes from the oven's heat, Mixed with oil, now it's ready to meet. Or wafers anointed, baked with care, Offering on the griddle, flour and oil in there.
Cut in pieces, drizzle oil on the lot, When it’s on the pan, give it all you got. Bring it forth to Yahweh’s holy place, Priest at the altar, giving thanks and grace.
No yeast, no honey in this holy fire, Burn none on the altar, it’s Yahweh’s desire. Season with salt, covenant’s embrace, Never without it, in the offering’s space.
First fruits come with fresh grain and fire, Crushed and mixed with oil, raising higher. Frankincense laid, it’s a meal divine, Burned by the priest on Yahweh’s line.
The aroma rises, the offering’s right, In the holy fire, a precious sight. Aaron’s sons feast on what’s left behind, Offerings to Yahweh, in them we find.
When you bring a peace offering, here’s the deal, From the herd, male or female, make it real.
Spotless and pure, before Yahweh it's laid, Hand on the head, then it's slain where the priests prayed.
Aaron’s sons, priests, sprinkle blood on the altar flame, The sacrifice, the fire, to Yahweh’s name.
The fat on the innards, kidneys, liver’s cover, Take it all away, then burn it, let the smoke hover.
On the altar wood, where the fire's burning bright, Offering to Yahweh, aroma's pure delight.
From the flock now, if lambs are what you bring, Spotless, pure, before Yahweh, do your thing.
Hand on the head, at the Meeting Tent it’s slain, Aaron’s sons, the blood around the altar, again.
Fire offering, the fat and tail, take away, By the backbone, entrails, innards, no delay.
Priests burn it up, the food of fire divine, Smoky scent to Yahweh, in the air it will entwine.
And if it’s a goat, bring it here, no joke, Hand on its head, before God, blood soaked.
Sprinkle on the altar, just like before, Fat, kidneys, liver, take it all, restore.
Priests burn it all, offering’s smoky rise, Pleasant aroma, reaching to the skies.
Always remember, through all generations wide, In your homes, no blood, no fat, let Yahweh’s word abide.
Yahweh told Moses, "Listen, this is the deal, Speak to Israel, make their sins real.
If the priest sins, brings guilt on the crowd, A young bull without defect, this offering's allowed.
Bring it to the Tent, lay hands, then take its life, Before Yahweh, the bull meets the knife.
The priest dips his finger in blood, sprinkle it right, Seven times before Yahweh, make the veil bright.
Blood on the altar's horns, incense sweet, Pour the rest at the base where burnt offerings meet.
Take the bull's fat, kidneys, and liver too, Burn them on the altar, that's what you do.
Skin, meat, head, legs — take it all out, Burn it outside the camp, where ashes shout.
If all Israel sins, but the deed's unknown, When the truth comes out, the sin must be atoned.
Bring a young bull, the elders lay hands, Before Yahweh, the bull falls by commands.
Blood in the Tent, sprinkled seven-fold, Horns of the altar, as the ritual's told.
Fat on the altar, a fire's embrace, Forgiveness follows, sin leaves no trace.
A ruler's sin, unaware at first, When it's known, he brings a goat unrehearsed.
Hands on the goat, offering's site, Blood on the altar, a sacred rite.
All of its fat, like peace offerings laid, Atonement made, forgiveness paid.
Common folks sin, unwitting they do, A female goat, without flaw, will do.
Hands on its head, sin offering's plight, Blood on the altar, forgive through the night.
Fat like before, a sweet aroma's lift, Atonement granted, Yahweh's gift.
If a lamb's brought, female without defect, Hands on the head, kill as respect.
Blood on the altar, pour at the base, Fat's removed, burned in its place.
In all these offerings, forgiveness's the goal, Atonement secures, and heals the soul.
When you hear a call, a chance to speak, But stay silent, your guilt will peak. Touch something foul, unseen by your eye, Later you find out, can't deny the why.
If you touch what's unclean from a man, Once you know, guilty you'll stand. Swear an oath, good or bad from the lip, Forget about it, but guilt's got a grip.
Admit your wrongs, confess your sin, Bring an offering, let atonement begin. Can't afford a lamb? No need to freeze, Two birds will suffice, Yahweh to please.
Blood on the altar, a sin offering laid, Atonement made, your debts repaid. If even the birds are beyond your reach, Fine flour will do, no frankincense to breach.
Priest takes a handful, burns it on the flame, Sin's forgiven; Yahweh's mercy's the same. Trespass the holy, unaware of the wrong, A spotless ram's the price, strong and long.
Add a fifth more, to make things right, Priest makes atonement, sin's out of sight. Even unknown sins carry the blame, Bring forth a ram, atone just the same.
Guilt before Yahweh, no matter the scene, But forgiveness awaits, washed pure and clean.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, right on the scene, "If anyone sins and treats their neighbor mean, In matters of deposit or bargain gone astray, Or steals, oppresses, lies in any way—
If guilty of sin, they must make it right, Return what they took, bring it to the light. Add a fifth to the value, pay it back in full, On the day they're found guilty, not just when they're cool.
Bring a ram without defect, that's the deal, For the trespass offering, for the priest to seal. He'll make atonement, offer it before Yahweh's face, Then forgiveness is given, guilt erased.
Yahweh spoke to Moses once more, "Command Aaron, these laws they can't ignore: The burnt offering stays on the altar's flame, Through the night till morning, the fire stays the same.
Put on linen garments, remove the ash with care, Change clothes, take it outside, clear the air. Keep the fire burning, wood each morning lay, Burn the fat and offerings in Yahweh's way.
The meal offering's law, Aaron's sons present, Take fine flour, oil, frankincense, as they're meant. Burn it on the altar, sweet aroma rise, Rest is eaten holy, no yeast in the guise.

Aaron's sons eat it, in the holy court they meet, Without yeast, it's their portion, a perpetual treat. Each male from Aaron's line, this is their decree, Touching these offerings, set apart, holy shall be.
Yahweh spoke again, "Aaron's offering's clear, When anointed, flour's tenth part, day and year. With oil on a griddle, soaked and baked, A pleasant aroma to Yahweh, never faked.
Anointed sons shall offer it, this statute stands, Wholly burned to Yahweh, by priestly hands. No priest's meal offering shall be consumed, It's burned completely, none assumed.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, once more the news, "The sin offering's law, these words you must use: Where the burnt offering's killed, sin offering's slain, It’s most holy, part of the priestly domain.
The priest shall eat it, in a holy place, Court of the Tent, where sacred's the space. Touch its flesh, be holy, wash blood from clothes, The vessel that's used, break or clean as it goes.
Every priestly male eats, it's holy, no joke, But if blood enters the Tent, burn it in smoke.
This is the law, the holy code, where offerings are slain, In the place of burnt fires, where blood does rain.
The fat is gathered, tail and innards, laid bare, The kidneys, the liver, handled with care.
Priests burn it on the altar, a fire divine, It's a trespass offering, Yahweh's holy sign.
Every male priest may eat, in a sacred place, Holy food, holy space, a holy race.
"Like the sin offering, the trespass is the same, The priest who offers it knows the claim."
The priest keeps the skin, a burnt reward, Meal offerings baked, priestly accord.
"Offering to Yahweh, a peace sacrifice you give, Thanksgiving cakes with oil, that’s how you live."
One cake from each, lifted up high, Given to the priest, who sprinkles the blood nigh.
Eat the flesh on the day it is given, Leave none till morning, a law from heaven.
"A vow, free will, next day you can eat, Third day’s meat, burn it with heat."
Unclean meat? Burned, not for eating, Keep Yahweh’s peace offerings, pure in their seating.
"Touch not the unclean, don't eat in shame, Your soul shall be cut off, bear the blame."
Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Tell Israel, heed, No fat, no blood, that is my creed."
"The fat of the dead, or torn, not for food, Eat it not, or be cut off, understood?"
"Peace offerings to Yahweh, bring with your hands, Fat and breast waved, as the Lord commands."
Priests burn the fat, but Aaron gets the chest, The right thigh goes to the priest, part of the rest.
"For Aaron’s sons, the wave, the heave, Portions from Israel, for them I leave."
Consecration for Aaron, and his sons too, From offerings by fire, from Israel's view.
These are the laws from Sinai's land, Offer to Yahweh, obey His command.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, here's the plan, "Take Aaron, his sons, get the oil, garments in hand.
Grab the bull and two rams, bread unleavened, Gather the crowd at the Tent, make sure it's heaven."
Moses did what Yahweh had said, Congregation gathered, full of dread.
"This is what Yahweh’s commanded," Moses declared, Aaron and sons all got washed and prepared.
He dressed Aaron in a tunic, sash tied tight, Robe, ephod, breastplate, shining bright.
Turban on his head with a crown of gold, As Yahweh commanded, the story unfolds.
Anointing oil Moses spread all around, Sanctified the tabernacle, altar, ground.
Poured oil on Aaron, sanctified his head, Clothed his sons, just like Yahweh said.
The sin-offering bull, they laid hands on its brow, Moses killed it, blood on the altar now.
Purified the altar, atonement made, Burned the bull’s fat, as Yahweh bade.
Ram of burnt offering, hands laid again, Blood sprinkled, cut into pieces then.
Burned on the altar, aroma sweet, As Yahweh commanded, Moses' feat.
Second ram for consecration, hands laid once more, Blood on ear, thumb, toe, poured on the floor.
Fat and bread waved, offering in the air, Burned on the altar, smoke in the air.
Oil and blood on Aaron, garments too, Sanctified the priesthood, holy and true.
"Boil the meat, eat it at the Tent's door, Seven days inside, till vows are no more.
Do this as Yahweh’s atonement for you, Stay in the Tent, keep Yahweh’s commands true."
Aaron and sons followed every command, As Yahweh directed, through Moses' hand.
On the eighth day, Moses set the scene, Called Aaron, sons, elders — a holy routine. "Bring a calf and a ram, pure as can be, Lay them before Yahweh, as an offering decree.
Tell Israel, 'A goat for your sins, A calf and a lamb, pure, without sins. A bull and a ram, for peace they shall bring, Yahweh appears, His glory will swing.'"

They gathered 'round the Tent, congregation was tight, Moses spoke, "Do this, Yahweh's glory will ignite." He turned to Aaron, said, "Near to the altar step, Make atonement for you and the people's debt."
Aaron approached, the calf he did slay, His sons gave him blood, by the altar it lay. Finger dipped, blood on horns, base soaked deep, Fat and organs burned, Yahweh's command he'd keep.
Meat and skin sent outside, with fire they'd meet, Burnt offering slain, blood on the altar complete. Piece by piece, head to flame, Washed the parts, the altar they claimed.
Goat for the people, sin offering's call, Just like the first, offered for all. Burnt offering up, ordinance set, Meal offering burned, morning's duet.
Bull and ram slaughtered for peace, Blood sprinkled 'round, offerings didn't cease. Fat tails, kidneys, all the rest, On the altar, the fat did rest.
Wave that breast and thigh high, Before Yahweh, watched sky. Aaron lifted hands, blessings did flow, From sin, burnt, and peace, blessings did grow.
Into the Tent, Moses and Aaron both went, Came out, blessed the crowd, in Yahweh's glory they were sent. Fire from Yahweh, offering consumed, The people shouted, faces to the ground they were doomed.
Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron’s line, Took their censers, put fire, thought it'd be fine. But it was strange fire, not a command, Before Yahweh they stood, it got out of hand.
Fire blazed forth, Yahweh’s fierce flame, Devoured them right there, in His name. Moses turned to Aaron, solemn and deep, "This is Yahweh’s word, His holiness we keep."
Aaron stood silent, holding his peace, Moses called kin, giving commands with ease: "Come close, carry them out from the holy place, Outside the camp, in their tunics, no trace."
To Aaron and sons, Moses clearly said, "Don’t mourn as usual, keep your heads; Let Israel cry for the fire Yahweh lit, Stay in the Tent, for the oil’s on you, admit."
Yahweh spoke clear to Aaron and his crew, "No wine in the Tent, or death comes to you. This rule stands forever, through all your days, Distinguish the holy, teach Israel My ways."
Moses spoke on, to Aaron’s sons who remained, "Take the meal offering, as Yahweh ordained. Eat it beside the altar, no yeast—most holy, ‘Cause it’s your share, a command not lowly."

The waved breast, the heaved thigh, eat in clean space, Your portion, your sons’, with your daughters in place. Wave it before Yahweh, your portion forever, As commanded, no changes, remember, be clever."
Moses then checked, the sin offering’s fate, It was gone, all burned, he got irate. "Why didn’t you eat it in the holy place? It’s for atonement, don’t lose that grace."
Aaron replied, his voice low and grave, "Today’s offerings happened, all that we gave; Had I eaten, would it please Yahweh’s sight?" Moses heard Aaron, and found it alright.
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron, real clear, “Tell Israel what’s good to eat, lend me your ear.
From animals that roam and graze the land, Those with split hooves and cud in their hand.
Don’t touch the camel, though it chews smooth, No split hoof, unclean, it’s not the move.
The hyrax, the hare, chew but lack the break, Unclean they are, no meat on your plate.
The pig’s hooves split, but it don’t chew the cud, Unclean to you, don’t eat, don’t touch that mud.
In waters, fins and scales are the key, If they lack these, they’re not for thee.
Detest those swimming without scale or fin, An abomination, don’t let them in.
Birds like eagles, vultures, kites of black, Unclean these wings, don’t take them back.
Owls and gulls, hawks and such, Don’t touch these birds, you’ll lose your touch.
Insects that fly, but walk on all fours, An abomination, don’t open those doors.
Yet locusts, katydids, crickets, and grasshoppers, They’re okay to eat, jumpin’ like talkers.
Touch their carcass, you’re unclean till night, Wash your clothes, cleanse away the blight.
Animals with paws or half-split feet, Unclean they are, not for your treat.
Touch their bodies, unclean till day ends, A rinse and repeat, no need to pretend.
Creeping things that slither and crawl, Unclean they are, don’t heed their call.
If their dead bodies touch your gear, Wash those items, till the end is near.
God said, “I am holy, be like Me, Don’t defile yourselves, stay clean, be free.
I brought you out from Egypt's land, Be holy, follow My command.”
The law is clear for beasts of all kind, Distinguish the clean, keep purity in mind."
Yahweh to Moses, hear what I say, "Speak to Israel, guide them this way.
If a woman births a son, seven days she's unclean, Just like her monthly time, you know what I mean.
On day eight, that's when it's done, Circumcise the flesh of her young one.
Thirty-three days, purifying flows, No holy touch until that time goes.
For a daughter, two weeks she's apart, Sixty-six days for the purifying start.
When purification days are through, Bring to the priest, here's what to do:
A lamb for burning and a dove for sin, At the Tent of Meeting, let the cleansing begin.
The priest offers them up to Yahweh's throne, Atonement made, she's cleansed, she's home.
This is the rule for birthing, girl or boy, Let the purification bring cleansing joy.
If a lamb she can't afford to find, Two doves or pigeons will do just fine.
One for burning, one for atoning, The priest makes her clean, no more groaning."
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron with might, "If a man has a spot or a scab that's bright, Bring him to Aaron or one of his sons, Let the priest decide what must be done.
Is the hair white? Is the plague deep? Pronounce him unclean, don’t let him keep. But if the spot isn't deeper and hair stays the same, Seven days alone, the priest will proclaim.
On the seventh day, check him again, Is it stable, or does it remain? If it rests, another seven days, Watch it close, in all its ways.
If it fades, then he's clean, wash his gear, But if it spreads, the priest must steer. Look again, if it's white, but flesh is raw, Chronic leprosy, beyond nature's law.
When the skin's all white, from head to feet, If it's all covered, he's clean in defeat. Yet raw flesh says uncleanness stays, The priest will judge in all these ways.
Boils, burns, and spots so white, Priest examines by day or night. If the hair turns or the plague digs deep, Declare unclean, let him not weep.
On the skin, if spreads it might, Unclean he is, until it's right. But if it stays or fades away, He is clean, the priest will say.
In the beard or on the head, Yellow thin hair, by priest is read. If the itch spreads not, and black hairs grow, He's clean once more, let him know.
If it's just a harmless rash, He is clean, no need to dash. Bald or forehead without a scare, Clean he is, let him wear.
But red-white plague on the bald head found, Unclean he is, priest will pronounce around. The leper cries, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’ Dwelling alone, unseen, unseen.
Garments too, with plague so green, Priest examines, seven days intervene. If it spreads, burn the clothes in fire, If it fades, wash—higher and higher.
Mildew on threads, it's a test, Priest decides, clean or unrest. This is the law for spots and mold, The priest determines, truth be told."

Yahweh spoke to Moses, laying it down clear, "Here's the law for a leper when cleansing is near. Bring him to the priest, out from the camp's hold, The priest checks him out, sees if the plague's been controlled.

If leprosy's healed, then here's what you'll need: Two clean birds, wood of cedar, scarlet, and hyssop proceed. One bird gets killed in an earthen jar, under running stream, The living bird's dipped with scarlet and hyssop, to seal the dream.

The priest sprinkles the leper seven times to proclaim, "You're clean now," he says, and lets the living bird take aim, Flying into the open field, free as a breeze, The leper washes clothes, shaves, bathes, and feels the peace.

Seven days outside his tent, then on the seventh day, Shaves off all his hair, washes, cleans, he's okay. By day eight, it's time for lambs and flour untold, As offerings mixed with oil, a ritual bold.

The priest sets the scene at the Tent of Meeting's door, Waves the lamb for trespass, it's all part of the core. Kill the lamb for trespass, in the holy place it goes, Blood on ear, thumb, and toe, that's how the ritual flows.

Oil's poured in the palm, sprinkled seven times before, Some on the ear, thumb, toe, mixing blood and oil more. Rest of the oil anoints his head, a holy sign, Atonement made, cleansed and clean by divine design.

If he's short on cash, brings what he can afford, Two doves or pigeons, offerings to the Lord. The priest makes atonement, with oil and birds in flight, The cleansing ritual's done, everything's set right.
Yahweh spoke again, laying it down plain, "When you enter Canaan, and mildew brings pain, The house owner tells the priest, 'There's a plague in sight,' Empty the house, inspect it by daylight.
If greenish-red streaks deeper than the stone, Seal the house seven days, leave it alone. Return on the seventh, see if the plague has grown, Stones are pulled, and the house is overthrown.
Scrape inside, mortar out to an unclean place, New stones, fresh plaster, give it a new face. If mildew returns, breaking out full force, The house comes down, timber and stones, no remorse.
But if the house stays clean, with no plague in the air, Pronounce it clean, for the plague’s no longer there. Two birds, cedar, scarlet, cleanse the place, Blood and water, set the house in grace.
The living bird flies free, into the open field, Atonement made, the house is healed. These are the laws for leprosy and itch, For garments and houses, whether clean or rich.
Swelling, scabs, spots, this is how you know, When it's unclean or clean, let the law show."
Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron, set the word, "Tell the people, listen close, make sure it's heard.
If a man has a discharge, he's unclean, no doubt, Whether it flows or stops, that's what it's about.
Every bed he lies on becomes defiled, Everything he touches, gotta wash it, mild to wild.
Touch his bed, wash your clothes, take a shower, Till evening comes, you're unclean, that's the power.
If you sit where he sat, same rules apply, Wash up, clean up, wait till night draws nigh.
Touch his body, wash your clothes, don't delay, Bathe in water, wait it out till the end of day.
If he spits, wash what you wear, Till evening, uncleanness there to bear.
Ride his saddle, it's unclean, Touch what's under, stay unseen.
Touch without rinsing, wash it all, Wait till evening, that's the call.
Earthen vessel he touches, break it down, Wooden one, rinse it, don't let it drown.
When he's cleansed, count seven days clear, Wash his clothes, bathe away any fear.
On day eight, bring two birds to the gate, Priest makes atonement, it's Yahweh's fate.
If there's an emission, bathe the body whole, Wait till evening, let time roll.
Garments and skin, wash them down, Till evening comes, in uncleanness drown.
Man and woman, if they lie, Bathe till evening, let it dry.
If a woman bleeds, she's unclean for seven, Touch her, wait till evening, then you're forgiven.
Lies on her bed, it's unclean, Sits anywhere, same hygiene.
Touch her bed, wash clothes, bathe, Evening comes, then you're saved.
Touch her seat, same rules apply, Wash and wait till night passes by.
If a man lies with her, impurity flows, Seven days unclean, everybody knows.
If her blood flows beyond the time, Treat it like her period, follow the rhyme.
Unclean for all those days, stay aware, Her bed, her seats, all need care.
Seven days after cleansing, then she's free, Bring two birds to the priest, sin offering to see.
Separate the people from uncleanness within, To keep them safe when the tabernacle's in.
This is the rule for discharge and flow, Keep it clean, that's how it goes."
Yahweh spoke to Moses after Aaron's sons’ fall, "Tell Aaron, don't come near the Most Holy at all,
Without a bull and a ram for the offerings' flame, Clothed in holy linen, washed in water, pure in name.
Two goats from the people, one ram on the side, A bull for his sin, for his household to abide.
Cast lots for the goats at the Tent's front door, One for Yahweh, one to roam the wilds, nothing more.
"Kill the bull for himself, atonement he must make, Take burning coals and incense, let the holy smoke rise and shake.
Sprinkle bull's blood on the mercy seat east, Seven times with his finger, to cover sins' beast.
Then the goat for the people, do the same as before, Sprinkle its blood on the mercy seat, cleanse the Holy's core.
Make atonement for the tent, where uncleanness dwells, Till no transgression lingers, where Yahweh's presence swells.
No one enters while atonement's in motion, For himself, his household, and all Israel, devotion.
Out to the altar, cleanse it with blood, Sprinkle seven times, purge the sin-flood.
Now the live goat, hands lay on its head, Confess all the sins, let the past be shed.
Release it in the wilderness, to a solitary land, Let it carry iniquities, by a ready man's hand.
Change clothes, wash up, bring offerings to flame, He and the people, free from sin's claim.
Burn the fat on the altar, let fire purify, The scapegoat's handler must cleanse before coming by.
Burn the bull and the goat outside the camp, Wash up and return, leaving no sin's stamp.
"This day shall be forever, on the tenth of the month, Do no work, seek atonement, rest from the hunt.
A Sabbath of solemn rest, afflict your soul, Cleanse before Yahweh, be made whole.

God spoke again, "If anyone sins, Confess and make it right, let the restitution begin. Add a fifth to the guilt, and pay it back, If no one's left to pay, to the priests it’ll track.
