A year-old lamb, for trespass made right, For days now void, restore them to light.
When the vow is fulfilled, to the Tent come near, Offer lambs without defect, peace is clear.
Bread unleavened, cakes with oil mixed, Priest presents the offerings, everything fixed.
The Nazirite shaves, hair on fire it lies, Under peace sacrifice, smoke to the skies.
Priest takes the ram's shoulder, cakes, and wafer, Waves before Yahweh, holy hands of the shaver.
Now the vow's complete, wine they can take, Nazirite law fulfilled, no mistake.
Yahweh’s words to Moses, Aaron must hear, "Bless Israel now, make my promise clear.
Yahweh bless you, keep you always near, Shine His face upon you, grace you hold dear.
Lift His countenance, give you peace and rest, My name on Israel, through you they'll be blessed."
Moses set up the tabernacle right, anointed and blessed, With furniture pure, altars at their best.
Princes of tribes stepped up with pride, Offering gifts with wagons by their side.
God said to Moses, "Accept what they bring, For the Levites' service, for the Tent's needs, they sing."
Moses took oxen and wagons, gave Gershon two, Four went to Merari, under Ithamar’s view.
But Kohath got none, they carried on their back, The sanctuary's service, no wagon they'd lack.
Princes brought offerings to the altar that day, Each prince on his own, in a dedicated way.
Nahshon from Judah, first to present, Silver, gold, and cattle, his offerings sent.
Next came Nethanel, from Issachar’s line, With trays of silver, and offerings so fine.
Eliab from Zebulun, with gifts on the third, Platter, bowl, and incense, his offerings heard.
Elizur of Reuben, on day four he came, With similar gifts, in Yahweh’s name.
Shelumiel of Simeon, day five was his call, He brought his portion, giving his all.
Eliasaph from Gad, on day six he gave, With offerings rich, his faith displayed.
Elishama from Ephraim, seventh in place, His gifts presented with reverent grace.
Gamaliel of Manasseh, day eight he brought, His offerings, just like those before, were sought.
Abidan from Benjamin, on the ninth day, Silver and gold, in the same array.
Ahiezer of Dan, with offerings on ten, Brought the same gifts as those before him did then.
Pagiel from Asher, day eleven he stands, Bringing the same gifts with devoted hands.
Ahira of Naphtali, on the twelfth day, Completed the cycle, with offerings to lay.
The altar's dedication, with gifts strong and bold, Twelve silver platters, twelve bowls, twelve ladles of gold.
Bulls, rams, and goats, in numbers they came, A dedication complete, each one the same.
Moses entered the Tent, to Yahweh he spoke, God's voice from the mercy seat, his heart awoke.
God told Moses, "Aaron's got a task, Light those lamps, make the light last." Aaron did it, lit up the scene, Just like God said, everything was clean.
The lamp stand's gold, beaten, not fake, From base to flowers, the craftsman's take. God showed Moses the pattern in sight, Every detail made just right.
God spoke again, "Levites you've got to cleanse, Take them out, make amends. Sprinkle water, shave them clean, Wash their clothes, make them keen."
"Bring a young bull, fine flour mixed with oil, Another bull for sin, make those offerings toil. Present the Levites at the Tent's domain, Gather the people, make it plain."
"Lay hands on Levites, for Yahweh they're a wave, Aaron will offer, their service they'll save. Levites touch bulls, a sin and burnt disguise, Atonement made, on Yahweh's rise."
Set them before Aaron, offer once more, Separate them, they're mine to the core. "The Levites enter, serve the Tent's call, They're mine from Israel, I chose them all."
"Firstborn are mine, from Egypt's wake, Levites are taken for Israel's sake. Gift to Aaron, to serve and atone, Keep Israel safe, no plague to bemoan."
Moses, Aaron, all Israel complied, Levites purified, washed, and sanctified. Wave offering given, atonement done, Levites ready, service begun.
Yahweh spoke, "Levites start at twenty-five, At fifty, they retire, no longer strive. Assist their brothers, help in the tent, This is their duty, how their time is spent."
In the wild Sinai, Yahweh spoke with flair, To Moses, His voice echoed through the desert air. “Tell Israel, keep Passover, mark the date, Fourteenth evening, don’t be late.”
Moses told them, “Do just as He said, Passover’s coming, prepare the bread.” They obeyed in Sinai, under moonlight's glow, Just as Yahweh commanded, in the desert below.
Some men approached, unclean from the dead, “We’re kept back, Yahweh’s feast, can’t be fed.” Moses said, “Hold on, let me hear the call, Yahweh’s command will settle it all.”
Yahweh spoke, “If unclean or distant you be, Still keep Passover, I decree. In the second month, on the fourteenth night, Eat with herbs and bread, by firelight.”
“Leave none till morning, don’t break a bone, Follow the statute, you’re not alone. But if clean and near, yet fail to keep, That soul shall be cut off, sins to reap.”
“If a stranger wants to join the feast, Let him follow every rule, not the least. One law for all, stranger or native-born, United in the statutes, no one’s torn.”
When the tabernacle rose, cloud covered it, Fire by night, in heaven it lit. At Yahweh’s command, they moved or stayed, The cloud's position was their parade.
Day or night, week or year, Where the cloud stayed, they held dear. Yahweh’s word was their guide, In His command they did abide.
Cloud up, they moved; cloud down, they rest, At Yahweh’s word, they did their best. In the desert vast, His will they sought, Following His lead, in His wisdom they were taught.
"Make two trumpets of silver," said Yahweh with grace, "Beat them from metal, for the gathering place.
Blow them both, and the crowd will come near, To the Tent of Meeting, they gather right here.
One trumpet sounds, and the leaders unite, Heads of the thousands, approach in the light.
Blow an alarm, east camp will roam, Blow it again, and the south side goes home.
For gatherings, just blow, no alarm for the show, Aaron's sons, the priests, are the ones in the know.
In war's grim face, sound the alarm loud, You'll be remembered by Yahweh, stand proud.
In joy, in feasts, and new month delights, Blow over offerings, and peace ignites.
In the second year, second month, day twenty, The cloud rose up, they journeyed plenty.
Out from Sinai, they followed the lead, The cloud rested in Paran, they moved with speed.
Judah led first under Nahshon's command, With tribes by their side, in covenant they stand.
Gershon and Merari took down the tabernacle frame, Reuben advanced, as Elizur called names.
Kohathites carried the sacred, no delay, Others set up before they made way.
Ephraim's camp moved, Elishama in charge, Manasseh and Benjamin followed the large.
Dan’s rear guard with Ahiezer’s call, Asher and Naphtali, they moved them all.
Moses spoke to Hobab, "Come travel our way, To the land Yahweh promised, come without delay."
Hobab replied, "I’ll return to my own, To familiar land where I’ve grown."
Moses implored, "Don’t leave us, we need your sight, Guide in the wilderness, be our guiding light.
Good from Yahweh, you’ll share in this too, Journey with us, and He'll be good to you."
Three days they traveled, Ark of Covenant ahead, Seeking a resting place, where they'd be led.
Cloud of Yahweh by day, shading the way, From camp they marched, in His presence they stay.
"Rise up, Yahweh," Moses declared, "Scatter the foes, let none be spared."
When resting, he prayed, "Return to us now, To Israel's thousands, with mighty vow."
In the camp, folks were complaining, loud and clear, God heard them moaning, His fire drew near.
Flames burned the edges, sparking fear and dread, "Cry to Moses!" they said, and the fire was dead.
Named it Taberah, 'cause there it did ignite, But the mixed crowd still craved more bites.
"Who'll give us meat?" they began to cry, "Remember fish, free in Egypt? We sigh.
Cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, garlic we crave, Now it's manna, manna—day by day, wave by wave."
Manna like seed, looked like bdellium stone, Ground in mills, boiled, tasted fresh oil alone.
Moses heard weeping, it struck him to the bone, "Why, God, have you left me carrying this load alone?
Did I give birth to them, that I should care? Where will I find meat? Their cries are everywhere.
If this is my plight, end my life, let it be, I'm too weak, don’t let them see my misery."
God said, "Gather seventy elders, wise and known, Bring them to the Tent, you're not alone.
I'll share your spirit; they'll carry that weight, And for my people, meat is their fate.
Prepare yourselves, for tomorrow’s feast, Not just days but a month, till you say 'cease.'
You wept to Me, said Egypt was sweet, You'll eat your fill, till meat's no treat."
Moses replied, "Six hundred thousand strong, How will you supply meat all month long?"
God answered, "Has My hand grown short? Watch and see; my promise won’t thwart."
Moses gathered the elders, seventy in line, God's Spirit on them, they prophesied, divine.
Eldad and Medad, still in the camp, Prophesied too, igniting a spiritual lamp.
Joshua cried, "Moses, stop their voice!" Moses said, "I wish all could rejoice."
A wind from God brought quail around, Day and night, quail covered the ground.
They gathered them up, the least ten homers wide, But God's wrath struck, a plague did slide.
Named the place Kibroth Hattaavah in the sand, For those who craved, here they stand.
From there, they moved to Hazeroth's land, And settled again, led by God's hand.
Miriam and Aaron, they spoke out loud, Against Moses, over the wife that he vowed.
"Has God spoken just to him?" they cried, "He speaks with us too," but God was not shy.
Moses, humble, the meekest on earth, God heard their words, and He knew their worth.
Suddenly He spoke, called them to the Tent, "Moses, Aaron, Miriam," His message sent.
In a cloud He came, right at the door, Called Aaron and Miriam, and they did implore.
"Listen now to my words," God declared, "I speak in dreams, to prophets prepared.
But Moses, my servant, he's not like the rest, With him, I speak plainly, he's truly the best.
Why weren't you afraid, to slander his name?" God's anger burned, and He left them with shame.
The cloud lifted, and there it was shown, Miriam leprous, her skin like snow, alone.
Aaron turned, saw his sister's plight, "Forgive our sin, we've acted without sight!"
"Don't let her be like the dead," Aaron pled, Moses cried out, "Heal her, God," he said.
"If her father had spit, she'd hide seven days, Let her stay outside, then heal her ways."
Seven days passed, she was out of the camp, The people waited, till her return from the tramp.
Then they journeyed on, with lessons learned, From Hazeroth to Paran, they moved, discerned.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, here's what He said, "Send men to Canaan, see where you're led. Pick a prince from each tribe, a leader in rank, To spy out the land, from river to bank."
Moses obeyed, sent them out from Paran, Leaders of Israel, each a strong man. From Reuben, Shammua, son of Zaccur, Simeon's Shaphat, son of Hori, for sure.
Judah's Caleb, son of Jephunneh, bold, Issachar's Igal, son of Joseph, we're told. Ephraim's Hoshea, son of Nun, strong and keen, Benjamin's Palti, son of Raphu, on the scene.
Zebulun's Gaddiel, son of Sodi, stands, Manasseh's Gaddi, son of Susi, in the plans. Dan's Ammiel, son of Gemalli, in the zone, Asher's Sethur, Michael's son, not alone.
Naphtali's Nahbi, son of Vophsi, strides, Gad's Geuel, son of Machi, he abides. Moses called Hoshea, Joshua by name, Sent them to Canaan, fortune or fame.
"Head south," he said, "and climb high, Check out the land, strong or weak, tell me why. See the cities, camps or strongholds they keep, The soil, the wood, the secrets that sleep."
So up they went, from Zin's wild sand, To Rehob's gates, surveying the land. To Hebron they trekked, where Anak's sons stay, Grapes and figs from Eshcol, carried away.
Forty days later, they came back to report, To Moses and Aaron, told tales of the sort. "The land flows with honey, milk so sweet, But giants and walls, make us retreat."
Caleb rose up, stilled the crowd's fear, "Let's go and take it, the victory's near!" But the others said, "They're stronger than we, The land eats its own, it's not meant to be."
"The Nephilim are there, giants so tall, We felt like grasshoppers, ready to fall." Yet their tale spread fear, a shadow so wide, As the children of Israel, trembled and sighed.
The people cried out with a mournful sound, Their hearts heavy, they gathered around.
"Why did we leave Egypt's land, Just to die here, by Yahweh's hand?
Let's go back, find another way, Choose a leader, return today."
Moses and Aaron hit the ground, Before the crowd's angry, restless sound.
Joshua and Caleb, clothes torn, Spoke of the land they had sworn,
"The land's good, so rich and fine, Flowing with milk, honey, divine.
If Yahweh's pleased, He'll lead us in, Don't rebel, we'll surely win."
Yet the crowd, with stones in hand, Threatened them, made their stand.
Yahweh's glory then appeared, His voice to Moses, loud and clear:
"How long will they doubt my might? I'll make a nation strong, in their spite."
Moses pleaded, "What will they say? You led them here, show them the way.
Your name's known, your power's great, Forgive them now, don't seal their fate."
Yahweh replied, "I've heard your plea, But those who doubted won't see the land, not through me.
Caleb, with a spirit true, He'll enter in, his seed too."
Yahweh spoke, wrath in His tone, "In this wilderness you'll be alone.
Forty years, for forty days, You'll wander lost in the haze."
The spies who spread the false report, Paid the price in Yahweh's court.
But Joshua and Caleb stayed alive, From that land, they'd not be deprived.
The people mourned, they rose to fight, "We'll go, we've seen the light!"
Moses warned, "Don't disobey, Yahweh's not with you today."
But they climbed the mountain high, Ignoring Yahweh's clear reply.
The Amalekites came down swift, With strength and force, they gave no lift.
The people fell, defeated, torn, Their disobedience left them forlorn.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, clear and strong, "Tell Israel when they come along,
Into the land, I promised to give, Make offerings by fire, for me to receive.
Burnt offerings, vows, free will at your feasts, Pleasant aromas rise with the beasts.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil, it’s divine, And wine for the drink, measure it fine.
For each lamb, each ram, bring it right, A meal offering, a sacrifice, a pleasing sight.
Every bull gets its share, don’t you forget, Flour, oil, and wine, make the table set.
Native-born or foreign, all the same, One statute, one rule, in Yahweh’s name.
When you enter the land, and eat the bread, Offer your first dough as a wave, ahead.
If you err, forget these commands, Bring a bull for atonement, to Yahweh’s hands.
The priest will make atonement, your sins will clear, For errors done without knowledge, no need to fear.
If one sins unwittingly, a goat will do, The priest will atone, Yahweh forgives you.
But if with high hand, a soul defies, Cut off they'll be, no more lies.
In the wilderness, a man gathered sticks, On Sabbath he was caught, his fate was fixed.
Yahweh commanded stoning, no mercy to lend, Israel executed, as Yahweh did send.
Then Yahweh spoke, with wisdom and might, "Fringes on garments, a reminder in sight.
A cord of blue on the edge you'll place, Remember my commands, keep your faith.
I'm Yahweh your God, out of Egypt I brought, Be holy to me, remember what I taught."
Korah and his crew, they started to rise, Challengin' Moses, bringin' surprise. Two-fifty leaders, men of renown, Standin' tall, tryin' to take him down.
They said, “Moses, you take too much on your plate, We’re holy too, we all relate! Why you lift yourself above the rest?” Moses heard, fell down, distressed.
“In the morning,” said Moses, “God will choose, He’ll show who’s holy, who will lose. Korah, bring your censors, light the flame, Tomorrow we’ll see who’s callin’ His name.”
Moses spoke, “Levi, hear me right, God's brought you close, givin' you the sight. Yet you want the priesthood, grabbin' more, Against Yahweh, you wage this war.”
Dathan and Abiram, Moses did call, “We won't come up, we'll not fall. You brought us from milk and honey's land, Now we're in the wilderness, this ain't grand.”
Moses got angry, spoke to the Lord, “Don’t accept their offering, hear my word. I didn’t take nothin', no donkey in sight, I've done them no wrong, not a single slight.”
Moses to Korah, “Tomorrow's the day, Bring your censers, come and pray. Yahweh's glory will show what’s real, Fire and incense, His truth will reveal.”
Yahweh's glory shone bright, "Sinners, separate, before I smite." Moses down, face to the ground, “God, spare them, one man sinned around.”
“Get away from Korah,” Moses said, “Don’t touch their tents, or you’ll be dead.” The earth opened wide, swallowed them whole, Korah and crew, down they roll.
People ran, screaming, “We’ll be next,” Fire from Yahweh burned the rest. Censers taken, turned to bronze, A sign of what went wrong.
People complained, “You killed our kin!” Cloud covered the Tent where Yahweh's been. “Step away,” Yahweh warned again, Wrath unleashed, a plague did begin.
Moses commanded, “Aaron, make it stop, Incense now, before they drop.” Aaron ran, stood between life and death, Stopped the plague, gave them breath.
Fourteen thousand, seven hundred gone, The plague halted, Aaron won. Returned to Moses, their work done right, The plague was stopped, saved from blight.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, his voice clear and bold, "Gather rods from each tribe, let the story unfold. One for each house, twelve rods in line, Each name written clearly, each sign to define.
Aaron's name on Levi's, for that tribe's head, Place them in the Tent where my presence is spread. The rod that buds, it's the one I've chosen, Silence the murmurs, their complaints will be frozen."
Moses spoke, and each prince gave, Twelve rods in total, each tribe's stave. Aaron's rod there among the rest, In the Tent before Yahweh, the ultimate test.
Next day came, Moses entered the Tent, Behold Aaron's rod! Blossoms it sent. Sprouted, budded, bloomed, almonds ripe, A miracle shown, an end to the gripe.
Moses brought the rods, showed them all, Each man took his rod, saw Aaron's call. Yahweh said, "Put Aaron's rod back in its place, A sign against rebellion, to limit their space."
Moses did just as Yahweh had bade, To quell their complaints, the foundation laid. The people cried out, "We're doomed, we're lost! Approach the tabernacle, and we'll pay the cost!
Will we all perish, is this our end?" With fear in their hearts, on Yahweh they depend.
Aaron, Yahweh spoke, hear these words divine, "You and your sons, the priesthood's line. Bear the weight of the sanctuary's care, Levi’s tribe stands with you, to serve and share.
Keep commands, guard the Tent — that's your call, But don't touch the sacred, or you'll fall. Stay close, keep responsibility tight, A stranger comes near — they're out of sight.
Perform your duty, shield from wrath's rise, For Israel's peace, heed these ties. I've taken Levites, a gift, my decree, For the Tent’s service, they're dedicated to me.
Priesthood's yours, a sacred role to fulfill, Strangers come near, they face the chill. "Wave offerings, holy, are yours," I say, Your sons' forever, in the priesthood's sway.
Holy offerings, meal, sin, and more, Eat like it's sacred — it's yours to the core. Wave offerings too, for you and your kin, Clean in your house, let the feast begin.
Best oil, vintage, grain — first fruits are yours, Bring to Yahweh, open the stores. Firstborn of flesh, man or beast, Redeem the unclean — that's the least.
Cattle, sheep, and goats — they remain, Sprinkle blood, burn fat, in Yahweh's name. Meat of offerings, it's yours, understand, A covenant of salt, forever at hand.
No land inheritance, Yahweh’s your gain, Tithes for the Levites, a service chain. Israel keeps distance, sin to avoid, Levites serve, their task deployed.
Moses, my message to the Levites take, "From Israel's tithe, a wave offering make. Tithe of the tithe, to Yahweh present, To Aaron's hands, the offering's sent.
Give the best, holy in sight, As threshing floor and wine press might. Eat it anywhere, your service’s due, With no sin burden — this is what's true.
Profane not the holy, respect the name, So you won't perish, avoid the shame."
Yahweh spoke out to Moses and Aaron, no delay, "Here's the law, listen up, hear what I say.
Bring a red heifer, perfect, no defect or yoke, Hand her to Eleazar, in camp she'll be broke.
Eleazar takes her blood, with a finger, a sweep, Sprinkles it seven times, before the Tent, keep it neat.
Burn the heifer in sight, skin, meat, blood ignite, Add cedar, hyssop, scarlet, in the fire so bright.
Priest washes his clothes, bathes in water's embrace, Returns to the camp, unclean till night takes its place.
The one who burns her, too, wash and bathe, Unclean till the evening, in the water they're saved.
A clean one collects ashes, stores them outside, Use it for cleansing, a law to abide.
Touch a dead body, unclean seven days, Purify on third and seventh, or be cut away.
In a tent where a man dies, unclean all who enter, Every open vessel, unclean at the center.
Touch the slain in the field, a grave or a bone, You're unclean seven days, don't stand alone.
Take ashes, pour water, let it mix in the vessel, Hyssop and water, all impurities wrestle.
Third day, seventh day, sprinkling's done, Wash clothes, bathe, by evening, it's a clean run.
But fail to purify, and be cut from the crowd, Defiles Yahweh’s sanctuary, no impurities allowed.
Perpetual statute, wash after the sprinkle, Touch impurity, unclean till stars twinkle.
Whatever the unclean touch, it spreads their stain, Unclean till evening, till night's calm reign."
In Zin, the people stayed, where Miriam laid, Her life came to an end, in Kadesh she was laid.
No water in the land, the people were upset, Against Moses and Aaron, their complaints were set.
"Wish we’d died with kin, why lead us here to fall? This place is barren, no crops, no fruits at all!"
From the crowd they fled, to the Tent's gate, Fell on their faces, awaiting Yahweh’s fate.
"Take the rod," said Yahweh, "speak to the rock's face, Water it will flow, to quench the people's chase."
Moses took the rod, as Yahweh had decreed, Gathered all the people, their thirst he would heed.
"Hear me now, you rebels, shall water come from stone?" Struck it twice with the rod, the water made its own.
Waters rushed out, the people and beasts drank well, But Yahweh's voice rose, with a truth to tell.
"Because you lacked trust, my name you did not raise, You won't lead them into the promised place."
Meribah’s waters, a story of strife and test, Where Israel quarreled, and Yahweh was blessed.
Moses sent word, to Edom’s king with hope, "Let us pass through, we won’t stray or grope."
But Edom’s response was cold as stone, "You shall not pass, leave my land alone."
Israel begged once more, offering peace in their plea, But Edom stood firm, with a threat and decree.
So Israel turned, from Edom’s harsh command, Journeyed on to Hor, as Yahweh planned.
At Mount Hor, Yahweh’s voice did proclaim, "Aaron will be gathered, his time has come to claim."
Moses took Aaron, Eleazar by side, On top of Mount Hor, where Aaron would abide.
Striped of his garments, Eleazar was dressed, Aaron died there, in his eternal rest.
The whole congregation, saw Aaron’s end, Wept for thirty days, for their priest and friend.
In the South, King Arad had heard the news, Israel's coming, so he'd better choose. He went to war, took captives in the fight, Israel vowed to Yahweh, "Give us might."
"If you deliver, we'll destroy their town," God listened, brought the Canaanites down. Called it Hormah, where they did prevail, Onward toward Edom, their spirits frail.
Complaints rose up, "Why this desert trek? No bread, no water, food makes us wreck." God sent snakes, venom struck them all, Israel cried to Moses, "Pray, don't fall."
Moses did, and God replied clear, "Make a snake, lift it high, no fear. Look and live, that bronze serpent's key," Moses raised it up for all to see.
Israel journeyed, camped in the land, Through Oboth, Iyeabarim, by God’s hand. On to Zered and beyond the divide, Moab's border, where Arnon's waters glide.
Wars of Yahweh spoke of this turf, "Vaheb in Suphah," the valleys' worth. To Beer they traveled for God’s supply, "Gather 'round, I'll give water," was God’s reply.
"Singing to the well, spring up!" they cried, Princes dug deep, where life abides. From Mattanah to Nahaliel they roamed, Up to Pisgah, where they called home.
Israel sent word to Sihon, king strong, "Let us pass, we’ll do you no wrong." Sihon refused, brought his army's might, Israel fought, took the land that night.
From Arnon to Jabbok, they claimed the ground, In Heshbon's cities, victory was found. Proverbs spoke, "Heshbon's flame burns bright," Moab's defeat was clear in sight.
"Woe to you, Moab!" cries of despair, Children of Chemosh taken there. Israel dwelled where Amorites stood, Moshe's spies took Jazer, understood.
Then to Bashan, Og rose to fight, God said, "Fear not, you'll claim his might." Just as with Sihon, the land was won, Israel prevailed, no foe left to run.
Israel camped by Moab’s plain, Where Balak saw what they had gained.
Moab feared, their numbers vast, Said to Midian, "They won’t last."
"An ox licks grass, so they consume, Balak’s reign may find its doom."
Messengers sent to Balaam’s land, "Curse them, for they’re too grand."
"From Egypt, they came to be, Covering earth like a vast sea."
"Curse them, so I might win, Drive them out, take back my kin."
Moab’s elders, rewards in hand, To Balaam spoke Balak’s command.
"Lodge here, I’ll seek Yahweh’s voice, I’ll bring back His choice."
God asked Balaam, "Who are these men?" "Brought by Balak, to curse with pen."
"Don’t go, don’t curse, they’re blessed," Balaam to Moab, "Yahweh says no quest."
Princes returned, "He won’t engage," Balak sent more with greater wage.
"Come curse, gain great honor, I’ll do whatever you ponder."
Balaam said, "Even treasure, I can’t defy, Yahweh’s word is my guide."
"Stay, I'll seek Yahweh’s night reply," God said, "Go, but heed My word, don’t lie."
Balaam rose, saddled the donkey, God’s anger burned, angel stood ready.
Donkey saw angel, sword in hand, Turned from the path, out to the land.
Balaam struck, turned her back again, She saw the angel in the narrow lane.
Crushed his foot, he struck with might, Angel blocked left and right.
Donkey lay down, Balaam’s wrath grew, Struck her hard, but she knew.
Yahweh opened her mouth to speak, "What did I do, for this harsh streak?"
"You mocked me, if I had a sword, I’d have killed you, with this cord."
"Am I not your trusty steed? Have I ever been in need?"
"No," he admitted, then saw with fright, Yahweh’s angel in the light.
"Why strike her thrice?" the angel asked, "Your perverse way is my task."
"Donkey saved you, turned away thrice, Else you’d be gone, and she’d suffice."
"I have sinned," Balaam confessed, "If it's wrong, I’ll turn, if you suggest."
"Go, but speak what I say," So Balaam went on his way.
Balak met him at Moab’s gate, "Why delay? Honor awaits."
Balaam said, "I’m here to speak, What God says, I will repeat."
To Kiriath Huzoth they came, Balak sacrificed, in Yahweh’s name.
Next morn, to Baal’s high place, Balaam saw the people’s face.
Balaam said to Balak, "Seven altars, make them grand, Prepare seven bulls, seven rams in this land." Balak followed through, just as Balaam had planned, A bull and a ram on each altar did stand.
Balaam spoke to Balak, "Stay by your offering's flame, I'll seek Yahweh's word, see what He'll proclaim." To the heights he ascended, seeking divine acclaim, God met him there, and spoke to his name.
Balaam reported, "Seven altars I've built, A bull and a ram on each, the incense spilt." Yahweh put His word in Balaam's mouth, "Return to Balak, let the truth go south."
He came back to Balak, who stood by the fire, Princes of Moab with him, their eyes filled with desire. Balaam began his chant, from Aram he'd come, "Curse Jacob, defy Israel," Balak's beating drum.
"How can I curse whom God has blessed? This nation stands tall, unoppressed. From the rocky heights, their strength I can see, A people alone, bound to be free."
"Count their dust? Who can even endeavor? May I die as they, blessed forever." Balak cried out, "What have you done? I sought their curse, but blessings you've spun!"
Balaam replied, "I speak what Yahweh imparts, His words in my mouth, direct to your hearts." Balak pleaded, "Try another place, See just a part, let curses trace."
To Zophim's field, atop Pisgah they went, Seven altars again, their offerings sent. "Stand by your flames," Balaam said, taking leave, To meet with God, His word to receive.
Yahweh spoke again, placed words in his mouth, Balaam returned, the plan heading south. Balak asked, "What did Yahweh reveal?" Balaam spoke, "Listen, here's the deal:
God's no man, no lies, no mistaken vow, He blesses, who can reverse it now? In Jacob, no fault, no sin in His sight, Yahweh's with them, their king's delight."
"Out of Egypt God brought them strong, Like a wild ox, they cannot go wrong. No enchantment can hold them, no diviner's spell, 'What has God done?' the world will tell."
"A lioness rising, ready to strike, Till prey is devoured, their strength's a spike." Balak sighed, "Neither curse nor bless, Your words bring me no rest."
Balaam replied, "Didn't I say it true? Yahweh's words command what I must do." Balak, persistent, "Another place we'll find, Perhaps God will permit your curse this time."
On Peor's peak, looking into the sands, Balaam instructed, "Seven altars, our final stands." Balak complied, once more with the plan, A bull and a ram on each altar grand.
Balaam saw pleasing Yahweh was the game, No divination now, just the wilderness to claim.
Lifted his eyes, saw tribes in their places, Spirit of God came, filled him with graces.
"Words of God I hear, vision of the Almighty," "Falling down, eyes open, all truth in clarity."
"How good are your tents, Jacob, Israel's homes," "Like valleys, gardens, where clear water roams."
"Water flows from his buckets, seeds in the stream," "King higher than Agag, kingdom's esteem."
"God brings him strong out, like a wild ox might," "His foes' bones crushed, arrows take flight."
"He lies like a lion, who dares wake his rest?" "Blessed are those who bless, cursed spurned at best."
Balak’s anger flared, clapped his hands in wrath, "I called you to curse, but blessings you path."
"Flee to your place, no honors await," "Yahweh blocks your honor, seals your fate."
Balaam replied, "Didn't I say it clear?" "Can't stray from Yahweh, His words I revere."
"House filled with riches, silver, and gold," "Can't change the message Yahweh has told."
"I'll go to my people, but listen up now," "I'll tell of the future, hear this vow."
"Vision afar, a star from Jacob's side," "Scepter rises, Moab crushed with pride."
"Edom, Seir, shall fall to the hand," "While Israel valiantly takes command."
"Amalek's first but ends in demise," "Kenite's stronghold, still wasted, it lies."
"Kittim's ships will come, afflict the shore," "Destruction follows, the end of war."
Balaam stood, returned to his own space, Balak too left, with anger's trace.
In Shittim, Israel stayed, but trouble was ahead, They fell for Moab's daughters, into mischief they led.
Called to false gods' altars, they ate, kneeled, and bowed, Joined with Baal Peor, and Yahweh's wrath was loud.
God told Moses, "Hang the chiefs up high, Let my anger turn away, let justice touch the sky."
Moses said to the judges, "Deal with every man, Who followed Baal Peor, strike them where they stand."
Then came a man with a Midianite dame, Right before all eyes, no shame in their game.
Phinehas saw it, his heart in a flame, Grabbed his spear, to put an end to the shame.
He struck them both, stopped the plague's cruel course, Twenty-four thousand gone, oh the remorse.
God spoke to Moses, this is what He said, "Phinehas has turned my wrath, no more bloodshed.
For his zeal, my covenant of peace he receives, An everlasting priesthood, for all his family's leaves."
The man was Zimri, from Simeon's line, The woman, Cozbi, Midian's design.
God told Moses, "Fight the Midianite fight, For their deceit with Peor, set things right."
After the plague, God called to Moses, said with might, “Count my people, those ready to fight.” In Moab's plains, by Jordan's flow, Moses and Eleazar made sure they'd know.
Reuben's sons, the count began, Forty-three thousand, in a warrior clan. From Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi's line, Eliab's sons rebelled, crossed the divine.
When Korah’s crew faced their doom, The earth opened wide, swallowed up in gloom. Yet Korah's sons lived; they didn’t die, Their numbers stayed, while others said goodbye.
Simeon’s tally, twenty-two thousand strong, Counting Nemuel, Jamin, Zerah, where they belong. Gad's tribe next, with a roll call too, Forty thousand five hundred, the dream they pursue.
Judah's sons listed, Er and Onan gone, Seventy-six thousand with Perez marching on. Issachar’s group, sixty-four thousand plus, From Tola to Shimron, they made a fuss.

Zebulun's families counted, sixty thousand and more, From Sered, Elon, Jahleel, they marched forth to explore. Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, With fifty-two thousand, their ranks were a grand hymn.
Benjamin's numbers, forty-five thousand six, With Ard and Naaman, they joined the mix. Dan and Asher, with families vast, Naphtali's forty-five thousand, marching fast.
“Grant the land by number,” God commanded, with a plan, “To the many, more land; to fewer, less span.” The Levites special, no land for their claim, But counted they were, in honor, not in name.
From Gershon to Kohath, Levi’s sons stand, Amram’s line through Moses, Aaron, a righteous band. With strange fire, Nadab and Abihu fell, Their tale a warning, a story to tell.
Moses and Eleazar counted anew, In Moab's plains, Israel's strength they knew. But none remained from Sinai's old count, Except Caleb and Joshua, whose faith did surmount.
Five daughters of Zelophehad stepped near, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, Tirzah clear.
They stood before Moses, the priest, the crew, At the Tent of Meeting, they spoke what was true:
"Our father died in the wilderness, you see, Not with Korah's crowd, just his own decree.
He left no sons, just daughters here, Why should his name disappear?
Give us a share, let his name survive, Among his brothers, let it thrive."
Moses took their cause up high, Before Yahweh, the Most High.
Yahweh spoke, straight and right, "The daughters speak, they have the light.
Give them a share, rightful and real, Among their father's brothers, seal the deal.
Tell Israel, 'If a man leaves no son, His daughter takes the inheritance won.
No daughter, then it goes to the brothers, Still no brothers? To the father's others.
And if kin are nowhere to be found, Pass it on, keep it sound.'
This rule I declare, just and strong, A statute for Israel, where it belongs."
Then Yahweh said, "Moses, climb high, See the land for Israel, under the sky.
Once you've seen, you'll join the rest, Like Aaron, your brother, laid to rest.
For you defied my word in Zin, At Meribah's waters, you didn't begin."
Moses answered, with a plea, "Appoint a leader, God of all we see.
One to lead, in and out, So they're not like sheep, wandering about."
Yahweh chose Joshua, Spirit-driven, "Lay hands on him, the charge is given.
In front of Eleazar, make it known, Commission him, let it be shown.
Give him authority, let them obey, He'll guide by the Urim, lead their way."
Moses did as Yahweh spoke, Hands on Joshua, the Spirit woke.
He was set before the crowd, Commissioned strong, Moses proud.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, words clear to relay, “Tell my people, bring offerings, don't delay.
See my aroma's sweet in seasons set, Two male lambs, perfect, each day met.
One in the morn, one as the sun sets, Fine flour and oil, the recipe’s set.
From Sinai it came, a fire offering's scent, A drink poured out, in holiness, spent.
Evening comes, repeat the morning's due, For a pleasant aroma, offering anew.
On the Sabbath, two lambs without a flaw, Double flour and oil, the offering’s law.
New months call for bulls, rams, and seven lambs more, With fine flour and oil, pour as before.
Wine’s poured in fractions, each measure known, Monthly offerings, on altars shown.
One goat for sin, alongside the daily flame, Yahweh's commands, all offerings the same.
In the first month, Passover's here, Unleavened bread for a week is clear.
A holy gathering, work set aside, Burnt offerings pure, Yahweh's delight.
Two bulls, one ram, seven lambs without blame, Flour and oil blend, their offering’s fame.
Seven days straight, the scent rising high, Adding to the daily, reaching the sky.
The seventh day calls for sacred rest, No work, just gather, Yahweh’s blessed.
First fruits bring, a new feast in weeks, Holy convocation, no work, just peace.
Bulls and rams, seven lambs burn bright, Fine flour with oil, perfect in sight.
One goat for atonement, a sin’s release, With the regular offering, Yahweh’s feast.
Follow these commands, without defect, An aroma to Yahweh, in all respect.
Seventh month begins, hear the trumpet sound, A holy convocation, no work around. Burnt offerings rise, aroma sweet and grand, A bull, a ram, lambs without a blemish stand.
Fine flour mixed with oil, a feast they create, Three tenths, two tenths, each portion's fate. One male goat for sin, atonement's made, With new moon offerings, a fire display.
On the tenth day, souls afflict, work's undone, Another holy gathering, fire offering begun. A bull, a ram, seven lambs, perfect, pure, Meal offerings with oil, Yahweh's allure.
Fifteenth day brings a feast, seven days of cheer, Thirteen bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs appear. Meal offering portions, precise they bring, One male goat for sin, in Yahweh's sing.
Second day, twelve bulls, two rams, lambs all around, Meal and drink offerings, ordinances abound. One goat for sin, offerings proceed, Continual burnt offering, Yahweh's creed.
Third day, eleven bulls, same ram and lamb count, According to the number, each sacrifice amount. A goat for sin, alongside burnt fire, Meal and drink offering, as Yahweh requires.
Fourth day, ten bulls, two rams still, Fourteen lambs, perfect, fulfill His will. Meal and drink offering, numbers precise, A goat for the sin, continual sacrifice.
Fifth day, nine bulls, rams, lambs remain, Offerings follow, with a goat for the stain. Continual burnt offering, steady and true, As Yahweh commands, the fire renews.
Sixth day, eight bulls, two rams, lambs stand tall, Meal and drink offerings, the numbers call. A goat for sin, burnt offering stays, Following Yahweh's ordained ways.
Seventh day, seven bulls, the ritual's flow, Two rams, fourteen lambs in a holy show. A goat for sin, offerings persist, Continual devotion, Yahweh won't resist.
Eighth day assembly, solemn, no work be done, One bull, one ram, seven lambs, a ritual run. Offerings bring aroma, Yahweh's delight, With vows and free will offerings, in His sight.
Moses speaks, the children hear, every command, As Yahweh instructed, they understand.
Moses spoke to the tribes with a serious tone, "This is what Yahweh has commanded, don't leave it alone.
When a man makes a vow, binds his soul with a bond, He must keep his word, be true and strong.
And when a young woman pledges in her father's place, Her father hears it, stays silent, her vows stay in grace.
But if her father says no on that very day, Her vows won't stand, forgiven, they're cast away.
If she's married and vows from her lips overflow, Her husband hears and is silent, then the promises go.
But if he forbids her when he hears her say, Her vows are void, Yahweh forgives her that day.
For a widow or divorced, her vows stand alone, What she binds stays, no need to atone.
If she swore in her husband's house, a binding oath, And he said nothing, then her vows are both.
But if he nullifies the day he hears them clear, Her vows won't stand, Yahweh's forgiveness is near.
Every vow, every oath to afflict the soul, Her husband can uphold, or make them null.
If he says nothing day by day, They stand firm, no words to sway.
But if he voids them after hearing her speak, He bears the iniquity, strong or weak.
These are Yahweh’s statutes Moses did share, Between husbands, wives, fathers, daughters, everywhere."
Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Take a stand, Avenge Israel on Midian, by my command." Moses told the people, "Arm up for war, Yahweh's vengeance is what we're fighting for.
One thousand from each tribe, that's the crew, Twelve thousand warriors, ready and true." Sent with Phinehas, the priest by their side, With trumpets ready, they marched with pride.
They struck Midian down, as Yahweh had said, Every man, every king, lay among the dead. Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba all fell, Balaam too, by the sword's fierce knell.
They captured women, and children too, Took flocks and goods, everything in view. Cities burned, encampments in flame, They took it all, in Yahweh's name.
Back they came with captives and spoil, To Moses and Eleazar, their reward for toil. But Moses was angry at the leaders of war, "Why spare the women, who led us to fall?
Kill every male child, and a woman who knows a man, Keep the virgins alive, that's the plan. Camp outside, purify on the third and seventh day, Cleanse your clothes, in every way."
Eleazar spoke, "Here's what Yahweh commands, All metals through fire, water purifies the lands. On the seventh day, wash and be clean, Then return to camp, as Yahweh's deemed."
Yahweh spoke, "Count up all the plunder, Divide it in halves, don't make a blunder. A levy to Yahweh from the warriors' share, One in five hundred, be aware.
A tribute to the priest, a wave offering to make, The rest to the Levites, for Yahweh's sake." Moses and Eleazar did as told, Counting sheep, cattle, donkeys, and gold.
The captains came near with their gold in hand, "Not one man lost, just as Yahweh planned. Here's the gold, for atonement's call, A memorial to Yahweh, for one and all."
Moses took the offering, in the Tent it lay, A reminder of battle, in Yahweh's way. The children of Israel, guided by His light, With offerings of gold, in Yahweh's sight.
Reuben and Gad with livestock in the land, Saw Jazer and Gilead, a place so grand. They went to Moses, Eleazar too, "Check this land, good for livestock, what can we do?
If we find favor in your sight, Let us stay here, don't make us fight. Don't bring us over the Jordan, let us stay, It's perfect for our herds, we want to stay."
Moses replied, "Will you sit while others fight? Discourage Israel? That's not right. Remember your fathers, who made hearts heavy, When spies returned, they weren't ready.
God's anger burned, He swore in wrath, None from Egypt would see the path, Except Caleb and Joshua, loyal and true, For they followed Yahweh, through and through.
Now you rise, like your fathers' sin, Turning God's anger towards us again. You mustn't stray, or else you’ll pay, Wander the wilderness another day."
They spoke up, bold and clear, "We'll build sheepfolds, our loved ones near. But we'll arm ourselves, go to war, Only return when the land's secure.
Our inheritance lies on this side, But we'll fight with you, side by side. We promise, Moses, we'll do just as you say, We'll help all Israel, come what may."
Moses said, “If you fight for Yahweh’s cause, Then the land will be yours, no pause. But if you don't, your sin will shout, Your promise broken, your truth found out.
Build those cities, build those folds, Keep your word, as the promise holds.” Gad and Reuben agreed, "We’ll obey, We’ll do what you command, come what may."
Moses spoke to leaders, priests, and all, "If Gad and Reuben heed the call, Give them Gilead if they fight, If not, in Canaan, they'll find their right."
"We'll cross armed, ready for the fight, Our land eastward, a pleasing sight." Moses gave them kingdoms, a great expanse, And cities they built, they seized their chance.
Gad and Reuben built strong and high, Their cities rose to meet the sky. Manasseh's sons took more land, A promise kept, just as planned.
Israel's journey, it began with a shout, Leaving Egypt’s chains, no doubt they were out. With Moses and Aaron leading the way, "Go forth," said Yahweh, "and do not delay."
From Rameses they set their stride, Passover done, with the Lord as guide. Egyptians mourned, their firstborn gone, While Israel marched with a hope so strong.
Succoth was their first camp site, Then to Etham, where day met night. Back to Pihahiroth, by the sea they stood, Baal Zephon watched as they crossed for good.
Through the sea's heart, wilderness ahead, To Marah's bitter waters and Elim's spread. Springs and palms, a brief reprieve, Then onward again, they would not leave.
By the Red Sea, in Sin they stayed, In Dophkah camp, their fear allayed. Alush came and Rephidim dry, Sinai's wilderness, under the sky.
Kibroth Hattaavah hosted their cry, To Hazeroth, then Rithmah, they fly. Rimmon Perez, then Libnah next, Rissah to Kehelathah, no longer vexed.
Mount Shepher rose, Haradah too, Makheloth, Tahath, the journey grew. Terah, Mithkah, and Hashmonah's camp, Moseroth where their spirits wouldn't damp.
Bene Jaakan, Hor Haggidgad's call, Jotbathah, Abronah, they journeyed all. Ezion Geber, Kadesh in Zin, Mount Hor saw Aaron, his life did end.
"Speak," said Yahweh, "to those who roam, In Canaan’s land, you'll find your home. Drive them out, make the land your own, Destroy their idols, to me alone."
"Take the land by lot," He decreed, "To each tribe, I will heed. But leave them not, or they’ll be thorns, Harassing you from dusk till morn."
"Inherit well, but heed my voice, Or your fate will be their choice." Israel's journey, a tale of old, A promise kept, as the story's told.
Yo, Yahweh spoke to Moses, made it plain, "Tell Israel, when you hit Canaan, claim your domain.
From the wilderness of Zin, your south side starts, Border runs east from the Salt Sea, mark the charts.
Southward, up Akrabbim, loop through Zin, Past Kadesh Barnea, Hazar Addar, it begins.
Swing from Azmon to Egypt's brook, you see, And there your border ends, at the sea.
West side's the great sea, let it ride, That's your western edge, ocean-wide.
Now north from the great sea, Mount Hor is your mark, To Hamath’s entrance, Zedad's where you embark.
Ziphron to Hazar Enan, north line's complete, That's where your boundary takes a seat.
East starts at Hazar Enan, down to Shepham true, Past Riblah, east of Ain, where it all comes through.
Down to the Jordan, ending Salt Sea's embrace, Your land outlined, borders in place.
Moses told Israel, "This land's your lot, Yahweh's gift to nine tribes, half-tribe's got a spot.
Reuben, Gad, Manasseh already claimed their share, East of Jordan, Jericho, sunrise glare.
Yahweh spoke again, said, "Check these names, Eleazar, Joshua, they'll play the dividing games.
One prince per tribe, they’ll split it fair, Judah's got Caleb, Jephunneh's heir.
Simeon's Shemuel, Ammihud's his dad, Benjamin's Elidad, Chislon's lad.
Dan's got Bukki, son of Jogli’s crew, Manasseh's Hanniel, Ephod's son, true.
Ephraim's got Kemuel, Shiphtan's child, Zebulun’s Elizaphan, Parnach's styled.
Issachar's Paltiel, Azzan’s his kin, Asher’s Ahihud, Shelomi's within.
Naphtali's Pedahel, Ammihud's seed, Yahweh's command, dividing's their deed.
These are the ones, Yahweh decreed, To split Canaan's land, fulfill the need."
In the plains of Moab, by Jordan's flow, Yahweh spoke to Moses, let the people know: "Command Israel, give Levites their share, Cities to live in, with pastures laid bare.
From city's wall, one thousand cubits wide, These lands for livestock, possessions to bide. Two thousand cubits, measure east to west, North and south too, give the Levites the best.
Refuge cities, six to be set, For those who slay, but not with intent. Forty-two more, total forty-eight, From Israel's lands, this shall be their fate.
Cross the Jordan, into Canaan's land, Set these cities as refuge, by My command. For the slayer's escape, from vengeance they hide, 'Til judgment's call, let justice decide.
"Six cities of refuge, three here, three there, Beyond Jordan, in Canaan, a place to spare. For Israel's children, stranger, and guest, These cities offer refuge, a place of rest.
"If one strikes with iron, stone, or wood, And death ensues, he's a murderer, understood. The avenger of blood shall do his part, When he meets the killer, he'll end his heart.
"But if it's done without hate or spite, Unintentional harm, no malice in sight, The congregation will judge, decide their fate, The slayer returns to refuge, where he'll wait.
Stay in the city, 'til the high priest's demise, Step outside, face blood's avenger's cries. After the priest's death, back to own land, This law stands firm, through generations grand.
"Murder demands witnesses, two or more, One voice alone can't settle the score. No ransom accepted for murderous guilt, Blood cleanses blood, for the land is spilt.
"Do not defile the land where I rest, For I, Yahweh, dwell among the blessed." With justice and refuge, the land's laws hold tight, In the midst of His children, God sets things right.
The heads of the tribes came near, had something to say, Stood before Moses, no delay.
"We got a command from Yahweh to keep it fair, Inheritance by lot, make sure it’s square.
Zelophehad’s daughters got land in their name, But if they marry outside, things won’t stay the same.
Their land will shift to another tribe's claim, Our fathers' share will lose its fame.
When jubilee hits, their land will move, Our inheritance won’t be smooth."
Moses replied, "The tribe of Joseph speaks true, Here's what Yahweh commands for you:
‘Let Zelophehad’s daughters choose their own, But only within their father's zone.
No land will jump from tribe to tribe, Keep the inheritance inside your vibe.
Every daughter with land must marry near, Stay in the family, keep it clear.
No inheritance will shift around, Each tribe will keep its ground.’"
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, they heard the call, Married their kin, kept the land for all.
Their inheritance stayed with Manasseh's line, The tribe's future, clear and fine.
These are the words Yahweh spoke through Moses's hand, To guide the tribes in the promised land.
Moses spoke to Israel, out in the wild, Beyond the Jordan, where the desert's not mild.
Eleven days from Horeb, the journey was made, In the fortieth year, all commandments conveyed.
He hit Sihon and Og, kings who fell, In Moab, Moses had the law to tell.
God said, "You’ve stayed long at this mount, Turn, take your journey, make every step count.
To the Amorites' hills, to every land, Go, take what I promised, as I planned.
I can't bear your burdens all alone, God's multiplied you, like stars you’ve grown."
Moses chose leaders, wise and sound, Judged with fairness, the truth they found.
"Don't fear man," Moses spoke clear, "God's judgment reigns, bring cases near."
Through the wilderness, they traveled far, Reached Kadesh Barnea, under God's star.
"God's given this land, go, don’t be dismayed," Scouts sent ahead, the promised land surveyed.
But fear took hold, hearts turned cold, "Giants await in cities bold."
Moses said, "Don't be afraid, God fights for you, He’s got you made."
Yet disbelief lingered, hearts of stone, God guided by fire, led alone.
God's anger rose, the promise delayed, "Only Caleb and Joshua," He said, "will be repaid."
"Your children will enter, though you disobeyed, Turn back to the desert," Moses conveyed.
They tried to fight, weapons in hand, God said, "Don’t go, I’ll not stand."
But they went, disregarding the voice, The Amorites chased them, left no choice.
Weeping came, but Yahweh didn’t hear, Stayed in Kadesh, the lesson was clear.
In the wilderness, we wandered, circling round, Mount Seir’s paths like a merry-go-round. God spoke, "You've circled long enough, take a turn, Head north, the lesson’s learned, it's time to discern."
"Pass through Esau's land, but don't provoke, They'll feel fear, but keep it gentle, no need to poke. Their land's not yours, just tread and buy, Food and water with silver, let peace be your tie."
"For forty years, I've watched you roam, Blessed your toil, you’ve never been alone. Passed Seir's paths, to Moab's edge, But don't fight Moab, respect the pledge."
Giants lived there, tall and strong, Called Emim by Moab, a name that’s long. Esau’s kin took the Horites’ place, Just as Israel would, in their race.
"Cross Zered's brook," God’s command was clear, Thirty-eight years pass, warriors disappear. God’s hand led, till they were gone, Now to Moab’s border, the journey drawn.
"Pass Ammon's land, but keep it calm, It’s Lot's possession, don't raise an arm. Filled with giants once, like Zamzummim, But Israel succeeded, with God's seraphim."
"Rise and move to Arnon's vale, Sihon's kingdom, it’s time to assail. Dread and fear on all will fall, As you approach with courage tall."
Sent words of peace to Sihon’s ear, "Let us pass through, have no fear. We'll buy food and drink, stay on the road, Just pass through, no heavy load."
But Sihon’s heart, God made hard, Wouldn’t let us pass, kept us barred. God said, "His land, now yours to claim, Begin the fight, make your name."
Sihon met us at Jahaz ground, God delivered him, victory profound. Cities fell, none left alive, Livestock taken, we did thrive.
From Arnon’s edge to Gilead’s grace, No city too high, God cleared the space. Only Ammon’s land stayed untouched, God’s command respected, His plan trusted much.
We turned and faced Bashan, Og's crew came for war, Met us at Edrei, ready to settle the score. Yahweh said, "Don't fear, I've given you the land, Do to him what you did with Sihon's hand."
Yahweh delivered Og, we struck him down bold, No one was left, their story was told. Sixty cities fell, each fortified and tall, Walls, gates, and bars, we seized them all.
Villages without walls, we left none behind, Destroyed like with Sihon, wiped out their kind. Livestock and treasure, we took it as our own, From Arnon to Hermon, the land was shown.
One giant remained, Og's bed of iron fame, Nine cubits long, the children of Ammon know his name. We claimed the land, split it among tribes, To Reuben, Gad, Manasseh, all the lands we'd describe.
Jair named Havvoth Jair, his legacy to stay, Gilead to Machir, among the tribes it lay. To Reubenites, Gadites, lands of fertile worth, From Arnon to Jabbok, stretching across the earth.
Then I said, "Arm up, men of valor, go fight, But your families stay safe, until comes the night." Joshua was told, "You've seen Yahweh's might, He fights for you, so bring victory's light."
I pleaded with Yahweh, "Let me see the land, Beyond the Jordan, the mountains so grand." But Yahweh was firm, "Stop this talk of yours, Climb Pisgah, look over, but cross no shores."

"Commission Joshua, give him strength to lead, He'll guide the people, fulfill the promised deed." So we lingered near Beth Peor, in the valley's expanse, Waiting for the time when our destiny would advance.
Listen up, Israel, hear the laws I share, Live by them, possess the land with care.
Don't add, don't take from the words I speak, Keep Yahweh's commands, stay strong, not weak.
You've seen Baal Peor's fate, how they fell, But the faithful are alive, and doing well.
I've taught you statutes, as Yahweh decreed, In this land you're to live, follow and lead.
Keep them close, that's your wisdom bright, Nations will see, and say, "What a sight!”
What nation has a God as near as He, Who hears our call, who sets us free?
