No man shall take his father's wife, Respect the bond, honor life.
Don't step into Yahweh's crew, if you've been crushed or cut, The forbidden union's kids, in the tenth gen, still shut,
No Ammonites, no Moabites, in Yahweh's place they won't belong, For bread or water they didn't bring, hired Balaam to do you wrong,
But God flipped the script, turned Balaam's curse into a blessing, 'Cause God loved you, that's the lesson,
"Don't seek their peace, don't chase their gain forever," But Edomite's your kin, and Egyptian's where you lived, so don't sever,
Their third-gen kids can join the assembly crew, But when at war, keep yourself clean, obey what's true,
If by night unclean you become, step outside and wait, Bathe at evening, come back when the sun's late,
Outside the camp, make sure you dig a hole, Cover what you leave, keep the camp whole,
For God walks among you, delivering and protecting, Keep it holy, or he'll be rejecting,
Don't return an escaped servant to his master's land, Let him choose his home, welcome him with open hand,
No daughters or sons in Israel shall prostitute, Don't bring their wages to God, that's absolute,
Lend to your brother without interest, keep it fair, Charge a foreigner, but let the brother's burden be air,
When you vow to God, don't you lag or slack, Fulfill your promise, or sin will attack,
But if silent you stay, no sin in your way, Keep your word, do as you say,
In a neighbor's vineyard, eat grapes at your leisure, But no basket, just hand for your pleasure,
In their fields, pluck grain by hand, no sickle touch, Respect what's theirs, don't take too much.
If a man takes a wife, he writes her a note, Sends her away, if love won't float. She can marry again, find another man, But if he leaves her, or dies, as planned,
The first can't take her back as his bride, For Yahweh says that's not to abide. Don't let the land fall to sin, my friend, The gift from God must not descend.
If you marry anew, stay home for a year, Cheer up your wife, keep her near. Don't pledge a millstone, don't take a life, Keep your dealings clear, free of strife.
Caught stealing a brother, selling for gain? That thief must die, cleanse the stain. Leprosy strikes, follow the priests, Observe their ways, or face the beasts.
Remember Miriam on Egypt's road, Lending means outside, no house code. Return the pledge, let him sleep tight, Be righteous before God, all's right.
Don't oppress the poor who serve, Pay them daily, give what they deserve. No death for another's sin, Each answers for their own within.
Justice for strangers, orphans, widows too, Remember Egypt, God saved you. Leave the sheaf, the olives, the vine, For those in need, let them dine.
Don't forget you were once a slave, Now do what's commanded, be brave.
When there's beef and they head to court, The judges speak, give their report. The good gets praise, the bad gets shame, If he's guilty, stripes mark his name.
No more than forty, that's the rule, Don't go over, don't be cruel. Just let him learn, but not degrade, He's still your brother, let respect be paid.
Don't muzzle the ox when it's working hard, Let it eat, don't disregard. If brothers live and one brother's gone, His widow's not left to mourn alone.
The brother steps up, takes her hand, Raises a child to honor his man. But if he won't, she speaks her mind, "He's left his brother's name behind."
Elders call him, hear his plea, If he insists, "I won't agree." She removes his sandal, spits in his face, A sign he's failed his brother's place.
Known as the man with no shoe to claim, The one who forgot his brother's name.
If a wife intervenes in a brawl, Grabs what's private, heed the call. Her hand is lost, don't show pity, Harsh but true in this ancient city.
Keep your scales and measures right, Honest weights in the day's light. Yahweh sees all deceitful ways, For just weights, you'll live long days.
Remember Amalek’s sneak attack, Hit the weak ones at the back. When rest comes from every foe, Erase Amalek, let their memory go.
Inherit the land Yahweh assigns, Don't forget, keep this in your minds.
When you hit the land Yahweh your God gives true, Claim it, live it, make it home—it's all for you.
Gather the fruit, the first from the soil, Put it in a basket, begin your loyal toil.
Go to the place Yahweh sets His name, Meet the priest, declare your claim.
Say, "I profess to God today, We've reached the land promised in His way."
The priest takes the basket, sets it down, Before Yahweh's altar, in the holy town.
"My father was a Syrian, on the brink of decay, Went to Egypt, few but grew strong in a mighty way.
Egyptians oppressed us, made our lives tough, But we cried to Yahweh, He said enough’s enough.
With a mighty hand, He took us from that place, Signs and wonders, He showed His divine grace.
Brought us here, to this promised ground, Flowing with milk and honey—all around.
Now I give the first fruits, Yahweh, it’s for You, Lay it down, worship, gratitude runs true."
Rejoice in the bounty, in the Levite's cheer, For you, the stranger, all who are near.
In the third year, tithe is the name of the game, Give to Levite, foreigner, orphan, widow—feed the flame.
Say to Yahweh, "I've done what You've said, Given what was holy, in Your path I tread.
Didn't eat in mourning, nor when unclean, Listened to Your voice, kept my actions keen.
From Your holy place, hear my prayer, Bless us, Yahweh, in Your loving care."
Yahweh commands, keep these words close, With heart and soul, follow what He chose.
You've declared Yahweh, your God, today, Promised to walk in His righteous way.
Yahweh declares you're His cherished lot, High above nations, a holy people's plot.
In praise, name, and honor, you'll stand tall, As Yahweh's own, His command is all.
Moses said to Israel, "Listen, hear what I say, Keep these commandments, follow them today.
When you cross the Jordan, to the promised land, Set up great stones, coat them with plaster by hand.
Write on those stones, all the laws you know, In the land of milk and honey, where you'll go.
On Mount Ebal, set those stones real high, Build an altar with uncut stones that touch the sky.
No iron on them, just as I command, Burnt offerings to Yahweh, with your hands.
Rejoice and eat, peace offerings made, His words on stones, in plain view laid.
Moses and priests called out to the crowd, "Be silent and listen!" their voices loud.
"You are Yahweh's people, obey His call, His statutes and commands, follow them all."
Mount Gerizim will bless, with voices strong, Simeon, Levi, Judah, they stand where they belong.
Mount Ebal will curse, it's Reuben's stand, Levites shout curses, all over the land.
"Cursed is the one with idols secret and sly," And all the people answer, "Amen," they cry.
"Cursed who dishonors parents, or moves a stone, Leads the blind astray, leaves justice alone."
"Cursed who lies with kin or kills in the night, Takes a bribe to shed blood, in Yahweh's sight."
"Uphold the law, or cursed you will be," All the people say, "Amen," in unity.
Listen close, hear the voice, God's commands ain't a choice, "Lift you high," He said, "above every nation's noise."
Blessings rain down, city and field, Your body and ground, with abundance they'll yield.
Your basket, your dough, blessed as they rise, When you enter and exit, blessings in your eyes.
Enemies come one way, scatter seven-fold, Barns fill with blessings, more than you can hold.
"Be my people," God swore, "walk in my way," Nations will see, and they'll tremble in dismay.
Skies open treasure, rain falls on your land, Lend to nations, never borrow, as God planned.
"Head not tail," God said, "above, never below," Obey His word, don't stray, keep it in tow.
But if you turn away, curses will unfold, City and field, they'll leave you cold.
Basket and dough, cursed in the strife, In and out, cursed, in every part of life.
Enemies rise, confusion will reign, Until you're destroyed by the weight of your pain.
Pestilence clings, fever and blight, Skies of bronze, ground of iron, no respite.
"Rain dust down," said God, "until you're undone," Enemies strike, and you'll be on the run.
Bodies for birds, no one to shoo, Boils and madness, blindness too.
Grope at noon, in perpetual night, Oppression and robbery, no savior in sight.
Wife with another, house not your home, Vineyard's fruit, you'll never own.
Ox taken, donkey gone, Children to strangers, hope withdrawn.
Foreigners rise, you fall low, Lend to them, not to you, that's how it will go.
Curses chase you, till you're no more, For not heeding God's voice, closing the door.
"Nations will come," fierce and unknown, Eat your fields, leave nothing to own.
Walls besieged, trust in vain, In hunger and siege, you'll eat flesh in pain.
Tender man turns, eyes to evil gaze, No food to share, in distressful days.
Delicate woman, her heart goes cold, In hunger's grip, even love grows old.
If you disregard the words in this book, Plagues will follow, as fear's hook.
Diseases return, Egypt's dread, Till you're few, stars dimmed and fled.
Scattered wide, earth's ends to roam, Serve strange gods, far from home.
No rest found, heart in constant dread, Morning to night, wish for what's ahead.
Return to Egypt, by sea's dark route, Offer yourself, but no one's about.
Moses stood and called all of Israel, "Hear! You've seen what Yahweh did, made Pharaoh disappear.
Signs and wonders, trials so grand, But hearts and eyes not fully understand.
Forty years I led you, wilderness wide, Clothes and sandals, still good, did not divide.
No bread, no wine, to make you see, That Yahweh's your God, guiding free.
When Sihon and Og came for the fight, We struck them down, claimed our right.
Gave their land to Reuben, Gad, Manasseh's zone, Keep Yahweh's covenant, make it your own.
Stand today in Yahweh's sight, Heads, tribes, elders, in the light.
Little ones, wives, and strangers too, All who cut wood, and draw water for you.
Enter the covenant, Yahweh’s decree, "Be my people, let me be."
Not just you, but those to come, Remember Egypt, where you were from.
See the idols, stone and gold, Turn away, stay in Yahweh's fold.
No root of poison, no heart astray, Yahweh’s wrath for those who stray.
"The curse will fall," Yahweh declares, Blot out their name, no pardons, no dares.
Future folks will see the land, Sulfur, salt, no grass, barren sand.
"Why this wrath?" the nations will cry, "They broke Yahweh's bond, that's why."
Served other gods, left Yahweh behind, Anger burned, land undermined.
Secret things are Yahweh's own, But what’s revealed, is ours alone.
To keep the law, to do what's right, Yahweh's word, our guiding light.
When blessings and curses fill your mind, Recall them all, don't leave them behind.
Among the nations where you're driven, Turn back to Yahweh, your heart's been given.
With all your soul, obey His call, Yahweh will release you, break the wall.
From every land where you've been scattered, He'll gather you, your heart unshattered.
He'll bring you back to your fathers' land, You'll possess it, like a king you'll stand.
He'll do you good, your numbers grow, More than before, His mercy flow.
Yahweh will change your heart's direction, To love Him fully, feel His affection.
Enemies cursed, while you arise, Obey His word, make it your prize.
Prosperity in all your labor, Fruit of your body, Yahweh's favor.
His voice, His law, hold them tight, Turn to Him with all your might.
Commands not distant, they're near and clear, No need to ask, "Who's bringing it here?"
Not beyond seas, no distant quest, The word's in your heart, it knows you best.
Life and death, they stand before, Choose life today, and live much more.
Love Yahweh, follow His ways, In His land, prolong your days.
But if you turn and walk astray, Worship idols, lose your way.
Then perish you will, in this land, Across the Jordan, without His hand.
Heaven and earth bear witness true, Life and death set before you.
Choose life, you and your kin shall live, Love Yahweh, obey, and give.
For He's your life, your days to prolong, In the land He promised, where you belong.

Moses stepped up, words ready to flow, "Listen up, Israel, there's something you should know. I'm one-twenty today, can't come and go no more, Yahweh said, 'Moses, you ain't crossing this Jordan shore.'
But don't you worry, God Himself will lead, He'll wipe out nations, make 'em scatter like seed. Joshua's your man, he's gonna guide your way, Just like Yahweh promised on another day.
Remember Sihon and Og, those kings got beat, Yahweh crushed their lands, laid 'em down at your feet. Be strong, courageous, don't you dare feel small, Yahweh's got your back, He won't let you fall."
Moses called Joshua for all to see, "Be strong, be brave, lead 'em to victory. Yahweh's with you, He won't let you go, Don't be scared, don't let your courage get low."
Moses penned the law, gave it to the priests, "Every seven years, read it for the feasts. Gather everyone, men, women, and kids, Teach 'em to fear Yahweh, do all He bids."
Then Yahweh spoke, “Moses, time's running out, Bring Joshua to Me; let there be no doubt.” In the Tent of Meeting, a cloud did descend, Yahweh said, "Moses, your journey's at an end.
This people will stray, chase gods not their own, My anger will rise, they'll reap what they've sown. But teach them this song, let it ring in their ears, A witness for Me through all of their years.

When the land's theirs, flowing with milk and sweet honey, They'll get fat, turn away, forget who saved 'em from money. Troubles will come, but this song will stay true, A reminder of what they forgot to do."
Moses wrote the song, taught it that day, Commissioned Joshua, "Lead them the right way. Take the law, place it by the Ark's side, A witness against you, let it be your guide.
I know you're stubborn, even while I'm alive, After I'm gone, will your faith survive? Gather the elders, let them hear this word, Let heaven and earth be the witnesses stirred."
Moses sang the song, every word clear, To remind Israel of Yahweh, keep Him near.
Listen up, skies, hear me, earth, when I speak, My words like rain, gentle, so unique.
"Yahweh's name I’ll proclaim, so great, The Rock, his ways perfect, never late."
But the people turned, crooked and wrong, They forgot the God to whom they belong.
"Is this how you repay the Almighty's grace, The Father who saved you, set your place?"
Remember the past, the old days of yore, Ask your elders, they'll tell you more.
God set the nations, each with its own, Israel's his portion, his very own throne.
Found in the desert, waste howling and wild, He cared and protected, like a father to a child.
Like an eagle's wings, spread and wide, Yahweh led them, no others by his side.
He gave them riches from the land so sweet, Milk, honey, and grain, at their feet.
But Jeshurun grew fat, kicked and turned, Forgot the Rock from whom they’d learned.
Provoked by idols, anger was stirred, Sacrificed to demons, not his word.
"See now, I’ll hide my face, see their fate, A faithless generation, filled with hate."
Jealousy burned, with gods they adored, A fire consumed, from earth to the core.
"I’ll heap evils, spend arrows in strife, Hunger and beasts, they’ll know my knife."
Nations void of counsel, so blind, Enemies will rise, leave them behind.
"See your gods, where’s their aid? Can they save you, the choices you made?"
"I alone am He, no one can save, I wound, I heal, from cradle to grave."
"Vengeance is mine, when the time is near, Calamity rushes, instills them with fear."
Yahweh will judge, compassion he’ll give, For his people, in mercy, they’ll live.
"Rejoice, nations, Yahweh’s right, Avenge his own, lead to the light."
Moses spoke the words, the song of his heart, Joshua beside, ready to impart.
"Keep these words, they’re your life and way, Cross over Jordan, where you will stay."
God spoke to Moses, "Climb up, see the land, But not to enter, just understand."
Moses would see from afar, not near, For past missteps, the consequence clear.
"Look, but don’t touch, this is the decree, Israel will enter, but not you, nor me."
Moses stood and blessed the crowd, his words were strong, his voice loud. "Yahweh came from Sinai's peak, from Seir He rose, His glory did speak.
From Mount Paran He shone bright, ten thousand holy ones in His sight. At His right, a fiery law He gave, to His people, the ones He'd save.
He loves them all, they're in His hand, they sit at His feet, they understand. Moses gave the law to keep, an inheritance for Jacob deep.
Reuben's tribe, let them survive, never let their numbers dive. For Judah, he called on Yahweh’s might, to bring him home, to win each fight.
"Levi," he said, "has sacred stones, proven in trials, they've held their own. Teach the laws, the incense burn, bless their skills, for justice yearn."
Benjamin dwells under Yahweh's care, safe and sound in a love so rare. Joseph's land, blessed with earth’s best, mountains and fruits, he's truly blessed.
Zebulun and Issachar, rejoice and call, gather the people, offer it all. Gad's a lioness, he takes his claim, righteousness in Yahweh's name.
Dan, a cub, leaps fierce and free, Naphtali's favor, full as can be. Asher's strength like iron bars, blessed with children and under the stars.
No one like God who rides the skies, beneath His arms, His people rise. Israel safe, with grain and wine, Yahweh saves, His help divine.
Happy is Israel, saved by Yahweh's might, tread on high places, His shield is right."
Moses climbed up from Moab's plain, to Nebo's peak so high, He's opposite Jericho, with a view that touched the sky.
God showed him lands wide, from Gilead to Dan, Through Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh—what a plan!
All the land of Judah, stretching to the Western Sea, Jericho, the city of palms, down to Zoar's territory.
God spoke clear, "Here's the land I swore to Abraham's line, To Isaac and Jacob, their offspring's future sign.
I've let you see it with your eyes, but you won't cross that shore.” So in Moab's land, Moses lived no more.
He died as God said, buried deep where none can say, In Moab's valley, his grave unknown to this day.
At a hundred and twenty, his sight still strong, His strength not waned, though his days were long.
Israel wept thirty days, mourning in the Moab sand, Till tears dried and they moved by God's command.
Joshua stood ready, wisdom in his hand, For Moses touched him, making him grand.
No prophet like Moses has risen since that day, Face to face with God, leading in His way.
In Egypt's land, he performed every sign, Mighty deeds and wonders, his legacy divine.
Moses’ mighty hand, awesome deeds in sight, A leader unmatched, leading them to light.
Moses is gone, Joshua steps to the line, Yahweh speaks, "It's your time to shine.
"Moses is dead, now rise and lead, Cross the Jordan, fulfill the need.
"Every place your foot will tread, I've given you, just like I said.
"From Lebanon to Euphrates wide, To the Great Sea where the sun slides.
"None can stand, all your days, As with Moses, I'll guide your ways.
"Be strong, be brave, lead this crowd, To the land promised, loud and proud.
"Observe the law, don’t turn aside, In success and prosperity, you'll abide.
"Meditate on this day and night, Keep it close, do what’s right.
"I've commanded, don’t show fear, For Yahweh your God is always near."
Joshua commands, with a voice so clear, "Prepare yourselves, the time is near.
"In three days, the Jordan we’ll cross, Possess the land, gain not loss."
To Reuben, Gad, Manasseh he spoke, "Moses' words, no idle joke.
"Your families stay on this side, But you must cross, with brothers ride.
"Help them rest as you were blessed, Then your land will be possessed."
The people replied, ready to go, "Where you lead, we will follow.
"As we listened to Moses, so to you, May Yahweh be with you in all you do.
"Rebellion will face death's toll, Be strong, be brave, that’s our goal."
Joshua sent his spies from Shittim's place, "Check the land, Jericho, see every face." They slid into Rahab's house to rest, A secret spot, a hidden nest.
The king heard news, his heart in a bind, "Israelite spies? I need them to find!" He sent word to Rahab, "Hand them over, They came here to spy, uncover, discover."
But Rahab was smart, she hid them well, She spun a tale the king couldn't quell, "Men came by, yes, but where they went, I don't know, chase fast, be diligent."
Up on the roof, under flax they laid, While pursuers chased, the gates firmly stayed. She whispered to them under the night, "Yahweh's with you, a fearsome sight."
"We heard of the sea that split so wide, The Amorite kings you cast aside. Our hearts have melted, spirits fled, 'Cause your God rules above our heads."
"Swear to me by Yahweh's might, Show kindness back, protect our light, Save my family, keep us alive, When Jericho falls, let us survive."
"Our life for yours," the spies did vow, "When Yahweh gives us this town, We'll keep our promise, deal true with you, But keep this secret, speak only what's due."
Down by the cord, they slipped through the wall, "Hide in the mountains, 'til pursuers fall." The spies agreed, "Here's what to do, Tie the scarlet thread, make your mark true."
"When we come back, stay in your space, Anyone outside, they're not in a safe place. Keep silent, and we'll hold our word, Tell one soul, and the deal's disturbed."
"Let it be as you have said," she sighed, The scarlet thread in the window tied. Three days passed, hidden from the chase, Then they returned to Joshua's place.
"Yahweh's given us this land," they declared, "The people tremble, their spirits bared." The spies' report, a promise grand, The land was theirs, by God's hand.
Joshua rose at dawn, ready to lead the way, From Shittim to Jordan, where they'd camp and stay.
Three days passed, the officers took their stride, "In sight of God's ark, you'll follow and abide.
Keep your distance, a space you must hold true, This path is new, it's fresh, it's made for you."
Joshua to the crowd, "Sanctify tonight, Tomorrow Yahweh's wonders, a wondrous sight."
To priests, he called out, "Lift the ark, go ahead, Cross before the people, take the path we tread."
Yahweh spoke to Josh, "I'll lift you high, you'll see, With Israel watching, like Moses, you'll be.
Tell the priests at the brink, 'Stand in Jordan's flow,' Watch the waters stop, let the story grow."
Josh gathered Israel, "Hear what God has planned, He'll clear the way, drive enemies from the land.
The living God leads, the ark goes before, Twelve men from the tribes, for what's in store."
"When priestly feet touch Jordan's rolling tide, Waters will halt, the path will open wide."
Tents left behind, the people made their quest, Priests at the water's edge, stood the test.
Water rising high, like a wall so steep, Jordan parted wide, in one mighty heap.
The priests stood firm, dry ground 'neath their feet, Israel crossed over, their victory complete.
When the nation crossed the Jordan, standing tall, Yahweh spoke to Joshua, gave him a call:
"Take twelve men, one from each tribe, And have them lift stones from where the waters divide.
Place them where you camp tonight, A reminder of this powerful sight."
Joshua gathered the chosen twelve, Said, "Step into the river, where the priests dwell.
Each carry a stone on your strong shoulder, A tale to tell when your children get older.
When they ask, 'What’s the story behind these stones?' Tell them how the Jordan's waters turned to bone.
With Yahweh’s ark, the waters did part, And these stones will forever be close to our heart."
The people obeyed and brought stones to the shore, A testament to God's mighty roar.
Joshua placed stones in the river's flow, Where the priests with the ark stood, long ago.
The priests held their ground, their task was clear, Until all God commanded was brought near.
Forty thousand soldiers, armed and ready, Crossed the river, their hearts steady.
On that day, Joshua's name grew great, Feared like Moses, by Israel's state.
Yahweh spoke again, clear as day, "Tell the priests it's time to walk away."
Joshua echoed, "Priests, come forth from the tide," And as they did, the waters returned wide.
Camped in Gilgal, east of Jericho’s gate, The twelve stones stood, their story innate.
Joshua said, "When asked by your kin, 'What do these stones mean?' Let the story begin.
Yahweh dried up Jordan, just like the Red Sea, So the whole world knows, His might you will see.
Remember His power, remember His hand, Fear Yahweh your God, in this promised land."
The kings heard tales, their hearts did quail, No spirit left, their courage frail.
Water dried, the Jordan crossed, Fear filled their souls, a line was tossed.
Yahweh said, "Joshua, grab those knives, Circumcise again, renew their lives."
Joshua moved, with flint in hand, At foreskin hill, he took a stand.
Those who left Egypt, warriors brave, Died in the desert, none to save.
In the wild they roamed, forty years, long and wide, Till the old warriors faded, the promise denied.
Their children rose, a new generation’s birth, Joshua circumcised them, claimed their worth.
When all was done, healing came fast, The camp settled down, pain didn’t last.
Yahweh spoke, "Reproach of Egypt's gone away," Gilgal's the name, a new dawn in display.
In Gilgal’s embrace, they camped, they ate, Passover kept, aligned with fate.
Unleavened bread, grain from the ground, Manna ceased, new food they found.
Joshua near Jericho, eyes lifted high, A man with a sword, ready to try.
"Are you friend or foe?" Joshua asked bold, "Commander of Yahweh, truth's been told."
Joshua bowed low, face to earth, "What does my lord say, what's this worth?"
"Remove your sandals, this ground is holy," Joshua obeyed, approached it slowly.
Jericho's gates were locked up tight, no one's goin' in or out, Israel camped outside those walls, no doubt, God's got a plan, a route.
The Lord told Joshua, "Jericho's yours, with its king and might, March 'round the city for six days, warriors ready to fight."
"Seven priests with trumpets, rams' horns in hand, On the seventh day, seven laps, like planned."
"When you hear that trumpet blast, shout loud with all your soul, And those walls will crumble down, you'll take control."
Joshua called the priests, "Lift the ark, let's move, Seven trumpets lead the way, it's time to groove."
"Advance!" he said, "March 'round, armed and bold, Wait for my command to shout, let the story unfold."
Day by day, they circled once, silent and slow, Until the seventh day, they marched seven times, ready to blow.
When the horns blew long, Joshua yelled, "Shout out loud, For Yahweh's given us this town, let’s make Him proud!"
The city's devoted, all's for Yahweh, except Rahab's crew, She hid our spies, she'll survive, along with her family too.
"Silver and gold, the Lord's treasure they’ll be, But take nothing else, or cursed you will see."
The people roared, the trumpets blared, the walls fell flat, The army charged in, victory in their hat.
They destroyed it all, man and beast alike, Israel took Jericho with power and might.
Joshua sent spies to Rahab's place, as he swore, Saved her and her kin, brought them through the door.
They burned the city, left nothing standing tall, Gold and silver in Yahweh’s house, they took it all.
Rahab lived in Israel, her story's no bluff, For she protected those spies, proved courage enough.
Joshua spoke a curse, "Rebuild Jericho, you'll pay, Firstborn for the foundation, youngest for the gates that day."
So Yahweh was with Joshua, his fame spread wide, Israel knew their leader, with God by his side.
Israel stumbled, broke the rule, took what's devoted, not so cool, Achan grabbed, Yahweh's wrath, burned hot, that's the aftermath.
Joshua sent spies to Ai's gate, "Check it out, don't hesitate." They said, "Just a few thousand will do, no need for everyone to go too."
But three thousand men went, tried to fight, They fled, Ai chased, hearts melted, lost the light.
Joshua tore his clothes, fell to the ground, Dust on heads, elders all around.
He cried, "Lord, why bring us here just to lose, Amorites will hear, how will we choose?
Canaanites will mock, our name erased, What of Your name, what's to be faced?"
Yahweh spoke, "Get up, why on your face? Israel sinned, broken covenant, a disgrace.
Stolen goods hidden, can't stand and fight, Destroy what's taken, make it right.
Sanctify, prepare, tomorrow's the test, Tribes come near, find the one detest.”
Morning came, tribes gathered by, Judah chosen, no need to lie.
Family by family, down to the core, Achan stood guilty, couldn't ignore.
Joshua said, "Tell me, son, your act, Give glory to Yahweh, state the fact."

The Philistines seized him, put out his eyes to blind, Bound him in bronze, in prison to grind.
Yet his hair began to grow, a silent sign of might, Philistines, in triumph, gave praise to Dagon's light.
"Our god has delivered Samson, our foe," they declared, Called him to perform, but underestimations were dared.
Samson said to the boy, "Let me feel the pillars strong," The house was full, three thousand looked on.
He prayed, "Lord Yahweh, remember me this day, Strengthen me once more, let the Philistines pay."
He pushed the pillars with all his power inside, "Let me die with them," he called, and with that, allied.
The house fell down, lords and people alike, More died in his death, avenged with his final strike.
His family came and took him, to bury him with care, In Manoah's site, twenty years his justice did declare.
In the hills of Ephraim lived a man named Micah, He told his mom, "I took your silver, now let's make it right, yah."
His mom blessed him, "May Yahweh's favor come," "I'll give the silver back, now let's get something done."
She dedicated the silver with a plan in her head, For a carved image and molten, she said.
Micah returned the cash, and she took a slice, Gave it to a silversmith, made idols nice.
Micah's house of gods was filling fast, He crafted an ephod, built a worship that would last.
No king in Israel, folks did what they pleased, Everyone living their life with ease.
From Bethlehem Judah, came a Levite young and bold, Traveling to find a place to unfold.
Micah asked, "From where do you come?" The Levite replied, "Bethlehem Judah's my home."
Micah said, "Stay with me, be my priest, wear my cloth, Ten silver pieces yearly, food and clothing, no froth."
The Levite agreed, content in his spot, Like a son to Micah, loving what he got.
Micah made it official, the Levite his guide, In Micah's house, the priest would abide.
Then Micah declared with hope so loud, "Yahweh's blessings are guaranteed; with a Levite, I'm proud."
In the days when no king led, Danites sought land to tread, Inheritance elusive still, so they sent heroes with skill.
Five men from Zorah set to roam, to spy and claim a home, "Go explore," their kin said loud, till they reached Micah's crowd.
They knew a voice, a Levite keen, asked, "Who brought you to this scene?" "I'm a priest for hire," he said, "Micah's house is where I'm led."
"Consult God for us," they pled, "We seek success ahead." "Go in peace," the priest replied, "Yahweh's favor's on your side."
To Laish these five men went, found a land without torment, Safe, secure, no ruler's sway, far from Sidon, lone to stay.
Back they rushed to brothers bold, "The land is good as gold. Arise, no time to waste, it's wide, and ours to take with pride."
The Danites armed and ready, marched on, six hundred steady, Camped in Judah for a night, then onward, hearts alight.
"Do you know in Micah's place, lie treasures, idols, and grace?" Five men whispered this clue, "Consider what you must now do."
To Micah's house they came once more, with weapons at the door, Took the ephod, teraphim, images carved and grim.
"What are you doing?" the priest implored, "Join us," they said, "and be adored.
"Hold your peace, come be our guide, a priest for tribe and kin abide." The priest agreed, glad with choice, took the treasures, joined their voice.
They took off with treasures in tow, leaving Micah in sorrow. Micah rallied but couldn't win, against Dan's might he could not begin.
"You stole my gods and priest," he cried, "What’s left for me inside?" Danites warned, "Hold your tongue, or meet angry men among."
Realizing their strength too grand, Micah returned to his own land. To Laish went Dan's fierce band, took the city with sword in hand.
They burned it down, no rescue came, built anew and changed its name. Named it Dan for lineage's pride, once Laish, now their side.
They set up Micah's image high, with priests to lead and not defy, Till Shiloh's house held God's might, the image stood in Dan’s sight.
In the days when Israel had no king to abide, A Levite took a concubine for his side. Out of Bethlehem Judah, she fled away, To her father's house, she went to stay.
Four months passed, her husband came to plead, With donkeys and a servant, to meet her need. Her father welcomed him, with joy in his face, Three days they ate, drank, and took up space.
On the fourth day, morning came, he sought to go, “Stay for bread,” the father said, “tarry slow.” They sat, they ate, the father urged with cheer, “Stay the night, make your heart merry here.”
The man rose to leave, the dawn of day five, “Stay 'til evening,” the father did strive. But the Levite, his heart set to roam, Refused the stay, sought his way home.
Near Jebus, as the sun began to set, The servant suggested they go in and rest. But the master pushed on, "Not here, not with these, To Gibeah we'll go, on the road with ease."
In Gibeah, they sat in the street, No one offered them a place to retreat. An old man from Ephraim, working late, Saw them there and joined their fate.
“Where do you travel? From where do you hail?” “From Bethlehem Judah, on Yahweh's trail. No one has taken us in, yet we lack no need, Straw, fodder, bread and wine, all we feed.”
The old man said, “Peace be upon your way, Come to my house, where you can stay.” They ate, drank, made merry through the night, When wicked men came, with evil in sight.
“Bring out the man,” they wickedly shout, The master pleaded, “Don't carry this out! Take my daughter, his concubine instead, But spare this man, leave this dread.”
They wouldn't listen, seized the woman by force, Abused her all night without remorse. At dawn she fell by the Levite's door, Her hands on the threshold, her spirit no more.
“Get up,” he said, but her silence was grave, He placed her on the donkey, to home he gave. In his house, with a heart filled with grief, He cut her body, piece by piece.
Sent twelve parts throughout the land, A message of horror, a call to stand. “All who saw it proclaimed with fear, No such deed had been done, or heard here.”
Israel gathered, a mighty scene, from Dan to Beersheba, all keen, In Mizpah they met, standing as one, four hundred thousand strong with sword drawn.
Benjamin heard of Israel's rise, asking, “What caused this despise?” The Levite spoke, his voice did quake, “In Gibeah, my concubine they did take.”
“They aimed to kill, surrounded our place, they harmed her and left disgrace. I sent her parts through Israel's land, a call for justice—take a stand!”
Israel vowed as one to fight, “We won't return home 'til we make it right. Against Gibeah we'll cast the lot, ten men per hundred to gather a plot.”
They sought Benjamin, demanded the men, “Give up the wicked, make peace again!” But Benjamin stood, refusing the plea, they prepared for battle, fierce as can be.
Israel's swords four hundred thousand in hand, Benjamin's twenty-six thousand did stand. “Who fights first?” they asked the sky, “Judah,” Yahweh answered, “let them try.”
Israel rose at dawn's first light, to face Benjamin, prepared for the fight. Gibeah's men did fierce attack, twenty-two thousand Israelites fell back.
Israel's tears flowed, they cried to the Lord, “Shall we fight again?” And He gave the word. They faced Benjamin, again they did meet, but eighteen thousand more faced defeat.
Then Israel fasted, wept in despair, and offered sacrifices with heartfelt prayer. “Shall we continue, or give up the fight?” “Go on,” said Yahweh, “I'll give you the night.”
With ambush set, they moved with stealth, against Gibeah, they crept with health. Benjamin struck, thinking they'd won, but Israel's plan had just begun.
The ambush rose, smoke filled the air, Benjamin turned and saw despair. With Israel's might, Benjamin's fall, twenty-five thousand in total, that was all.
Now Benjamin fled, but Israel pursued, surrounding them, their strength renewed. Eighteen thousand fell, valor in vain, the rest fled, seeking shelter from pain.
To the rock of Rimmon, six hundred fled, while their cities burned, Israel's anger spread. In fire and fury, they left no stone, bringing justice, their message shown.
In Mizpah, Israel made a vow, "No daughters to Benjamin, not now." In Bethel, voices raised, tears were shed, "God, why is one tribe's future dead?"
They built an altar, offerings burned bright, Asked, "Who didn't come to Yahweh's sight?" Mizpah's oath was a heavy load, Those absent faced death's harsh code.
Israel wept for Benjamin, their kin, "A tribe's cut off, how to begin? No daughters to give, what can we do? Find who missed the assembly view."
Jabesh Gilead, not a soul came through, Counted heads, none in the crew. Valiant men, twelve thousand strong, "To Jabesh, right the wrong."
"Strike with the sword," they did declare, Destruction left no one there. Four hundred maidens found alive, To camp Shiloh, they did arrive.
Peace to Benjamin, at Rimmon's rock, Brought the women, yet still in shock. The tribe broken, a breach in the land, Elders questioned, made their stand.
"An inheritance must stay, Benjamin's name, But our daughters can't join the claim." A plan was hatched, a feast at Shiloh, Daughters danced, and men lay low.
"Watch the vineyards, catch your bride, When fathers protest, we'll provide. Say, 'Not taken by battle's might, Nor given, so you stay right.'"
Benjamin moved, took the chance, Found wives among Shiloh's dance. Back to their land, cities rebuilt, Each tribe departed, paths were split.
No king ruled in those days, Each did right in their own ways.
In the days of judges, famine hit the land, A man from Bethlehem, with a plan in hand. Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and two sons, Left for Moab, where their new life begun.
In Moab, sadness came, Elimelech passed, Naomi was left, her sons the only cast. Mahlon and Chilion married women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, the lives they now had.
But tragedy struck, the sons died too, Naomi left alone, not knowing what to do. She heard that Yahweh gave bread to her land, So she rose up, with daughters-in-law by hand.
Naomi said, “Turn back, find rest at home, May Yahweh bless you, wherever you may roam.” They wept and said, “No, we will stay with you,” But Naomi insisted, “This is what you must do.”
“Go back, my daughters, I have no more sons, I’m too old now, my time has come. Why wait for what’s not to be? Yahweh’s hand has turned against me.”
Orpah wept, kissed, and finally turned back, But Ruth clung tight, her resolve intact. Naomi urged, “Follow like your sister, go,” But Ruth replied, “I won’t leave, no, no.”
“Where you go, I will go, where you stay, I stay, Your people, my people, come what may. Your God, my God, in life and in death, Not even death will part our breath.”
Naomi saw Ruth’s firm resolve, Stopped urging, let the problem solve. Together to Bethlehem they traveled on, The city buzzed, “Is this Naomi, come and gone?”
“Don’t call me Naomi, call me Mara now, For the Almighty’s dealt bitterly, somehow. Full I left, empty I return, Yahweh’s testified, in His ways I learn.”
So Naomi returned, with Ruth by her side, Back to Bethlehem, where harvests abide. At the start of barley season, they arrived, Hope and new beginnings were revived.
Naomi had a kin, a wealthy man indeed, From Elimelech's line, Boaz was his seed.
Ruth the Moabitess, with courage anew, Said, "Let me glean in the fields, find favor too." Naomi nodded, "Go ahead, my dear," Ruth ventured forth, her goal was clear.
She landed in Boaz's field, no plan, A twist of fate led her to that man. Boaz arrived from Bethlehem's land, "May Yahweh bless you," he commanded the band.
"Who's this young lady?" Boaz did inquire, His servant replied, "The Moabite with Naomi, she came to inspire. She asked to glean, from dawn 'til now, Just a short rest, she took a bow."
Boaz spoke to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter true, Stick with my maidens, don’t leave this crew. Watch the field, follow them near, I told the men, no harm comes here."
"When you're thirsty, drink from our well, Safety and kindness, with us you'll dwell." Ruth bowed low, "Why such favor to me? A foreigner here, yet kindness I see."
Boaz replied, "I've heard of your deed, For Naomi's sake, how you've left your creed. May Yahweh repay, His wings your shield, Israel's protection, in His field."
Ruth thanked him, eyes shining bright, Boaz invited her to dine that night. "Come, eat bread, dip morsel in the sauce, Join my reapers, no need for loss."
She ate her fill, saved some for later, Boaz ensured her gleaning was greater. "Let her glean among sheaves, leave her some grain, Do not rebuke her, let her sustain."
Ruth worked 'til dusk, her hands did strive, An ephah of barley, she managed to derive. Back to the city, her bounty in hand, Naomi saw, her joy was grand.
"Where did you glean? Who showed such grace?" "With Boaz," Ruth said, "In his field, I found my place." Naomi blessed him, "For his kindness shown, He's kin to us, we're not alone."
Ruth recalled his words, "Stay near my crew, 'Til harvest ends, his protection's true." Naomi agreed, "Stay close, my daughter dear, In Boaz's field, you'll find no fear."
So Ruth stayed close, through barley and wheat, With Naomi, her days were replete.
Naomi said, "My daughter dear, let me find you rest, With Boaz, our kin, who truly is best. Tonight, he'll be winnowing barley grain, Wash, anoint, and dress—go seek what you gain.
Wait till he's eaten, drunk, and then lay low, Once he's asleep, to his feet you'll go. Uncover his feet, and then lay down, He'll tell you what to do when he turns around."
Ruth replied, "All you say, I will do." She went down, and followed Naomi's cue. Boaz ate, drank, and his heart was light, Lay by the grain heap, ready for the night.
Ruth approached soft, uncovered his feet, Lay down, midnight came—Boaz stirred from sleep. "Who are you?" he asked, startled, to see, "I'm Ruth, your servant; spread your garment over me.
You're a kinsman," she spoke, bold and true, Boaz replied, "Blessed be you! You've shown kindness, not seeking the young, Whether rich or poor, your worth is sung.
Fear not, my daughter, I’ll do all you ask, The city knows your worth, a noble task. Yet there's one closer, a kinsman near, If he redeems, let him; if not, I'm here.
Stay till the dawn, and rest your head, In the morning, see what lies ahead." At her feet, Ruth lay till morning light, Rose up quietly, before the first sight.
Boaz said, "Keep this discreet and neat, Bring your mantle, hold it tight and neat." He filled it with six measures of barley, a load, She carried it back to Naomi’s abode.
Naomi asked, "How did it go, my dear?" Ruth told all, with barley to share. "He said, 'Don't go empty—take this gift, Until it’s settled, in him I place my trust, swift.'"
"Wait, my daughter, this man's resolute, He'll not rest till the matter's absolute."
Boaz at the gate, sat down to wait, The kinsman passed by, Boaz called, "Don't hesitate!"
"Come here, sit down," Boaz did greet, Ten elders joined them, took their seat.
"Naomi's land's up for sale, you see, Elimelech's plot, will you redeem?" said he.
"If you redeem, go on and take the land, But if not, let me know, understand?"
The kinsman agreed, "I'll redeem it, sure," But Boaz dropped a detail, couldn't ignore.
"When you buy that field, Ruth comes too, To honor the dead, that's what you'll do."
The kinsman stepped back, "Can't mess with my own, Take my right, Boaz, the land's your zone."
In Israel, they swapped shoes for the deal, The kinsman passed it, Boaz sealed it with zeal.
"You all witnessed today," Boaz declared with pride, "I've bought all Elimelech's, and Ruth as my bride."
The elders and people said, "We witness this, May she be like Leah, Rachel, bring bliss."
Boaz took Ruth, she became his wife, Yahweh blessed her, with new life.
Naomi cradled the boy, her heart's delight, "Blessed be Yahweh, who makes things right."
Named Obed, he'd carry the family flame, Father of Jesse, David's claim to fame.
From Perez to Hezron, Ram to Amminadab, Nahshon to Salmon, lineage they had.
Salmon to Boaz, who fathered Obed, Obed to Jesse, then King David was bred.
In Ramathaim Zophim, a man named Elkanah, Two wives he had, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah bore children, but Hannah was bare, Yearly they'd worship in Shiloh, offering each share.
Elkanah to Peninnah and her kids did provide, But to Hannah, his love, a double portion beside. Though Yahweh closed her womb, Peninnah would tease, Hannah wept bitterly, her heart never at ease.
Elkanah asked, "Hannah, why is your heart sore? Am I not better than ten sons and more?" But Hannah prayed deeply, tears flowed like a stream, Promised a son to God, if He'd fulfill her dream.
Eli the priest saw her lips move without sound, Thought she was drunk, but no drink was around. She pleaded, "I'm pouring my soul, not filled with wine, Out of pain and sorrow, I utter each line."
Eli said, "Go in peace; may God grant your choice." Her heart felt lighter, hope found its voice. They worshiped at dawn, to Ramah they trod, Elkanah and Hannah, blessed by God.
Time passed, Hannah conceived, a son she bore, Named him Samuel, "Asked of Yahweh," she swore. Elkanah went to make his vow, true and sincere, But Hannah said, "I'll wait till our child is clear."
Elkanah agreed, "Do what you deem right, May Yahweh's word stand firm in His sight." When Samuel was weaned, to Shiloh they came, With offerings in hand, to honor God's name.
Hannah spoke to Eli, "Remember me here? I prayed for this child, my words sincere. Now I give him to Yahweh, for all his days, To serve and worship, in all of his ways."
Hannah prayed with a heart full of joy, In Yahweh she found strength, no one could destroy. "My mouth's wide with triumph, my foes in retreat, In Your salvation, my heart skips a beat.
No one holy like Yahweh, no rock like our Lord, Proud words are empty, let humility be stored. Yahweh's knowledge weighs every act, Mighty bows break, while the weak gain tact.
Those once full, now work for their bread, The hungry are fed, the barren has spread. Yahweh brings life and takes it away, He humbles and lifts, come what may.
From dust to thrones, the needy He lifts, Raising them high with royal gifts. For the earth's pillars belong to Yahweh’s might, The wicked in darkness, silenced from sight.
Those who clash with Yahweh will shatter and fall, He thunders on high, His justice for all. Strength to His king, His anointed He'll raise, Elkanah returned home, giving God the praise.
But Eli's sons were wicked, they knew not the Lord, Priests taking the offerings they could not afford. With forks they took, not waiting their turn, Despising God's gifts, they refused to learn.
Yet Samuel served, clothed in linen fine, With a robe from his mother, year after year in line. Eli blessed them, praying for more, Yahweh answered, giving children galore.
Eli's sons sinned, he heard of their deeds, Sleeping with women, ignoring his pleas. "Why commit sins, bringing shame to our name?" But they ignored him, seeking no change.
A man of God came with a message so stark, "Didn't I choose you, give you a mark? Why disrespect My offerings, choosing your kin? Now, far be it from Me, for you've let sin in.
Your house will fall, no old man will last, Sorrow will come, your glory will pass. Hophni and Phinehas, in one day will die, I’ll raise a priest true, under My eye.
Those left will bow, seeking bread and plea, For honor and hope in My presence to be."
Young Samuel served before Yahweh's own, Eli old, with vision nearly gone.
Rare were visions, God's word was still, In the temple, God’s lamp hadn't gone nil.
Samuel laid where the ark had its place, Yahweh called out in the quiet space.
"Here I am," Samuel ran to Eli’s side, "I didn't call," Eli replied, "let it slide."
Once more, "Samuel!" the call was clear, Again to Eli, "I didn't call, my dear."
Samuel knew not Yahweh's voice yet, But Eli perceived what Samuel met.
Eli advised, "Next time, just say, 'Speak, Yahweh; your servant hears today.'"
Yahweh called, "Samuel! Samuel!" He said, "Speak; for your servant hears," Samuel pled.
"Behold," said Yahweh, "a thing I shall do, Israel will tingle when they hear it too.
Against Eli's house, it's all set to unfold, The iniquity known, the truth must be told."
Samuel lay till dawn, afraid to share, Eli called, "My son, what did Yahweh declare?"
"Tell me all, hide nothing from my view," Samuel told it all, Eli knew it was true.
"It is Yahweh, let Him do what's best," Samuel grew, God’s words he possessed.
From Dan to Beersheba, all knew the name, Samuel, a prophet, in Yahweh's fame.
Yahweh returned, in Shiloh’s light, Revealed to Samuel, God's word in sight.

Samuel spoke, Israel listened, ready for war, Against the Philistines, camped by Ebenezer's door. The Philistines stood tall, ready for the fight, Israel went down hard, four thousand lost that night.
Back at camp, elders cried, "Why this defeat? Let’s fetch Yahweh's ark, bring victory on our feet." To Shiloh they sent, for the ark of His might, With Eli’s sons, they brought it back in sight.
When the ark arrived, Israel shouted loud, The earth shook, echoing the proud. Philistines heard and trembled in fear, "The ark of God is here!" they cried, “Woe, oh dear!”

“They struck Egypt once, can we withstand their power? We must fight strong, this is our hour!” So they braced for battle, with courage they fought, Israel fled, thirty thousand lives there were caught.
The ark was seized, Eli’s sons fell, A messenger ran, their fate to tell. Eli sat waiting, heart tense with dread, Hearing news of the ark, he fell and was dead.
Phinehas' wife, near birth, heard the news, Her husband gone, she had much to lose. She gave birth and named her child with a sigh, Ichabod, “God’s glory has left,” was her cry.
"The glory has departed," she whispered, forlorn, For the ark was lost, leaving Israel torn.
The Philistines took the ark, brought it to Ashdod's land, Placed it next to Dagon, their idol, grand.
Morning came, Ashdod folks rose to see, Dagon facedown, a sight of mystery.
They picked him up, set him right once more, But next morning, same fate as before.
Dagon lay broken, head and hands on the floor, Only his body left by the door.
Priests of Dagon feared, the threshold they'd shun, Yahweh's power on Ashdod—none could outrun.
Yahweh’s hand was heavy, tumors struck them down, Ashdod’s borders trembled, fear spread through the town.
Men of Ashdod said, “This ark can't stay, His hand is fierce, we must send it away.”
Philistine lords gathered, seeking what to do, “Send it to Gath,” they decided, “Let it pass through.”
In Gath it went, but trouble followed still, Yahweh’s hand struck again, with a painful chill.
Tumors on the people, small and great, Confusion and cries, sealing their fate.
They sent the ark to Ekron, but the cries began, “They’ve brought the ark to kill us, to kill every man!”
Philistine lords convened, troubled with dread, “Send it back home, or we’ll all end up dead.”
Panic in the city, God’s hand heavy and grim, Those left alive, prayed and cried out to Him.
Seven months Philistines had the ark in their land, Calling priests and diviners to lend a hand,
"What to do with Yahweh's ark?" they asked, "Where to send it, what's the task?"
"Don't send it empty, give a trespass fee, Five golden tumors, and mice there'll be."
For the lords of Philistine, for the plague on you all, Images to glorify Israel's God so tall.
"Don't harden your hearts like Pharaoh's crew, Release His hand, let it not trouble you."
"Prepare a new cart, two cows without yoke, Tie them there, separate calves—no joke."
Place the ark on the cart, the gold by its side, Send it on its way, let Yahweh guide.
"If it finds its border, Beth Shemesh ahead, Then it's He who brought this dread."
So the men took the cows, tied them with care, Put the ark on the cart, offering to bear.
Cows headed straight, lowing all the way, Philistine lords followed, in dismay.
Beth Shemesh folk harvesting in the field, Eyes lifted, saw the ark revealed.
The cart stopped in Joshua's land so wide, Wood split, cows sacrificed, nothing to hide.
Levites took the ark, placed it on the stone, Offered sacrifices, worship shown.
Philistine lords saw and went back home, Ark returned, and the message was known.
Golden tumors, golden mice, cities all aligned, To the great stone where Yahweh's ark reclined.
But they peeked inside, Beth Shemesh men, Yahweh struck them, mourning began.
"Who can stand before this holy God?" they cried, "To whom shall the ark go?" they sighed.
They called Kiriath Jearim folks, "Come here, The Philistines returned the ark, come take it near."
The men of Kiriath Jearim came real quick, Took Yahweh's ark, up the hill, it was slick. Into Abinadab’s house, it found its rest, Eleazar consecrated, to guard it with zest.
For twenty long years, the ark stayed in place, Israel lamented, seeking Yahweh’s grace. Samuel spoke up, to Israel's hearts, "Turn to Yahweh, that's where it starts.
Put away idols, serve Him alone, He’ll deliver you, make His power known." Israel listened, cleared out the old, Served Yahweh only, their faith emboldened.
Samuel called, "Meet me at Mizpah's gate, I'll pray to Yahweh, let's set things straight." They gathered, they fasted, water poured down, Confessed their sins, as Samuel wore the crown.
Philistines heard, they gathered with might, Israel feared, in the looming fight. They pleaded with Samuel, "Cry out to our God, To save us from their threatening squad."
Samuel took a lamb, offered it whole, Cried to Yahweh, pouring out his soul. As the Philistines neared, ready for war, Yahweh thundered loudly, shook them to the core.
Israel chased them, struck them down hard, Pushed them back, 'neath Beth Kar's guard. Samuel set a stone, Ebenezer its name, "Yahweh helped us," they all proclaimed.
Philistines subdued, stopped crossing the line, Yahweh's hand held firm, in Samuel's time. Cities restored, peace with Amorites, Samuel judged, through days and nights.
Yearly he traveled, Bethel to Mizpah round, Judgment and justice in every town found. Back to Ramah, his home so dear, Built an altar to Yahweh, year by year.
Samuel got old, his sons took the stand, But they strayed from his path, corrupted the land. In Beersheba they judged, but they chased after gold, Took bribes, twisted justice, breaking the mold.
Israel's elders came, gathered in Ramah's town, "You're old, your sons fail, so bring us a crown. Make us like others, a king on the throne," But Samuel was troubled, felt all alone.
He prayed to Yahweh, seeking His say, Yahweh spoke clear, "Listen, don't dismay. They reject not you, but me as their King, Since Egypt they've turned, now doing this thing.
Hear their demand, but make sure they know, The king's heavy hand, how his power will grow." Samuel warned them, spoke Yahweh's decree, "The king will take sons, for his chariots they'll be.
Captains and soldiers, harvesting lands, Crafting his weapons, working with hands. Daughters for perfume, baking, and more, Fields and vineyards, he'll take and store.
A tenth of your seed, vineyards and fruit, To officers, servants, he'll recruit. Your servants and flocks, he'll claim as his own, You'll be his servants, your freedoms overthrown.
You'll cry out loud, for the king you chose, But Yahweh won't hear, you'll reap what you sow." Yet the people refused, their hearts were set, "We want a king, like the others, no regret.
To judge us, to lead, to fight our fight," Samuel took their words, repeated them right. Yahweh said, "Let them have their way, Give them a king, as they say."
Samuel sent them all back to their home, Israel would have a king, not alone.
In the land of Benjamin, Kish was the man, A mighty dude with a courageous plan. His son was Saul, tall and grand, No one like him in all the land.
Kish's donkeys roamed and strayed, "Saul," he said, "go, find where they've laid." Through Ephraim's hills, they made their way, Searched Shalishah, Shaalim, no luck that day.
In Zuph, Saul said, "Let's head home, Dad will worry, left alone." But the servant said, "Hold up, bro, A man of God nearby, let's ask where to go."
Saul replied, "What can we bring? Our bread is gone, got not a thing." The servant showed a silver piece, "Let's give this, and gain some peace."
"Good plan," said Saul, "let's track him down," Maidens said, "The seer's in town." They hurried on, with hope in sight, Found Samuel before the night.
God spoke to Sam the day before, "From Benjamin, I'll send one more. Anoint him prince, he'll lead the fight, Against Philistines, with might and right."
Saul met Sam at the city's gate, "Where's the seer?" he asked, not late. Samuel said, "You're eating with me, Tomorrow, all you need, you'll see."
"Don't stress the donkeys, they're back home, Israel's riches are yours alone." Saul said, "But I'm just a Benjamite, The smallest tribe, why this delight?"
Samuel set them in the place of honor, Thirty gathered, as they pondered. The cook brought forth the special meat, Saved for Saul, now ready to eat.
