On the twenty-fourth day of the month, they gathered in a scene, Fasting, wearing sackcloth, with dirt, they leaned. Israel stood apart, from foreigners they estranged, Confessed their sins, their fathers' wrongs, unchanged.
They stood up in place, reading the law's decree, A fourth of the day in worship, confessing earnestly. Jeshua, Bani, on the stairs they stepped, Cried to Yahweh, as their voices leapt.
"Stand up and bless Yahweh, our God forever praised, His glorious name, above all blessing raised! He's Yahweh alone, made heaven's high dome, Earth and its fullness, sea's endless foam."
He chose Abram, and called him Abraham, Found a faithful heart, made a covenant grand. The land promised, from Canaanite to Jebusite, Given to his seed, in God's righteous sight.
Saw their pain in Egypt, by the sea they cried, Signs and wonders against Pharaoh, in pride. Split the sea apart, on dry land they crossed, Their enemies drowned, in the waters tossed.
Pillar of cloud by day, fire by night, Guided them steady, in Yahweh's light. He came down at Sinai, gave right rules, Statutes and commands, through Moses' tools.
Bread from the sky, water from the stone, Promised land to take, as their own. But they turned proud, necks hardened and stiff, Ignored commandments, God's gifts they missed.
Made a calf of gold, "This is your God!" they cried, But Yahweh's mercy, stayed by their side. Pillar of cloud stayed, by night fire's glow, His Spirit instructed, manna did flow.
Forty years sustained, clothes and feet intact, Kingdoms and peoples, were their lands backed. Children multiplied, stars in the sky, Entered the land, promises not a lie.
Took cities and lands, filled with good things, Yet disobedient, they rebelled against the King. Prophets killed, laws cast aside, Delivered to foes, their cries amplified.
When they cried, God heard their plea, Sent saviors to set them free. But after rest, evil returned, Enemies ruled, lessons unlearned.
Yet God's mercy, never did cease, Though they turned away, He offered peace. Kings and priests, fathers too, Ignored commandments, hearts untrue.
"Behold, we're servants in this fruitful land, Kings hold power, as sin expands. In distress we stand, yet make a vow, A covenant sealed, before God now."
Sealed by Nehemiah, the governor, in the lead, Then Zedekiah, Seraiah, followed the creed.
Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur took their stand, With Amariah, Malchijah, a righteous band.
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, on the scroll, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, played their role.
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch stood tall, With Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, they call.
Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah, the priests in line, Levites like Jeshua, strong, divine.
Binnui of Henadad, Kadmiel, the crew, Shebaniah, Hodiah, in faith they grew.
Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan add to the list, Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, they persist.
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah again, Hodiah, Bani, Beninu, these were the men.
Chiefs of people: Parosh, Pahathmoab, stand, Elam, Zattu, Bani, strong in the land.
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, names in the set, Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, don’t forget.
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, in their might, Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, in the light.
Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai, in their place, Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, in grace.
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, they came, Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, known by name.
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, in line, Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, divine.
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, stand tall, Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, gave their all.
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah, closed the crew, The people, priests, Levites, all in view.
Separated from the lands, in God’s law they found, Moses' commandments, in unity, they’re bound.
“Don’t give our daughters to the land’s folk,” they swore, “Nor take theirs for our sons,” they vowed once more.
No buying goods on Sabbath, rest is the key, Every seventh year, debts forgiven, be free.
Yearly ordinances, a third of a shekel, For the house of God, where righteousness dwells.
Show bread, meal offerings, burnt offerings too, For Sabbaths, new moons, holy feasts, they knew.
Casting lots for the wood, by father’s decree, “Burn on Yahweh’s altar,” year by year, faithfully.
First fruits of ground, first fruits of trees, To Yahweh's house, as grateful as can be.
Firstborn sons, livestock, herds and flocks, To the priests who minister, all as the Law instructs.
First fruits of dough, wave offerings pure, New wine, oil, tithes, Levites ensure.
Priests and Levites, tithe upon tithe they bring, To the house of our God, where the praises ring.
Offerings of grain, new wine, and oil, In the sanctuary, their faith won’t spoil.
"We won’t forsake the house of our God," they say, In unity and strength, they’ll walk His way.
Princes in Jerusalem, that's where they stay, The rest cast lots, to see who'd make their way.
One in ten moved to the holy ground, While others in different cities were found.
Blessings on those who chose to dwell, In Jerusalem, where stories they’d tell.
Chiefs of the province, they took their stand, In city or country, they claimed their land.
Judah’s sons, like Athaiah, Uzziah’s seed, In Jerusalem, they lived, with courage and creed.
Maaseiah, from the line of Baruch he came, Sons of Perez, valiant, known by name.
Benjamin’s boys, led by Sallu with pride, Nine hundred twenty-eight, they reside.
Joel was overseer, Judah second in command, Together they ruled this sacred land.
Priests like Jedaiah, Seraiah, they served, God's house their realm, never unnerved.
Brothers worked, eight hundred twenty-two, Adaiah's clan, chiefs, stood strong and true.
Amashsai’s kin, mighty men indeed, One hundred twenty-eight, they lead.
Levites like Shemaiah, kept things intact, Shabbethai, Jozabad, with oversight exact.
Mattaniah began the thanks and prayer, Levites in the city, they were always there.
Gatekeepers like Akkub stood at the gate, One hundred seventy-two, they watched and wait.
In cities of Judah, others took their claim, Temple servants at Ophel, known by name.
Uzzi the overseer, making sure it’s right, Singers had provisions, every day and night.
Pethahiah by the king’s side, handling affairs, Children of Judah lived in towns with their cares.
From Kiriath Arba to Beth Pelet wide, Through Ziklag to En Rimmon, they reside.
Benjamin from Geba to Bethel’s ground, All these towns, their roots were found.
In fields and valleys, craftsmen laid their stake, From Levite divisions, new homes they’d make.
Zerubbabel's crew, they rose up with a shout, Priests and Levites, they were stepping out.
Leading the charge were Seraiah and Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, on fire.
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, in line, Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, shining fine.
Mijamin, Maadiah, and Bilgah in the game, Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, carrying the flame.
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah too, Heads of priests in Jeshua's days, they knew what to do.
Levites came next: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, With Judah, Mattaniah, they rang the thanksgiving bell.
Bakbukiah and Unno, their brothers close, In their appointed roles, they did the most.
Jeshua fathered Joiakim, who fathered Eliashib, Eliashib to Joiada, passing on the crib.
Joiada to Jonathan, his line did flow, Jonathan to Jaddua, steady as they go.
Priests in Joiakim's day, heads of homes, you see, Seraiah's house had Meraiah, Jeremiah had Hananiah, free.
Ezra had Meshullam, Amariah had Jehohanan, Malluchi had Jonathan, Shebaniah had Joseph's clan.
Harim had Adna, Meraioth had Helkai's name, Iddo had Zechariah, Ginnethon had Meshullam's fame.
Abijah's son was Zichri, Miniamin and Moadiah's Piltai, Bilgah's line was Shammua, Shemaiah had Jehonathan nearby.
Joiarib's Mattenai, Jedaiah's Uzzi, Sallai's Kallai, Amok's Eber, flying high.
Hilkiah's Hashabiah, Jedaiah's Nethanel, Levites were recorded, like a story to tell.
Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, In praise and thanks, they did excel.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam strong, Gatekeepers guarding, where they belong.
In Joiakim's days, with Nehemiah, the boss, Ezra the scribe, no matter the loss.
Dedication day at Jerusalem's wall, Levites gathered, with glad thanksgivings all.
Singers from regions, villages they came, To praise with harps, and lift up God's name.
Priests and Levites purified all, People, gates, and wall — they stood tall.
Princes of Judah up on the wall, Two great companies, giving it their all.
One group to the right, toward the dung gate stride, Hoshaiah and half the princes walked with pride.
Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam in their lane, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah, no shame.
Priests with trumpets, Zechariah leading the pack, Brothers with instruments, never looking back.
Ezra the scribe, leading the parade, To the water gate, east they'd invade.
The other company met them there, Half the people followed, climbing the stair.
Above Ephraim’s gate, the old gate they passed, Fish gate to sheep gate, standing steadfast.
Two companies gave thanks in God's own abode, Priests and singers, lifting the load.
Great sacrifices offered, joy so profound, Women, children, with joy they resound.
Rooms for treasures, offerings stored, Priests and Levites, their duty restored.
Singers, gatekeepers, according to command, David and Solomon, singing hand in hand.
In days of old, they praised God’s might, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah, kept it tight.
Portions to singers, gatekeepers they gave, Levites and Aaron’s sons, for whom they saved.
Opened the book, the words were read, The law was heard, here's what it said:
"Ammonites, Moabites, can't join this game, 'Cause bread and water they never came."
They hired Balaam to curse and fight, But God turned curses into blessings bright.
Heard the law, they took a stand, Separated the mixed from Israel's land.
Priest Eliashib, with Tobiah's hand, Gave him a room, in God's house it would stand.
But I wasn't there, I was with the king, Returned to see what this mess would bring.
Saw Eliashib's deed, Tobiah's domain, Threw out his stuff, to cleanse again.
Put God's vessels back in their place, Restored the offerings, to show His grace.
Levites' portions were gone, not paid, Left their work, to the fields they strayed.
I asked the rulers, "Why's God's house forsaken?" Brought them back, got the gears awaken'.
Tithes of grain, new wine, oil too, Stored in treasuries, where they were due.
Set the faithful to manage that stash, "Remember me, God, for my deeds, not trash."
Saw work on the Sabbath, carts rolling in, Testified against them, calling out sin.
"Why do this wrong, and profane the day?" I shut those gates, kept burdens away.
Warned those merchants camping round, "Stay away, or I'll bring you down."
Levites purified, guarding the gates, "Remember me, God, my kindness is great."
Saw Jews with wives from lands afar, Children’s tongues mixed, setting the bar.
Contended hard, plucked hair, and swore, "Don't mix daughters and sons anymore."
Solomon's tale, a lesson learned, Foreign wives his heart had turned.
Chased out the priest with foreign kin, "Remember them, God, the faults within."
Cleansed them from outsiders' sway, Set priests and Levites to work and pray.
Kept the offerings, first fruits, all good, "Remember me, God, I've done what I could."
In the days of King Ahasuerus, from India to Ethiopia's might, He ruled over provinces, a hundred twenty-seven in sight.
On his throne in Susa's grand palace, he sat with pride, In his third year, a grand feast he did provide.
Princes and servants, all gathered for the show, The riches of his kingdom, he let them all know.
For one hundred eighty days, the splendor was displayed, Then a seven-day feast for all in Susa was made.
White and blue hangings, purple cords so fine, Golden vessels held the royal wine.
In the garden's court, both great and small, Every man's pleasure, the king's decree for all.
Queen Vashti, too, held a feast for her own, In the royal house, where her power was shown.
On the seventh day, the king, merry with wine, Called for Vashti, his queen so fine.
But Vashti refused the king's command, His anger burned, like fire on the sand.
To the wise men, the king called for advice, "What shall we do? Vashti's disobedience isn't nice."
Memucan spoke, "Not just you, my king, she wrongs, All the people, princes, where she belongs."
"If word spreads, wives will defy, Contempt will rise like clouds in the sky."
"Let a royal decree be written with haste, Vashti banished, replaced with no waste."
"When proclaimed, wives will honor their men, From the greatest to the smallest, they'll know when."
The king and princes agreed with the plan, Letters were sent, man's rule over his clan.
So went the word, to each province and place, In every tongue, every people, no race.
King’s wrath cooled, he recalled Vashti’s scene, Servants said, “Seek virgins to make a new queen.”
“Gather them from provinces wide, To Susa’s citadel, let them reside.”
The plan pleased the king, officers spread, With Hegai in charge, beauty rituals led.
Mordecai, a Jew, in Susa he stayed, With Esther, his kin, whom he had raised.
Esther was fair, with beauty so bright, Orphaned young, she shone like light.
King’s decree echoed through halls, Maidens gathered, within Susa’s walls.
Esther taken to the king’s domain, Hegai saw her, his favor she’d gain.
Cosmetics, food, and seven maids too, To the best place in the house she flew.
“Keep your people unknown,” Mordecai said, As he paced every day, anxious, full of dread.
Each woman’s turn, a twelve-month prepare, Sweet scents and oils filled the air.
To the king’s house, they’d go at night, Return to wait in morning light.
Esther’s moment, she sought no excess, Hegai’s advice, nothing more, nothing less.
Taken to the king in Tebeth’s chill, His heart she captured, with grace and will.
Crown on her head, queen she became, Feast declared, in Esther’s name.
Mordecai lingered at the gate, Listening, watching, early to late.
Two eunuchs plotted against the throne, Mordecai heard, he wasn’t alone.
Told Esther, who told the king, Plot unraveled, justice did ring.
Both were hanged, truth revealed, Chronicles penned, their fate was sealed.
King Ahasuerus raised Haman high, Above the princes, reaching for the sky.
Servants at the gate all bowed down, But Mordecai stood firm, didn’t frown.
"Why disobey the king's command?" they said, Yet Mordecai stood, wouldn’t bow his head.
Told Haman of the Jew who refused the call, Haman's anger rose, wouldn’t let it fall.
Not just Mordecai, but all his kin, Haman plotted where the dark began.
First month, Nisan, the lot was cast, Twelfth month, Adar, the day was fast.
To the king, Haman spoke of a scattered race, "Different laws, they dishonor your face.
If it pleases you, let them be erased, Silver will follow, your coffers embraced."
The king gave his ring with mighty power, "The silver is yours, use it this hour."
Scribes wrote all that Haman decreed, Letters sent out with a swift, urgent speed.
Destroy young and old, every Jew in sight, On the twelfth month's thirteenth night.
The letters spread, a decree so grim, The city of Susa felt its dim.
The king and Haman sat to drink in glee, But Susa was confused, couldn’t see the spree.
Mordecai learned what had gone down, tore his clothes, sackcloth draped 'round, In the city he cried, a wail so loud, grieving in the midst of the crowd.
To the king's gate he approached, but no sackcloth allowed inside, Across provinces, mourning spread wide, with fasting, tears, in sackcloth they cried.
Esther heard the news, her heart heavy with the weight, Sent clothes to Mordecai, but he refused to change his state.
Hathach, the eunuch, went to meet Mordecai, Found him by the gate, heard his desperate cry.
Mordecai shared the scheme, Haman's wicked plan, Coin to destroy Jews, a shadow over the land.
He handed the decree, urged Esther to plead, To the king for mercy, for the Jews in need.
Hathach brought the message back, Esther listened with care, "Approach without a call means death, I'm aware."
Esther's words returned to Mordecai's ear, He responded with a message, crystal clear:
"Don't think you'll escape when trouble's near, Help will come, but your family may disappear.
Perhaps you were made queen for a time like this, To stand up, take courage, don't dismiss."
Esther replied with a bold, steady breath, "Gather all the Jews, fast 'til there's nothing left.
Three days, nights, no food or drink for me, I'll go to the king, risk it all, if need be."
Mordecai obeyed, spread the word all around, In unity they fasted, hope in silence found.
On the third day, Esther dressed in royal wear, Stood in the court, bold, in the king's lair. The king on his throne, with eyes sharp and keen, Saw Esther and favored the queen.
He lifted his scepter, a golden rod, Esther approached, touched the scepter of God. “What do you wish, Queen Esther?” he said, “Half the kingdom's yours, just nod your head.”
Esther replied, “If it pleases the king, Join me and Haman at the banquet I bring.” “Bring Haman quickly,” the king gave the call, To Esther’s feast, they went, standing tall.
At the banquet of wine, the king was keen, “What do you desire, my gracious queen?” Esther answered, “If it pleases you still, Join me tomorrow, the feast I’ll fulfill.”
Haman left joyful, his heart a grand tune, Till Mordecai sat firm, a thorn in his bloom. Yet anger inside, Haman held it tight, Went home to boast of his glory and might.
Told his riches, his rise in king's place, And how Esther invited him alone to grace. “Still, it’s worthless,” he said with spite, “Mordecai sits there, in plain sight.”
His wife Zeresh and friends had a plan, “Build gallows tall, fifty cubits span. In the morning, speak to the king with pride, Hang Mordecai, then banquet with stride.”
This pleased Haman, so he made it be, A gallows stood tall, a grim decree.
The king couldn't sleep, tossing in his bed, Called for the chronicles to be read.
Mordecai's deed was found in the scroll, Two eunuchs' plot, he had controlled.
The king asked, "What honor has been shared?" "Nothing," said the servants, "nothing's been declared."
"Who's in the court?" the king declared, Haman was there, his evil plan prepared.
"Bring him in," the king did say, Haman entered, thinking he’d have his way.
"What should be done for the man I favor?" Haman thought it was him, feeling like a savior.
"Royal clothes, the king's own ride, Crown on the horse, let him stride."
"Proclaim his honor through the city square, For the king’s delight, let all be aware."
"Hurry," said the king, "do this for Mordecai, Leave nothing undone, don’t even try."
Haman dressed Mordecai, led him through the streets, Humbled and mourning, with his pride in retreat.
He went home, head covered, full of dread, Told his wife and friends everything he said.
"If Mordecai’s Jewish, you can’t win this race, You'll surely fall, can't keep the pace."
While they spoke, the king's men arrived, To take Haman to Esther's feast, he strived.

Esther's banquet's on with the king and Haman in sight, The king leaned in, asking Esther, "What's your wish tonight? Tell me your request, queen, don't hesitate to speak, Even half my kingdom, if that's what you seek."

Esther replied, "If I've found favor in your eyes, Spare my life and my people's, before all hope dies. We're sold to be destroyed, slain, left to expire, If just for slaves, I'd keep quiet, but the stakes are higher."

The king, now tense, asked, "Who's behind this wicked plot?" Esther pointed, "It's Haman, the enemy, the rot!" Fear gripped Haman, the king stormed out with fire, As Haman begged Esther, for his life's desire.

When the king returned, Haman fell where Esther lay, The king shouted, "Will he assault my queen today?" Guards moved quick, covered Haman’s face in shame, Harbonah spoke up, calling out Haman's name.
"Behold, the gallows, fifty cubits in the sky, Built for Mordecai, who spoke truth, not a lie." The king ordered, "Hang him on what he made," So Haman hung high, and the king's wrath swayed.
Justice saw its day, the plot was reversed, The king's anger cooled, Haman's curse was cursed.
In the palace, King Ahasuerus made a decree, Gave Haman's house to Esther, set Mordecai free. The king took off his ring, once on Haman's hand, Passed it to Mordecai, who now took command.
Esther fell at the king's feet, tears in her plea, "End Haman's evil plans, let my people be." The king held out his scepter, golden and bright, Esther rose to speak, standing tall in the light.
"If it pleases you, king, and I find grace, Reverse Haman's letters, let my people embrace. How can I watch my kin face such doom? How endure their destruction, their impending gloom?"
King Ahasuerus turned to Mordecai and the queen, "Haman's been hanged, I gave you his scene. Write now in my name, seal it with my ring, For no man can reverse the word of the king."
Scribes were summoned in Sivan's month, day twenty-three, Mordecai's commands inked for all to see. From India to Ethiopia, provinces wide, Every tongue and tribe, the message couldn't hide.
Letters sealed with the king's ring, swiftly sent, On royal horses, through each province they went. The Jews could gather, defend, and fight, Against any who'd attack, in Adar's twelfth night.
The word spread fast, the decree was clear, Jews prepared for that day, without fear. Couriers pushed on by the king's command, In Susa, the news was grand.
Mordecai in blue and white, crowned with gold, Entered the city, the story told. The Jews rejoiced, light and honor in their way, Feasting and gladness on this victorious day.
In every town, where the king’s words rang, Jews celebrated, and their praises sang. Many joined them, feeling the fear, For the triumph of the Jews was crystal clear.
In the twelfth month's flow, Adar's thirteenth day, The king's decree was near, the stage set to slay.
Enemies hoped to conquer, take control, But tables turned, Jews conquered, taking their toll.
In cities they gathered, ready for the fight, No one could withstand them, their power, their might.
Princes and governors stood by their side, For Mordecai's fame made all fear and abide.
Mordecai grew mighty, his reputation soared, Throughout the provinces, his influence roared.
Jews struck with swords, enemies laid low, Destruction reigned, their strong will did show.
In Susa's citadel, five hundred met their end, Ten sons of Haman, they did apprehend.
The king heard the news, five hundred were dead, "What's your request, Esther?" he graciously said.
Esther spoke, "If the king pleases, one more day, Hang Haman's sons high, let justice have sway."
The king agreed, the decree was proclaimed, On gallows hung, Haman's sons were framed.
Jews in Susa gathered, another day they fought, Three hundred more slain, plunder they sought not.
Seventy-five thousand in provinces wide, Fell to the Jews, the victors with pride.
On the thirteenth day, they rested, found peace, Feasting and gladness, their joys did increase.
Village Jews declared the fourteenth a feast, Sending gifts of food, their joy never ceased.
Mordecai wrote, letters sent near and far, To keep the days Adar, a time of joy, a star.
Days of gladness, sorrow turned to cheer, Feasting and gifts, every single year.
Purim they named it, from the "Pur" that was cast, A time to remember those days that had passed.
Letters sent out, Esther and Mordecai declare, Peace and truth, a legacy to share.
The command confirmed, Purim etched in the book, A story of victory, the path they took.
King Ahasuerus, he raised the stakes, Tribute on the lands, across the sea breaks.
Power and might, his acts well-spun, Mordecai's greatness, second to none.
The chronicles hold the deeds so grand, In Media and Persia, his rule did stand.
Mordecai the Jew, right at the throne, Great among his people, never alone.
Beloved by many, his heart was true, For his people's good, he always knew.
He spoke of peace, with wisdom's glance, For all his kin, he took a stance.
In the land of Uz, there lived a man named Job, Blameless and upright, dodging evil like a pro.
He had seven sons and three daughters so fair, His wealth immense, beyond compare.
Seven thousand sheep and camels by the thousands, Oxen, donkeys, his household was astoundin'.
The greatest man in the East, no doubt, His family feasted, joy all about.
After the feasts, Job would rise at dawn, Offerings made, for sins that might spawn.
"Maybe my kids have cursed God in their heart," So Job played his faithful, protective part.
He did this continually, showing his belief, While in heaven's court, a brewing grief.
God's sons gathered before the Lord, Satan slipped in, with his deceitful chord.
"Where've you been?" God asked with a gaze, Satan replied, "Roaming earth's maze."
"Seen my servant Job, upright and true?" God's words were firm, "In him, no evil brew."
Satan challenged, "Job's piety isn't free, He's blessed on all sides, can't you see?
But take it away, he'll curse you, no doubt," God allowed the test, His faith devout.
"All he has is yours to test, But spare his life, let him stand the rest."
Job's day turned dark, disaster struck, Messengers ran, bringing tales of muck.
"The Sabeans raided, took your oxen away, Servants fell by the sword that day."
Another rushed in, "Fire from the sky, Sheep and servants, burned alive."
Then another came, "Chaldeans swept like bands, Camels gone, servants slain by their hands."
Finally, the worst news did unfold, A wind struck, left his kin cold.
Yet in all this, Job did not falter, He tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to alter.
"Naked I came, naked I'll return, God gives, God takes, His name I'll affirm."
Job didn’t sin, he didn't accuse, Held firm to his faith, didn’t refuse.
Gather 'round, let me set the scene right, Heavenly beings came, shining bright.
They stood before Yahweh, presenting their case, But Satan joined them with a bold face.
God asked, "Where you been, Satan? Speak your mind." Satan said, "Roaming earth, walking to find."
Yahweh spoke, "Have you seen my man Job? Upright and blameless, around the globe."
Satan smirked, "Skin for skin, man'll trade it all, Touch his flesh, watch him fall."
Yahweh allowed, "He's in your hand, But spare his life, understand?"
Satan struck Job with sores so dire, From head to toe, they burned like fire.
Job scraped his skin, sat in the ashes alone, His wife's words cut, but he stood firm like stone.
She said, "Curse God, let death be nigh." He replied, "Foolish talk, I'll not defy."
"Shall we take the good and not the bad?" In all his pain, his lips didn't go mad.
Job's friends heard, they came to see, Eliphaz, Bildad, Zophar—three.
They came to mourn the friend they knew, But from afar, they couldn't construe.
They tore their robes, dust in the air, Silent vigil, just showing they care.
Seven days, seven nights, no word said, For they saw his grief, heavy as lead.
Job opened his mouth, cursed his birth, "Perish the day I was brought to this earth.
Let darkness claim the day I was born, Let no light shine, let it be forlorn.
Let shadows lay claim, let clouds cover, Let blackness reign, no day to discover.
Let that night be seized by thickest shade, No joy, no voice, let its presence fade.
Curse it like those who call the beast, Let stars stay dark, let their shine cease.
Why didn’t the womb become my grave, Why wasn't I spared from life to save?
Why did knees hold me, why did I suckle, Why wasn’t I spared life's relentless struggle?
In death, I'd rest with kings and the wise, With princes in gold, where no trouble lies.
Where the wicked stop their troubling ways, Where weary souls find restful days.
Prisoners free from master's call, Small and great, there equal in all.
Why is light given to those in sorrow, Who dig for death, no hope for tomorrow?
Rejoicing in grave's embrace at last, Why light to the lost, whose hope has passed?
My sighs come before I eat each meal, My fears realized, my fate's a cruel deal.
I'm not at ease, no rest in my heart, Trouble finds me, tearing me apart."
Eliphaz stepped up, ready to speak, "Will you be grieved, if I take a peek? You've taught the masses, made weak hands strong, Your words lifted the fallen, helped them along.
But now it's on you, and you start to wail, It touches your soul, makes your spirit frail. Your piety's your confidence, your ways your hope, Isn't that enough for you to cope?
Remember now, who perished guilt-free? The upright never cut off, can't you see? Those who plow trouble, reap the same, By God's breath, they perish, by His anger's flame.
Lions roar, fierce and loud, But their teeth break, even the proud. Old lions waste, prey won't be found, Lioness cubs scattered all around.
A secret came, whispered to me at night, As the visions danced, and sleep took flight. Fear and trembling shook my bone, A spirit passed, left me alone.
Couldn't see its form, but I heard it say, "Can man be just, as God any day? He trusts not His servants, charges them all, Even angels, before Him, fall.
And how much more, those made of clay, Crushed to dust, at the end of the day. From dawn to dusk, they fade, Gone forever, without accolade.
Their tent cords plucked, wisdom none, They die silent, their journey done."
Call out now, who hears your call? To which holy one will you turn at all?
Resentment slays the foolish man, Jealousy kills, that's the plan.
I've seen fools rise and take their place, But cursed is their dwelling, gone without a trace.
Their kids are lost, far from safe embrace, Crushed at the gate, no saving grace.
Hungry take their harvest, no mercy shown, Traps await, substance overthrown.
Trouble's not born from dust alone, Man's born to spark like a rolling stone.
"But me, I seek God, commit my cause," He does great wonders, without pause.
"He gives rain, fields are watered, renewed, Raises the lowly, mourners are blessed, pursued."
Crafty plans He frustrates, hands can't scheme, Wise in craftiness, their plans lose steam.
Darkness in daytime, they grope around, He saves the needy, justice is found.
The poor have hope, injustice shut tight, Happy the corrected, God's light is bright.
"He wounds and binds, heals every scar, Delivers in troubles, no evil's bar."
In famine, redeemed from death's cold sword, Hidden from tongues, peace is restored.
Laugh at destruction, no fear of beast, Stones and animals, all make peace.
Tent in peace, nothing missed, Your offspring great, in life's list.
Grave in full age, like grain in season, Hear this wisdom, for life's good reason.
Job stood up with anguish, pain, and despair, Wishing his suffering could be weighed in the air.
Heavy like sand, his words rushed out fast, God’s arrows hit deep, his spirit couldn’t last.
"Does a donkey complain when the grass is lush? Or does an ox moan when his food's a plush?"
Tasteless is life, like food with no salt, He’s tired of the blandness, his soul wants to halt.
"Oh, let my desire be granted by God above, To crush me or release me from this love."
In pain, he'd find solace, holding his ground, Not denying the Holy One's words that resound.
Strength’s not endless like stones, nor flesh like bronze, All help’s gone, wisdom’s vanished, nothing on.
To the faint, a friend's kindness is owed, Even if they've strayed from the Almighty’s road.
Brothers like streams that dry and fade, Ice turns to water, in heat they evade.
Caravans in search, left distressed in their call, Confident in nothing, terrified they fall.
Did I beg for gifts or ask for your aid? Or seek liberation from the oppressor's blade?
"Teach me now, I’ll hold my peace and stand, Show me my error, help me understand."
Words of truth hold power, but yours miss the mark, You criticize words that fly in the dark.
"Would you gamble on orphans, sell your friend away? Look at me truly, I’ve got nothing to betray."
Let there be no injustice, return and see, Right is my cause, let truth set me free.
Is my tongue unjust, or do I speak in vain? Can I not taste what’s mischievous and plain?
Isn't life on earth like a hired hand’s plight? Days drag on like laborers longing for night.
I’m stuck with months of misery, can't seem to sleep, Toss and turn in the dark, the night not mine to keep.
My flesh is dressed in worms, my skin breaks anew, Days fly like a weaver’s swift shuttle, hope’s out of view.
Life's but a breath, soon you'll see me no more, Like a cloud that vanishes, gone to Sheol’s door.
No coming back home, home's now a ghost, Silent I won’t be, as my spirit's engrossed.
"Am I a sea monster, needing a guard? My bed offers comfort, but dreams hit me hard."
Terrified by visions, I choose death over breath, Loathe this life, just leave me alone, embrace death.
Why point me out, make me your concern, Visit each morning, test at every turn?
If I've sinned, tell me, O watcher of men, Why this burden, why this mark, again and again?
Pardon my faults, take my sins away, Soon I'll lie in dust, search all you may.
Bildad stepped in, ready to reply, "How long you gonna let those words fly by?
A mighty wind, that's all I hear, Does God twist justice? Nah, that's clear.
Kids sinned, they faced the cost, Handed to their deeds, the line they crossed.
Seek God hard, lay it down with might, If pure and upright, you'd find the light.
From small starts, you’d grow large, Inquire the past, let their wisdom charge.
Our days on earth, just a shadowy mix, Learn from the fathers, knowledge they fix.
Papyrus and rush, can't grow alone, Without mire and water, they ain't grown.
Green's the sight, not yet cut down, Withers faster than reeds in town.
Forget God, and your hopes will fade, Trust like a web, too easy frayed.
Lean on your house, it won’t stand tall, Cling hard as you might, it’ll still fall.
Sunshine green, shoots spread wide, Roots hug rock, where stones abide.
When uprooted, earth won't recall, From the ground, others will stand tall.
God won't cast the blameless aside, Evildoers? He ain't on their side.
Fill your mouth with laughter's cheer, Lips bursting with shouts sincere.
Haters dressed in shame's attire, The wicked's tent consumed by fire."
Job spoke up, feeling the weight, "How can man with God debate?
If He argues, who can reply? A thousand questions, no answer why.
Wise in heart, His strength's immense, Who defies Him, with no defense?
Mountains move, unaware they shift, Earth shakes, pillars lift.
He commands the sun, yet it stays, Seals the stars, dims their rays.
He alone treads the ocean's waves, Creates the constellations, none He saves.
Past finding out, His wonders soar, Marvels countless, forevermore.
He passes by, unseen, unknown, Who can stop Him, claim His throne?
His anger won't withdraw or fade, Even Rahab's helpers, dismayed.
How could I, a mortal, speak, When even righteousness feels weak?
Call and answer, still I doubt, In storms, He breaks me, inside and out.
Strength and justice, He defines, Righteousness, my word confines.
I am blameless, but life I scorn, Blameless perish, in God's storm.
Injustice reigns, judges blind, If not Him, then who's defined?
Life's swift, like runner's path, Eagles swoop, ships cut the wrath.
Forget my woes, put on a smile, Yet fear stalks me all the while.
Condemnation feels near at hand, Why labor in this barren land?
Snow and lye can't make me clean, In the ditch, my clothes demean.
He's not like man, a different breed, No umpire here to intercede.
Remove His rod, fear aside, Then I'd speak, with nothing to hide."
I'm weary of my soul, man, tired of this life, Gonna speak my pain, cut through like a knife.
To God, I cry, "Don't condemn me, show me why, Why you contend with me, make me want to die.
Is it good you oppress, despise what you've made, Smile on the wicked, like a twisted charade?
Do you see with eyes like a mortal man's gaze? Are your days like ours, passing in a haze?
You seek out my sins, iniquity you find, Though you know I'm clean, I'm trapped in this bind.
Your hands shaped me, framed every bone, Yet here I am, feeling so alone.
Remember, I'm clay, your creation, your plan, Will you turn me to dust, like the fate of a man?
Poured out like milk, curdled like cheese, Clothed in skin and bone, knit with such ease.
You gave life, kindness, preserved my soul, But kept your plans hidden, a mystery whole.
If I sin, you mark it, no forgiveness in sight, Wicked or righteous, my head can't take flight.
If I stand tall, you hunt me like a beast, Your power unleashed, never to cease.
Witnesses against me, your anger's no jest, Life's a battle, no peace, no rest.
Why was I born? Should've skipped this strife, Wished I’d gone from womb to grave, no life.
Aren't my days few? Give me a break, Let me find comfort before shadows take.
To the land of darkness, where no light shows, Where order's gone, only midnight knows."
Zophar steps up, ready to reply, "Should all those words just pass on by?
Should endless talk make you seem right? When you boast, should we stay quiet, not fight?
You claim you're pure, clean in sight, But oh, if God would speak, show His might!
He'd reveal wisdom, secrets in store, Much more than you've ever bargained for.
Can you grasp the mystery of God's plan? His heights and depths, beyond any man.
Higher than the heavens, deeper than the grave, Wider than the earth, broader than the waves.
If He acts, who can oppose His might? He sees the false, detects wrong in the night.
An empty mind grows wise, it's said, Like a wild donkey's colt, untamed, unled.
So set your heart, hands stretched to the sky, If wrong's in your grasp, cast it goodbye.
Then pure you'll stand, no need to fear, Your past like water, no longer near.
Life will shine brighter, clearer than noon, Darkness like morning, gone too soon.
Secure you'll rest, hope in your soul, Safe and sound, none will take control.
But the wicked's eyes will fail, they see, No escape, their hope's to cease to be."
Job stood up, voice strong and clear, "Y'all think you're wise, like wisdom's gonna disappear.
But I've got insight, I've got my own, I know what you know, I'm not alone.
I'm the punchline, though I call on the Lord, The righteous, the blameless, they get ignored.
To those at ease, misfortune's a joke, Ready to pounce on those who choke.
Robbers thrive, while provoking God's their game, Holding their idols, they feel no shame.
But check the animals, they'll teach you things, Birds in the sky, their wisdom sings.
Talk to the earth, it'll show you the way, Fish of the sea got plenty to say.
Who doesn’t see Yahweh's hand in all, Crafting life's breath, both great and small?
Doesn’t the ear test words like food, With age comes wisdom, that's understood.
With God there's wisdom and power with might, He breaks what’s built, locks you tight.
He dries the waters, or floods the ground, Strength and wisdom, endlessly profound.
Counselors stripped, judges turned to fools, Kings and their bonds, he adjusts the rules.
Priests stripped bare, the mighty fall, Trust and wisdom, he takes it all.
Princes shamed, the strong laid low, He uncovers shadows where secrets grow.
Nations rise, nations fall, Enlarge, destroy, he does it all.
Chiefs lose sight, they wander around, Stagger like drunks, their lost ground."
Behold, I've seen it all, heard it clear, What you know, I know, I'm not below, my dear.
I speak to the Almighty, that's my desire, But you're spinning lies, stoking no fire.
If you'd hold your tongues, you'd show some grace, Hear my plea, let my words take their place.
Will you speak for God with a deceitful tone? Show favoritism? Stand alone?
Will He not find you out when you deceive? His majesty, a force you can't perceive.
Your wise words turn to ashes in the breeze, Your defenses crumble, like clay with ease.
"Be silent, let me speak, bring whatever's due, Why risk my life, when I've got naught to pursue?"
He could kill me, hope fading to gray, Still, I'll stand my ground, come what may.
This will be my saving grace, No godless man shall see His face.
Listen close to what I declare, I hold my cause, my righteousness bare.
Who dares to challenge me? Stand and see, Then I'll be silent, spirit set free.
"Just spare me two things, then I'll have peace, Withdraw your hand, let the terror cease."
Call, and I'll answer, or let me speak, How many sins have I, so bleak?
Why hide your face, why make me an enemy? Chase a leaf, pursue dry stubble endlessly?
You've written bitterness, sins of the past, Bound my feet, marked my path fast.
I'm decaying, like a moth-eaten dress, A rotten thing, under stress.
Man born of woman, days so few, Full of troubles and struggles too. Like a flower, he blooms then falls, Shadows flee; heeds no calls.
Do You watch this fleeting breath? Judge him now or in his death? Clean from unclean, can it be made? Days are numbered, bounds are laid.
Let him rest till his work is done, Hope for the tree, when cut, it’s won. Roots may age, trunk may die, Water’s scent makes it rise high.
But man lies low, spirit flown, Waters dry, rivers moan. Man lies down, doesn’t rise, Till the heavens, new skies.
"Hide me, Lord, till wrath has passed, Set a time, remember at last. If he dies, will life restart? I’d wait for peace, for a new heart."
"You’d call, I’d reply, Your work—desired, no lie. Now you count each step I take, Watch my sins, each mistake."
Mountains fall, rocks move away, Water wears stones, dust is prey. Hope's destroyed, man departs, You change his face, torn apart.
Sons may rise, he doesn’t see, Brought low, no clarity. Pain in flesh, soul mourns within, Life’s brief tale, where to begin?
Eliphaz stepped up, with a question in his gaze, "Should a wise man talk nonsense, just a wind in a blaze?
Talk without purpose, speeches doing no good, You're throwing off fear, hindering your Godhood.
Your sins teach your tongue, crafty words you choose, Your own mouth condemns you, you just can't refuse.
Were you the first born, before the hills stood tall? Did you hear God's secrets, like you know it all?
What do you know that we don't understand? With us are the elders, gray heads in this land.
Is God's comfort too small? Are his words too light? Why's your heart flashing, setting God in your sight?
What is man to be pure, born of woman, to be right? He trusts not his holy ones, even heaven's not in his sight.
How much less a man, corrupt, drinking sin like water? Listen close now, let me show you the slaughter.
The wicked twists in pain, every day he cries, A terror in his ears, the destroyer never lies.
He doubts the light, waits for the sword, He searches for bread, darkness his reward.
Distress grabs him tight, like a king ready to fight, He's been proud against God, running blind in the night.

“Sing Zion's songs!” they taunted, voices loud, How could we sing Yahweh's song, feeling unbowed?
“If I forget Jerusalem,” I swore in pain, “May my right hand fail, may my skills wane.”
“Tongue to the roof, if I don't recall, Jerusalem above all, my greatest call.”
"Remember Edom's cry," when they cheered our fall, "Raze it to the ground!" their heartless call.
Babylon, oh Babylon, your time will come, Happy is he who repays, righting what's been done.
Joy for those who strike back, where pain had once been, In a world of harsh justice, against the unseen.
With my whole heart, I give thanks, no facade, Singing praises before the gods, my heart's applaud.
Bowing low toward your holy dome, Thanks for your Name, truth, and loving home.
Exalted high, your Word and Name do reign, When I call, you answer, strength in my soul, you sustain.
The kings of earth will join the praise, Heard your words, amazed in your holy blaze.
They'll sing of Yahweh's way, declare it grand, For Yahweh's glory spans across the land.
Though high and mighty, He sees the low, Proud from afar, but to the humble, close He'll show.
In trouble's midst, you revive my soul, Stretching your hand, making my enemies lose control.
Your right hand saves, my path you define, Forever kind, your love's divine.
Yahweh fulfills what concerns me, His plan, “Don't forsake the works of your hands,” is my stand.
Yahweh, you’ve searched, you know my game, From when I rise to when I came.
You see my thoughts from far away, You trace my steps and where I lay.
Words on my tongue, you know ‘em all, You hem me in, you make the call.

Where can I hide from your Spirit’s flight? From heaven to Sheol, you’re in my sight.
Wings of dawn, across the sea, Even there, your hand guides me.
If darkness tries to take its place, Still, you shine light and show your face.
In secret, knit in womb’s embrace, Your eyes saw me, your crafted space.
Fearfully, wonderfully, what you made, Your works I know, they don’t fade.
My frame you saw, in secret spun, Days written before there was one.
How precious, God, your thoughts, the sum, More than sand, when morning's come.
Kill the wicked, God, I plea, Bloodthirsty ones, don't let them see.
They speak against you with wicked aim, Enemies take your holy name.
I hate them, God, with perfect hate, Your foes and mine, they won’t relate.
Search my heart, know what I’ve got, Try my thoughts, see my plot.
See if wicked ways I tread, Lead me on your path instead.
Deliver me, Yahweh, from the evil crew, Protect me from violent men, what they might do. Plotting mischief deep in their hearts, Always gearing up, ready for war to start.
Tongues sharp as a serpent's bite, Viper's poison, they speak with spite. Yahweh, guard me from wicked hands, From violent schemes and their devious plans.
The proud set traps on my way, Cords of a net, hoping I'll stray. I called to Yahweh, "You're my God, my plea," Listen to my cries, Lord, hear and see.
Yahweh, my strength, my battle shield, You've covered my head, my protector in the field. "Don't grant the wicked their desires, Don't let them rise, fueled by their fires."
Let their own words bring them down, Burning coals on their heads, let them drown. Flames consume them, pits hold them tight, Let them never rise, lost in the night.

Surely the righteous will give thanks, In Your presence, the upright ranks.
Yo, I call on you, Yahweh, come fast to my plea, Listen to my voice as I call urgently.

"Our bones scattered like earth when it's torn," Yet my eyes on you, Yahweh, where refuge is sworn.
Keep me safe from traps they've set, From snares and plans in the dark net.

Deliver me from those who are too strong, Bring my soul out, where I feel I belong.
Thanks to your name, I’ll shout loud, I’ll sing, The righteous will surround, your goodness they'll bring.
Yo, Yahweh, hear my plea, listen to my cry, In your truth and justice, lift me high.
Don't judge me harsh, 'cause none can stand, In your sight, no living soul is grand.
The enemy's chasing, got my soul on the run, Crushing me low, like the grave's dark sun.

"Who is man," says Yahweh, "that I care for his frame? His life is but a breath, like a shadow, he came." Part the heavens, oh Yahweh, come down with might, Touch the mountains, let them smoke, burn bright.
Lightning strike and scatter them wide, Send your arrows, watch foes run and hide. Stretch your hand from above, rescue me, From the great waters, set me free.
Foreign tongues speak deceit, their words lie, Their right hand's falsehood, reaching for the sky. "I'll sing a new song," I declare to my King, On a ten-stringed lyre, praises I bring.
You give salvation to kings, David you save, Rescue me too, from the sword's deadly wave. Foreign hands deceitful, falsehood they boast, Deliverance I seek from this hostile coast.
Sons like nurtured plants, daughters like thrones, Stores full of provision, wealth overflows. Sheep in thousands grace our fields, Oxen strong, heavy loads they wield.
No breaking in, no cries in the street, Peace and joy where life’s complete. Happy are the people, in Yahweh they dwell, Blessings abound, hear the glad story we tell.
I'll lift you up, my God, my King, Praising your name, forever I'll sing.
Each day I'll raise a brand-new song, Forever your praises, all day long.
Great is Yahweh, beyond all measure, His greatness a vast, unsearchable treasure.
One generation to the next will tell, Of mighty acts that ring like a bell.
I'll think on your majesty, so grand, Your wondrous works, all you’ve planned.
They'll speak of your power, your awesome might, I'll declare your greatness, shining so bright.
The memory of your goodness will flow, With songs of righteousness, hearts aglow.
Yahweh is gracious, merciful, slow to ire, His loving kindness, a consuming fire.
Good to all, tender mercies abound, Over all his works, his love is found.
All your works will thank you, Yahweh, loud, Your saints will lift you, among the crowd.
They'll speak of glory, kingdom's power, Proclaiming your might in this very hour.
Your kingdom's everlasting, forever it stands, Your dominion throughout all lands.
Yahweh, faithful in word and deed, Upholds the fallen, meets their need.
Eyes look to you, for food you provide, You open your hand, and all are satisfied.
Righteous in ways, gracious in acts, Yahweh is near when truth attracts.
He fulfills desires of those with fear, Hearing their cries, he'll draw near.
Yahweh preserves all those who love, But destroys the wicked from above.
My mouth will praise Yahweh's fame, Let all bless his holy name.
Praise Yah! Let's shout and sing While I breathe, to Yahweh, my praises bring.
Trust not in princes, man-made schemes, Their spirits depart, vanish like dreams.
Happy the one with Jacob's God at his side, Hope in Yahweh, a trusted guide.
He created the heavens, earth, and seas, Keeps truth forever, sets captives free.
He feeds the hungry, raises the low, Opens blind eyes, lets justice flow.
Yahweh loves the righteous, strong and true, Lifts the fallen, supports them too.
He preserves the stranger, protects those alone, Turns the wicked's path, like a rolling stone.
Yahweh reigns eternal, no end in sight, Praise Yah forever, shine His light!
Praise Yah, it's good to sing, lift your voice to the King, Jerusalem's built, outcasts He'll bring,
He heals the hearts that are broken, no lie, Counts all the stars, calls each by the sky,
Mighty and great, His power and mind, Upholds the humble, the wicked He'll find,
Sing to Yahweh, thank Him with song, Clouds in the sky, rain where it belongs,
Grass on the mountains, food for the beasts, Ravens He feeds, for them He'll release,
Strength of a horse, not His delight, Those who fear Him, bring Him sight,
Jerusalem, Zion, lift your praise high, Strengthened your gates, children nearby,
Peace within borders, wheat finest of all, His word on the earth, swiftly it calls,
Snow like wool, frost like the ash, Hail like pebbles, cold with a crash,
He sends His word, melts them away, Winds blow, waters flow, all in His sway,
His word to Jacob, laws for His own, No other nation, His ordinances shown,
Praise Yah, in all that you say!
Praise Yah from the skies so high, Angels and armies, echo the cry.
Sun and moon, stars that gleam, Heavens above, join the theme.
"Let 'em praise my name," Yahweh said, He spoke the word, the world was spread.
He set the rules, they'll never sway, Fixed them firm, night and day.
From the earth, to the depths below, Sea creatures, storms that blow.
Mountains tall, hills that rise, Trees with fruit, cedar skies.
Wild beasts, livestock, birds in flight, All creation, day and night.
Kings and people, princes, judges, too, Young and old, join the view.
"Let 'em praise my name," Yahweh's claim, His name's exalted, above all fame.
His glory’s high, beyond earth and sky, He lifts his people, reaching high.
"Raise the horn, let saints proclaim, Israel's near, praise my name."
Praise Yah, let the chorus ring, To the heavens, let praises cling.
Sing to Yahweh, a song that's brand new, In the saints' assembly, His praise rings true.
Let Israel dance for the One who made, Children of Zion, in joy they're arrayed.
Praise His name with dance, tambourine, and harp, Yahweh delights, salvation's His art.
The humble He crowns, in glory they stand, Saints sing for joy, His will they command.
High praises of God in their mouths they wield, A two-edged sword in their hands revealed.
Vengeance on nations, punishments they bring, Kings in chains, nobles bound under wing.
Judgment written, executed with might, Saints in honor, bask in His light.
Praise Yahweh! Let His glory resound, In righteousness, His people are found.
Praise Yah, in His holy place, In the sky for His mighty grace.
Praise His acts, mighty and grand, His greatness stretches across the land.
Blow the trumpet, let it ring, Harp and lyre, let praises sing.

Cymbals crash, loud and strong, Resounding cymbals join the song.
Let all with breath lift their voice, Praise Yah, let the earth rejoice!
Solomon speaks, son of David's line, Wisdom and knowledge, both divine.
Learn the ways of justice and right, For the young and simple, bring insight.
Wise folks listen, grow their brain, Understanding deepens, like the rain.
"The fear of Yahweh starts it all," While fools ignore wisdom's call.
"My son, heed your father's creed, Mom's teachings, let them lead.
A crown of grace upon your head, Chains of honor where you're led.
If sinners say, 'Come join our ride,' Stand firm, don’t step to their side.
If they plot to spill blood, lie in wait, Avoid their path, don't take the bait.
Their feet rush to evil, a wicked race, But it’s their own lives they disgrace.
Greed for gain, it snatches life, Cuts like a knife, brings strife."
Wisdom shouts in the street's loud hum, In the city gates, she says, "Come!
How long, simple ones, will you love the plain? Turn to me, break free from the chain.
I've called you out, yet none would heed, So laugh I will, when you’re in need.

Hate knowledge, ignore the divine, Eat the fruits of your own design.
Fools' ease leads to their demise, But those who listen, they’re the wise.

Listen up, if you take these words, plant them deep in your soul, Tune your ear to wisdom, make understanding your goal.
Cry out for insight, raise your voice to the sky, Seek wisdom like silver, search for her, don't pass by.

Her house leads to the grave, her path's a one-way track, No one returns from her hold, no one's coming back.

Yo, my son, don't forget what I teach, hold it tight, Keep my commands in your heart, day and night.

"Trust in Yahweh with all your soul, Don't lean on your thoughts, let Him make you whole."

"But don't think you're wise in your own eyes, Fear Yahweh, depart from lies."
It'll be health to your body, bones made strong, Honor Yahweh with your wealth, and you can't go wrong.

For Yahweh corrects the ones He loves, Just like a father's gentle shoves.
Happy is the one who finds wisdom’s prize, Her worth's beyond silver, gold, or skies.
More precious than rubies, she stands tall, Her riches and honor, in her hands, call.
Her paths are peace, pleasant every way, She's a tree of life, hold tight, don’t sway.
By wisdom, Yahweh formed the earth we see, Understanding holds the heavens, wild and free.
"Let wisdom and discretion never leave your sight, They'll be life to your soul, grace in your light."
Walk secure, never stumble on your track, When you lie down, sweet sleep has your back.
Don't fear sudden dread, nor wicked’s fall, Yahweh's your confidence, He hears your call.
"Don’t withhold good when it's in your hand, To neighbors, be kind, understand."
Don't scheme against those who trust you near, Don't fight without reason, keep your conscience clear.
Don't envy violence or choose its path, Yahweh's with the righteous, but the wicked face wrath.
He mocks the mockers, gives grace to the meek, The wise gain glory, fools face defeat.
Yo, listen up, sons, hear your father’s sound, Pay attention 'cause wisdom is what’s going down.
I was once a child, my father’s pride, Tender in my mother’s sight, love amplified.
He said, “Keep my words, let 'em sink in your heart, Hold tight to my teachings, let life truly start."
“Get wisdom, get understanding, don’t you forget, Stick to my words, they’re the best you’ll ever get."
“Don’t let wisdom go, she’ll guard your way, Love her deeply, she’ll keep you every day.”
“Wisdom is key, no matter the price, She’ll lift you up, make your life nice."
“She’ll crown your head with splendor and grace, Embrace her; you’ll find honor in her embrace."
Hear me, my son, take in these sayings, Long life’s the reward, with wisdom’s displaying.
I’ve shown you the straight paths to tread, In your walk, you'll never be misled.
Run with freedom, stumble you won’t, Hold instruction tight, let her go, you don’t.
Shun the path of wicked, don’t even glance, Turn away quick, don’t give evil a chance.
They don’t sleep 'til they’ve done some wrong, Their bread's wickedness, violence's their song.
But the righteous path, it’s like dawn's light, It shines brighter ’til day becomes bright.
The wicked’s way is shadowed in dark, They stumble blind, never hitting the mark.
“My son, my words, keep them close, In your heart, let them be the most."
“They’re life and health to the body and soul, Guard your heart; it makes you whole."
“Avoid perverse talk, let your lips be true, Keep focused, let your gaze cut through."
“Make your path level, keep it straight, Don’t turn aside, steer clear from hate."
"Remove your foot from evil's track, Stay on course, never look back.”
Listen up, son, hear my wisdom call, Tune your ears, don't let knowledge fall.
An adulteress's lips drip honey so sweet, But her end is bitter, sharp as a sword's deceit.
Her steps lead down to the grave, Crooked paths she won't save.
So heed my words, don't stray away, Keep far from her, don’t be led astray.
Or you'll lose honor to those who deceive, Years lost to cruelty, wealth they thieve.
You'll groan at the end, body worn and torn, "Why did I hate wisdom, why did I scorn?"
"I ignored my teachers, their words I defied, Now here I stand, on ruin's side."
Drink from your own well, let it flow, Keep it yours, let no others know.
Bless your spring, joy in your youth's bride, Her love's a treasure, with her abide.
Why chase the allure of another's snare? Yahweh sees all, beware of despair.
Wicked deeds ensnare, sins tightly bind, Without instruction, he's lost in his mind.
In folly's shadow, astray he'll stay, Lost and wandering, far from the way.
If you pledged for your neighbor, struck hands in a deal, You’re trapped by your words, caught in what you feel.
Listen up, son, get out of this snare, Run to your neighbor, lay it all bare.
No sleep for your eyes, keep them awake, Escape like a gazelle, quick moves you must make.
Look to the ant, lazy one, be wise, No boss, yet in summer her food she supplies.
How long will you sleep? When will you rise? A nap here, a nap there, poverty in disguise.
A rogue with a perverse mouth, causes pain, Winks his eye, signals feet, motions are plain.
Evil in his heart, discord he sows, Sudden calamity, that’s how it goes.
Six things the Lord hates, seven revile, Prideful eyes, false tongues, hands blood-stained vile.
Scheming hearts, quick feet to do wrong, False witness and discord, they don’t belong.
Son, heed your dad’s command, don’t stray, Mom’s teaching guides you every day.
Keep them close to your heart, tie them tight, When you walk, sleep, or wake, they’re your light.
Commands are lamps, laws shine bright, To guard you from danger in the night.
Beware the smooth words of a wife astray, Her beauty’s trap, don’t fall, walk away.
A harlot’s price is a crumb of bread, She hunts lives while leading them to dread.
Can fire be held without burning clothes? Walk on coals, escape unscathed, who knows?
Touch your neighbor’s wife, pay the price, Punishment follows, heed this advice.
Steal to eat, folks understand, But when caught, return sevenfold from your hand.
Adultery lacks sense, destroys your soul, Wounds and disgrace take their toll.
Jealousy’s fury, husband’s rage, No ransom will soothe, no gift will engage.
"Listen up, my son, keep my words tight, "Keep my commands for life, guard them in your sight.
"Wrap them on your fingers, like ties that don't part, "Etch them deep, write on the tablet of your heart.
"Call wisdom your sister, understanding your kin, "They'll guard you from strangers, from seductive sin.
From my window, looking through the lattice wide, I saw a young man, lacking sense, from his stride.
He passed near her corner, by her house he crept, In twilight's shadow, into darkness he stepped.
There she met him with attire of deceit, Loud, defiant, roaming every street.
She caught him, kissed him, brazen face, "Peace offerings are mine, I’ve found my place.
"I came to meet you, sought you with care, "My couch is ready, with tapestries rare.
"Perfumed with myrrh, aloes, and spice, "Let's revel till morning, in love we'll entice.
"My man’s not home, gone on his way, "With money in hand, he'll return another day."
Her words were smooth, her trap was set, He followed her path, without regret.
Like an ox to the slaughter, a fool to his fall, An arrow in his liver, unaware of it all.
Now sons, listen, heed my call, Don’t walk her path, don't let your heart stall.
Many are wounded, mighty her slain, Her house leads to Sheol, paths of death's domain.
Wisdom's crying out, she's raising her voice loud, On high places, crossroads, she's drawing a crowd. At the city gates, by the entry doors she stands, Shouting to the people, reaching out her hands.
"I call to you, men! My voice to mankind, Simple ones, get wise! Fools, open your mind! Hear me speak excellent things, truth from my lips, Wickedness I shun, no deception in my scripts.

Every word I speak, in righteousness it flows, Plain to the understanding, clear to those who know. Take my instruction over silver, my knowledge over gold, Wisdom beats rubies, can't be bought or sold.
I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, find knowledge and taste, Hate evil and pride, leave arrogance and waste. Counsel and sound knowledge belong to me, Kings reign by my power, ruling righteously.
I love those who love me, seek and you'll find, Riches and honor, prosperity of the kind. My fruit's better than gold, my yield's choice and rare, I walk the path of justice, distributing fair share.

Yahweh owned me in the beginning, before the earth's dawn, From everlasting, before the world was on. When depths were empty, I was there, when springs weren't born, Before mountains and hills, before fields of corn.
When he set the heavens' circle, I stood beside, Clouds formed above, deep waters abide. Sea's boundary he gave, earth's foundations laid, I was there, his craftsman, in delight I stayed.

Rejoicing always in his world, sons of men my joy, Now listen, my sons, blessed are those who deploy, Hear instruction, be wise, don't turn away, Blessed is the one who hears, by my gates they'll stay.

Find me and find life, Yahweh's favor they’ll see, But sin against me, harms the soul, not free. Those who hate me love death, choosing the wrong course, Wisdom calls you still, listen to the source."
Wisdom’s got a house built, pillars stand tall, Carved seven strong, she’s got it all.
Meat’s prepared, the wine mixed fine, Table’s set, ready for dining time.
Maidens sent, voices on high, Calling from the city's sky:
“Simple ones, come inside, Turn here, let wisdom be your guide.”
“Eat my bread, drink my wine, Leave your past, walk in line.”
Correct a mocker, you’ll get scorn, Reprove the wicked, face their storm.
But tell a wise one, they’ll love you, Teach the righteous, their learning’s new.
"Fear of Yahweh starts it all, Understanding stands tall."
By wisdom, your life extends, Years multiply, no pretend.
Wise or mock, it’s yours to own, Bear your burden all alone.
The foolish woman, loud and proud, Undisciplined, she draws a crowd.
Sitting high, she calls out loud, To those passing by in the crowd:
“Simple ones, come right here, Empty minds, don’t you fear.”
“Stolen water, sweet as can be, Secret food, pleasures you’ll see.”
But spirits linger in her hall, Her guests in Sheol, they fall.

Righteous mouths, springs of life they provide, While the wicked speak violence, can't hide.
Hatred stirs conflict, love heals all, Wisdom on lips, the foolish fall.
Lay up your knowledge, wise men do, Foolish mouths near ruin, they lack the clue.
Rich man's wealth, his city strong, Poverty's the poor's destruction song.

Righteous tongue, choice silver shines, Wicked hearts, worth little, no refined lines.
Lips of the righteous feed many, they thrive, Foolish lack understanding, fail to survive.
Yahweh's blessing brings wealth, trouble's none, Foolish love wickedness, wisdom's understanding won.
Wicked fears will find them, righteous desires met, Whirlwind takes the wicked, righteous stand yet.
Vinegar to teeth, smoke to eyes, Sluggard's a burden, leaves sender’s cries.
Fear Yahweh, lengthen days, Wicked years shorten, their hope decays.
Righteous joy, their hope a stronghold, Wicked ways destruct, as truth is told.
Righteousness stands firm, they won't be moved, The wicked will fall, their place disproved.

When the wicked die, their hopes all fade, Expectations of power quickly degrade.
The righteous escape, trouble sheds its weight, While the wicked end up in their place of fate.
The godless mouth can destroy a friend, But the righteous with knowledge will defend.
When the righteous prosper, the city's glad, But when the wicked fall, cheers are had.
The upright's blessing lifts a town high, The wicked's words bring it down to die.

Gossip betrays like a serpent's hiss, But a trustworthy spirit keeps secrets amiss.

Collateral for strangers brings pain and woe, Those who refuse find security, though.
