Grabbing a dog’s ears, meddling in fights that aren’t their own, Madmen shoot flames, then claim, "Just a joke!" as deception’s throne.
No wood, no fire; no gossip, peace will conspire, Contentious tongues kindling strife, whispers dig deeper, inspire.
Silver gloss on clay pots, fervent lips, yet hearts of rot, Charming speech hides evils deep, deception sewn in the plot.
"Don’t believe the charming voice, seven abominations hide," Malice wrapped in deceit, in public, evil can't abide.
Dig a pit, fall in it; roll a stone, watch it roll back home, Lying tongues breed hate’s tone, and flattery leads to ruin alone.
Don't boast about tomorrow, you don't know the deal, What a day's gonna bring, it's hidden, it's real.
Let another man praise you, not your own lips, Strangers speak for you, let your pride take a dip.
A stone's heavy, sand weighs you down, But a fool's irritation is the heaviest crown.
Wrath's cruel, anger’s a storm, But jealousy, who's gonna weather that form?
Better with a rebuke that's open and clear, Than love that's hidden, nowhere near.
A friend’s wounds are faithful, let them sting, While enemy kisses might mean something.
A full soul loathes the honeycomb’s touch, But to the hungry, bitter’s never too much.
A bird leaves its nest, a man his home, Wandering, wondering, no place to roam.
Perfume and incense bring joy profound, Like a friend’s counsel, a treasure found.
Don't leave your friends or kin behind, Stay close, not just through bloodlines.
Be wise, my child, fill my heart with pride, So I can face my foes, nothing to hide.
A wise man sees danger, takes to his feet, The simple walk on, only to meet defeat.
Take his coat when he pledges for another, Hold tight when he's tangled with a wayward lover.
Bless your neighbor too loud, early at dawn, He’ll take it the wrong way, like a curse drawn.
Drip, drip of rain, contentious wife’s bane, Like grabbing the wind, slipping oil in vain.
Iron sharpens iron, face to face, A friend’s countenance, in that space.
Tend the fig tree, eat the fruit you grow, Serve the master, honor will flow.
Water reflects face, heart mirrors man, Sheol's never filled, neither is man's plan.
Silver's in the crucible, gold feels the heat, A man’s refined by praise, a lesson complete.
Grind a fool with grain, pestle in hand, His foolishness sticks, won’t leave the land.
Know your flocks, check your herd’s health, Riches fade, crowns don't guarantee wealth.
Hay's removed, new growth will come, Grasses gathered, plenty for some.
Lambs for clothing, goats for the field, Goat's milk flows, family's meal is sealed.
The wicked run off with no one in chase, But the righteous stand bold, lions in their place.
Rebels crown rulers, chaos their fate, Yet knowledge and wisdom keep order straight.
The poor man oppressing, like rain that won't stop, Leaves the fields barren, no food in the crop.
Abandon the law, and wicked you praise, Keep it strong, and justice you raise.
Evil's blind to justice, lost in the night, Seek Yahweh, and you'll find the light.
Integrity trumps riches, better to be poor, Than twisted in wealth, lost at the core.
Wise sons follow law, not gluttons' delight, Bringing shame to fathers, it's not right.
Wealth that grows from greed, what a trap, Goes to those who help, bridging the gap.
Close your ears to the law, your prayers go unheard, Injustice leads astray, with every word.
The blameless walk straight, they inherit the good, While traps catch the wicked, misunderstood.
The rich think they're wise, but can't fool the poor, For understanding sees through, wisdom galore.
When righteous win, it's glory aflame, In wicked rise, men hide in shame.
Conceal your sins, no prosper you'll find, Confess and renounce, mercy's not blind.
Blessed is the one who walks with fear, Harden your heart, and trouble draws near.
A wicked ruler's a roaring lion, People are helpless, in fear they're cryin'.
Tyrants lack judgment, but those against ill-gain, Their days will be long, without any pain.
A fugitive of blood, tormented till death, No support to find, till their last breath.
Walk blameless, and safety you'll embrace, But perverse ways lead to a fall from grace.
Work your land, food will abound, Chasing fantasies, poverty's ground.
Faithful and blessed, no riches to chase, Hunger for wealth, leads to disgrace.
Partiality's wrong, for bread men will fall, Stingy and hasty, poverty will call.
Rebuke with truth, find favor and grace, Flattery falls flat, leaves no trace.
Robbing parents, claiming no wrong, Partners with destruction, they belong.
Greedy hearts stir strife, while trust brings peace, Yahweh prospers those who find release.
Trust in yourself, end up the fool, Walk in wisdom, and be kept cool.
Give to the poor, and lack you'll not know, Close your eyes, curses will show.
Wicked rise, men hide away, When they fall, the righteous sway.

When you’re rebuked and stay stiff, watch out, my friend, Destruction comes quick with no remedy to mend. Righteous folks bring joy, people cheer, they thrive, But with wicked rulers, folks barely survive.
Love wisdom, make your father beam with pride, But waste it all, and you’ll be left high and dry. A king with justice keeps the land secure, But bribes tear down the house, that’s for sure.

Flattering words lay traps, keep your wits keen, The evil get caught, while the righteous stay serene. The righteous seek justice, care for the poor, But the wicked stay blind, needing more, more, more.

Mockers cause trouble, but the wise make things right, In court, fools rage, lacking peace, no insight. Bloodthirsty folks hate the upright with might, While fools vent their anger, wise men hold it tight.
When rulers heed lies, wickedness spreads far, Both rich and poor see life through His bar. A fair king for the poor, his throne stands tall, Correct with the rod, avoid the shameful call.
Wickedness rises, but sin meets its end, Correct your son; peace and joy he’ll send. No revelation, chaos breaks loose, But laws bring blessings, a strong truce.
Words won't teach a servant who won't heed, Hasty words outpace fools, planting a bad seed. Raise a servant well, watch him shine, Angry folks stir strife, in sin they entwine.
Pride drags you down, humility brings grace, Befriend a thief, your soul's in a bad place. Fear's a trap, trust in Yahweh, be safe, Justice comes from Him, not man's embrace.
The wicked despise the upright's way, The righteous detest the wicked each day.
Yo, Agur speaks, his words unfold, To Ithiel and Ucal, stories bold. He claims no wisdom, says he's blind, Never grasped the Holy kind.
"Who ascends to heaven, then comes down? Who grips the wind, makes the waters drown? Who laid the earth from end to end? Tell me his name, the name he'll send."
"Every word of God, pure as gold, A shield to those in His hold. Don't twist His words, don't add lies, Or He’ll call you out, no disguise."
"Two things I seek, don't pass me by, Before my last breath, before I die. Keep lies and falsehoods far away, Give neither wealth nor empty tray.
Lest I be full, forget His name, Or steal in shame, and bring Him blame." "Don’t slander a servant, beware the curse, Or guilt will trap you, things get worse.
A generation that curses sires, Eyes so lofty, stoking fires. Pure they think, yet drenched in sin, Swords for teeth, they grin and win."
"The leech cries 'Give,' never enough, Four things crave, always tough: Sheol, a womb bare and dry, Thirsty earth, fire reaching high."
"Mock your dad, disobey your mom, Ravens feast, young eagles come." "Three amaze, four perplex my mind: Eagle, serpent, ship, man with a kind.
An adulterous woman, sneaky game, Eats, wipes her mouth, feels no shame." "Three things make earth shake with fear, Four it can't bear, let me make it clear:
Servant as king, a full fool's might, An unloved wife's wedding night. Four small, yet wisdom they claim: Ants store food, hydrax seek rock’s fame.
Locusts, no king, yet advance strong, Lizards in palaces, where they belong." "Three march proud, four walk with grace, Lion's roar, greyhound's pace.
Male goat's stride, king's command, None dare rise, none dare stand. Lift your pride, think evil and loud, Cover your mouth, don’t be proud.
As milk churns butter, nose yields blood, Wrath forced too far, brings a flood."
"Oh my son, my womb's delight, Don't give your strength to places that fight.
A king should know, don't sip that wine, Don't let it blur that justice line.
Give strong drink to the perishing, they're the ones, Let them forget the trouble that runs.
Open your mouth for those with no voice, Judge fair, be the needy’s choice.
Now, who can find a woman worth it all, Priceless like rubies, she stands tall.
Her husband trusts, gains in her embrace, She does good, no harm, sets the pace.
Seeks wool and flax, eagerly she works, Like merchant ships, her duty never shirks.
She rises while it's still dark, Feeds her house, ignites the spark.
Considers fields, buys them on sight, Plants a vineyard, her future's bright.
Strength on her waist, arms so strong, Her merchandise is good, all night long.
Hands on the spindle, she spins the thread, To the poor, her kindness is spread.
Snow? She's not afraid, her house is clad, In scarlet, in warmth, nothing's sad.
With tapestry, she decks her space, Fine linen and purple, her style, her grace.
Her husband sits with the elders, proud, Gate-respected, in the crowd.
Linen garments she crafts and sells, Sashes to merchants, her tale tells.
Strength and dignity, her attire's gleam, She laughs at the future, her dream.
Wisdom flows when she opens her mouth, Kindness and truth, her path, her south.
Her home she watches, no idle bread, Her children rise, in blessings they're fed.
"Many do noble things," her husband calls, "But you excel, you stand them all."
Charm deceives, beauty's vain array, But she who fears Yahweh earns praise today.
Give her the fruit her hands have made, Let her works in the gates never fade."
The Preacher speaks, son of a king's decree, "Vanity of vanities, all's vanity," said he.
What does man gain from working under the sun's heat? Generations come and go, but earth's still on its beat.
The sun rises and sets, racing back to its start, The wind turns south, then north, a never-ending art.
Rivers flow to the sea, yet the sea's never filled, Round they go, their courses, as the Maker willed.
All things bring weariness, beyond what words can say, Eyes never satisfied, ears hear all day.
What has been will be again; nothing new on this ground, "See, it's new!"—but it's just the same old sound.
No memory of the past, nothing lasts in the mind, What comes won't be remembered by those who follow behind.
I, the Preacher, once a king, sought wisdom's heavy toll, A burden God has given to weigh upon man's soul.
I've seen all under the sun, it’s chasing after breeze, What's crooked can't be straightened, lacking can't appease.
I said, "I've gained wisdom above all, above the rest, Wisdom and knowledge have filled my chest."
Yet knowing madness and folly, I found it all wind's play, For with much wisdom comes grief, sorrow grows each day.
I said to myself, "Come on, let's test with glee, Enjoying pleasure—but it's just vanity."
Laughter’s just foolish, mirth has no gain, I searched for joy, for my heart to sustain.
Wine to cheer, yet wisdom my guide, I sought folly's lure, to see what's inside.
Built mighty works, houses tall and grand, Planted vineyards, works of my own hand.
Gardens and parks, trees in lines, Pools of water, forests in design.
Servants aplenty, born in my space, Herds and flocks, riches embraced.
Silver and gold, treasures amassed, Singers and music, pleasures that last.
I grew great, more than all before, In wisdom I stood, but wanted more.
What my eyes desired, I didn’t refrain, Joy in labor, my heart's domain.
But all my works, they were vanity’s thread, Chasing the wind, no profit ahead.
I turned to wisdom, madness, and folly, What’s new for kings? It’s all melancholy.
Wisdom's light beats folly's dark, Yet both meet the same end, life's stark.
"As fools go, so will I," I said in my soul, Wisdom’s just vanity, a never-ending toll.
The wise and the fool, both forgotten in time, Death takes all, erasing the climb.
Life turned bitter, work under the sun, Vanity chased, nothing won.
I hated my toil, left to another, Who knows if he'll be wise or blunder?
It's all in vain, labor for naught, Despair in my heart, at what I've wrought.
Wise labor leaves for fools to gain, It's vanity, a great evil's claim.
What’s left for man, from toil's race? Sorrows by day, hearts at night misplaced.
Best to eat, drink, enjoy what you do, This I saw, it's from God, true.
Who can enjoy more than me? God gives wisdom, joy, generously.
To the sinner, work with no end, Passing to those who God befriends.
It's all vanity, a wind-chasing game, Yet from God's hand, the joys came.
There's a season for all, a time to live and die, Time to plant seeds and then reach for the sky. A time to break, a time to mend, A time to tear down, a time to build again.
Time to cry, let the tears flow, Time to laugh, let the good times show. Dance in the sunlight, mourn in the night, Gather your stones, or toss them from sight.
Embrace your loved ones, then let go, Seek what's lost, or let it blow. Keep it close, or throw it away, Silence your mouth, or have your say.
Love's got a time, hate's got one too, War might come, but peace can break through. What's the point of all this toil? I've seen the burdens, felt the soil.
God's made it all beautiful, right on time, Placed eternity in hearts, yet left us blind. Rejoice and do good, as long as you live, Eat, drink, enjoy—the gifts He gives.
What God does stands forever, unchanged, Nothing added, nothing rearranged. Time's been and gone, and here it comes again, Justice tarnished, even where it should reign.
I thought, "God will judge the good and bad, Every work, every purpose that we've ever had." In my heart I said, we're tested like beasts, All share breath, all life will cease.
Dust to dust, we all return, Who can tell where spirits yearn? So I saw, better to find joy in your toil, For who knows what the future will spoil?
I looked and saw oppression done under the sun, Tears of the oppressed—comfort there was none. The oppressors held power, their grip was tight, Yet no comforter for the ones in fright.
I praised the dead, more peaceful in their rest, Than the living who still face life's cruel test. Better yet, is he who's not seen the day, Evil under the sun, kept far away.
Labor and envy fill a man's plight, It's all vanity, chasing wind in flight. The fool folds hands, ruins himself with ease, Better quietness, than labor without peace.
Vanity again, beneath the sun's glow, One stands alone with no son, no bro. "Why do I toil, soul left to deprive?" Such misery, no joy kept alive.
Two together, stronger than one, Good reward for labor, when work is done. If one falls, the other lifts him high, Alone he falls, no help nigh.
Two lying close, warmth they gain, One alone, cold's bitter reign. Together they stand, against one they fight, Threefold cord, strong and tight.
Better a poor youth, wise in his way, Than a foolish king, stubborn in sway. Out of prison, came to reign, Born poor, yet broke the chain.
I saw all living, under the sun's span, With the youth who led, the young man. No end to people, they followed in mass, But future forgot him—vanity's glass.
Step with care, you approach God's place, Listen close, don’t rush to state your case. Keep your words few, let them be wise, God’s in heaven, where your thoughts rise.
Dreams come with worry, words with a fool, Vow to God, follow through, that's the rule. Better not to vow, than vow and forget, Don't let your mouth lead to regret.
Don’t cry mistake to the messenger’s face, Why provoke God, and wreck your place? In dreams and talk, vanity is found, But fear God, let reverence abound.
See the poor oppressed, justice stolen, Don’t be shocked, hierarchy’s holdin’. The earth’s for all, from king to field, To the worker, its bounty shall yield.
Love silver? You’ll never have enough, Chase abundance, find vanity tough. More goods, more mouths to feed, What’s left for the owner’s need?
Labor’s sleep is sweet, rich man’s not, Wealth guards harm, riches rot. Riches lost, a son with none, Naked he came, naked he’s gone.
Toil for the wind, what gain is there? Dark days, frustration, sickness, despair. What’s good is simple, eat, drink, rejoice, In work’s fruits, make the choice.
Riches and joy, gifts from above, God fills your heart with love. Forget past days, let joy’s song start, God keeps your soul with joy in your heart.
Under the sun, a burden so heavy to see, Riches and honor, yet no power to be free.
A man has it all, but can't take a bite, An outsider feasts, in the dead of night.
Vanity calls, an evil disease, A man with no joy, no soul at ease.
Father a hundred, live long and proud, But an empty soul, no burial shroud.
"Better the child who never saw light, Than a man with years, yet no delight."
Born in vanity, departs in the dark, Never seen the sun, no lasting mark.
Thousand years lived, but no joy found, Doesn't all end in the same ground?
Working for food, the appetite unfed, Wise or foolish, still chasing bread.
"Eyes see the real, desires stray wide, It's vanity, wind-chasing, no place to hide."
Names given long ago, man known true, Can't fight the mighty, it's nothing new.
"Words spin vanity, what does it gain? Life's a shadow, all the same."
Who knows what's good in life's brief span? Who can tell what follows for any man?
A name that rings true is better than scent, And death's sweet release over birth's first event.
Better to mourn where the hearts can see, Than feast in the house of false ecstasy.
Sorrow's face, though it may seem rough, Shapes the heart, makes it good enough.
The wise dwell where mourning is found, Fools dance where laughter's the sound.
Hear the rebuke from the wise, take the cue, Not the fool's song that's empty and untrue.
Like crackling thorns beneath a pot, Foolish laughter's all for naught.
Extortion makes the wise man fall, A bribe takes understanding's call.
Better an end than to start with pride, Patience is better with nothing to hide.
Quick to anger, avoid that trap, It rests with fools, it's a clumsy wrap.
Don't question the past with a mind so tight, It's not wise to say, "The past was right."
Wisdom, like wealth, offers defense, But knowledge preserves with common sense.
Consider God's work, who's straightens His ways? Crooked or straight, it's His mighty gaze.
Joy in good times, consider in pain, Both sides He made, like sunshine and rain.
Seen it all in my vain days, Righteous perish, wicked live in their ways.
Don't overdo righteousness or wisdom's role, Why destroy yourself or lose control?
Avoid wickedness, don't play the fool, Why die too soon, breaking the rule?
Hold on to this, but don't let go of that, Fear God and rise from where you're at.
Wisdom's strength is tenfold in the wise, More than rulers beneath the skies.
No one on earth is perfectly just, All have sinned, betrayed their trust.
Don't heed each word that's spoken around, Lest you hear curses where none should sound.
Knowing you've cursed just as much, In your heart, you've felt that touch.
Tried wisdom, sought its grace, But it drifted to a distant place.
Deep and far, wisdom hides its face, The scheme of things, a complex space.
Turned and sought to know what's true, Wickedness is folly, madness too.
A woman's snares, more bitter than death, Traps like chains, stealing breath.
"Behold I've found this," the Preacher said, A thousand men, not a woman in thread.
God made man upright, pure and clean, Yet they search for schemes unseen.
Who’s like the wise, who sees it clear? A wise man’s face shines, loses fear.
"Keep the king's command," I say, You swore it to God, don’t stray.
Don’t rush out, don’t do wrong, The king’s word is law, it’s strong.
His command keeps you from harm, The wise know time’s gentle charm.
There’s a time for each endeavor, Though man’s burden’s heavy forever.
He can’t foresee what’s ahead, No one knows what will be said.
No power over spirit’s flight, Can’t control death’s final night.
War gives no sweet release, Wickedness won’t bring peace.
I’ve seen the wicked laid low, From holy to forgotten, they go.
Evil punished slow, hearts grow cold, Men set on sin, bold and old.
Sinners live long, crimes in scores, But those who fear God, He restores.
The wicked, days shadowed, brief, They lack God’s fear, find no relief.
Righteous suffer, wicked enjoy, Vanity plays with man, like a toy.
So I say, find joy in your days, Eat, drink, work in God’s ways.
I sought wisdom day and night, The labor of earth was in my sight.
God's work is vast, hidden from man, Though he seeks, finds whatever he can.
The wise think they know the plan, But God’s work, they can’t understand.
I laid it down, straight to my heart, Righteous and wise, their works play a part. In God's hand, they’re held tight, Love or hate, who can see that light?
Same event hits all, righteous or wicked, Good and clean, or those unpicked. Sacrificer or not, they face the same fate, Good and sinner both meet their date.
Under the sun, one evil remains, Madness in hearts, breaking the chains. Alive, there's hope, even for the least, A living dog, better than a dead beast.
The living know their end's in sight, The dead, forgotten, out of the light. Love and hate, gone from their mind, No more share in what they left behind.
So go, eat your bread, drink with delight, God’s accepted your work in His sight. Wear white, keep your head anointed, Live joyfully, love appointed.
Whatever you find, do it strong and right, For in Sheol, there’s no work, no light. I saw races not won by the swift, Battles not claimed by the strong in the lift.
Time and chance, they trip us all, Like fish in a net, or birds that fall. Wisdom I saw, shining so bright, A poor man's wisdom saved through the night.
Though wise words are quiet, they’re better than shouts, Better wisdom than war, no doubts. Yet one wrong, destroys much that's good, In the silence, wisdom should.
Dead flies in perfume make it stink bad, A little folly outweighs wisdom you had.
A wise heart's on the right, fool's on the left side, Walking the road, the fool's foolishness can't hide.
If the ruler's spirit rises, stay calm, hold your space, Gentleness can lay offenses to rest in their place.
I've seen an evil under the sun, Errors from rulers that can't be undone.
Folly high on a throne, while the rich sit low, Servants on horses, where princes should go.
Dig a pit, you might fall in, that's the risk you take, Break a wall, a snake could bite, it's a chance to make.
Carve a stone, get hurt by it, a cut that may sting, Split wood, face danger, it's a hazardous thing.
A blunt ax takes more strength, sharpen it well, Skill brings success, that's the story to tell.
If a snake bites before it's charmed, no profit's won, A charmer's tongue's useless if the work ain't done.
A wise man speaks with grace, his words are a gift, A fool's swallowed by his lips, can't get a lift.
Foolish words start simple, end with madness, He multiplies words, can't see future sadness.
Fools' work wearies them, don't know the way to go, Lost in their talk, no city they know.
Woe to the land with a child as king, Princes feast in the morning, what chaos they bring.
Happy the land with a noble king's son, Princes eat for strength, not drunken fun.
Sloth lets the roof sink, idle hands let it leak, A feast for laughter, wine for joy, money speaks.
Don't curse the king, not even in thought, A bird might hear you, and tell what you wrought.
Cast your bread on waters wide, it’ll come back, just wait and see, Give a portion, share with seven, maybe even eight, let it be.
Clouds full of rain drop down to ground, trees fall and stay where they land, Watch the winds, you'll never sow, look at clouds, and harvest? Can't.
You don’t know wind’s secret path, or how bones grow within the womb, God’s work, a mystery all around, in the light and in the gloom.
Morning, sow your seed in faith, evening, don’t hold back your hand, Which will prosper? You don’t know, both could flourish on the land.
Sweet's the light, the sun's a joy, eyes delight in morning’s glow, Live your years with smiles and cheer, but remember, darkness will show.
Rejoice in youth, let your heart be glad, follow the ways you choose to know, But remember, before the Lord, for all your actions, you’ll stand and show.
Remove sorrow, cast off evil, youth and dawn are fleeting days, Life's a vapor, like the mist, remember always, God’s wise ways.
Remember your Creator while you're still young, Before hard times hit and life becomes unsung.
Before the sun fades and the moon's light goes dim, When stars lose their sparkle, clouds roll in on a whim.
When protectors shake and the strong bend low, When work grinds to a halt, and time moves slow.
Doors closed in the street, sound of grinding fades, Birdsong wakes the sleeper, music shrouds in shades.
Fear climbs heights, terror waits on the road, Almond blossoms bloom, heavy is the load.
Desire dwindles, everyone heads home, Mourners fill the streets where the shadows roam.
Before silver cords snap, golden bowls break, Pitchers shatter at springs, wheels no longer take.
Dust returns to dust, the spirit goes back, To God who gave life, the eternal track.
"Vanity of vanities," the Preacher declared, "All is vanity," in this world we shared.
Though wise, the Preacher taught with care, Sorting proverbs, truth beyond compare.
His words sharp, like well-driven nails, From the shepherd's hand, wisdom prevails.
Books unending, knowledge wears you thin, But listen, my son: let your learning begin.
Fear God, keep commandments, it's the whole man's claim, For every deed will meet judgment's flame.
Good or evil, all will be revealed, In God's sight, nothing stays concealed.
Solomon's song, a tale of love's delight, "Your kiss is sweeter than wine," she recites.
Your oils, your scent, finer than gold, Your name's like perfume, a story retold.
"Take me away, let's run with haste, Into the king's rooms, where joy's embraced."
Dark but lovely, she stands with pride, "Like Kedar's tents, no need to hide."
"Don't gaze at my skin, sun-kissed and warm, My brothers' wrath became my norm."
"Where's your flock at noon?" she calls, "Why should I veiled wander these walls?"
He speaks, "Oh beauty, follow the way, By shepherds' tents, let your young goats play."
"You're a steed in Pharaoh's chariot ride, Cheeks adorned, jewels on your side."
"Gold earrings we'll craft, silver inlay, While the king dines, my perfume's display."
"My beloved's myrrh, so close, so near, Henna blossoms from En Gedi appear."
"Behold, you're beautiful, dove-like eyes, And our verdant couch, where love lies."
"See our home's beams, cedar strong, Firs are our rafters, where we belong."
Rose of Sharon, lily's grace, In the valleys, love finds its place.
Among thorns, my love shines bright, Apple tree stands, a pure delight.
In his shadow, I find rest, His fruit's sweetness, I am blessed.
Banquet hall, love's banner flies, "Strengthen me," my heart cries.
Left hand cradles, right hand holds, Love's embrace, as time unfolds.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, hear my plea, Don't stir love 'til it’s ready to be."
Oh, hear his voice, my love's approach, Leaping mountains, hills encroach.
Like a young deer, swift and near, At the window, he appears.
"Rise up, my love, come with me, Winter's gone, set us free.
Flowers bloom, songs abound, Turtledove's voice, sweet sound.
Figs ripen, vines in bloom, Fragrance fills every room."
"Dove in rock, come out, be seen, Your sweet voice, face serene.
Catch the foxes, the vineyard’s foe, For our blossoms, let love grow."
My beloved's mine, and I am his, Among the lilies, love is bliss.
'Til day cools and shadows part, Turn, my love, follow your heart.
In the night I lay, seeking the one my soul adores, Looked and searched, but found closed doors.
Jumped from bed, hit the streets wide, Seeking my love in the city's stride.
Watchmen found me, they saw me roam, "Seen my love?" I asked as I wandered alone.
Barely passed them, my heart took flight, Found my love, held him tight.
Brought him home, wouldn't let go, To my mother's room, where love would grow.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, hear me clear," "Don't wake love before it draws near."
Who's this rising from the wild, Pillars of smoke, smellin' sweet and mild?
Look, it's Solomon's ride in style, Sixty warriors strong, marching in file.
Swords at the ready, experts in fight, Guardians against the fears of night.
Solomon's chariot, crafted with care, Wood of Lebanon, silver flare.
Gold base, purple seat, love inlaid, Jerusalem's daughters, their craft displayed.
Step out, daughters of Zion, see him crowned, On his wedding day, pure joy abound.

You're stunning, my love, pure delight I proclaim, Your eyes like doves, framed by your veil, a gentle flame. Hair cascading like goats on Gilead's grand slopes, Teeth like fresh-shorn flocks, no missing hopes.
Lips of scarlet thread, your mouth speaks grace, Temples like pomegranate, behind the veil, in place. Your neck, a tower of David, shields hang and sway, Strength of mighty men, in every way.

Like grain that's reaped with a strong arm's sweep, Or olives left on branches, no longer to keep.
Yet remnants reside, in branches they stay, Two or three clinging, still holding sway.
Eyes turn to their Maker on high, Respect for Israel's Holy One, they won't deny.
No more altars made by their hands, No more creation by their commands.
Strong cities like desolate woods, Forsaken places, where silence broods.
"You forgot your salvation’s God, Ignored the strength of your rock, how odd.
You plant your seeds, foreign and new, Yet the harvest flees, sorrow comes due."
Nations roar like seas in a storm, Rushing waters, a mighty form.
But He rebukes, they scatter wide, Chased like chaff, with nowhere to hide.
Evening terror, morning's calm, Gone are those who brought us harm.
Beyond Ethiopian streams, wings rustling in flight, Ambassadors sail on papyrus boats, out into the night.
"Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and sleek, Where the rivers divide, a people mighty and unique."
World inhabitants, hear! When banners rise on the hill, A trumpet blast echoes — be silent, be still.
Yahweh says, "I'll be still, watchful from my place, Like sunshine's heat or dew's gentle embrace."
Before the harvest, when blossoms fade away, He'll snip with pruning hooks, the spreading boughs he'll sway.
Left for ravenous birds, beasts roam and feast, Birds in the summer, animals in winter's least.
In time, gifts to Yahweh from this tall, smooth nation, Treaders of land, with rivers' separation.
To Mount Zion, Yahweh's name presides, The mighty offering, from the rivers' divide.
Yahweh rides on a cloud, swift as night, To Egypt's land, where idols take fright.
"Egypt will tremble, hearts melt inside, Brother against brother, no place to hide."
Their spirits fail, their wisdom torn, Seek idols and charmers, feeling forlorn.
"A cruel lord, a fierce king's hand, Will rule with power over the land."
Waters dry up, rivers run foul, Nile's fields vanish, meadows disavow.
Fishermen mourn, nets empty, bare, Workers in cloth, in sorrow they stare.
Zoan's princes, foolish and blind, Counsel once wise, now left behind.
"Where's your wisdom?" Yahweh demands, "Let them tell you, if they understand."
Egypt's astray, lost in dismay, Like a drunkard, they stagger each day.
No work remains, no head or tail, Fear grips the hearts, courage will fail.
Five cities speak the Canaan tongue, Swear to Yahweh, where hope had sprung.
Altar and pillar stand in the land, A sign and witness, Yahweh's command.
They cry for help, a savior He sends, Strikes and heals, making amends.
Egypt returns, to Yahweh they call, Assyria and Egypt, worship for all.
Israel joins, a blessing unfolds, "Egypt, my people," Yahweh holds.
Assyria, His work, Israel, His own, Together they stand, in blessings they've grown.
In the year Tartan rolled into town, Sargon sent him to throw Ashdod down.
Yahweh spoke to Isaiah, "Go, my son, Shed your sackcloth, let your feet run."
Isaiah stepped, naked and bare, For three long years, he didn't care.
Yahweh said, "As Isaiah walked, Egypt and Ethiopia must heed what's talked.
The king of Assyria will lead them away, Captives will march, nothing to say.
Naked and bare, young and old, Their shame exposed, stories told.
Dismayed they'll be, their hope in despair, Ethiopia and Egypt left bare.
On that day, the coast land cries, 'Where's our help? Where's our prize?'
'We fled for shelter, we sought escape, From Assyria's grip, yet how can we reshape?'"
Whirlwinds from the south, sweeping wild and free, From the wilderness, a vision I see. Treachery abounds, destruction in place, Elam, rise up, attack with pace.
My thighs ache, anguish takes its toll, Like a woman's labor, seizing my soul. Pain so deep, I can't hear or see, My heart flutters, horror grips me.
Twilight's peace turned to trembling fear, Princes, rise up, the moment is near. "Go," said the Lord, "set a watchman high, Let him declare what meets his eye."
Horsemen in pairs, troops coming strong, Listen well, as they march along. He roared like a lion, "I stand my ground, Day and night, I watch and sound."
"Fallen is Babylon," the echoes resound, Images broken, idols hit the ground. Threshing and grain, Yahweh's decree, What I've heard, now you see.
Voices call from Seir, a watch of the night, "The morning comes, so does the night. Inquire if you will, come back and see, What the watchman’s eyes decree."
Arabia's burden, in forests they hide, Dedan's caravans, seeking a guide. Water for the thirsty, bread for the run, Fleeing the swords, the battle's begun.
"Within a year," the Lord spoke clear, Kedar's glory will disappear. Few archers remain, the strong will fall, Yahweh declared it, the God of all.
In the valley of vision, what’s up on the roof? Shouts in the city, but no sword as proof.
Rulers ran, arrows fly, bound and gone, “Look away, let me weep, for my people are done.”
Confusion and treading, walls break, cries high, Elam’s quiver, chariots ride, shields rise to the sky.
Valleys filled, horsemen at the gate, Judah’s cover gone, now armor's the state.
Breaches in David’s city, waters pooled, Houses counted, broken, walls renewed.
Reservoirs built, but they forgot the plan, Ignored the One who knew, from the very first span.
Called to weep, mourn, sackcloth, and tears, But they feast, “Tomorrow we die, so cheers!”
Yahweh whispers in my ear, can't overlook, “Your sin stays till death, by the book.”
“Go to Shebna,” says the Lord, “Ask him why He carves a high tomb, like he'll never die.”
Yahweh will toss him, spin him ‘round, Like a ball thrown far, he'll hit the ground.
Chariots lost, pride in disgrace, Out of office, out of place.
Eliakim called, robe, and belt bestowed, Key of David on his shoulder, the path showed.
He'll open doors no one can close, A nail in place, where glory grows.
Glory hangs, vessels from cups to pitcher, But one day the nail will give, can’t hold the fixture.
“The nail will fall,” Yahweh declares, “The burden cut off, for I’m aware.”
Howl, ships of Tarshish, hear the news so dire, Tyre's laid waste, no house, no entry to inspire.
From Kittim's land, the word is revealed, Coast dwellers silent, their fate is sealed.
Merchants of Sidon, across the sea they sail, Nile's harvest their wealth, nations prevail.
Sidon, now ashamed, listen to the sea, "I've birthed no one, no youths raised by me."
Report to Egypt brings nothing but pain, The fall of Tyre, a loss, a gain.
To Tarshish flee, coast inhabitants wail, Is this your ancient city, once joyful, now frail?
Who plotted against Tyre, crowned with might, Princes and traders, earth's honor in sight.
Yahweh planned it, to humble pride’s throne, All earth's honor, brought to the ground alone.
Pass like the Nile, Tarshish’s own child, No restraint now, roam the wild.
His hand on the sea, kingdoms shaken, Yahweh commands, Canaan's stronghold taken.
"You'll rejoice no more, Sidon's daughter oppressed, Go to Kittim, find no rest."
Chaldeans rise, once naught but a name, Assyrians built them, towers of fame.
Howl, ships of Tarshish, your fortress undone, Seventy years Tyre forgotten, under the sun.
Like a song of a prostitute, Tyre will sing, With harp in hand, memories to bring.
After seventy years, Yahweh will see, Tyre will trade, like before she'll be.
Her goods for Yahweh, not stored away, For those before Him, food and clothes to stay.
Yahweh's got the earth, flips it around, Makes it empty, scatters folks all over town.
Priests and people, all the same fate, Servants and masters, equal in their state.
The earth's drained dry, laid utterly bare, For Yahweh spoke, and now it's in despair.
The earth mourns, fades away, world grows thin, High folks languish, feeling it deep within.
Polluted lands from laws they broke, An everlasting promise, gone up in smoke.
"The curse devours," Yahweh said, it's true, Few men remain, the guilty's due.
New wine mourns, vines are weak, Merry hearts sigh, joy's grown bleak.
Tambourines silent, no more rejoice, The harp's joy fades, gone is the voice.
Wine without songs, drinks turn sour, In a city confused, in its final hour.
Crying in streets, joy's gone away, Desolation hits, gates in decay.
Like olives shaken, remnant few, Shout Yahweh's majesty from seas' view.
"Glorify Yahweh," from east, rise and sing, Righteous glory from earth's edge they bring.
But I cry, "Woe is me!" Treachery's reign, Fear, the pit, the snare, mix in the pain.
Flee the fear, fall in a pit's snare, Earth's foundations tremble, beware.
Earth's torn apart, stagger like a drunk, Disobedience heavy, down it sunk.
Yahweh punishes high and low, Prisoners gathered, no place to go.
Moon and sun in shameful plight, For Yahweh reigns on Zion's height.
Glory before His elders, stands, The earth in awe of His mighty hands.
Yahweh, my God, your name I raise high, For wonders you've done, planned long before the sky.
You turned a city into rubble, a fortress to dust, A stranger's palace, no more—a place unjust.
Strong people will honor, nations in awe, For you've been a refuge, a haven without flaw.
In storms and heat, you’re the cool, calming breeze, A shade from the chaos, you put hearts at ease.
You silence the noise, like heat in dry land, Clouds bring relief, with your mighty hand.
On this mountain, a feast of the best, Choice meats and wines, where all are blessed.
You'll tear the veil covering nations wide, Death swallowed forever, tears wiped aside.
"Behold our God! Our Savior at last!" In Yahweh’s salvation, our joy will be vast.
Your hand rests on the mountain, the proud brought low, Moab trodden down, like straw where waters flow.
Spreading hands like a swimmer, pride will be met, High walls crumbled, dust settles the debt.
We got a strong city, walls of salvation stand tall, "Open the gates for the righteous who heed my call." Keep your mind steady, peace on the way, Trust in Yahweh, an everlasting Rock each day.
High cities brought down, laid low to the dust, The poor tread over, their steps are just. The just walk straight, paths made right, In your ways, Yahweh, we seek you at night.
"My soul yearns in the dark, my spirit seeks light, When your judgments rain, the world learns what's right." Show favor to the wicked, they just won’t see, Your hand is lifted, Yahweh’s majesty.
"Peace ordained for us, you’ve done all our work," "Other lords ruled us, now only your name we affirm." The dead won’t rise, their memory fades, You’ve grown the nation, Yahweh, your glory cascades.
In trouble, they seek you, prayers rise in need, Like a woman in labor, we cry, and plead. We birthed the wind, no deliverance found, But your dead will live, rise from the ground.
"Awake, sing from the dust, earth will release, Enter your rooms, hide till the storm sees peace." For Yahweh comes out, justice to impart, The earth will reveal the blood, the truth in every heart.
Yahweh's got a sword, hard and strong, Leviathan's gonna learn where it belongs.
In that day, hear the vineyard's sweet call, "I, Yahweh, keep it, protect it all.
Watering it every moment, night and day, No harm shall come, no enemy's play.
I'm not wrathful, but briers beware, I'll march on them, burn them, I'm fair.
Hold my strength, make peace with me, Come, let it be, come, let it be."
Jacob will root, Israel's bloom in sight, Filling the world, fruit shining bright.
Did they fall like those who struck them down? Or did they rise, wearing a new crown?
Sins washed away by the east wind's blast, Altar stones crushed, their past is past.
The city stands empty, deserted like a wild, A lone calf lies, where branches are piled.
When boughs wither, broken, burned to flame, No compassion left, but who's to blame?
Yahweh shall thresh from river to stream, Gathering Israel, fulfilling the dream.
In that day, hear the trumpet's sound, Assyria's lost, Egypt's found.
They'll worship Yahweh on the holy hill, In Jerusalem, hearts fulfilled.
Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim's crew, Drunk on the wine, their glory askew. A fading flower in the valley so fine, Lost in their drink, overcome by the vine.
Behold, the Lord sends one fierce and strong, Like hail and a storm, sweeping along. The pride of Ephraim, trampled underfoot, Beauty fades like a fig, soon to be took.
In that day, Yahweh will shine bright, A crown of glory, a beacon of light. Justice and strength for those who fight, Turning the battle back at the gate, with might.
Priests and prophets, stagger and sway, Lost in their visions, led astray. Tables full of filth, vomit and grime, Who will learn knowledge, in this time?
"Precept on precept, line after line," He'll speak in stammers, not in the divine. "This is the rest," He said, but they turned away, So they’ll stumble and fall, night and day.
Hear the Lord's word, you who mock, Thinking your lies are a shelter, a rock. "We've made a deal with death," you say, But Yahweh declares a different way.
"Behold, in Zion, a cornerstone set," Justice and truth, the measure met. Your covenant with death, it won't stand, Swept away by hail and mighty hand.
The scourge will pass, terror in its wake, Morning by morning, the earth will shake. The bed's too short, the blanket's too tight, Yahweh will rise, in power and might.
So heed the speech, listen and hear, The voice of the Lord, crystal clear. Does the farmer plow forever, no end? He knows when to sow, when to mend.
God instructs in wisdom, in plan, Threshes with care, by His hand. From Yahweh comes counsel, profound, In His wisdom, true answers are found.
Woe to Ariel, city where David camps tight, Year by year, feasts roll, but comes the night.
"I'll distress Ariel," Yahweh's words burning, Mourning, lamentation, altars, yearning.
I'll encamp around, siege your very ground, Your voice whispers low, dust-bound sound.
Foes like dust, scattered chaff in flight, In an instant—sudden, out of sight.
Yahweh's wrath thunders, quakes, storms, and fire, A vision like a dream, faded desire.
Hungry man dreams he's had his fill, Wakes up empty, craving still.
Thirsty man drinks in dream's own light, Awakens faint, thirst's not in sight.
Pause, wonder, blind in deep sleep’s keep, Drunk, not from wine, eyes closed, seers weep.
A sealed book’s words no wise can read, "The Lord says, 'This people honors in word, no deed.'"
"Marvelous work," Yahweh plans to unfold, Wise men’s wisdom, hidden and cold.
Woe to those hiding, deeds in the night, "Who sees us?" they whisper, out of sight.
The potter's hand, clay can't ignore, "You didn't make me," clay cries more.
Lebanon soon a fruitful field to show, Deaf will hear, blind eyes will glow.
Humble rejoice, poor men sing, Ruthless brought low, justice they bring.
Yahweh speaks of Jacob's light, "No more shame," faces bright.
Children, the work of His hands, they'll see, "Sanctify My name," in awe they'll be.
Those who err will find their way, Grumblers receive instruction, a new day.
"Woe to the rebellious ones," Yahweh declares with might, "Counsel you take, but not in My sight. You form alliances without My Spirit's grace, Adding sin upon sin, you're losing the race.
You head down to Egypt, not seeking My view, Trusting Pharaoh's strength, but shame'll come through. The refuge of Egypt, a shadow to deceive, Princes at Zoan, ambassadors' reprieve.
Ashamed, you'll be of a people no aid, A burden you carry, alliances mislaid. Through lands of lions, vipers in flight, Riches on donkeys, camels in sight.
Egypt's vain help, no purpose, no gain, "Rahab who sits still," I've called her in vain. "Write it on tablets," a record to last, A rebellious people, ignoring the past.
Seers they tell, "Don't see!" Prophets they implore, "Prophesy lies, pleasant things at the core." "Get out of the way," they demand, so bold, Turning from the path, their stories unfold.
Because you despise, trust oppression's embrace, Your wall will crumble, shatter without trace. Like a potter's vessel, in pieces you'll fall, Nothing left to gather from the crumbling wall.
"Rest and return," the Holy One calls, "Strength in quietness," but deaf to His halls. "We'll flee on horses," you state and you boast, But swift are your foes, and you'll flee the most.
One thousand will run from the threat of one, Left like a beacon when the fleeing's done. Yet Yahweh waits, gracious and just, Mercy He holds for those who trust.
Dwell in Zion, no tears shall you shed, He'll hear your cry, and answer instead. Adversity's bread, affliction's drink, Yet teachers visible, to guide when you think.
Turn right or left, you'll hear Him say, "This is the path, walk in this way." Throw away idols, silver and gold, Unclean they are, let the new story unfold.
Rain for your seed, bread from the earth, Livestock in pastures, a sign of rebirth. Oxen and donkeys eating savory feed, Brooks on mountains, fulfilling your need.
Moon like the sun, sun sevenfold bright, Yahweh binds wounds, His people in sight. From afar His name comes, anger and smoke, Lips with fire, nations to provoke.
A song in the night, a feast in His name, Flutes to the mountain, joy in acclaim. Yahweh's voice, strong, will make enemies fear, With tambourines and harps, His justice is near.
For Assyria's stroke, His rod will descend, Yahweh's breath, like sulfur, will bring it to end. The pyre is prepared, deep with much wood, His stream of sulfur, kindles it good."
Woe to those who head to Egypt for aid, Trust in horses, think their power won't fade. Chariots many, horsemen strong, But forget Yahweh, and that’s where they're wrong.
God’s got wisdom, brings disaster in line, His words stay true, rise against evil time. Egyptians are men, not divine or grand, Their horses are flesh, not spirit in hand.
When Yahweh's hand stretches out, beware, Both the helper and helped will fall, a snare. "Like a lion growling over its prey, I’ll fight on Zion, guard it day by day.
Like birds in flight, I'll protect this place, Deliver and keep Jerusalem in grace." Come back, Israel, from your revolt, Cast away idols, break the gold and silver bolt.
"The Assyrian falls, not by man's sword, A force unseen will bring him toward Defeat. He’ll run, his young will bow, In terror his rock will crumble now."
Says Yahweh, within Zion his fire will burn, Jerusalem's furnace, where the tables turn.
A king will come with justice in his hand, Princes ruling wisely across the land.
A man like a shelter from the fierce storm’s lash, Streams in a desert, shade from the sun’s harsh.
Eyes wide open, ears that truly hear, Hearts understanding, tongues speaking clear.
Fools won't be called noble, scoundrels lose their fame, Folly's their language, with error they shame.
Fools speak folly, hearts plot their deceit, Empty the hungry, let the thirsty’s need repeat.
Scoundrel’s ways are twisted, plotting wicked plans, Destroying the humble with lies from their hands.
But noble minds conceive noble dreams, And in their noble acts, truth gleams.
"Rise up, you women, hear my call," I say, "You careless daughters, heed my words today.
Soon you'll be troubled, harvest will fail, Tremble, strip off ease, your comforts pale."
Beat your breasts for fields once lush and fine, Thorns and briers take over the vine.
Desolate palaces, joy's city now empty, Wild donkeys and flocks roam aplenty.
Until the Spirit rains from on high, Turning wilderness to fields lush and wide.
Justice will make its home in barren lands, Righteousness will flourish with steady hands.
Peace and quiet confidence will remain, My people dwell safe in the new domain.
Hail may flatten, but blessings flow, For those who sow by waters, seeds they sow.

Woe to those who destroy, not yet destroyed, Those who betray, though they’ve never been annoyed. When you're done with your deeds, the tables will turn, The destruction and betrayal you will soon learn.
"Yahweh, be gracious, we wait for your might, Our strength every morning, our salvation in fright." Thunder rolls, people scatter in dread, Nations flee when His presence is bred.
Plunder, like caterpillars, men will seize, Locusts leap on the spoils with ease. Yahweh's on high, Zion's filled with justice deep, Stability and wisdom, treasures we keep.
Valiant ones cry, peace ambassadors mourn, Desolate highways, covenants are torn. Land in languish, Lebanon fades away, Sharon's a desert, Bashan and Carmel decay.
"Now I will rise," Yahweh's voice booms, "I'll lift myself up, in my power you'll consume. Chaff and stubble you'll conceive and bear, Your breath a fire, consuming air."
Like burning lime, people's downfall we see, Far and near hear His might, acknowledge His decree. Sinners in fear, trembling in Zion's face, Who can withstand the everlasting blaze?
Righteous walkers, blameless talkers, they survive, Despising oppression, rejecting the bribe. Dwell on high, fortress made of rock, Bread and water, sure as a clock.
Eyes see the king, in beauty's embrace, A land once distant, now a visible place. Heart remembers terror, where are the counters now? Gone is the speech you can't comprehend, somehow.
Zion, your festivals, Jerusalem stands, A quiet tent, its stakes held by strong hands. Yahweh with majesty, rivers wide, No ship will steer, no oars will glide.
Yahweh our judge, lawgiver, and king, He saves us, His praises we sing. Rigging untied, sails failing to spread, Great plunder divides, the lame are well-fed.
None will say, "I am sick," in this forgiven city, Inhabitants dwell free from iniquity.
Come gather 'round, all nations, lend your ear, Listen close, let the world and its contents hear.
Yahweh's anger's fierce, the armies face His wrath, They're handed to slaughter, no escape, no path.
Bodies cast out, the stench rises high, Mountains melt in the blood, red rivers never dry.
The sky's army dissolves, rolls up like a scroll, Leaves fade from the vine, like a story untold.
"My sword's drunk its fill," the judgment's set, Targets Edom next, "On the cursed they'll be met."
Yahweh’s sword drips blood, soaked and fat, Lambs and goats fall, rams are laid flat.
Great slaughter in Edom, Bozrah's the scene, Blood drunken land, dust greasy sheen.
A day of vengeance, a year for Zion’s cause, Streams turn to pitch, sulfur in the dust draws.
It burns unquenched both night and day, Smoke rises forever, waste it will stay.
Pelicans and porcupines will call it home, Owls, ravens dwell where no nobles will roam.
Thorns in the palaces, nettles in the forts, Jackals own the courts, ostriches in retorts.
Desert beasts and wolves have their meeting ground, Wild goats call out, night creatures find sound.
Arrow snakes nest, hatch, and lay, Kites gather with mates, in this decay.
Search Yahweh's book, nothing will miss its place, His words command, His spirit gathers grace.
The lot is cast, measured by His hand, Generations hold what's been planned.
The wilderness shouts, dry land's got a smile, Desert's blooming roses, stretching for miles.
It blossoms with joy, with song and pride, Lebanon's glory, Carmel, Sharon by its side.
They see Yahweh's glory, a sight so grand, Strengthen weak hands, make firm every stand.
"Strong hearts!" to the fearful, "Fear not, hear the call! Your God comes with power, to save you all."
Eyes of the blind, they open wide, Deaf ears hear, no need to hide.
The lame one leaps, like a deer so spry, Mute tongues sing, waters flow and fly.
Burning sands turn to pools, thirst gone, Grass grows where jackals lay at dawn.
A highway rises, called "The Holy Way," For those in truth, it's the chosen day.
Lions absent, no beasts roam here, The redeemed walk on, in joy and cheer.
Yahweh's ransomed return, singing to Zion, Everlasting joy crowns them, like a lion.
Gladness and joy, they hold and sway, Sorrow and sighing, chased far away.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's reign, Assyria's king brought Judah pain,
Sennacherib attacked with force and might, Took every fortified city, day or night.
Rabshakeh came from Lachish with an army bold, Stood by the aqueduct, stories to be told.
Eliakim, Shebna, Joah stepped out to meet, Rabshakeh's words, they couldn't beat.
"Tell Hezekiah," Rabshakeh did say, "The great king speaks, hear me today.
What’s this trust, this confidence in you? Your counsel's vain, your strength too.
You lean on Egypt, that broken reed, Pharaoh will pierce, he won’t meet your need.
You say, 'We trust in Yahweh, our God,’ Yet Hezekiah removed altars, odd.
Make a pledge, join Assyria's way, Two thousand horses, if you ride today.
Turn not to Egypt's chariots here, My master's weakest you should fear.
Did Yahweh not send me to destroy? This land's mine to break, not to enjoy."
Eliakim and crew said, "Speak Aramaic please, Not in our tongue, let the people be at ease."
Rabshakeh shouted out in Hebrew loud, "Listen, people, gather 'round.
Don't let Hezekiah lead you astray, He can't save you, hear what I say.
‘Make peace with Assyria, come out, be free, Eat from your vine, drink from your tree.
Until we take you to lands anew, There’s grain, wine, just like you knew.
Don’t be fooled by Hezekiah's call, No god has saved their land at all.
Where are Hamath's gods, Arpad's divine? Samaria fell, and they'll align.
No god saved them from my king’s hand, Why should Yahweh save this land?’”
Silence fell, no reply was made, For the king's command, they obeyed.
Eliakim, Shebna, Joah, clothes torn in grief, Told Hezekiah Rabshakeh’s disbelief.
Hezekiah hears the news, tears his clothes, sackcloth worn, Heads to the house of Yahweh, weary and worn.
Eliakim and Shebna, priests in tow, sent on a ride, To Isaiah the prophet, in whom they confide.
Hezekiah says, "It's a day of trouble, rebuke, and rejection, The birth pains come, yet there's no strength for this connection.
Pray, maybe Yahweh will hear Rabshakeh's defiance, And rebuke his words with divine reliance.
Pray for the remnant, the few who remain, Lift up your voice and help us sustain."
Isaiah speaks, "To your king, this word convey, Yahweh says, ‘Fear not the words that came your way.
I'll put a spirit in him, news he will hear, Return to his land, his end draws near.’"
Rabshakeh returns, finds Assyria in fight, The king's left Lachish, gone to Libnah's light.
News of Tirhakah, Ethiopia's king, "He's come to war," the news does ring.
Messengers sent with words of disdain, "Don't trust your God, you'll be in pain.
Look at Assyria's wrath on all lands, No gods saved them from our hands."
Hezekiah reads the words in despair, Spreads it before Yahweh, in earnest prayer.
"Yahweh of Armies, enthroned on high, You alone made earth and sky.
Hear Sennacherib's challenge, see his game, Save us, prove your holy name."
Isaiah sends word, "Yahweh heard your plea, The daughter of Zion mocks with glee.
Who do you defy with your boastful tone? Against the Holy One, you've raised your throne.
With chariots and pride, you claim this land, But Yahweh's might, you can't withstand.
I know your moves and your rage against me, Back you’ll go, to where you should be.
A sign awaits, the remnant will thrive, Eating from the land, they'll stay alive.
Out of Jerusalem, survivors will rise, Yahweh's zeal will break these ties."
"No arrow shall hit, no siege will stand, I protect this city by my own command.
For David’s sake, this city I'll save, Assyria's king won’t dig a grave."
Yahweh's angel strikes in the dark of night, 185,000 fall, dawn brings the sight.
Sennacherib, humbled, to Nineveh he returns, In his own god's house, his fate he learns.
His sons with swords end his reign, Esar Haddon takes the king's chain.
Hezekiah lay sick, facing death's call, Isaiah the prophet spoke, "Set your house, y'all.
Yahweh says, ‘Your time's up, make amends, For soon your life's journey comes to an end.’"
Hezekiah turned, eyes fixed on the wall, Prayed to Yahweh with a heart sincere and small.
"Remember, Yahweh, how I've walked in Your truth, Done what’s good since the days of my youth."
Tears flowed bitterly down the king's face, Pleading for mercy, for a little more grace.
Yahweh's word then came swift and clear, "Isaiah, tell Hezekiah, have no fear.
‘God of David says, ‘I’ve heard your prayer, Seen your tears, fifteen more years I'll spare.
I'll rescue this city from Assyria's might, Defend it with power, defend it with light.
Here's the sign, a miracle I’ll make, The shadow on the sundial, ten steps back it'll take.’"
The sun reversed its course, a wonder to see, Hezekiah's life extended, his spirit set free.
In his writing, the king expressed his despair, "I was heading to Sheol, no life left to spare.
No more to see Yah in the land of the living, Cut off like a tent, my life unraveling.
Morning to night, my bones felt the break, Like a weaver's loom, my end You’d make.

Then he spoke, "What can I say of this grace? He spoke to me, saved me from this place.

Isaiah said, "Take figs for a healing balm, Lay it on the boil, restore the king’s calm."
Hezekiah asked, "What's the sign, I must know, That to Yahweh's house my steps will go?"
Merodach Baladan, Babylon's king, Sent gifts, heard Hezekiah's bell did ring. Recovered from sickness, feeling fine, Hezekiah showed off all that's mine.
Silver, gold, spices, oil, and more, Opened up his house, showed every door. Isaiah the prophet came and asked, "What did they say? From where, at last?"
"From far-off Babylon," Hezekiah replied, "They've seen my treasures, nothing to hide." Isaiah spoke with a word from Yahweh, "Days are coming, hear what I say.
All your riches, all stored away, To Babylon will go, none will stay. Sons of yours taken, made eunuchs then, In the Babylon palace, among those men."
Hezekiah nodded, "Yahweh’s word is true, For now, there’ll be peace, in days I view." Thus the story ends, a lesson clear, What you show today may disappear.
"Comfort, comfort my people," God declares, "Speak to Jerusalem, calm all her cares. Her war is done, her sins are pardoned, Double for her sins, from Yahweh's hand it's garnered."
A voice cries out, "Prepare the way in the wild, Level the highway, make it smooth and styled. Every valley raised, each mountain laid low, Uneven ground will level, rough places will flow."

"Keep silent and still, islands, hear my decree, Let the people gather strength, then come talk with me. Let's meet up for judgment, settle what's right, Who from the east was called, with kingdoms in his sight?

"Idol worshippers turned back in shame, They'll see their gods can't stake a claim." "Hear, you deaf, look, blind, to see, Who's more blind than my servant be?"
"See much, observe not, ears open wide, But listen not," the truth they hide. Yahweh's law lifted, righteousness raised, Yet people snared, in prisons caged.
Who'll hear, who'll listen for the hour near? Jacob plundered, Israel in fear. Yahweh's wrath burned like fire untamed, Yet heeded not, nor heart inflamed."
Yahweh speaks to Jacob, to Israel's name, "Fear not, I've redeemed you, you're mine to claim.
When waters rise, I'll be by your side, Through fire you'll walk, unburned, in stride.
For I am Yahweh, your God, your Savior, Egypt given in ransom, Ethiopia's favor.

Fear not, I'm with you, east to west I'll call, North give 'em up, south don't stall.

From time's dawn, I'm He, none can resist, I will work, who dares to insist?"
Yahweh, your Redeemer, Holy Israel's King, Says, "For you to Babylon I've sent and will bring.

Forget old things, behold the new, A way in wilderness, rivers in view.
Wild beasts honor me, for waters I give, To quench my chosen, to help them live.

Let us reason, plead together, make your case, First fathers sinned, teachers disgraced.
Princes defiled, Jacob becomes a curse, Israel an insult, for better or worse."
"Listen up, Jacob, my chosen crew, I'm Yahweh, who made and formed you. Don't be scared, Jacob, my servant true, Jeshurun, I've picked you too.
I'll pour water on the thirsty land, Spirit on your kids, blessings so grand. They'll spring up like willows by the stream, Claiming my name, living the dream.
One shouts, 'I'm Yahweh's!' loud and proud, Another writes 'to Yahweh,' vows avowed. Here's what Yahweh, Israel's King, now says, "I'm the first, last, in all my ways.

Carved images, they got no soul, Makers of idols, they dig their own hole. Smith swings the ax, works in the coal, Arm gets weary, can't fill the bowl.

"Remember, Jacob, you're my own, I made you, my servant, never alone. Blotted out sins like clouds in the sky, Turn back to me, your redemption's nigh.

"Ask what's coming, I'll share my design, The work of my hands, all things align.

"Look to me, be saved, ends of the earth, All knees will bow, knowing my worth.

Bel bows low, Nebo drops to the ground, Their idols are heavy, they're dragging around.

"Listen up, Jacob's house, you left in the cold, From birth to gray hairs, I'm your strength to hold.

"Who can you compare to me, none can relate, Gold from the bag, silver to create.
They hire a smith, make a god, bow low, Yet it stands still, no help in the woe.

From east, like a bird, I call on my own, I've spoken, I'll act, my plans are known."
"Listen, stubborn hearts, you're far from the mark, But my righteousness nears, igniting the dark.

Babylon, sit down in the dust, no throne to call your own, Your days of being delicate, those days have flown.

"Our Redeemer," Yahweh speaks, "The Holy One's decree, Daughter of the Chaldeans, now you're sitting silently."
No longer the mistress, kingdoms slip away, Anger with my people, I let you have your way.
But you showed no mercy, laid a heavy yoke, Claimed you'd be a princess forever, spoke like a joke.
Heed the warning, pleasure seeker, sitting secure, Saying, "I'm the only one," your heart that's pure no more.

Trusted in your wickedness, thinking unseen, Your wisdom twisted, now disaster unforeseen.
"Mischief falls upon you," God declares it loud, Desolation sudden, darkening your proud.
Stand with your enchantments, see if they prevail, Astrologers and stargazers, their efforts will fail.
Like stubble in the fire, they'll burn away, No warmth, no comfort, nothing left to say.
Your labors are in vain, traffickers depart, No one there to save you, each will break apart.
Hear, house of Jacob, called by Israel's name, Out of Judah's water, but truth's not your claim.
You swear by Yahweh, mention His might, But truth and righteousness are out of sight.
You call the holy city your home, Rely on God, Yahweh of Armies known.
I spoke of old things, declared them clear, Suddenly they happened, as you hear.
You’re obstinate, with iron necks, Your brow's like bronze, but still, I check.
I told you before they came to pass, So you won't claim idols made them last.
You've heard it all, now see and declare, New things I've shown, beyond compare.
Created now, not from before, You didn't hear, but I've opened the door.
Yes, from the past, ears were shut tight, But I've known your ways weren’t right.
For my name, I hold my wrath, Refined, not as silver, but in affliction's path.
For my sake alone, I act with grace, My glory I won't let another embrace.
"Listen, Jacob, Israel called by me, I'm the first, the last, eternally.
My hands laid earth's foundation wide, Heavens spread out at my side.
Gather and hear, among them, who can say? Yahweh’s love moves Babylon his way.
I’ve spoken, called him forth, Prosperous paths he's set to go forth.
Come close, hear my decree, I spoke openly, from start, see?
Yahweh, your Redeemer, speaks true, Leads you wisely, teaches what’s due.
Oh, if you'd listened, peace like a river you'd see, Righteousness waving like the sea.
Offspring as sand, grains without cease, Their name enduring in my peace.
Leave Babylon, flee with songs of praise, "Yahweh's redeemed Jacob," in joyous ways.
No thirst in deserts, waters from rock, Split the stone, let the waters unlock.
"There’s no peace," Yahweh’s words ring, "For the wicked," echoes the King.
Listen up, islands, hear my call, Yahweh named me from the womb, y'all.
My mouth's sharp, like a sword in hand, Hidden in His shadow, part of His plan.
He called me out, "You’re my servant, my pride, In you, Israel, I will be glorified."
But I said, "I worked, nothing gained, Yet my justice is with Yahweh, unstained."
He formed me, made me strong, To bring Jacob back where they belong.
"It’s light work to restore Israel's fate, You’ll shine for nations, salvation's gate."
To him who’s despised, Yahweh proclaimed, "Kings and princes will rise, know your name."
"I’ve answered in time, helped on salvation’s day, Preserved you for people, your strength won’t decay."
To the bound, "Come out!" to darkness, "Reveal!" They’ll feed on treeless heights, with pasture to heal.
No hunger, no thirst, the sun won’t scorch, For mercy guides them with springs that torch.
"I’ll make mountains roads, highways elevated, From far they’ll come, as I’ve related."
Sing, heavens, earth, break in song, Yahweh comforts, makes the weak strong.
But Zion cries, “Forgotten, forsaken!” "Can a mother forget? Her love unshaken."
"Engraved on my hands, your walls remain, Children return, those who hurt will wane."
Look around, they gather near, "Like a bride, you’ll dress, no need to fear."
Your land, once waste, now too small, The devoured flee; you’ll stand tall.
"Who bore these?" you’ll say, in disbelief, Alone you were, now joy relieves.
Yahweh's hand lifts up high, Nations bring your children nigh.
Kings and queens, bow to the earth, Know Yahweh’s promise, mighty in worth.
"Can the strong keep their captive hold? No, I'll rescue; your story’s retold."
Oppressors will feast on their own, All flesh will know Yahweh’s throne.
Yahweh saves, Redeemer, Mighty One, Jacob's strength, His will be done.
Yahweh asks, "Where's that divorce you think I gave? Did I sell you off? No way, it’s sin that made you slaves.
When I came calling, why was there no one around? Is my arm too short to lift you from the ground?
I dry the seas with just a rebuke, make rivers dry, The fish rot away, no water, they die.
I cover the heavens in darkness, sackcloth's their sheet, The Lord Yahweh speaks words that weary souls greet.
Morning by morning, He wakes my ear to learn, His teachings I hear, His wisdom I yearn.
I didn't rebel, didn't turn my back in fear, Faced the beatings, the shame, the spit, stayed near.
The Lord Yahweh helps me, I won't be ashamed, Face like flint, strong, His trust proclaimed.
Who'll accuse me? Stand up, let's see, The Lord helps, who can condemn me?
Adversaries age like clothes, moths eat them away, Trust Yahweh, walk in light, come what may.
But those who light their own fire, torches ablaze, Will lie down in sorrow, lost in their own haze."
"Listen up, seekers of the right, Look to your roots, the rock's in sight. Abraham's call, when he was alone, Blessed and made many, he's not on his own.
Yahweh comforts Zion with grace, Wilderness blooms, Eden's embrace. Joy and gladness singing loud, Thankfulness rising, melody proud.
"Listen, my nation, hear my decree, A law from me, justice for all to see. Righteousness near, salvation's out, Islands will wait, in my arm they shout.

"Those who know the righteous path, Fear not man nor insults' wrath. Moths and worms will eat away, But my salvation's here to stay.
Awake, awake, Yahweh's might, Break the sea, pierce the night. Redemption song, to Zion they sing, Joy everlasting, on their heads it clings.

But the wicked churn like a restless tide, No peace for them, in waters they hide.
"There is no peace," says God, "for the wicked's way," In their troubled seas, they forever sway.
Cry out loud, don’t hold back, lift up your voice, Tell my people 'bout their sins, let ‘em hear your choice. They seek me daily, act like they care, As if they do right, like they’re always fair.

They ask for my judgments, draw near with delight, But they wonder, “We fast, why's our plight outta sight?” "You see, on your fast day, you chase your own gain, Oppress your workers, ignore their pain.
You fast with strife, fistfuls of hate, Think that's the way to get through Heaven’s gate? Is this the fast that I’ve chosen for you? A day to bow, sackcloth, ashes too?
Nah, I chose to break wicked chains, Undo the yokes, free folks from their pains. Share your bread, bring the homeless in, Clothe the naked, that's where it begins.
Then your light breaks out like morning’s embrace, Healing comes quick, righteousness makes its case. Call out to Yahweh, and He'll reply, ‘Here I am,’ He’ll say, when you cry.
Stop the pointing, the wicked speech, Pour out to the hungry, practice what you preach. Your light will rise in the darkness, shout, Yahweh will guide, no doubt.
You'll be a garden, watered and bright, A spring that flows, day and night. Rebuild the ruins, raise up the past, Repairer of Breach, a title that’ll last.
Turn from your ways on the Sabbath day, Delight in Yahweh, let His honor stay. Ride the high places, fed with Jacob’s grace, For Yahweh’s spoken, and that’s your place."
Yahweh’s arm ain't short, it can still save, His ear ain't dull, He hears every wave.
But sins have built a wall, a great divide, Made Him hide His face, where could He abide?
Your hands, stained with blood, fingers in deceit, Lips spilling lies, tongues wicked on repeat.
Justice's gone missing, truth can't find its way, Chasing empty dreams, birthing sin each day.
Hatching deadly eggs, spinning webs so sly, Eating brings death, vipers lurking by.
These webs can’t clothe, works of sin won't hide, Violence in their hands, righteousness denied.
Feet rush to evil, swift to spill blood, Thoughts full of ruin, paths lead to the flood.
Peace is unknown, justice can't be found, Paths twisted and crooked, silence all around.
Justice far, light has turned to night, Groping like the blind, lost without sight.
Roaring like bears, bitter moans fill the air, Looking for justice, but none is there.
Sins stacked high, they testify and scold, Transgressing, denying, hearts grown cold.
Justice turned back, truth's on the street, Uprightness locked out, defeat's complete.
Truth lacking, those who stand alone are prey, Yahweh sees this mess, displeased by the decay.
No intercessor found, no one to save, His own arm brings salvation, His righteousness brave.
Righteousness as armor, salvation on His head, Vengeance clothing Him, with zeal as His thread.
Repaying deeds, wrath for foes, From east to west, His glory grows.
"A Redeemer's coming," Yahweh's voice resounds, "To Zion, to those turning around."
"My covenant's firm, My Spirit won't flee, My words in your mouth, for eternity."
"Arise, shine, your light's come, it's true, Yahweh's glory's rising, shining on you. Darkness wraps the earth, thick and deep, But Yahweh's light on you will never sleep.
Nations drawn to your brilliant display, Kings step up to the dawn of your day. Look around, see them gather near, Sons and daughters from far will appear.
You'll see and glow, heart swelling wide, As the sea’s abundance flows to your side. Wealth of nations, riches untold, Camels bring gifts, frankincense, and gold.
Flocks of Kedar, rams will serve, To my altar, their offerings will curve. "Who flies like clouds, like doves on the breeze?" Islands and ships bring sons across seas.
Foreigners building, kings at your call, Once struck in wrath, now my mercy's your all. Gates wide open, never shut tight, Wealth of the nations pours in day and night.
Nations against you will fade and break, Cypress and pine to your beauty's sake. Those who mocked, now bowing low, Call you Yahweh’s City, Zion aglow.
Once forsaken, now you’ll shine bright, A joy for ages, in Yahweh's sight. Milk of nations, royal supply, Know I’m your Savior, never pass by.
Bronze for gold, iron for silver trade, Peace and righteousness your rulers made. No more violence, no more woe, Walls of Salvation, Gates of Praise will show.
Sun and moon, no longer your light, Yahweh's your everlasting sight. Mourning's over, your sun will stay, Your moon won't fade, night turns to day.
All righteous, the land you’ll claim, Branch of my planting, lifting my name. Little to thousands, small to strong, Yahweh will make it, won't take long."
Yahweh's Spirit's on me, I'm anointed for the humble mission, Preachin' good news, lifting hearts with precision.
Sent to bind the broken, set the captives free, Proclaimin' liberty, release for all to see.
Declare the year of favor, vengeance day on the mark, Comfort for the mourners, light in Zion's dark.
Garlands for ashes, joy for mourning's weight, Praise replaces heaviness, righteousness they cultivate.
Rebuild old ruins, raise what’s left behind, Repair the cities, from past sorrows unwind.
Strangers feed your flocks, foreigners in your fields, Priests of Yahweh you'll be, the glory of nations yields.
Double for your shame, rejoice where others scoff, Everlasting joy, in their land they'll top it off.
"For I, Yahweh, love justice, hate the crooked scheme, Reward in truth is given, an everlasting dream."
Offspring known worldwide, blessed by Yahweh's decree, All will see and know, His blessings come to be.
Rejoice in Yahweh, my soul's joyful tune, Clothed in salvation, righteousness’ bloom.
Like earth births its buds, like gardens spring anew, Yahweh sparks righteousness, praise for nations too.
For Zion’s sake, I won't keep still, For Jerusalem's good, I climb this hill, Till her righteousness shines like dawn's first light, And her salvation like a lamp burning bright.
Nations will see your righteous ways, Kings will behold your glorious days. You'll get a new name from Yahweh's own breath, A crown of beauty, a diadem of faith.
No longer Forsaken, nor Desolate, Hephzibah and Beulah, your new state. For Yahweh delights in all that you do, Your land's like a bride, made new.
Watchmen on walls, they never sleep, Day and night, their vigil they keep. Call on Yahweh, don’t take a break, Till Jerusalem's praise, the earth will shake.
Yahweh's sworn by His own strong hand, "Your grain won't feed a foreign land. The wine you've worked for, it's yours to enjoy, In My courts, with songs of joy."
Go through the gates, prepare the way, Build the highway, clear stones away. Lift up a banner, let it unfurl, Yahweh proclaims to the whole wide world:
"Daughter of Zion, see your salvation near, With His reward, His presence here." Called "Holy People, Yahweh’s Redeemed," "Sought Out, Not Forsaken," you'll be esteemed.
Who comes from Edom, garments dyed in red? Striding strong, with glory spread. "It is I, righteous in speech, mighty to save," Clothing stained like one who treads in a wine wave.
"I've trod the press alone, no one at my side, In anger, I trampled, in wrath I did stride. Their lifeblood on my clothes, stained deep, A day of vengeance in my heart I keep.
No one to help, none to uphold, My arm brought salvation, my wrath took hold. Trod down the people, made them drunk in my ire, Their lifeblood outpoured, a tale of my fire."
I'll speak of Yahweh's kindness, his praise I'll sing, All he's bestowed, the goodness he brings. "Surely these are my children, honest and true," He became their Savior, in love he drew.
In affliction, he was there, an angel to redeem, In love and pity, he bore them, like a dream. But they rebelled, his Spirit they grieved, He turned an enemy, from blessings they were relieved.
Remember Moses, leading them through the sea, His Holy Spirit, among them, set them free. Parting waters, in glory, with strength he came, He led them safe, to build his name.
Look down from heaven, see us here below, Where's your zeal and power, your love to show? You're our Father, Redeemer from the start, Even if Abraham doesn't know, you're in our heart.
Why let us wander, why our hearts turn cold? Return, Yahweh, for your people of old. Adversaries tread where we once stood tall, Now like strangers, not called by your name at all.
Tear the heavens, come on down, let mountains quake and shake the ground. Like fire on brushwood, flames ignite, make water boil, show your might.
Make your name known to foes, renowned, let nations tremble all around. You did amazing things of old, came down, the mountains you controlled.
No ear has heard, no eye has seen a God like you who intervenes, For those who wait, you pave the way, for the righteous, clear the day.
"You were angry, we confessed, for long in sin we were oppressed. Now we ask, can we be saved? Our deeds like rags, we're enslaved."
Like leaves we fade, blown by the breeze, our sins like winds, with no ease. No one calls your name aloud, from us, your face, you have shrouded.
Yet you, Yahweh, are our Father, the clay to mold, the hand you offer. "Don't be furious, don't hold the past, we're your people, we ask at last."
Your holy cities, now laid bare, Zion's wilderness, no one there. Jerusalem's a desolate scene, a house once praised, now unseen.
Burned with fire, pleasant places waste, "Will you stay silent, leave us disgraced?" Yahweh, will you hold back your hand, or punish us as you have planned?
Yo, I'm sought by the ones who didn't ask, Found by the seekers shadowed in the past. "See me, see me," I called on a flock, Who never bore my name, yet still I rock.
Hands stretched wide to a wild, rebel clan, Walking a twisted path, ignoring the plan. They spark my fury, face me with their schemes, Sacrificing in gardens, dreaming cursed dreams.
Chillin' with the dead, secret spots at night, Eating swine's flesh, broth of things not right. "Stay away," they say, "I'm holier than you," Smoke in my nose, flames burning through.
"Look, it's written, can't stay silent, no way, Gonna repay, fold sins in your bay. Your sins, your fathers', together they climb, Incense on the mountains, blasphemy in rhyme."
Yahweh speaks, "There's new wine in the vine, Don't destroy it, blessings in line. From Jacob's seed, my mountains they'll claim, Chosen ones dwelling, in my holy name.
Sharon's fields for flocks, Achor's resting grace, For those who've sought me, found their place. But you who forget, turning Fortune's card, Destined for the sword, life hits hard."
"When I called, you turned away, Did evil deeds, didn't hear what I say. So Yahweh says, my servants will dine, While you hunger, thirst on the vine.
They'll rejoice, you'll wail in the night, Your name a curse, fading from sight. New name for my servants, a truth in their heart, Old troubles forgotten, fresh start.
Behold, new heavens, new earth I create, Past wiped away, don't contemplate. Jerusalem, my joy, her people my delight, No more tears, no cries in the night.
No infant short-lived, no elder with lost days, Children living long, in blessed ways. Build homes, plant vines, eat their yield, Their work enjoyed, nothing concealed.
