Labor not in vain, nor birth in despair, Yahweh’s blessed offspring, in His care. Before they call, I’ll answer, I’m near, While they speak, I’m ready to hear.
Wolf and lamb together will feed, Lion eats straw, serpent on dust it will lead. No harm, no destruction on my holy hill, Yahweh speaks, peace, be still."

Heaven's my throne, earth's my footstool, you see, "What house will you build? Where's my place to be?" My hand made it all, everything you know, But the humble and contrite, they're the ones I'll show.
An ox killed is like a man's life taken, Sacrificing lambs, with evil mistaken. Offerings of pigs' blood, incense to idols, They chose their ways, embraced vile titles.
I’ll bring their fears, delusions they'll find, Called out, they ignored, my voice left behind. They did what I hate, what I can't delight, Now here comes their reckoning, day and night.
Listen, those trembling at my word's sway, "Your brothers hate, cast you away. They’ll say, 'Let Yahweh's joy appear,' But disappointment’s all they’ll hear."
A voice from the city, temple's echoing sound, Yahweh repays enemies as justice comes around. Before pain struck, a child was born, Who’s ever seen a land in a day form?
"Will I bring to birth, not deliver the life?" Says Yahweh, your God, the one ending strife. Rejoice with Jerusalem, let joy fill your heart, In her abundance, you shall take part.
Peace like a river, nations' glory will stream, Carried in comfort, life's sweet dream. "As a mother comforts, so shall I," In Jerusalem, tears will dry.
You'll see it, rejoice, your bones will thrive, Yahweh's hand with his servants alive. He comes with fire, chariots in flight, Judgment fierce, like flames in the night.
Yahweh’s sword, it will cut through all, Many will fall, to their end they’ll crawl. Those purifying in gardens, pig’s meat they eat, Abominations end in their defeat.
"I know their works, their thoughts, their deeds, Time is near, nations will heed. A sign among, to the world they'll go, To declare my glory, make it known."
Brothers from nations, offerings they bring, To Jerusalem's mountain, where praises ring. "I’ll select priests, Levites true, As the new heavens and earth come through."
From moon to moon, Sabbath's rest, All flesh will worship, in Yahweh's nest. They'll see transgressors, bodies unquenched, In eternal fire, their fate entrenched.
Jeremiah's the son of Hilkiah, priest in Anathoth's land, Yahweh's word to him, on Josiah's command.
In the days of Jehoiakim, the king's reign spanned, Till Zedekiah's rule, and Jerusalem's stand.
Yahweh speaks to me, "Before birth, you were mine, A prophet to nations, your role's divine."
I said, "Lord Yahweh, I'm just a youth, Can't speak for you, that's the truth."
But Yahweh replied, "Don't say you're just a kid, You'll go where I send, do as you're bid.
Don't fear them, for I'm by your side, To rescue you, my words will guide."
He touched my mouth, His words in my core, "Over nations, kingdoms, you'll uproot, restore.
Uproot and tear down, destroy, overthrow, Build and plant, make my kingdom grow."
"Jeremiah, what do you see?" came the divine call, "I see an almond branch, standing tall."
"Seen well," He said, "My word will not fall, I watch over it, fulfilling it all."
A boiling pot, tipping from the north, "Evil's coming forth, from that direction it'll start.
All kingdoms will come to Jerusalem's gate, Against Judah's cities, they seal their fate.
Judgments for wickedness, they left me behind, Worshiping false gods, their own hands' designs.
So gird your waist, stand tall and declare, Don't fear the faces of those who stare.
I've made you a city, strong like iron and bronze, Against kings, princes, priests, and lands beyond.
They'll fight you, but won't succeed, For I am with you, my word is your creed."
Yahweh's word came to me, clear and bright, "Go tell Jerusalem, listen tonight.
I remember your youth, your wedding's delight, Chasing me in deserts, not a land in sight.
Israel was holy, first fruits of my hand, Whoever devours him, will not stand."
Hear Yahweh's word, O house of Jacob, All Israel's families, up in the wake-up!
"What wrong did your fathers in me see? They wandered far, to idols they'd flee.
Where's Yahweh who led from Egypt's woes, Through deserts, pits, shadowy throes?
I brought you to lands of fruit galore, But you defiled my gift, made it impure.
Priests ask not, 'Where's Yahweh's grace?' Rulers rebel, prophets lose their place.
I'll contend with you, and with your kin, Look at Kittim, check out Kedar's sin.
Has a nation swapped its gods for a loss? But my people traded glory at a cost.
Beware, heavens, be shocked and afraid, My people left living waters they'd once craved.
Broken cisterns they trust, no water they hold, Is Israel a slave, in captivity's fold?
Young lions roar, land laid to waste, Cities burned, their cries displaced.
Memphis and Tahpanhes, they break your crown, You forsook Yahweh, when he led you around.
Why run to Egypt, sip Shihor's stream? Assyria's river, just a fleeting dream.
Wickedness will correct, backsliding will chide, Forsaking Yahweh, the bitterness inside.
Once I broke your yoke, burst your chains, Yet on high hills, you played the games.
I planted noble vine, pure seed of truth, Now degenerate branches, oh where's your youth?
Wash with lye, scrub and clean, But your iniquity's seen, it's not washed clean.
How can you claim, 'I'm pure, no Baals pursued'? Check your valley, know what you do.
Swift as a dromedary, wild donkey gone wild, Craving the wind, untamed and riled.
"Don't go bare, keep thirst at bay, But you love strangers; you stray.
Like a thief caught, with shame in his eyes, Israel's ashamed, prophets and lies.
Wood and stone, called father and mother, Turned their backs, in trouble they holler.
Where are your gods in the time of need? For many as your towns, O Judah, take heed.
Why fight me, all have gone astray," Says Yahweh, as clear as day.
"I struck your children, but they ignored, Your sword devoured prophets, my word?
Consider Yahweh, am I a dark land? Why do they say, 'We've broken the band?'
Can a bride forget her jewels, her dress? Yet my people forget me, in times of stress.
You teach the wicked love, with ways so deft, Innocent's blood on your skirts is left.
'I'm innocent,' you say, but I see the sin, Judgment comes, for you can't begin.
Why change your ways, why wander so? You'll be ashamed of Egypt, as you were long ago.
Hands on your head, leaving in shame, Yahweh rejects your trust, nothing you gain."

"If a man sends away his wife, then she leaves, Takes another man and returns, is it right to believe?" But you’ve roamed with many a lover, still come back to me, Says Yahweh, "Lift up your eyes, tell me what do you see?

You’ve waited on roadsides like those in the desert, unseen, You've stained the land with ways that are unclean. So the rain is withheld, skies refuse to pour, Yet your forehead’s bold, you feel no shame anymore.
Will you not cry out and call me 'Father of my youth?' Will anger last forever? Is that the truth?" You've spoken and acted, did evil your own way, Yahweh says, "Israel's strayed, what can I say?

She climbed every high mountain, under each green tree, Played the harlot there, wasn't faithful to me. I thought she'd return, but she stayed on her track, Judah watched her sister, yet didn't turn back.

Israel's betrayal led to divorce, a certificate I gave, Yet Judah, she wandered, no fear did she save. Played lightly with stones and wood, it's understood, Her heart wasn't true, though she thought it should.
"Backsliding Israel's more righteous," Yahweh declares, "Go north, say, 'Return,' for I care. I won’t stay angry, merciful I will be, Just admit your wrongs, come back to me."
"Return, lost children," Yahweh does proclaim, "I’m your husband, come back, don’t be the same. From cities and families, I’ll gather you near, Bring you to Zion, where you’ll have no fear.
Shepherds will guide with wisdom to share, When you multiply, my covenant you’ll no longer bear. Jerusalem, Yahweh’s Throne, all nations will come, No more stubborn hearts, just a unified hum.
Judah and Israel, together they'll stand, Out of the north to the promised land. I long to place you among sons, give you lands of delight, “You’ll call me Father, follow me right."

But like a wife who leaves, Israel’s broken the pact, Weeping on heights, for Yahweh they lacked. "Return," says Yahweh, "and I’ll heal your ways, We acknowledge, you're our God, through all our days.
Help from the hills, and mountains, all in vain, Salvation's in Yahweh, remember His name. Our shame has eaten the work of our hands, With flocks, herds, daughters, and sons across the lands.
In shame we'll lie, with confusion in place, We’ve sinned from youth, turned from God's face."
"If you return, Israel," Yahweh's decree, "Put away your sins, come back to me. Swear truth and justice, righteousness too, In me, the nations will find what's true."
"Break up your ground, don't sow with thorns, Circumcise your hearts, my wrath warns. A trumpet in Judah, let the cry ring, Head for the cities, let safety cling."
"A lion emerges, destruction rides, Your land laid waste, where no one hides. Sackcloth and lament, Yahweh's anger fierce, The king's heart fails, priests' shock will pierce."
"Ah, Lord Yahweh!" I cried in dismay, "Peace you promised, but swords betray." A hot wind scorches, judgment draws near, Swift as eagles, chariots appear.
"Jerusalem, cleanse from wickedness, How long will evil in your heart rest? From Dan a voice, a cry from the hills, Watchers surround, with hostile wills."
"Your deeds bring this pain, bitter the taste, Destruction comes, nothing left to waste. Foolish people, skillful in sin, No knowledge of good, nowhere to begin."
"I saw the earth, void and bare, The mountains trembled, shadows in the air. Cities fallen, Yahweh's wrath descends, Yet a full end, he suspends."
"The land mourns, the skies turn black, I've spoken, no turning back. Cities flee from horsemen's might, Forsaken thickets, no soul in sight."
"Adorned in vain, lovers despise, Amidst desolation, hear Zion's cries. A voice like a mother in labor's pain, 'Woe is me!' is the mournful refrain."
Run the streets of Jerusalem, look and seek, Find a just man, truth they speak. If you do, pardon I'll grant, Though they swear by Me, it's just a chant.
"Yahweh sees truth," but they've gone astray, Struck, ungrieved, turned away. Faces harder than stone, they refuse to learn, To the great men, now I must turn.
But even the wise have broken the yoke, The bonds they burst, their promises broke. A lion, a wolf, a leopard on the prowl, Transgressions many, sin on the prowl.
"How can I pardon?" Yahweh cries, Children forsake, believe in lies. Fed and full, yet they stray, Neighing for lust, night and day.
"Shall I not punish?" Yahweh demands, "Go tear the walls, obey My commands. Israel, Judah, treacherous they’ve been, Denied Yahweh, in deceit they spin."
Prophets like wind, words are gone, With fire and wood, they'll be undone. A nation comes, mighty and vast, Language unknown, like shadows they cast.
Eating harvests, daughters' bread, Beating cities, leaving dread. "But even then," Yahweh's grace, "I won't end you, just leave a trace."
When questioned why these things you face, "Foreign gods you've chased, now displaced." Hear this, foolish, without sight, Eyes and ears closed tight.
"Don't you fear Me?" Yahweh asks, Sea bounds I set, waves in tasks. Yet hearts are hard, revolting they've gone, Forgotten the rain, the harvest's dawn.
Iniquities turn blessings away, Wicked men trap, lead astray. Rich in deceit, fat and bright, Neglect the needy, ignore the plight.
"Shall I not punish?" Yahweh declares, Horrible deeds, nobody cares. Prophets lie, priests mislead, And My people love the deceit they feed.
So what will you do when the end is near? With truth ignored, in trembling fear?
"Flee for safety, Benjamins, run out of town, Blow that trumpet loud, let the warning go around.
Evil's coming from the north, destruction's in its eyes, The delicate daughter of Zion, she cries and sighs.
Shepherds and their flocks will camp on her ground, They’ll pitch tents around her, a siege all around.
"Prepare for war! Get up, it's noon, and we're late, Shadows grow long, but we won't hesitate."
"By night we’ll rise, destroy her grand halls, Her palaces will crumble, her pride will fall."
Yahweh of Armies says, "Cut down the trees, Build a mound 'gainst the city, bring her to her knees.
Oppression flows like water from a well, Violence within her, a never-ending tale to tell."
"Jerusalem, heed, or be desolate, alone, An uninhabited land, where no seeds are sown."
"They'll glean Israel like grapes off the vine, Hand to basket, not leaving a sign."
"To whom can I speak, who’ll hear my word? Their ears are blocked, my voice unheard."
"I'm weary from holding wrath inside, Pour it on the young, there’s nowhere to hide."
"Houses and fields will be given away, For my hand stretches over them today."
"From least to greatest, they're greedy for gain, Prophets and priests, they lie without shame.
Crying 'Peace, peace!' when there ain't none to find, Ashamed? Not at all, they're out of their mind."
"Stand by the roads, ask for paths of old, Find the good way, let your soul be consoled."
"Listen to the trumpet, watchmen call aloud, But they cover their ears, defiant and proud."
"Listen up nations, hear what’s said, Evil's coming, it’s what their thoughts bred."
"Frankincense and cane, your offerings fall flat, I won't accept them, what's up with that?"
"Stumbling blocks set before father and son, Neighbors and friends, all will be undone."
"A people rise from the north, a nation stirred, Cruel and fierce, their war cries heard.
With bow and spear, they ride like the sea, Against you, daughter of Zion, no chance to flee."
"Hands grow weak, we're gripped by fear, Anguish like labor, the danger’s near."
"Don't go to the fields, stay off the way, Enemy swords and terror every day."
"Put on sackcloth, roll in the ash, Cry for the loss, like losing your last."
"I’ve made you a tester, a fortress to see, Their rebellious ways, their slanderous spree."
"Bellows blow, the lead's in the fire, In vain they refine, wickedness won't tire."
"Rejected silver, that's what they'll be, For Yahweh's rejected their deceit and greed."
Yo, Jeremiah got a word, straight from Yahweh's mouth, "Stand at the gate, preach to Judah, north and south."
He said, "Listen up, here’s what Yahweh commands, Change your ways, and dwell in this land.
Don't believe the lies, 'Yahweh’s temple, temple,' they say, If you do right, you'll stay, if you obey.
Do justice, protect the weak and the poor, Don't shed blood or worship gods anymore.
Then this land's yours, like I promised your kin, Ancient forever, but now you're caught in sin.
You're trusting in words that won't do a thing, Steal, murder, lie, then Baal's praises you sing.
Come to my house, think you're safe and free, Doing all these wrongs, thinking no one will see.
"This house a den of robbers?" Yahweh cries, "I've seen it myself with my own eyes.
Go to Shiloh, where my name used to dwell, Look what I did there 'cause they didn't do well.
You've ignored my calls, my early rise, So Shiloh's fate will be your demise.
Cast you out, like Ephraim's crew, Don't pray for these people, I won't hear you.
In Judah's cities, Jerusalem's streets, Children gather wood, women knead sweets.
To the queen of heaven, offerings they pour, Thinking they're safe, but provoking me more.
"Is it me you anger?" Yahweh asks, "Or is it yourselves with your foolish tasks?"
My wrath's coming, gonna pour it strong, On man, beast, trees, it won't be long.
"Bring your offerings, add ‘em to your meat, I didn't ask for sacrifices when I made you free.
I said, 'Hear my voice, walk in my way, Be my people, and have a brighter day.'
But you turned away, stubborn hearts won, Backward you went, progress undone.
Sent prophets early, day after day, But you shut your ears, pushed them away.
Speak these words, they won't heed, Call them out, they won’t concede.
"This is a nation, deaf to God's voice, Truth has vanished, they've made their choice.
Cut your hair, lament on the high, Yahweh’s rejected, His anger's nigh.
Judah’s done evil, defiled His name, Built high places, to their shame.
Burning children in Topheth’s fire, Never commanded, nor was it desired.
The valley of slaughter it shall be called, Bodies for birds, no one appalled.
Glad voices in cities will end, Bride and groom’s joy, no longer lend.
Jerusalem's streets, Judah's ground, Will lie in waste, no joy to be found."
"At that time," Yahweh declared with force, Bones of kings and priests, they'll take their course.
Out from graves, spread beneath the sky, Worshipped the sun, moon, stars on high.
Not gathered, not buried, like dung they’ll lie, Death's preferred, life denied, they sigh.
"Do men fall and not rise up once more? Why does Jerusalem backslide, ignore?"
Clinging to deceit, they refuse to hear, No repentance, no echo of fear.
Like horses rushed to battle they fly, The crane knows the time, but my people ask why.
"We are wise," they claim, but it's a tale, The scribes' false pen, a deceitful trail.
Wise men dismayed, trapped in their plight, Rejected Yahweh, wisdom's taken flight.
Wives to others, fields will change hand, From least to greatest, greed fills the land.
"Peace, peace," they say, but it’s nothing but lies, No shame in sin, no blush, no cries.
"I will consume," Yahweh's decree, No figs, no grapes, bare the vine and tree.
"Why sit still? Assemble, take the silent road, For Yahweh has given us a bitter load."
Expected peace, but only dismay, Horses from Dan, the land to betray.
"I send serpents to bite and to sting," In sorrow, my heart’s a broken thing.
From distant lands, a cry rings out, "Is Yahweh in Zion?" They shout.
Provoked to anger with idols and pride, "Harvest has passed, salvation denied."
For Zion's daughter, my heart does mourn, Where’s the balm in Gilead for hearts torn?
Oh, my head's a waterfall, my eyes a spring of tears, Weep night and day for my people's fallen peers.
Wish I could find a place way out in the wild, Leave behind the treacherous, every deceitful child.
"They bend their tongues like bows, shooting lies," "They grow strong, not for truth, but for evil's ties," Yahweh cries.
"Watch your neighbor, trust no brother at all, They'll supplant and slander, watch you fall."
Friends lie, truth's a rare thing they speak, Lies roll off their tongues, makes them weak.
"In deceit, they live, refusing to know me," Through treachery, they refuse to see," says He.
So Yahweh speaks, "I'll melt and test their ways, How should I deal with these deceitful days?
Their tongues are arrows, deadly deceit they spread, Speak peace, but in their hearts, ambush lies ahead.
Shouldn't I punish them?" Yahweh asks with might, "Shouldn't My soul find vengeance, make it right?
I'll weep for the mountains, lament the scorched land, The birds and beasts gone, wilderness unmanned.
Jerusalem, I'll make heaps, jackals their home, Judah's cities desolate, where no one will roam."
Who can understand, who's wise to declare? The land's burnt up, like a wilderness, bare.
Yahweh says, "They've left my laws behind, Walked in stubbornness, Baals in their mind."
"Behold, I'll feed them wormwood's bitter drink, Poisoned water, scatter them, making them rethink.
Call the mourning women, let their cries rise high, Teach daughters lamentation, let tears never dry."
Death's crawling in windows, invading palaces grand, Cutting off children, young men in the land.
Yahweh's word, hear it loud and clear, "Dead bodies like dung, no one will come near."
"Don't the wise boast in wisdom, or the mighty in might, Or the rich in riches, for I am the light."
"Glory in knowing Me, kindness and justice I seek, Righteousness on earth, it's my delight," Yahweh speaks.
"Behold, days will come," Yahweh says with power, "I'll punish the circumcised only in outward hour.
Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab will learn, For all uncircumcised in heart, my wrath will burn."

Hear the word Yahweh drops, house of Israel, stand tall, "Don't follow the nations, don't fear their sky signs at all. The customs they chase are empty and vain, Cutting trees from the forest, craftsmen's work with the grain.
They deck with silver and gold, fasten with nails, But those idols, like palm trees, motionless tales. Don't fear 'em, they can't do harm or good, There's no one like Yahweh, understood?
You're great, Yahweh, your name's got might, Who would dare not fear you, King in the light? The wise men of nations, in their royal plan, Stand foolish and brutish, just wood in their hand.
They craft with silver from Tarshish, gold from Uphaz, Blue and purple clothes, their skill's just a jazz. But Yahweh's true, the living King, At his wrath, earth shakes, nations can't cling.

"You shall tell them: 'Gods not making the skies, Will perish from earth, under heavens, they lie.'" He's made earth with power, world with wisdom laid, He speaks, waters roar, vapors from the earth made.
Lightning for rain, wind from his hoard, Men brutish, goldsmiths aboard. Images fail, no breath, no life, Just vanity and delusion in strife.
Jacob's portion isn't like these, Maker of all, tribe of his ease. "Gather your wares," Yahweh calls with might, "Sling out the land’s folk, distress 'em tight."
"Woe is me," the cry's intense, "My wound is deep, and I bear the expense. Tent destroyed, cords broken, children gone, No one to pitch my tent, to carry on."
Shepherds foolish, no inquiry made, Flocks scattered, prosperity delayed. News from the north, a commotion's sound, Judah's cities to jackals, desolation found.
"Yahweh, correct me, but gentle, be mild, Not in anger, don't waste your child. Pour wrath on nations, unknown to your name, They've devoured Jacob, left only shame."
Jeremiah heard a word from Yahweh, clear and bright, "Speak to Judah, to Jerusalem, in the pale moonlight.
Tell them Yahweh says, 'Cursed is the one who won't hear, The words of this covenant, so perfectly clear.
I led your fathers from Egypt, from the furnace so hot, Said, "Obey my voice, do what I taught."
Be my people, and I'll be your God, see, I swore to your fathers, a land of milk and honey.'
I said, 'Amen, Yahweh,' echoing the call, In Judah's cities, Jerusalem's streets, I told them all.
'Listen to this covenant, do what is right, I warned your fathers from morning till night.
But they turned away, in their own hearts' desire, I brought the covenant's words, and now they're under fire.'
Yahweh said, 'A conspiracy in Judah unfolds, They chase other gods, breaking promises of old.
I'm bringing evil, no escape from the dread, They'll call to me, but I'll turn my head.
To their gods they will cry, who won't save them at all, A god for each city, to Baal they fall.'
So don't pray for them, no cries, no pleas, I won't hear them, down on their knees.
What has my beloved done, in my house so defiled? Lewdness abounds, holy flesh exiled.
I called you a green olive tree, beauty in sight, But a roar kindled fire, branches broken in the night.
Yahweh of Armies, planted you strong, Now brings evil, because they did wrong.
He showed me their doings, secrets they planned, I was like a lamb, led by the hand.
They said, 'Destroy the tree, his name erase,' But Yahweh of Armies, sees and keeps pace.
Yahweh says, 'Men of Anathoth, seek your life, Say, "Don't prophesy, or meet the knife."
But Yahweh says, 'Punishment will come their way, Young men by the sword, no more light of day.
No remnant left, no sons or daughters to mourn, The year of their visitation, wrath will be born.'"
When I talk to you, Yahweh, you're always right, But I've got questions under this night: Why do the wicked thrive and get ahead? Why are the tricky ones so well-fed?
You planted them, they've taken root, They're growing tall, producing fruit. Your name's on their lips, but hearts are cold, Near in word, far in soul, that's bold.
But you, Yahweh, you know my name, You see my heart, you test my frame. "Pull them out like sheep to the slaughter, Prepare their end, that's what they oughta."
How long will the land weep and mourn, While plants and beasts are wrecked and torn? The wicked say, "He won't see our fate," But their time's coming, it ain't too late.
"If footmen tire you out, what then with horse? In peace you're safe, but what about the Jordan's force? Even your own kin, your family line, Acted false, don't trust their kind words, fine."
"I've left my house, my heritage I cast, Handed over to foes, it's gone at last. My land's a lion, roaring against me, Turned away from her, let it be."
Is my land a prey, surrounded by birds? Gather the beasts, let actions match words. Shepherds have wrecked my cherished place, Made it mourn, a desolate space.
Destruction's come from high to low, Yahweh's sword cuts to and fro. Wheat they planted, but thorns they got, Worked so hard, yet profit they did not.
Yahweh says, "To those who steal my land, I'll pluck you up, with my own hand. But after wrath, comes compassion’s call, Back they'll come, each one and all."
"If they learn my ways and speak my name, Like they once spoke Baal's in shame, They'll stand with my people, strong and tall, But if not, I'll pluck and end it all," says Yahweh, echoing the hall.
Yahweh told me, "Go get a linen belt, wear it on your waist, don't let it melt." So I grabbed that belt, did just like He said, placed it on my waist, let His word be led.
Then He spoke again, "Take that belt you got, head to the Euphrates, find a rocky spot." I hid it there, the belt in the cleft of stone, followed His command, left it all alone.
After many days, "Go back," He said, "retrieve the belt from the place where it was bed." So I dug it out, saw it worn and torn, ruined and useless, its purpose all forlorn.
Then Yahweh spoke, "Judah’s pride I’ll break, just like this belt, their hearts I’ll shake. These stubborn folks, who won’t hear My call, who chase other gods, will stumble and fall.
For like a belt clings tight around the waist, Israel and Judah were meant to be embraced," says Yahweh, "but they turned away, left My name, My glory, in disarray."

"Speak to them," He said, "Yahweh now proclaims, 'Fill every jar with wine,' let it be their game." They'll ask, "Don't we know jars should be filled?" But Yahweh says, "I’ll fill them with what I’ve willed.
Drunkenness will strike the kings on their throne, priests, prophets, and people shall all be overthrown. 'I'll smash them together, father and son, no pity or compassion will be shown to anyone.'”
Listen up now, don’t let pride consume, for Yahweh has spoken, darkness will loom. Honor your God before shadows arise, and stumbling feet on dark mountains realize.
If you refuse, I’ll mourn for your pride, tears will fall for the flock taken aside. To king and queen mother, "Humble, sit down, your crowns are gone, lost is your renown."
Locked are the cities, no one to release, Judah’s captive, taken without peace. Look to the north, see what comes your way, where is your flock, who’ll lead you astray?
When friends turn to foes, sorrows will grip, like a woman in labor, they'll surely rip. Ask yourself why these have come to pass, your sins revealed, you’ve been caught at last.
Can a leopard change spots? Can skin be shed? Only then can evil turn to good instead. I’ll scatter them like chaff in the wild, it’s their lot, their trust in lies beguiled.
Your shame exposed, your deeds laid bare, your abominations, like a snare. Woe to Jerusalem, will you ever be clean? How long will it take for purity to be seen?"
Yahweh's word came down, Jeremiah in sight, Judah mourns, gates weep in the night.
On the ground they sit, dressed in black, Crying out, Jerusalem's lacking slack.
Nobles send kids to seek the water's flow, Cisterns empty, heads hung low.
Ground cracked, no rain in sight, Plowmen's hope takes flight.
Doe in the field, leaves young behind, No grass grows, the earth's unkind.
Wild donkeys stand on barren height, Pant like jackals, eyes lose light.
"Our sins scream out, but for your name's grace, Savior of Israel, don't turn your face."
"Why appear like a stranger to us, A traveler who won't stay, causing fuss?"
Yahweh in the midst, we're called by His name, "Don't leave us," we plead, "it's not the same."
Yahweh says, "They love to wander, Feet unrestrained, hearts grow fonder.
I won't accept them, their iniquity's clear, Punishment comes, it's drawing near."
"Don't pray for their good, I won't hear, Fasting or offering, none'll draw me near."
Sword, famine, pestilence, Yahweh's decree, False prophets speak lies, misleading spree.
"Visions they claim, I did not send, Deception in hearts, false messages blend."
Prophets, people alike, streets will fill, No burial for them, wickedness spill.
"I'll let tears flow, night and day, Virgin daughter broken, hope in dismay."
Fields filled with slain, cities with grief, Prophet and priest walk in disbelief.
"Utter rejection? Zion's wounds won't heal, Hope for peace vanishes, truth is revealed."
"Acknowledge our sins, Yahweh, we see, Don't break your covenant, set us free.
No nation's idols bring rain from the sky, Yahweh our God, hear our cry."
Therefore we wait for what Yahweh can bring, He alone makes life through everything.
"Even Moses and Samuel can't change my mind, This people must go, leave them all behind.
When they ask, 'Where do we go?' you'll reply, 'Yahweh says: Death, sword, famine, or captivity's sky.'
Four kinds I appoint," Yahweh declares, "Sword to kill, dogs to tear, birds and beasts everywhere.
Tossed among kingdoms for Manasseh's crime, Jerusalem's fate sealed in his wicked time.
Who will weep for you, who will care? You've rejected me, you've got despair.
I've stretched my hand, now you're destroyed, My compassion's gone, I'm annoyed.
Winnowed at the gates, bereaved of kin, Destruction's here, won't turn from sin.
Widows multiplied like sand by the sea, Noonday destroyer, terror suddenly.
Seven's mother weak, her spirit departed, Sun sets early, dreams thwarted, disheartened.
Woe is me, born into strife, Cursed though I lent neither debt nor life.
But Yahweh says, "I'll make you strong, Enemies will beg when things go wrong.
Can iron be broken, iron and bronze? Your treasures plundered, sins' response.
Enemies will take you to lands unknown, My fire burns, my anger's grown."
Remember me, Yahweh, don't forget, Patiently I wait, don't leave me yet.
Your words are joy, they fill my heart, I'm called by your name, set apart.
I didn't join in joy, alone I stayed, Filled with your anger, indignation's blade.
Why's my pain unending, wound unhealed? Will you be like a brook, waters concealed?
Yahweh says, "Return, I bring you back, Separate the precious, stay on track.
I'll make you a wall, bronze fortified, They'll fight but won't conquer, I'm by your side.
Deliverance from wicked hands, Redeemed from terrors, Yahweh stands."
Yahweh spoke, and it was clear to me, "Don't marry here or let your children be." For those born and raised in this land's embrace, Will meet grim fates, with no memorial trace.
"They'll die without tears, unburied they'll lay, Like waste on the ground, swept away. By sword and famine they'll find their doom, Feast for the birds, 'neath the sky's wide room."
Yahweh said, "Don't mourn or wail, I've pulled back my peace, my love will fail. Great and small will perish here, No one will mourn or shed a tear.
No bread of comfort, no solace to find, For mother or father, they're left behind. Don't join the feasts, don't eat or drink, Stay away from joy, let your heart sink."
Yahweh of Armies declares with might, "I'll silence joy from day to night. Bride and groom's voices will fade away, In your sight, in your day."
When they ask, "Why such doom and gloom?" Tell them, "For forsaking me, they sealed their doom. Chasing gods not of me, they strayed, Ignoring my law, my voice betrayed."
"You've done worse than those who came before, Following evil hearts, you shut the door. I'll cast you to lands unknown, There you'll serve gods made of stone."
But Yahweh says, "One day will come, When talk of Egypt's deliverance is done. Instead, they'll speak of the north's escape, And return to the land that was once their shape."
"I'll send fishermen to gather you back, Hunters will find you from every crack. My eyes see all, nothing's concealed, Their sins will be doubled, their fate revealed."
Yahweh, my strength, my refuge you are, Nations will come from lands afar. "Our fathers' lies we'll now disown, Crafted gods of wood and stone."
"Behold, I’ll make them see, My power, my hand, my identity. Then they'll know my name, Yahweh's the same."
Judah's sin, carved with an iron pen, Etched deep in hearts, on altars again. Children remember those high hills, green, Where poles of Asherah are always seen.
"My mountain, your treasures, plundered wide, For sins all across borders, they can't hide. You'll leave the heritage I gave, it's true, Serve enemies, in lands you never knew.
Cursed is the man who trusts in flesh alone, Like a desert bush, parched to the bone. Blessed is the soul who trusts in Me, Like a tree by the water, roots spread free.
He won't fear drought, his leaves stay green, In his fruitfulness, abundance is seen. The heart's deceitful, who can understand? I search the heart, and judge by every hand."
Riches gained not right, like eggs not laid, Soon leave the fool, where fake riches fade. A throne on high from the start's our claim, Yahweh, our hope, forsake Him, feel shame.
"Heal me, Yahweh," I cry, "and make me whole, Save me, for You are praise in my soul. They ask, 'Where's Yahweh's word?' Let them see, I follow, not rushing from Your decree.
Be my refuge when days turn vile, Disappoint them, who seek to defile. Don't let me stumble; let them fall, Bring double destruction on them all."
Yahweh said, "Stand at the gate, and call, Tell kings, Judah, hear Me all. No burdens on Sabbath, keep it pure, Just as I commanded before, for sure.
Yet they stiffened necks, refused the word, If you listen, your voices will be heard. Kings will come, on David's throne they'll ride, From near and far, they'll come inside.
Burnt offerings, sacrifice, they'll bring, Praises rise, to Yahweh, they'll sing. But if you won't listen, if you disobey, Fire will burn, consume the gates that day."
Yahweh spoke, "Jeremiah, rise and go, To the potter's house, where my words will flow." Down I went, saw the potter at his wheel, Crafting clay vessels, his skill was real.
The vessel marred, in his hands it lay, But he molded anew, in his own way. Then Yahweh spoke, "House of Israel, see, Just like this potter, you are clay to me.
I can break or build, pluck or plant, Turn from evil, or face what you can't. But if you disobey, turn from the light, The good I planned will vanish from sight.
Tell Judah and Jerusalem my plan, "Return from your ways, change while you can." But they say, ‘It's useless, we’ll follow our heart,’ Each stubbornly walking their own evil part.
Yahweh questions, “Among nations, who’s seen Such betrayal, such a terrible scene? Snow in Lebanon doesn’t fail to fall, Yet my people forget me, they heed no call.
They burn incense to gods that are fake, Walk twisted paths, ignoring what's at stake. Their land will be ruined, a hissing sound, Passersby shaking their heads all around.
Scattered by the east wind, enemies near, I’ll turn my back, calamity’s fear.” They plot against me, "Let's strike him, they say, Jeremiah's words, let's keep them at bay."
"Yahweh, hear me, they scheme my demise, I stood for them, tried to open their eyes. Yet they’ve repaid me with a pit of despair, Now let their cries echo in the air.

Let their children face famine, and swords take their men, Their plots against me bring judgment again. Don’t forgive their sins, let them face your might, Deal with them, Yahweh, in your anger's sight."
Yahweh spoke, "Go buy a potter's clay, With elders by your side, hear what I say.
To Hinnom's valley, follow the gate, Proclaim my words, don't hesitate.
"Listen up, Judah's kings, Jerusalem's crew, Yahweh of Armies has a message for you:
I'll bring a sound that'll make ears ring, On this land, chaos I'll bring.
They abandoned me, defiled this space, Offered incense, brought disgrace.
Baal's altars built high in the air, Children burned, they didn't care.
I never spoke or thought this plan, Now this valley's fate, understand:
Soon it'll be 'Slaughter,' not what you know, Judah and Jerusalem's counsel will go.
By the sword, they'll meet their doom, Birds and beasts will feast in gloom.
People aghast, they'll hiss and stare, Plagues will leave them in despair.
In siege, they'll eat their kin, Desperation thick, can't win."
Break the pot, shatter it on the ground, Say, "Yahweh's wrath will resound.
This city's broken, no mending it back, Topheth's their grave, under the attack.
Houses defiled, incense on the dome, Poured drinks to gods, far from home."
Jeremiah left, to the court he went, Spoke Yahweh's words, his message sent.
"On this city, every curse will fall, For they stiffened their necks, ignored my call."
Pashhur heard Jeremiah, prophet's voice loud and clear, But instead of listening, he struck him, put him near.
In the stocks at the gate, Jeremiah was confined, Next day, Pashhur released him, but a new name he'd find.
Jeremiah spoke, "Your name ain't Pashhur no more, It's Magormissabib, 'cause terror's what's in store."
"Yahweh declares, 'Terror to you and your friends, By the sword's cruel edge, Judah's storied line ends.
In Babylon, they'll carry treasures away, And there you'll end, in a foreign land stay.
All your riches and gains, precious things so fine, Into enemy hands, each will now align.
You and your house, in captivity bound, In Babylon's dust, your resting place found.'"
Jeremiah cried, "Yahweh, you pulled me in tight, Stronger than me, you prevail in this fight.
I've become a laughingstock, mocked every day, Crying 'Violence and destruction!' they say.
His word's in my heart like a fire in my bones, I can't hold it in, despite all the groans.
'Terror on every side!' they whisper and plot, Waiting for me to stumble, revenge they sought.
But Yahweh's with me, mighty and true, Persecutors stumble, their shame will accrue.
Yahweh of Armies, you test deep inside, Let me see your vengeance, in you I confide.
Sing to Yahweh! Praise His mighty hand, Saved the needy soul from the evildoers' band.
Cursed be the day that I first drew breath, The birth that brought joy now wishes for death.
Cursed the man who brought news, 'A boy's born today!' In ruined cities, let him ever stay.
Why, oh why, did I emerge from the womb? To face toil and sorrow, a future of gloom."
Jeremiah got a word from Yahweh, you know, Zedekiah sent Pashhur and Zephaniah to go. "Ask Yahweh for us," they said, with fear in their eyes, "King Nebuchadnezzar's coming, bringing war and cries."

Jeremiah said, "Listen, tell Zedekiah this, Yahweh's got a message, nothing you can dismiss: ‘I’ll turn back your weapons, what you hold in your hand, The Chaldeans are coming, they're gonna take a stand.
I’ll fight against you, with anger and might, Striking down man and beast, a terrible sight. Pestilence will sweep through, everyone will fall, Nobody's safe behind these city walls.
After that,’ says Yahweh, ‘Zedekiah will be caught, Delivered to the king of Babylon, what a plot! No mercy will be shown, swords will gleam, Against those left standing by the enemy team.’"
"Tell the people this," Yahweh's words began, "Two paths lie ahead, for every woman and man: Stay in the city, die from sword, famine, pest, Leave to the Chaldeans, and live, that’s the test.
My face is set against this city in wrath, It'll burn in the fire, as a witness of my path."
To the house of Judah, Yahweh's words so clear, "Justice and deliverance, every morning, hear. Or my wrath will blaze, a fire from your deeds, Punishment will come, like flames in the reeds.
I’m against you, O valley, O rock of the plain, You think you're untouchable, but it’s all in vain. I’ll punish you by what you’ve done, hear my word, Kindling a fire, devouring all you’ve heard."
Yo, Yahweh sends a message, clear and tight, To the king of Judah, gotta get it right. "Listen up, hear what I say, Justice and righteousness, do it today.
Save the oppressed, make it your quest, No wrong, no violence, put it to rest. Treat the foreigner, widow, and child right, Shed no innocent blood, don’t start a fight.
If you do this, kings will roll in style, Chariots, horses, mile after mile. But if you don't hear, let me make it plain, This house, desolation, nothing will remain."
Judah's house, you're precious like Gilead, But soon, deserted, you'll be sad. Destroyers with weapons, they’ll come fast, Your cedars cut, into the fire cast.
Nations passing by, they’ll wonder why, "Why did Yahweh let this great city die?" They’ll answer back, "Abandoned the covenant, Worshiped false gods, that’s the judgment."
Don't cry for the dead, but weep for the lost, Never returning, they’ve paid the cost. Shallum's gone, he won't come back, In foreign lands, his life's on track.
"Woe to builders of unrighteous walls, Who cheat their neighbors, in justice falls. Build wide houses, fancy and grand, But justice and mercy, they don't understand."
Your father's ways were right and just, He knew Yahweh, did what he must. But your eyes are greedy, shedding blood, Oppression and violence, it's in your flood.
Jehoiakim, they won’t weep for you, Buried like a donkey, beyond the blue. Cry out from Lebanon, Bashan, and Abarim, All your allies gone, your future grim.
In prosperity, you turned away, Refused to listen, day by day. Now shame and disgrace, they’ll come to you, Your wicked ways, they’re coming through.
Coniah, if a ring on my hand you were, Still I'd pluck you, let me be clear. Into Babylon's hands, you will fall, Not your land, but there’s your call.
Into exile, with your mother too, In strange lands, your life’s anew. Earth, hear Yahweh, loud and bold, Coniah's line, no more to hold.
No offspring will prosper, no throne to see, Ruling in Judah, it will not be."
"Woe to the shepherds," Yahweh's voice is clear, "They scatter my sheep, no visit, nowhere near.
You've driven them away, left them all alone, Now I'll visit your evil, make it known.
I'll gather my flock from lands far and wide, Bring 'em back to their folds, let 'em thrive inside.
New shepherds will rise, feed them right and true, Fear and dismay? Nah, they'll never pursue.
"Behold the days," Yahweh says with might, "A Branch from David will rise, set it right.
Judah saved, Israel at peace, he'll reign, Yahweh our Righteousness, his holy name.
The days are coming, no longer will be said, 'Yahweh brought Israel from Egypt,' instead,
'He led them from the north, every scattered clan, To dwell in their land, held by Yahweh's hand.'
Prophets, oh prophets, my heart is broke, Bones shake like a man who just awoke.
The land's full of curse, wilderness dried, Prophets and priests, in profane paths they stride.
Slippery darkness, they'll fall, not rise, Evil on them, Yahweh's justice flies.
Samaria's prophets, folly seen, Prophesied by Baal, they've been mean.
In Jerusalem's prophets, adultery, lies, Evildoers they strengthen, no one denies.
"Like Sodom, like Gomorrah," Yahweh cries out, Wormwood and poison, their fate devout.
"Don't heed their words," Yahweh warns, They speak visions from hearts that scorn.
"Who stood in my council?" Yahweh asks, To hear my word, to take on the tasks?
Yahweh's storm, a whirlwind will break, On the wicked's head, wrath he won't forsake.
Prophets ran, but I never sent, They spoke, but from me they're absent.
"Am I not near?" Yahweh demands, "Filling heaven and earth by my hands.
I've heard their lies, 'A dream! A dream!' they said, Forget my name, by dreams they're led.
The dreamer tells dreams, my word's the truth, "Isn't my word like fire?" Yahweh's proof.
Against false prophets, Yahweh stands, They steal my words, without my commands.
Lying dreams, they cause deceit, I never sent them, their words are weak.
When asked for Yahweh's message, here's your cue, "What message?" Yahweh says, "I cast off you."
Prophet, priest, people who claim my word, Punishment on them, justice deferred.
From your mouths, no more will my message flow, You've twisted my words, turned them into show.
The message from Yahweh, forget it for good, Perpetual shame, misunderstood."
Yahweh showed a vision, two baskets in view, After Babylon's king had taken Judah's crew.
One basket had figs that were ripe and sweet, While the other held figs that no one could eat.
Yahweh asked, "Jeremiah, what do you see?" I saw good figs and bad figs, clear as can be.
Then the word of Yahweh came to me, "Like these good figs, Judah’s captives I'll set free.
I'll watch over them, bring them back to this land, I'll build them up strong, with my own hand.
"I'll give them hearts that know I am Yahweh, They'll be my people, and walk in my way.
But those bad figs, they're beyond repair, Zedekiah and his kind won't find my care.
"To every kingdom, they'll be tossed around, A curse, a taunt, wherever they're found.
I'll send sword, famine, pestilence in my wrath, Till they're wiped from the land, down to the last."
That's the vision, clear and bold, The fate of Judah, plainly told.
Jeremiah got the word, Judah was in his sight, Fourth year of Jehoiakim, Babylon's first flight. For twenty-three years, I've spoken day by day, But y'all ain't listening, just turn away.
Prophets sent early, God's voice in their stride, “Turn from your evil, in the land abide. Don't chase other gods, don't provoke my wrath, Then I'll keep you safe, stay on my path.”
But you ignored, turned your ear away, Provoking anger, bringing judgment your way. Yahweh speaks, "You heard not my cries, So Babylon's comin', it's time to rise."
Nebuchadnezzar, my servant, will come, Turn your land to shock, make you feel numb. No joy or laughter, bride's voice will cease, Mirth turned to mourning, no light, no peace.
Seventy years, Babylon holds sway, Then I'll bring judgment, they'll repay. Desolation to the land, Chaldeans fall, Great kings rise, and Babylon crawls.
"Take this cup, wrath’s bitter drink, Nations will stagger, they'll fall, they'll sink. Sword in hand, make them reel, Jerusalem, Judah, all will feel."
Kings and lands, from Egypt to Uz, Philistines, Ammon, each has a buzz. The north, the south, all will drink, God’s wrath poured out, no time to think.
"Drink deep, feel the sword's might, Fall and rise no more, in the night. Yahweh calls, no nation unscathed, Sword on earth, His judgment engraved."
Proclaim His roar, His mighty shout, Judgment's here, no doubt about. From end to end, His controversy flows, Wicked to sword, His justice shows.
Evil storm, nation to nation, Yahweh's fury, no hesitation. Slain on earth, no one cries, On the ground, life's demise.
Shepherds wail, leaders weep, No escape, judgment's deep. Yahweh roars from His place, Land astonished, His fierce face.
In Jehoiakim’s reign, Yahweh’s word came, To Judah's cities, loud and clear, no shame.
“Stand in my house, deliver my decree, Speak every word, don’t omit, hear Me.
Maybe they’ll listen, turn from their wrong ways, I might hold back the wrath that for years it weighs.”
“Tell them,” Yahweh declared, “listen up, Walk in my law, don’t interrupt.
Heed my prophets, I send them to you, Rise early, sending, but you refuse.
If not, this house becomes Shiloh’s fate, This city a curse, destruction’s gate.”
Jeremiah spoke, the priests heard it all, They seized him quick, in Yahweh’s hall.
“You’ll die,” they cried, “for your prophecy, Calling this house Shiloh, city's desolate sea.”
Princes from the king’s house heard the scene, Sat by the gate, where the crowd had been.
Priests and prophets shouted, “He should die, He’s spoken against us, why, oh why?”
Jeremiah rose, his voice was strong, “Yahweh sent me to right this wrong.
Change your ways, listen to Yahweh’s call, He’ll relent from evil, no downfall.”
“Do as you will, I’m in your hand, But shed my blood, you’ll curse this land.”
Princes and people, they took a pause, “This man speaks truth, he breaks no laws.”
Elders stood up, their words rang through, “Micah spoke too, and Hezekiah knew.
Zion’s fields plowed, Jerusalem in heaps, Yet they didn’t kill him, Yahweh keeps.”
Another prophet, Uriah by name, Spoke like Jeremiah, met the same game.
Jehoiakim sought his life, Uriah fled, But from Egypt taken, soon he was dead.
Jeremiah spared by Ahikam’s hand, Protected from death, in Yahweh’s land.
In Jehoiakim's reign, a word came through, Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, here's what to do: "Make bonds, make bars, put them on your neck, Send them to the kings — show them respect.
To Edom and Moab, Ammon, and Tyre, Sidon too, with messengers — don't tire. Tell their masters this command from above, Yahweh of Armies, the God they should love.
'I made the earth, men, animals with power, Gave it as I saw fit, in the right hour. Now Nebuchadnezzar, Babylon's mighty king, Holds these lands — to him the nations bring.
All will serve him, son, and grandson, Till his time's up and his own land's gone. But if a nation won't bow under his yoke, They'll face sword, famine, pestilence — no joke.
Don't heed your prophets, dreamers, or those, Who say "Don't serve Babylon" — they're false, God knows. They're lying, pulling you from your land, I drive you out — it's Yahweh's hand.
But nations serving Babylon, that's the key, They'll stay on their land, live peacefully. Zedekiah, listen to these words I bring, Serve Babylon's king, find life in this thing.
Why die by sword, famine, pestilence, When Yahweh’s words show the consequence? Don't buy the lies of prophets that deceive, I didn't send them, don't be naive.
I spoke to priests and the people too, Yahweh says, "Don't let false words fool you. The vessels won't be back from Babylon fast, Their prophets lie — that tale won't last.
Serve Babylon, live — don't let the city fall, If they speak truth, let them to Yahweh call. The vessels in His house will stay away, Till Yahweh visits them one fine day.
Nebuchadnezzar didn't take 'em all, When Jeconiah and nobles heard the call. Yahweh of Armies says, vessels will go, To Babylon, till His visit — this you should know.
Then they'll return, restored to this place, Yahweh will bring them back, in His grace."
In the reign of Zedekiah, the scene was set, Hananiah spoke with a claim you won't forget. “In Yahweh’s house,” he said to the crowd, “‘I’ll break the yoke of Babylon!’” he vowed.
“In two years’ time, vessels will return, From Nebuchadnezzar’s grasp, watch them burn. Jeconiah and captives will come back too, The yoke of Babylon, I’ll break through.”
Jeremiah stood, his voice rang clear, “Amen, may Yahweh make it happen here. But listen now, to the word I proclaim, A prophet’s truth is known by the peace he can claim.”
Hananiah took the bar from Jeremiah’s neck, “Yahweh will break Babylon’s yoke,” he said in check. Jeremiah left, the moment intense, But Yahweh’s voice came, making perfect sense.
“Hananiah, your work is flawed, You break wooden bars, but here's the rod. Iron yokes on nations, Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, The animals too, under his domain.”
Jeremiah warned, his words did fly, “Hananiah, false prophet, you lead with a lie. Yahweh declares, your time is done, In this very year, your life's undone.”
In the seventh month, Hananiah fell, A prophet's life ended, with truth to tell.
Jeremiah writes from the city's core, To exiles far, behind Babylon's door.
He sends the word, to captives bound tight, Saying, "Live your lives, don't fight the night.
Build your homes and gardens, plant seeds in the ground, Grow your families, let your joy resound.
Seek the city's peace, and pray for its good, In its welfare, find your own livelihood.
Don't trust the false dreams, or prophets who lie, I didn't send them," says Yahweh, "they defy.
After seventy years, I'll bring you back home, With peace and hope, no more to roam.
Call on me, I'll hear, I'll be found by you, With all your heart, seek, find a future true.
I'll end your captivity, gather from the lands, Bring you back to where your freedom stands."
But for those who remain in the city alone, Yahweh's wrath comes, through sword and stone.
Rotten figs they'll be, scattered and lost, For ignoring my prophets, this is their cost.
Ahab and Zedekiah, liars in my name, To Babylon's fire, they'll be put to shame.
Shemaiah's words, false letters he sends, Punishment awaits, for him and his friends.
The captivity's lengthy, but do not despair, In the ground of your trial, sprout hope everywhere.
For Yahweh's plans are good, though long may it seem, In the end, you'll awaken from this distant dream.
Listen up, Jeremiah, hear what Yahweh’s sayin’, "Write it all down, every word I'm relayin'.
"The days will come when I’ll flip the scene, Bring back my people to where they’ve been.
Fear and trembling, voices of dread, But in the end, they'll rise from the dead.
Why do I see men holding their waist? Faces pale, like they've been chased.
A day unlike any, Jacob's in trouble, But he’ll be saved, make that hope double.
"On that day, I’ll break your chains, No more strangers with their reigns.
Serve Yahweh, and David will rise, Don't fear, Jacob, no more cries.
I'll save you from afar, your kids too, Bring you back home, safe and true.
I'm with you, says Yahweh, your guide, Nations fall, but you'll abide.
Your hurt's deep, wounds severe, Nobody to help, no cure near.
Lovers forgot you, left you alone, Your sins piled up, like a heavy stone.
Why weep over pain that won't go? For your wrongs, the punishment flows.
Those who devour will be devoured, Adversaries captured, no more empowered.
Health I’ll restore, heal those wounds, Zion the outcast, now renewed.
"I’ll bring back Jacob's tents, show compassion, City rebuilt, in glorious fashion.
Thankful songs from voices raised, Multiply them, be amazed.
Kids like before, strong congregation, Oppressors punished, no hesitation.
A prince from them, a ruler so bold, Draws near to me, hearts of gold.
"You’ll be my people, I’ll be your God, Watch Yahweh’s storm, striking hard.
His wrath won’t rest till it’s done, Understand it all when it's begun."
"At that time," Yahweh spoke with might, "I'll be Israel's God, in their hearts, alight." Survivors in the wild, they found my grace, Even when they wandered in a restless place.
"I loved you long, with love that won't fade, With kindness I drew you, though you've strayed." "I'll build you again, with tambourines in hand, Dance with joy across this promised land."
"Vineyards on Samaria's hills you'll plant anew, Watchmen call, ‘To Zion, let's go, me and you!’" "Sing for Jacob, shout for nations to hear, 'Save your people, Yahweh, bring them near.'"
From the north and farthest land, they'll form a throng, The blind, the lame, together they belong. With tears they'll come, led by rivers' gentle flow, "For I am their Father, I will make it so."
"Declare my word to distant shores, 'He scattered, He'll gather, like a shepherd restores.'" Ransomed from the stronger hand, now redeemed, To Zion they sing, to Yahweh's goodness streamed.
Like a watered garden, their souls will thrive, Young and old dance, mourning can't survive. "I'll turn their sorrow to joy," Yahweh decrees, "Satisfy the priests, my goodness will please."

But Rachel weeps, her children are no more, "Hold your tears," Yahweh whispers, "I'll restore." "They'll return from the enemy's grasp," He declares, "There's hope in the end, renewal in their lairs."
Ephraim's grief, like an untrained calf's cry, "Turn me, Yahweh, for I have gone awry." Confounded by shame, yet remembered dear, "My heart yearns for mercy, I'll draw him near."
"Set up signs, guide your heart back home, Turn again, Israel, no longer roam." "A new thing's created, a woman will surround, Judah's speech will bless, as they are unbound."
The weary, replenished, find rest at last, Yahweh's watch over them, unbroken, steadfast. "The days approach," Yahweh says with grace, "To sow Israel and Judah in this sacred space."

Their sour grapes no longer the children's fate, Each bears their iniquity, their own weight. "A new covenant I'll write on their hearts within, They'll know me, from least to greatest, cleansed of sin."
The sun and moon obey Yahweh's command, "If these depart, Israel won't stand," Yet Yahweh's promise holds the nation tight, "Forever they remain in my sight."
"The city's built, from Hananel's tower to the gate, Holy to Yahweh, in peace they'll wait." The land, once marred by death and decay, Is Yahweh's forever, unthrown and to stay."
In the tenth year of King Zedekiah's reign, Jeremiah locked up, prophecy brought him pain.
Babylon’s army was at Jerusalem’s door, Zedekiah asked, "Why spread these tales of war?"
"Yahweh speaks," Jeremiah did proclaim, "This city's Babylon's prize, it's not to remain.
Zedekiah won't escape, Babylon's king he'll meet, Face to face, his eyes he'll greet.
"They'll take the king to Babylon until I visit," declares Yahweh, "Fight all you want, but victory won't stay."
Jeremiah recounted, "Yahweh's word to me came, Hanamel's field in Anathoth, 'twas part of the game.
'Buy the field,' he said, ‘it's redemption time.’ When Hanamel approached, I knew it was divine.
Seventeen shekels weighed, the deal sealed and signed, Witnesses gathered, the legal deed aligned.
Baruch held the deed, in an earthen vessel stored, Houses and fields will rise again, declared the Lord."
Jeremiah prayed, "Ah Lord Yahweh, great is your might, You made the heavens and earth, nothing's beyond your sight.
Loving and kind, to thousands you show, Repaying the fathers for deeds long ago.
Signs in Egypt, your name's renowned, You delivered your people with miracles profound.
You gave them a land, milk and honey it flows, Yet they disobeyed, calamity now shows.
Siege ramps rise, Chaldeans take the city by sword, Yet you say, ‘Buy the field,’ oh Lord."
Then Yahweh spoke once more, "Is anything too hard, I'm the God of all, for sure.
The city to Chaldeans and Nebuchadnezzar will fall, They'll burn it down, despite cries and calls.
From youth, evil in my sight they've done, Provoked my anger, now they're on the run.
But I'll gather them back from lands far and wide, They'll dwell safely, with me they'll abide.
My people they'll be, I'll be their God, One heart, one way, they'll fear, they'll laud.
An everlasting covenant, I’ll not turn away, With joy I'll plant them, they’ll forever stay.
Fields will be bought, deeds signed anew, For I will reverse their captivity," declares Yahweh—the truth.
Locked up tight, but Yahweh spoke again, To Jeremiah in the guard's domain.
"Yahweh's my name, I form and I make, Call to me, great things I'll awake.
The city houses, broken down with might, Men fight the Chaldeans, fallen in the night.
But behold, health and cure I'll bring, Peace and truth, like a mighty spring.
Judah and Israel, I'll restore their place, Cleanse their sins, and grant them grace.
The city's name, a joy to behold, Nations will tremble at the story told.
Voices of joy, bride and groom they'll say, Thanks to Yahweh, His love will stay.
Flocks will roam once more in peace, In Judah's cities, new life will increase.
Behold the days, a Branch will rise, Justice and righteousness in David's eyes.
Judah saved, Jerusalem safe and sound, Yahweh our righteousness, all around.
David's throne will never stand bare, Priests will offer, a continual prayer.
If day and night can break apart, Then my covenant too will depart.
David's line, countless like the sand, Priests my ministers, they'll expand.
Don't say Yahweh's cast off chosen kin, For their captivity I'll turn, mercy will begin."
Yo, Jeremiah's got a word from Yahweh, it's dire, The king of Babylon's here, gonna set the city on fire.
"Zedekiah, listen up," Yahweh’s message is clear, "You can't escape Babylon, your fate’s drawing near."
"You’ll see the king face to face, eye to eye, But you'll go to Babylon, you won’t die by the sword, you'll die with a sigh."
"They'll mourn you like kings who’ve passed before, Burning incense, they’ll cry out, 'Ah Lord!' evermore."
Jeremiah spoke it, while battles raged on, Babylon’s army strong, and the cities nearly gone.
Then a covenant made, freedom proclaimed, Servants set free, but the people felt chained.
They turned and took back what they had let go, Yahweh's anger flared, his words began to flow:
"I freed your fathers from Egypt's land, Said every seventh year, release them, that was my command."
"You did right for a moment, then profaned my name, Brought back your servants, played this wicked game."
"Now hear me out, you’ve ignored my decree, So I’ll proclaim a freedom — to sword, plague, and misery."
"Enemies closing in, bodies left for the birds, Zedekiah and his princes, captured, you heard."
"I’ll bring Babylon back, make this city a blaze, Judah’s cities desolate, no one left to praise."
Word to Jeremiah, came straight from Yahweh, "Go to Rechabites, bring them, hear what they say.
Invite them in, offer wine in Yahweh’s house, Test their resolve, see if they stick to their vows."
So I gathered Jaazaniah, the whole Rechab crew, Led them to the room, where the sons of Hanan grew.
Bowls full of wine, I set before their eyes, Said, "Drink up, enjoy, don’t be shy."
But they replied, "No wine will touch our lips, Jonadab, our father, gave us these tips:
'No wine, no fields, no homes will we claim, In tents we dwell, nomads in name.'"
Obeyed Jonadab, their father’s command, No wine, no homes, just tents on this land.
But Babylon’s king brought fear to the land, They said, "To Jerusalem, take a stand."
Yahweh spoke again, His words to share, "Judah, listen up, do you even care?
Jonadab’s words, his sons they obey, But you ignore Me, day after day.
Prophets I sent, calling you back, Turn from your ways, but you’ve kept off track.
Jonadab’s sons, they honor and heed, Yet you, My people, won’t listen, won’t lead."
"So watch out, Judah, hear the alarm, Evil comes your way, see the harm.
Rechabites stand firm, obey and stay true, And for this loyalty, here’s what I’ll do:
Their line will remain, forever they’ll stand, Before Me, Yahweh, their legacy planned."
In Jehoiakim's fourth year, a word came clear, "Jeremiah, write my words for all to hear.
On a scroll, inscribe what I’ve said in the past, 'Bout Israel, Judah, nations, warnings vast.
Maybe Judah will heed, turn from sin's dark thread, If they change their ways, I’ll forgive them,’ God said.
Jeremiah called Baruch, his scribe with skill, Baruch penned God’s words, Jeremiah's voice to fill.
Jeremiah instructed, "I’m bound, can't enter there, So you read Yahweh’s words, let the people be aware.
On the fast day, read aloud in Yahweh's holy space, Maybe they’ll seek mercy, return to God’s grace."
Baruch followed through, did just as he was told, In Yahweh's house, the words of wrath were bold.
In the fifth year, ninth month, a fast was declared, Judah’s people gathered, God’s message shared.
Baruch stood and read in the house up high, Gemariah's room, beneath the clear blue sky.
Micaiah heard the words, urgency in his stride, To the king’s house he went, the news couldn’t hide.
Princes gathered round, scribes and noble men, Micaiah shared the words, told them what and when.
They called for Baruch, "Bring the scroll you read, Let us hear these words that make hearts dread."
In their presence, Baruch read each line, Fear sparked in their eyes, a message so divine.
"We’ll tell the king," they vowed, trembling with fright, "Baruch, how did you write?" they asked that night.
"Jeremiah spoke, I wrote it down," Baruch replied, With ink upon the scroll, he couldn't hide.
"Go, hide yourselves," the princes then implored, "Stay out of sight, don’t be ignored."
They took the scroll to the king’s winter den, But kept it aside, told the king again.
The king sent Jehudi, "Bring the scroll, let’s see," He read before the king, beside the blazing heat.
As Jehudi read, the king with knife in hand, Cut the scroll, fed it to the fire as planned.
No fear in their hearts, no garments torn, Despite the warnings, contempt was born.
Elnathan pleaded, "Please, don't burn this scroll," The king wouldn’t listen, stubborn his soul.
He ordered arrests, Jeremiah and Baruch, But Yahweh hid them, their capture forsook.
Then God spoke again, once the scroll burned away, "Write once more, Jeremiah, what I have to say.
Tell of Jehoiakim’s fate, for burning My word, No son on his throne, his end shall be heard.
Punishment will come, for servants and kin, The evil declared, for ignoring their sin."
Jeremiah took another scroll, Baruch wrote anew, The same words of warning, and more God did imbue.
Zedekiah ruled, but not by his own hand, Nebuchadnezzar's choice for Judah's land.
Yet he and his servants shut their ears tight, Ignoring Yahweh's words, no prophet in sight.
Zedekiah sent his men to Jeremiah, to say, "Pray to Yahweh for us, guide our way."
Jeremiah walked free, mingling with the crowd, Not yet in chains, still speaking aloud.
Pharaoh’s troops advanced, breaking the siege wide, Chaldeans backed off, dispersed to the side.
Then Yahweh spoke clear, through Jeremiah's voice, "Tell Judah's king, there's no other choice.
Pharaoh's aid is fleeting; they'll retreat back in haste, Chaldeans will return, laying the city to waste.
Don't fool yourselves, thinking they've gone, They'll rise again, and the city's forlorn.
Even if wounded, their strength shall inspire, They'll come back and burn this city with fire."
With Chaldeans gone, Jeremiah tried to leave, Heading to Benjamin, his portion to retrieve.
At Benjamin's gate, a guard called him out, "You’re defecting," he claimed, with a shout.
Jeremiah declared, "It's a lie, I'm true!" But they dragged him to the princes, who beat him black and blue.
Locked up deep, in the scribe's prison kept, Jeremiah waited, while the city slept.
Zedekiah called him, secret words exchanged, "What's Yahweh's word?" Jeremiah's voice ranged.
"There is a word," he said, without a quiver, "You’ll be delivered to Babylon's river."
Jeremiah then questioned, "Why am I here? What have I done to earn this fear?
Your prophets lied, where are they now? They said Babylon would never come, with a bow.
Please, my king, don't send me back there, To the scribe's house, where death's in the air."
Zedekiah heard, and moved him with a nod, To the court of the guard, with daily bread from God.
So Jeremiah stayed, held but fed, Awaiting the fate that lay ahead.
Shephatiah and the crew, they heard the news, Jeremiah spoke truth, and it shook their views. "Yahweh says, stay here and face your doom, But head to the Chaldeans, and escape the gloom."
"This city's handed over," Yahweh declared, To Babylon's army, the king prepared. The princes said, "Let's put this man down, He's causing fear, spreading panic in town."
King Zedekiah sighed, "He's in your hand, I can't fight you, I can't command." Into the dungeon, they let Jeremiah fall, No water, just mire, he sank with it all.
Ebedmelech the Ethiopian heard the plight, Went to the king, said, "This isn't right. Jeremiah's cast in, with famine and dread, Without rescue, soon he'll be dead."
The king ordered, "Take thirty men, go quick, Lift him from the dungeon, don't let him stick." With rags and cords, they pulled him high, Jeremiah's safe, no longer to die.
Zedekiah called for Jeremiah's word, "Tell me the truth, let it be heard." But Jeremiah feared, "Will you take my life? You won't listen, just cause more strife."
Yet Zedekiah swore, "As Yahweh lives, Your life, I won't give." Jeremiah spoke, "The Lord's decree: Go to Babylon's prince, your life will be free."
"But if not, this city will burn, Chaldeans win, and you'll have no turn." Zedekiah feared the defectors' scorn, But Jeremiah urged him, "Obey, be reborn."
"Refuse, and ruin's what Yahweh showed, Your house will crumble, down that road." Zedekiah pleaded, "Let no one know, If they ask, tell them where you wish to go."
The princes came, asked their things, Jeremiah spoke as advised by the king. He stayed in the guard, his patience vast, Until Jerusalem's fall came at last.
In Zedekiah's ninth year, Babylon marched with might, Nebuchadnezzar's army came, set Jerusalem in their sight.
By the eleventh year, the city wall was breached, The Babylonian princes entered, the city's heart they reached.
Zedekiah saw them come, he and his soldiers fled, Through the garden's gate by night, to Arabah they sped.
Chaldeans gave chase, caught him in Jericho's field, To Nebuchadnezzar they brought him, his fate was sealed.
Sons of Zedekiah fell before his eyes, Nobles of Judah, too, faced their demise.
His eyes were put out, bound in chains so tight, To Babylon they led him, out of Judah's sight.
Chaldeans burned houses, Jerusalem's walls came down, Nebuzaradan took captives, led them to Babylon's town.
Yet some poor folk stayed, vineyards and fields they gained, A new life in the land, though much had changed.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke of Jeremiah, a command he gave, "Protect him, do no harm, as he wishes, behave."
Jeremiah was freed, Gedaliah took him in, Among the people now, a new chapter would begin.
Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, words to Ebedmelech brought, “Destruction's coming, but you, fear not.”
“I'll save you that day," Yahweh's promise clear, "You'll escape with your life, for in Me you hold dear."
Jeremiah, chains released in the land, Nebuzaradan set him free, gave him a stand. "Yahweh spoke this doom, here it's done, 'Cause you sinned, now the deed’s begun.
Today you're free, the chains are gone, Choose your path, where you belong. Come to Babylon, I'll care for you, Or stay here, where you feel it’s true."
While he lingered, he heard the call, "Go back to Gedaliah, stand tall. Live among those left behind, Or choose the path you want to find."
Food and a gift, the captain gave, Jeremiah, now no longer a slave. He went to Mizpah, with Gedaliah stayed, Where Judah’s remnant had obeyed.
The captains heard, from the fields they came, Gedaliah's rule, now his name. Men, women, children, left in the land, Not taken captive, under Babylon’s hand.
Gedaliah swore, "Don’t fear the Chaldeans, Serve them well, live with reason. I'll be at Mizpah, for the Chaldean sight, Gather your fruits, in vessels tight."
Jews from Moab, Ammon, and Edom’s shores, Heard Judah had a remnant once more. Back they came, with wine in hand, To Gedaliah in Judah's land.
But Johanan warned, "Baalis sends strife, Ishmael's coming to take your life." Gedaliah, calm, didn't believe the threat, "False words, Ishmael's not a threat yet."
In secret, Johanan tried again, "Let me stop Ishmael, save us men. Why risk your life, let us live, Prevent the chaos that he might give."
But Gedaliah shook his head, said, "You speak falsely, let it be dead." The tension rose, but he stood unmoved, In Mizpah, where the remnant proved.
Seventh month rolls in, Ishmael's on the scene, Royal blood, ten men, a deadly team. They met in Mizpah, broke bread with Gedaliah, Then Ishmael rose up, dealt death with fire.
With swords they struck, Gedaliah fell, Governor no more, by Babylon's spell. Jews and Chaldeans, they met their fate, Ishmael's wrath, they couldn't escape.
Two days passed, no news had spread, Eighty men came, mourning the dead. From Shechem, Shiloh, with offerings in hand, Ishmael met them, tears in the sand.
He lured them in, "Come see Gedaliah," he said, But into the pit, those men were led. Yet ten men pleaded, "Spare us, we pray, We've hidden treasures, just let us stay."
He spared their lives, but the pit was filled, With bodies of those whom Ishmael killed. He took captives, the king's daughters bound, Off to Ammon, they were outward bound.
But Johanan heard, and gathered his band, To fight Ishmael, to take a stand. At Gibeon's waters, the clash was near, People rejoiced when Johanan appeared.
Captives turned back, glad to be free, Yet Ishmael escaped, with a menacing spree. Johanan gathered the remnants, moved on, To dwell near Bethlehem, before the dawn.
Fear of Chaldeans drove them to flee, To Egypt they aimed, seeking to be free. For Ishmael had killed, and the land was torn, Babylon's governor, now forlorn.
Captains and people, from least to the great, Came to Jeremiah, with worries so weight. "Pray to Yahweh for this remnant, so few, Show us the path, the things we should do."
Jeremiah replied, "I hear your plea, I'll pray to Yahweh, wait and see. Whatever He speaks, I'll tell you straight, Not a word will I keep, no delay, no wait."
They swore to obey, come good or bad, Yahweh’s witness, in this they were glad. "Whether it’s tough, or makes us feel free, We'll follow Yahweh, so well it will be."
Ten days passed, Yahweh spoke at last, Jeremiah called them, no time to contrast. "Yahweh says, stay in this land, I'll build, Not tear you down, your hopes fulfilled."
"Don’t fear Babylon, I’ll save you, I'll grant mercy, help you through. Return to your land, don't break the plan, Stay in this place, where you began."
"But if you say, 'To Egypt we go,' No war, no sound of trumpet, no woe. Hear Yahweh's word, Judah’s remnant, In Egypt, death awaits, your fears sent."
"Sword and famine will chase you down, In Egypt's land, you’ll wear a frown. For Yahweh’s wrath will outpour, As Jerusalem saw, you'll see it more."
"Don’t go to Egypt," Yahweh declared, "You’ve been warned, you should have cared. Deceit against your souls you’ve shown, Prayed for a word, yet truth's unknown."
"I’ve told you today, but you've not heard, Yahweh's commands, not a single word. You'll die by sword, famine, pestilence near, In the place you desire, where you steer."
Jeremiah spoke God's truth, every word he said, Azariah and Johanan shook their heads, "It's all in your head.
Jeremiah, you're lying, God didn't send you here, Saying 'Don't go to Egypt'—that's not what we hear.
Baruch's turned you against us, to hand us to Chaldeans, To take us captive, that's his dark scheming.
But they ignored the voice of Yahweh, their God, Johanan and his men on a path that was flawed.
They gathered Judah's remnant, men and women in tow, All the people left in Judah, they had to go.
With Jeremiah and Baruch, they made their way, To Egypt's land—they didn't obey.
Down to Tahpanhes, they arrived with haste, Ignoring God's word, they sealed their fate.
Then Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, clear and loud, "Take these stones, hide them in the crowd.
In Pharaoh's brickwork, where all can see, Say, 'Here Nebuchadnezzar's throne will be.'
The king of Babylon, my servant, he'll reign, His throne on these stones, it's all preordained.
Egypt will shatter, death and captivity, To the sword, the fire—it's their destiny.
He'll burn their gods' houses, take them away, Arrayed like a shepherd, he'll leave in the day.
Beth Shemesh's pillars, they'll break and burn, Egypt's gods' houses, to ashes they'll turn."
Jeremiah got the word, to Egypt's land he came, Speaking to the Jews, hear this message, feel the flame.
"Yahweh of Armies speaks, you've seen the ruin, Jerusalem's left empty, cities of Judah in ruin.
All 'cause of wicked deeds, incense to gods unknown, Provoking anger, my wrath has overthrown.
I sent prophets early, saying 'Don’t dare do this thing,' Yet you turned deaf ears, worshiping false gods like a king.
So my wrath poured out, in Judah's streets they fell, Wasted and desolate, in a sorrowful, silent shell.
Now Yahweh speaks again, why harm your own soul? Cutting off your kin, leaving not one whole.
Burning incense in Egypt, provoking with your hands, To become a curse, be scattered across lands.
Have you forgotten the sins of your fathers and kings? They walked not in my laws, disregarding all things.
So now I face you, cutting off all of Judah's might, Those who sought Egypt to live, consumed in the night.
By sword, famine, pestilence, they'll fall, A horror, curse, reproach — they won't stand tall.
No remnant will return, except the ones who flee, Yet all will see whose word will truly be.
The people answered Jeremiah, they wouldn’t heed the call, "We’ll do what we want, burning incense, offerings tall.
Back then life was sweet, food plenty, all was well, Now without our worship, sword and famine fell."
Jeremiah replied, "You think Yahweh forgot your actions? He remembers your incense, saw your transactions.
That's why desolation and curses now reign, You didn’t listen to His voice, hence the pain."
Jeremiah said further, "Hear Yahweh’s strong decree, You've declared your vows, now fulfill them, let it be.
Yet hear Yahweh’s word, your fate is clear, His name will no longer be spoken here.
Watched for evil, not good, by sword and famine consumed, Few will escape, back to Judah, where doom loomed.
This is your sign; Yahweh’s words will take their place, Pharaoh Hophra’s fate sealed, given to enemies who chase."
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign, Jeremiah spoke words that Baruch did gain.
"Yahweh, God of Israel, has this to say, To you, Baruch, listen, don't stray.
You cried out, 'Woe, for sorrow adds to my pain, I'm weary, groaning, seeking rest in vain.'
Tell him this, Yahweh's message is clear, 'What I've built, I'll break, what I've planted, I shear.
Do you seek greatness, things for yourself? Don't chase them, for I'll bring trouble to all else.'
Says Yahweh, 'But here's the deal, Your life I'll protect, it's the real seal.'"
The word came down to Jeremiah's ear, About nations far and nations near.
"Prepare your shield, get ready to fight, Mount the horses, stand up with might.
Polish those spears, put on the mail, Why do I see them dismayed and pale?
Mighty ones beaten, fleeing in fear, Terror's around, nothing is clear."
"Don't let the swift escape the fray, By Euphrates' river, they fall today.
Who rises like the Nile, high and wide? Egypt's waters surge like a pride.
'I’ll cover the earth,' Egypt boasts of power, 'I'll destroy cities, this is my hour.'
Charge, you horses! Chariots, rage! Mighty men, with strength engage.
For Yahweh's day, a vengeance to claim, The sword drinks blood, ends their game.
Go to Gilead, take balm for the pain, But healing escapes, all efforts in vain.
Nations hear cries, shame spreads wide, Mighty men stumble, side by side."
Yahweh spoke, a word to declare, "Babylon strikes, Egypt beware.
Shout in Egypt, Migdol, Memphis, hear, ‘Prepare for the sword, it's drawing near.’
Strong ones fall, they don't stand tall, Yahweh's push makes them all crawl.
‘Rise, return to our birthland,’ they say, Pharaoh's just noise, wasted the day.
'As I live,' Yahweh declares with might, Tabor and Carmel, he comes to fight.
Egypt, beautiful heifer, now desolate, From the north rides your fate.
Hired men like calves, fled away, On calamity's day, they can't stay.
Sound of a serpent, armies march on, Axes like woodcutters, Egypt's gone.
Yahweh says, 'I punish all in sight, Amon, Pharaoh, all in my might.
Into Babylon's hand, I’ll give them all, Yet Egypt will rise, as old days call.
But Jacob, don’t fear, my servant true, I’ll save you from lands, make you new.
Quiet and calm, Jacob returns free, No fear to be, for I am with thee.
I’ll end all nations, where you’ve roamed, But not you, Jacob, you’ll come home."
Yo, listen up, here's a tale from the land, Before Pharaoh's strike, Jeremiah takes a stand.
"Behold, waters rise, coming down from the north, Overflowing the land, pouring forth with great wrath.
Men will cry out, wails will fill the air, At the sound of hoofbeats, bringing despair.
Rushing chariots, wheels rumbling loud, Fathers too weak, not turning around.
