Daniel in the lion's den, the king felt low, "Your God will deliver you," he hoped so. A stone sealed the den, the king fasted that night, No sleep, no music, no joy in sight.
At dawn, he rushed to the lion’s den, "Daniel, servant of God, did He save you again?" Daniel replied, "My God sent an angel down, Shut the lions' mouths, no harm found."
The king rejoiced, pulled Daniel out, No scratch on him, no doubt. Those who schemed, met their fate, The lions showed them no delay, no wait.
Darius declared, to every nation and land, Fear Daniel's God, mighty and grand. He saves, He rescues, His kingdom's no lie, Daniel prospered, under kings far and nigh.
In Babylon's realm, Daniel had a dream so grand, Visions of beasts rising from the sea, across the land.
Four winds whipped the ocean's might, Four beasts emerged, each a startling sight.
First, a lion with eagle wings it bore, Plucked and stood upright, a man's heart at its core.
Next came a bear, raised on one side, With ribs in its jaws, "Devour!" it cried.
Then a leopard, swift with four wings and four heads, Dominion it seized, as the prophecy spreads.
The fourth beast was fierce, iron teeth did it wield, Crushed and devoured all, with strength unconcealed.
Ten horns on its head, but then a new horn arose, Eyes like a man, words bold as it grows.
Thrones were set, the Ancient of Days took his seat, Clothed in snow-white, with a fiery throne beneath.
A river of fire flowed, books opened wide, Countless stood before Him, His judgment was applied.
The boasting horn silenced, that beast cast to flame, Others lost dominion, but time still remained.
With clouds came One like a Son of Man, To the Ancient of Days, He approached, took His stand.
Given glory and a kingdom, forever to reign, All nations and languages served Him, no end to His domain.
Daniel's spirit was troubled, visions weighed on his mind, He sought understanding, the truth he did find.
"These beasts are kings, four rising from earth's face, But saints of the Most High will claim the kingdom's place."
The fourth beast, Daniel's focus, so strong and so wild, Iron and bronze, breaking nations, more fierce than a child.
Ten horns, ten kings, yet another will rise, Three kings he’ll topple, with great boasts and lies.
Waging war on the saints, for a time they'll bear the strain, Till the Ancient of Days comes, and justice will reign.
The kingdom eternal, to saints it will go, An everlasting dominion with a righteous glow.
Daniel's mind was troubled, thoughts hard to release, But he kept them within, seeking future peace.
In the third year of Belshazzar's reign, A vision to Daniel, clear and plain. In Susa's citadel, in my mind's eye, By the river Ulai, I watched the sky.
A ram appeared with two horns high, One rose last, reaching toward the sky. West, north, south, it roamed with might, No beast could stand, no one could fight.
Then from the west, a goat took flight, Never touching the ground in sight. A single horn between its eyes, Charged the ram with furious cries.
The goat struck hard, broke the ram's horn, Left it powerless, defeated, torn. The goat exalted, strong and bold, But its great horn broke, as the story's told.
Four horns rose where one had been, Toward the winds, a sight unseen. From one horn, a little one grew, To the south, east, land of the true.
It reached the stars, brought some down, Trampled them beneath its crown. It challenged the Prince, took His space, Burnt offerings, truth erased.
Heard a voice, a holy call, "How long will this vision fall?” “Two thousand, three hundred nights," he said, "Then the sanctuary shall be cleansed, not dead."
I, Daniel, sought to understand, A figure like a man took a stand. A voice called, "Gabriel, make him see, The vision’s meaning, let it be."
Gabriel approached, I hit the ground, "Understand, son of man, truth's profound. For the vision's set for the end of time, The ram and goat, their fates align."
"The ram, Media and Persia's kings, The goat, Greece’s first king brings. Four kingdoms rise, but lack his strength, In the latter days, deceit's length."
"A fierce king will rise, face severe, Destroy the strong, bring mighty fear. His power not his own, but great, Against the Prince, meets his fate."
"The vision's true of days ahead, Seal it up, let it be said." Daniel fainted, weak and worn, Yet rose again, though visions torn.
In the end, I wondered deep, The vision's secrets, yet to keep. The king's business resumed my days, Mysteries unknown, in their ways.
In Darius's first year, the Medes took the throne, Daniel read the books and knew the prophecy was shown. Seventy years for Jerusalem's desolation, So he turned to God with prayer and confession.
He prayed, "Oh Lord, great and dreadful, true, You keep your promise with those who love you. We've sinned, turned our back, gone astray, Ignored your prophets, pushed your words away.
To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, clear, But for us, confusion is what we fear. From Judah to Jerusalem, scattered wide, In lands where we dwell, because we defied.
"Mercy and forgiveness belong to you, Though we rebelled, we see it through. We ignored your voice, your laws we broke, The curse of Moses upon us, like a yoke.
Judgment came, your words confirmed, Jerusalem's plight, by evil wormed. Yet we didn’t seek your favor or truth, Our hearts stayed hardened, aloof.
"Lord, you brought us from Egypt's might, Renown for your power, a glorious sight. But we've sinned, done wickedly, we plead, Turn your wrath from Jerusalem’s need.
"God, hear the prayers of your servant now, Shine on your sanctuary, fulfill your vow. Turn your ear, see our desolation's call, Not for our sake, but for your mercy overall.
"Lord, hear. Lord, forgive. Do not delay, For your city and people bear your name, we say.” While Daniel prayed, confessed, and sought, Gabriel swiftly came with wisdom he brought.
"Daniel, beloved, I've come to give you sight, Seventy weeks are set, to make wrongs right. From command to rebuild, the Anointed will show, Through seven then sixty-two weeks you’ll know.
Troubles will come, but it will stand strong, The Anointed cut off, yet not for long. The city and sanctuary will face destruction, War and desolation, a grim instruction.
A firm covenant for one week will stand, Midway through, offerings will be banned. Abominations will spread, desolation will reign, Till the end, determined, wrath will gain.”
In the third year of Cyrus, Persia's king, Daniel got a vision, a war it would bring.
Three weeks of mourning, no bread, no wine, No anointing, just waiting on a sign.
On the twenty-fourth day, near the river's side, A man in linen, pure gold on his thighs.
Body like beryl, face bright like lightning's flash, Eyes like torches, arms and feet of bronze, a voice like a crash.
Daniel alone saw; his men couldn't bear, They quaked with fear, ran to hide, unaware.
Strength left Daniel, pale with no might, He heard the voice, then fell, face to the ground in the night.
A hand touched him, lifted him from the floor, “Daniel, beloved, understand once more.
Stand up, I've been sent to you this day.” Trembling, Daniel rose to hear what he'd say.
“Fear not, Daniel, your words reached the throne, From day one you sought, I wasn't alone.
The prince of Persia blocked me twenty-one days, Till Michael helped me, in heavenly ways.
Now I'm here to tell what's yet to unfold, Visions of future days, as the stories were told.”
Daniel mute, faced the ground deep in thought, A touch on his lips, strength again was sought.
“My sorrows heavy, no strength in me, How can I talk, when I'm weak as can be?”
Touched once more, he felt the power ignite, “Beloved, be strong, stand with your might.”
“I’ll speak now, tell me what you must say, For your words have strengthened me today.”
“Do you know why I'm here?” the man inquired, “I’ll return to fight, not yet retired.
The prince of Greece will come, but hear this truth, Michael your prince stands with me, forsooth.”
In Darius's first year, I stood tall, To confirm and strengthen, giving it my all. "Listen now, the truth I will show, Three kings in Persia, then a fourth with riches to grow.
He'll stir up trouble against Greece with might, A mighty king will rise, doing as he likes. But his kingdom will shatter, scattered like the breeze, Not to his kin, but divided with ease.
The southern king strong, but his prince stronger still, They'll join through a daughter, her strength will chill. Yet she'll falter, given up in the end, Along with those who tried to defend.
From her roots, one will rise in place, Into the fortress, he'll take his space. With gods and treasures, Egypt's where he'll go, Then return to his land, with what he stole.
His sons will rise, assemble great powers, Overflow the lands, like heavy showers. The southern king, angry, will wage a fight, But the northern king's force will take the night.
A multitude will rise, but pride's in vain, He'll cast down many, yet won't maintain. The north will gather, stronger than the past, With armies and wealth, they'll come at last.
In those times, many will rise against the south, But the violent will fall, failing their mouth. The north will take cities, the south will break, No strength to stand, no path to make.
He'll do as he pleases, in the land of delight, Destruction in hand, he'll harness his might. He'll send his daughter, but she won't stand, His plans will falter, not as he planned.
Turning to islands, his reach will expand, But a prince will stop him, on his own land. Then he'll stumble, fall, and disappear, As a tax collector briefly appears.
A contemptible one will rise instead, Through flattery, to the throne he's led. Breaking treaties, deceit in play, He'll grow strong, in a clever way.
Insecurity breeds his daring schemes, Scattering spoils, fulfilling dreams. He'll plot against strongholds, bide his time, Prepare for battle, in rhythm and rhyme.
Against the south, with strength he'll clash, But betrayal within will cause a crash. Both kings lie, seeking their gain, But the end's appointed, their plans in vain.
He'll return wealthy, against the covenant rage, Taking action, turning the page. The south he'll approach, not as before, Kittim's ships will push him to the shore.
Profaning the sanctuary, setting abomination high, Corrupting the wicked, spinning a lie. But those who know God will take a stand, Strong and resilient across the land.
The wise will instruct, though they'll fall, Helped by few, but answered the call. Refined in trials, pure they'll become, Until the end, when time's appointed sum.
A king will do as he wishes, above all gods, Marvels against God, sparking the odds. He'll prosper until the wrath is complete, Ignoring the gods, himself he'll seat.
Honoring fortresses with unknown gold, Ruling over many, stories untold. At the end, the south will face his wrath, The north's whirlwind, on a conquering path.
He'll enter the glorious land, overthrowing domains, Edom, Moab, Ammon, escaping chains. Egypt's treasures, under his power, Libya and Ethiopia, follow his tower.
But news from afar will trouble his mind, Fury unleashed, destruction he'll find. Between sea and holy mount, he plants his tent, Yet his end will come, and none will relent.
Michael stands up, the great protector in sight, For your people in trouble, ready to fight. A time of chaos like never seen, But deliverance for those whose names gleam.
The dust will awaken, the sleepers will rise, Some to life everlasting, some to despise. The wise will shine like the sky's bright face, Turning many to righteousness, holding their place.
“Daniel, lock these words, seal them tight, Till the end when knowledge takes flight.” I saw two figures by the river's side, One asked the man above the tide,
“How long till these wonders cease?” He raised his hands, swore by peace, “A time, times, and half a time, When holy power breaks, all will align.”
I heard, but could not understand, I asked, “What’s the end, tell me the plan?” “Go your way, Daniel, the words are sealed, Till time’s end, when all’s revealed.
“The pure will purify, the wise will learn, The wicked, in darkness, will never discern. From offering end to desolation's stay, Twelve ninety days will mark the way.
“Blessed are those who wait and survive, To reach thirteen thirty-five. Go your way, rest till the end of days, Inherit your lot, in eternal praise.”
Yahweh spoke a word, Hosea heard the call, In the days of kings, Judah and Israel stand tall.
He told Hosea, "Take a wife of the street, For this land's unfaithful, with deceitful feet."
So Hosea found Gomer, Diblaim's own, She bore him a son, in their home he's grown.
"Name him Jezreel," Yahweh did declare, "For the house of Jehu's blood, I will lay bare."
"In the valley, Israel's bow will break, The kingdom's reign, soon I will take."
Gomer conceived again, a daughter she bore, "Call her Lo-Ruhamah, mercy's closed door."
"I'll have mercy on Judah, they'll be saved by Me, Not by sword or battle, by divine decree."
Weaned was Lo-Ruhamah, then came a son, "Name him Lo-Ammi, for our union's undone."
Yet Israel's children will fill the sea's sand, Where 'not My people' stood, 'sons of God' will stand.
Judah and Israel, together they'll be, One head to lead, in unity they'll see.
For great is the day, Jezreel will shine, Yahweh's word fulfilled, His design divine.
"Brothers, you're my people!" Sisters, hear my call, "Contend with your mother, she’s not mine at all."
She needs to stop her ways, put down that disguise, Or I'll lay her bare, like the day she first cries.
No mercy for her kids, born of deceit, Their mother went astray, in shame she's complete.
"Chasing lovers for bread, water, flax, and wine, But I'll block her path, her way won't be fine."
She'll chase her dreams, but never them she'll find, Then she'll think, "Back to my first love, I was blind."
She forgot it was me, who gave the grain and gold, Now I'll take it back, leave her out in the cold.
Exposing her shame, in front of her crew, No one will save, nothing they can do.
Her feasts, her moons, her Sabbaths will cease, Her vines and figs, become wild with beasts.
"Forgetting me, for Baals she did crave," Says Yahweh, "In the wild, I’ll her enslave."
"I’ll speak soft, give vineyards for hope, She’ll answer like youth, no longer she'll mope."
"In that day," Yahweh says, "call me your own, Names of Baals gone, you'll forget all they've shown."
"A covenant with creatures, peace will reign, Bow, sword, and battles will no longer strain."
"Betrothed to me, forever we'll stand, In justice, kindness, compassion so grand."
Faithful you’ll be, you'll know Yahweh's name, Heavens and earth will respond to my claim.
Grain, wine, and oil, Jezreel will agree, Mercy for those unloved, my people you'll be."
"They'll call me God, and I'll say, "You're mine," A promise fulfilled, in love we'll entwine."
Yahweh spoke, “Go love her again, She's with another, but love won't end.
Like I love Israel, though they stray, Chasing other gods, in their own way.”
So I bought her back, silver and grain, Fifteen pieces, paid to ease the pain.
I told her, “With me, you'll stay, No more tricks, no other way.
No more playing roles of old, I'll be faithful, honest, bold.”
Israel will go days, empty and bare, No king, no prince, no worship to share.
No sacred stones, or idols to claim, They'll wait in silence, hearts aflame.
But they'll return, trembling in the night, Seeking Yahweh, their God, the shining light.
With David their king, they'll come to see, Yahweh's blessings, the final decree.
Listen up, Israel, hear Yahweh’s charge, "Inhabitants of the land, your sins are large.
No truth, no goodness, no knowledge in sight, Cursing, lying, murder take flight.
Stealing, adultery, breaking the line, Bloodshed on bloodshed, time after time.
The land will mourn, its dwellers waste away, Creatures of the field, birds of the sky, decay.
Fish of the sea will die, and none shall accuse, Your people like those priests who refuse.
Stumble by day, prophet stumble by night, “I’ll destroy your mother, for wrongs not made right.
Destroyed for lack of the knowledge you spurned, Rejected you’ll be, for my law you’ve unlearned.
Multiplied, yet sin grew unchecked, Glory to shame, what did you expect?
Feeding on sins, with hearts set on wrong, People and priest, where do you belong?
Eat but not filled, play but not grow, Abandon Yahweh, and reap what you sow.
Prostitution and wine take wisdom away, Consulting wood idols, led astray.
High places for sacrifice, incense burns, Under the shade where infidelity churns.
Daughters unpunished, for men do the same, Sacrifices with shame, none are to blame.
Israel, though astray, let Judah remain, Avoid Gilgal, Beth Aven, don’t profane.
Stubborn as a heifer, Israel’s plight, Yahweh can’t feed them in meadows of light.
Ephraim to idols, let him be, Rulers in shame, loving infamy.
The wind wraps tight, disappointment’s their end, Sacrifices in vain, no heart to mend."
"Listen up, priests, hear the call! Israel, king’s house, it's judgment for all.
You've been a snare at Mizpah, a net at Tabor’s gates, Rebels deep in slaughter, but I discipline these fates.
I know Ephraim, you can't hide from me, Ephraim’s played false, Israel’s not free.
Their deeds keep them from turning back, Spirit of betrayal, there's no Yahweh track.
Pride blinds Israel, they stumble and fall, Ephraim and Judah, both caught in the thrall.
They seek Yahweh with flocks, with their herds, But He’s withdrawn, leaving them unheard.
Unfaithful to Yahweh, bearing children untrue, The new moon will consume them, fields devoured, too.
"Blow the cornet in Gibeah, trumpet in Ramah loud! Battle cries in Beth Aven, Benjamin, stand proud!
Ephraim to ruins on rebuke’s heavy day, Among tribes of Israel, my truths will stay.
Judah’s princes move the landmarks, it’s true, My wrath floods over them like water, breaking through.
Ephraim oppressed, crushed by judgment’s chase, Chasing idols, it's a losing race.
To Ephraim, I’m like a moth, to Judah, decay, When Ephraim’s sick, Judah’s wounds display.
To Assyria, Ephraim runs, king Jareb sought, But no healing here, no cure will be bought.
I’ll be a lion to Ephraim, tearing them apart, To Judah like a young lion, a fierce new start.
I’ll carry off, none to rescue or save, Return to my place, until they seek and behave.
In affliction, they will seek my face, Earnestly searching, returning to grace."
"Let's return to Yahweh, torn and bruised, He'll bind us up, healing our wounds.
Two days gone, and He'll revive our breath, On the third, we'll rise, conquering death.
"Let's know Yahweh, press on, don't fail, Like the sun rising, His presence prevails.
He'll come like rain, springing forth the earth, Bringing life, bringing worth.
Ephraim, Judah, what's next for you? Your love fades like morning dew.
Prophets cut you, words struck like a flash, Judgment swift, a lightning crash.
"I desire mercy, not hollow sacrifice, Know Me, not just offerings, at any price.
Like Adam, you broke the bond, Unfaithful actions, too far gone.
Gilead, your iniquity's clear, Stained with blood, not to be revered.
Robbers ambush, priests do the same, On Shechem's path, they bring shame.
In Israel's house, horrors unfold, Ephraim's acts, stories retold.
Judah, your harvest's yet to be seen, When I restore fortunes, clean and pristine."
When I’d heal Israel, their sins are exposed, Ephraim’s iniquity, Samaria's woes. Falsehoods they commit, thieves slipping inside, Robbers on the prowl, nowhere to hide.
They don’t stop to think, I see all their deeds, Their own actions trap them, they won’t be freed. Making kings glad with their wicked, sly lies, Princes rejoice while their truth slowly dies.
Adulterers all, like ovens they burn, Baker stops stirring, waits for dough to turn. Princes got drunk when the king had his day, Joined with the mockers, they led him astray.
Hearts like hot ovens, plotting while they sleep, Baker snoozes on, but the fire runs deep. Flames devour judges, kings fallen low, None among them calls my name, it shows.
Ephraim blends with nations, pancake half-baked, Strangers take strength, and he's not awake. Gray hairs are sprouting, he doesn’t see it, Pride testifies, but to me, they won’t submit.
“Ephraim’s a dove, easily deceived, Calls Egypt, Assyria, by lies they’re grieved. I’ll spread my net, like birds they will fall, Chastise them strong, echo through their hall.
Woe to them now, they’ve wandered away, Destruction comes quick, for their heart’s astray. Though I’d redeem, they speak lies in my face, Howl on their beds, but turn from my grace.
They gather for grain, new wine, they crave, Turn from me, though I taught them to be brave. Return they do, but not to the Most High, Faulty bows they are, in rage they will die.
Princes fall by the sword, tongues full of rage, Egypt will mock them, trapped in their cage."
Blow the trumpet, hear it loud and clear, Like an eagle over the house, drawing near.
They broke my covenant, rebelled in my sight, Yet they cry to me, claiming they're upright.
Israel's cast aside the good they knew, Enemies chase them, relentless, in pursuit.
Kings they appoint, but not by my hand, Princes arise, I don't sanction these plans.
Silver and gold turned into false gods, Idols they've made, cast off, cut the odds.
"Samaria, toss that calf away!" My anger burns, they lead astray.
Crafted by hands, no God in sight, That calf of Samaria's doomed to plight.
Sow the wind, the whirlwind they reap, No grain left standing, no harvest to keep.
Israel's swallowed, nations make him small, Like a wild donkey, alone he falls.
To Assyria they've gone, lonely, astray, Ephraim, with lovers, pays betrayal's wage.
But I'll gather them back, though they're sold far and wide, Oppression will wither, won't long abide.
Ephraim's altars for sin, a multiplying shame, My laws written, now viewed as strange.
They sacrifice meat, but Yahweh turns away, He'll remember their sins, make them repay.
Back to Egypt, they'll face what they dread, Israel's forgotten, palaces instead.
Judah's cities, fortified and grand, But fire will come, devouring the land.
Israel, don't celebrate like the rest, Unfaithful to God, you failed the test.
You love the wages of a lover's deceit, At every threshing floor, where grain and wine meet.
Threshing floor's empty, wine press runs dry, New wine fails, and you ask why.
No place in Yahweh's land to dwell, Ephraim to Egypt, unclean food to sell.
No wine offerings, no joy to bring, Sacrifices like mourners' bread, a polluted thing.
"What happens on feast days?" you may ask, Gone, destruction's grip, a heavy task.
Egypt gathers, Memphis lays to rest, Nettles and thorns in tents infest.
Days of reckoning, judgment's near, Prophets called fools, insanity feared.
Ephraim's paths a snare, hostility in the air, Corruption deep like Gibeah's fare.
Found Israel like grapes in a wild scene, Fathers like figs, ripe and green.
But they turned to Baal Peor's shame, Abominable acts, they earned that name.
Ephraim's glory flies like a bird, No birth, no growth, no future heard.
Children raised, but grief's the way, Woe's the cry when God walks away.
Ephraim once like Tyre, so fair, But murderer's hand awaits them there.
"What to give, Yahweh?" they cry, A barren womb, dry breasts, is the reply.
"Wickedness in Gilgal, where I despise, Out of my house, no more ties.
Ephraim struck, roots dry, fruit's no more, Even the born, loved ones, gone from the core."
God will cast them, because they turned away, Wanderers among nations, they shall stray.
Israel thrives, a lush vine indeed, His fruit multiplies, feeds every need. With plenty of fruit, altars are raised, Prospered land, and stones are praised.
Heart divided, guilt will be found, Altars fall, stones hit the ground. Now they say, "No king to claim, No fear of Yahweh, what's in a name?"
Promises made, covenants fake, Judgment rises like weeds in a wake. Samaria's folks, in terror they cry, Mourn for the calves, their glory's gone by.
To Assyria, a gift it'll go, Ephraim's shame begins to show. Samaria's king drifts like a twig, Sinful heights, destruction big.
Thorn and thistle on altars sprout, Mountains hide us, hills block us out. "Israel, you've sinned since Gibeah's days," Battle doesn't stop, it stays and stays.
"I'll chastise with nations at hand, Bound to transgress, they'll understand. Ephraim's yoked, though thresher she loves, Judah will plow, Jacob's clods shove.
Sow righteousness, kindness you'll reap, Break your ground, Yahweh you seek. You’ve sown wickedness, reaped deceit, Trusted in men, now face defeat.
Battle roars, fortresses fall, Beth Arbel's day, echoes all. Bethel's fate for wickedness shown, At dawn, Israel's king dethroned."
When Israel was young, I loved him, called him outta Egypt's land, But they turned away, sacrificed to idols made by hand.
I taught Ephraim to walk, took him by the arm, He didn’t know I healed him, kept him from harm.
Drew him with love, lifted burdens from his neck, Bent down low, fed him, kept his life in check.
No return to Egypt—Assyria’s their king, They refused to repent, let the sword swing.
The bars will fall, cities laid to waste, Turned from me, called, but I won’t be chased.
“How can I let you go, Ephraim? Israel, how can I hand over? Like Admah, Zeboiim, my heart’s in turmoil, like a storm, it hovers.
Won’t unleash my anger, won’t destroy my own, For I am God, not man, I stand alone.
They’ll follow Yahweh, roar like a lion in the night, Children trembling from the west, seeking the light.
From Egypt like birds, out of Assyria they’ll flee, “I’ll settle them in houses,” says Yahweh, eternally.
Ephraim wraps me in lies, Israel in deceit, Judah strays, unfaithful, makes the cycle repeat.
Ephraim chases the wind, running wild with deceit, Deals with Assyria, sends oil Egypt's street.
God's got beef with Judah, Jacob's ways he surveys, He'll repay him for deeds, in those old twisted days.
Grabbed his brother's heel, even in the womb's space, Grew up strong, wrestled God face to face.
Fought with the angel, and he shed some tears, Pleaded at Bethel, where God calmed his fears.
Yahweh's the name, the God of renown, "Turn to your God, let justice wear the crown."
A merchant cheats, with scales that deceive, Ephraim boasts, "Riches I achieve!"
"But I'm Yahweh, from Egypt I led, In tents you'll dwell, like the old days," He said.
Prophets spoke visions, words made clear, But Gilead’s wicked, their altar heaps drear.
Jacob ran to Aram, worked for a bride, Israel preserved by prophets who guide.
Ephraim provoked, his anger won't fade, His blood remains, for his contempt he's repaid.
Ephraim spoke, the world would shake, But in Baal's guilt, sealed his fate, he'd break.
Crafted idols from silver, they made them by hand, "Human sacrifice," they whispered, kissed calves on command.
But like morning mist, they'll fade and be gone, Chaff in the whirlwind, smoke at dawn.
"I'm Yahweh, your God, from Egypt I led, Acknowledge no other; let that be said."
In deserts I knew you, where drought was king, They ate and were filled, then forgot everything.
Now I'm a lion, lurking in wait, A leopard on paths, sealing their fate.
Like a bear without cubs, with fury I'll tear, A lioness devours, a wild beast's glare.
Destroyed, Israel, rejecting my aid, "Where is your king?" I asked, you prayed.
I gave you leaders in anger's storm, Took them back when wrath took form.
Ephraim's guilt is stacking high, Sorrows like labor, oh how they cry.
Yet I'll ransom from Sheol's grasp, "Death, where's your plague?" I ask.
Compassion hidden, no mercy's light, East wind's coming, drying springs tight.
Samaria's guilt, rebellion defined, Sword will fall, their fate entwined.
Israel, return to Yahweh, don't delay, You've stumbled in sin, let His mercy display.
Bring words of repentance, come back to His side, "Forgive all our wrongs, in Your goodness abide."
Assyria won't save us, no horses we'll ride, No more idols made from our hands as our guide.
"In You, the fatherless find mercy and grace," Said God with love, "I’ll heal their disgrace."
"I'll be like the dew, make Israel shine bright, Blossom like lilies, roots strong in their might."
Branches will spread, beauty like the olive tree, Fragrance like Lebanon, rich and free.
Men will dwell in His shade, grains will revive, Blossom like vines, in His fragrance they thrive.
Ephraim, idols are done, I care for you now, I’m a green cypress, your fruit I endow.
Who is wise, who understands this decree? Yahweh's ways are right, walk them righteously.
The just stride forward, but rebels will fall, In His path, find wisdom, His call to us all.
Yo, listen up, elders, hear the word, Spread it through the land, let it be heard.
Did this happen in your fathers' days? Tell your kids, let the story blaze.
Locusts swarm, they eat, they feast, Devour the land, north, west, and east.
Wake up, drunkards, feel the pain, Sweet wine's gone, it's all in vain.
A nation strong, countless, fierce, Lion teeth, they grip and pierce.
Vines laid waste, figs stripped bare, Branches white, lost in despair.
Mourn like a bride in sackcloth dress, For her lost love, in emptiness.
Offerings cut from Yahweh's house, Priests mourn, for blessings doused.
Fields destroyed, the land in tears, Grain is gone, new wine disappears.
Farmers, be shamed, cry out loud, The harvest gone, beneath the cloud.
Vines are dry, figs gone too, Joy's withered with all we knew.
Priests, put on sackcloth, wail, Lie down mourning, let your cries prevail.
Call a fast, gather, pray and shout, The day of Yahweh's near, no doubt.
Food is gone, joy's cut away, The seeds rot where they lay.
Animals groan, pastures bare, Flames devour, lands in despair.
"Yahweh, hear my cry, my plea, Fire's consumed the land and tree."
Animals pant, brooks dried up, In the wilderness, no water cup.
Blow the trumpet, sound the alarm, in Zion’s peak, Let all tremble, for Yahweh’s day ain’t weak.
Darkness looms, a day of deep gloom, Clouds roll thick, like a shadowy tomb.
A dawn spreads over mountains, mighty and grand, Like none before, nor after, in this land.
Fire devours, a flame trails behind, Eden before them, a wasteland they find.
Like horses they appear, like horsemen they ride, Chariots rumble, like flames they glide.
People tremble, faces turned pale, Warriors run strong, never do they fail.
They climb like warriors, march straight and true, Breaking defenses, none can undo.
Rushing the city, scaling the wall, Through windows they enter, thieves with gall.
Earth shakes, the heavens quiver, Sun and moon darkened, stars lose their shiver.
Yahweh thunders, his army’s great, His command obeyed, none can abate.
“Even now,” says Yahweh, “return to me, With fasting, weeping, and mourning, hear my plea.”
“Tear your heart, not your clothes, come back to your God, Gracious and merciful, forgiving the flawed.”
Who knows? Blessings might follow, Offerings for Yahweh, no more sorrow.
Blow the trumpet, call the fast that binds, Gather the people, leave no one behind.
Priests weep and plead, “Spare your nation, Let not the world mock, with their provocation.”
Yahweh’s jealous for his people and land, He sends grain, wine, and oil by his hand.
The northern threat now pushed away, Into barren lands, their stench will sway.
Land, don’t fear, rejoice at Yahweh’s deeds, Fields grow green, the earth proceeds.
“Be glad, children of Zion, sing and praise, For Yahweh sends rain in measured ways.”
Threshing floors full, vats overflow, Years devoured by locusts, Yahweh will bestow.
You’ll eat your fill and praise his name, Never again will you suffer shame.
Know Yahweh’s among you, none else, just him, “My Spirit I’ll pour, let visions brim.”
Sons and daughters will prophesy, Old men dream, young see visions fly.
Wonders in heaven, earth’s pillars of smoke, Sun turns dark, moon’s blood cloak.
Call Yahweh’s name, and you’ll be saved, In Zion, among those he’s called, you’re engraved.
In those days, at that time, fortunes restored, Judah and Jerusalem, blessings outpoured.
All nations I gather, to Jehoshaphat's vale, Judgment comes down, justice prevails.
Scattered my people, divided my land, Boys for a price, girls traded by hand.
"What are you to me, Tyre and Sidon?" I speak, "Philistia, repayment? It’s judgment you seek."
Stolen my treasure, gold and my silver, Judah's children sold, greed makes you shiver.
I'll raise them up, from where they were sold, Your children in turn, Judah’s hands will hold.
"Proclaim it now, nations prepare for war, Mighty men rise, hear the battle roar."
Plowshares to swords, pruning hooks to spears, Weak ones declare, "I'm strong,” face your fears.
Nations surround, gather for the fight, Yahweh’s might descends, righting the night.
In the valley they rise, where judgment's decreed, Put in the sickle, ripe is the seed.
The wine press is full, vats overflow, Their wickedness great, in the valley they go.
Multitudes throng, in decision's domain, Yahweh’s day nears, in judgment’s plain.
Sun and moon dark, stars lose their light, Yahweh roars from Zion, shaking the night.
Yet He’s a refuge, a stronghold to stand, Israel’s safe, under His hand.
"You will know I'm Yahweh, dwelling in Zion high, Jerusalem holy, strangers won’t pass by."
Mountains drip wine, hills flow with milk, Brooks of Judah, with waters of silk.
A fountain from Yahweh, Shittim’s thirst quench, Egypt desolate, Edom's end is clenched.
But Judah remains, forever secure, Jerusalem stands, generations endure.
Blood cleansed at last, Yahweh in Zion, For His people’s peace, His presence relying on.

Amos stepped up from Tekoa, herdsman by trade, With visions of Israel, God's warnings he displayed. He spoke of roaring from Zion, a voice from Jerusalem's core, Shepherds' pastures mourning, Carmel's peak no more.

"Yahweh says: For three sins of Damascus, and then four, Punishment's coming, can't ignore, they've threshed with iron for sure. I'll send fire on Hazael's house, Ben Hadad's palaces will fall, Break the bar of Damascus, no escape for them at all."

"Yahweh continues: Gaza's next, for three sins, then one more, Captives delivered to Edom, justice they can't ignore. Fire on Gaza's walls, palaces burned to ash, Ashdod and Ashkelon will face my mighty clash."
Ekron's fate sealed, Philistines' remnant fade, Yahweh's hand against them, in darkness they'll be laid. "Yahweh warns Tyre: for three, plus four, Covenant forgotten, they'll face my fiery roar."
"Edom, you're guilty, brother pursued with the sword, Pity cast aside, wrath forever stored. Fire on Teman's stronghold, Bozrah's grand halls, Edom's anger won't save them from the fiery calls."

"Ammon's children, hear; for three sins, and then four, Cruelty to Gilead's pregnant, can't be ignored. Rabbah's walls will blaze, palaces devoured in the fight, Their king and princes in chains, lost in the night."
"Yahweh speaks, judgment true, Nations judged for what they do." Amos brings the warning clear, God's justice will appear.
"For three sins of Moab, for four, the score’s been tallied, Burned bones of Edom’s king, now justice will be rallied.
I’ll send fire on Moab, palaces will fall, With tumult and shouting, hear the trumpet’s call.
Judges cut down, princes meet their fate, This is Yahweh’s word, no one can debate.
For three sins of Judah, yes, for four they stray, Rejected my law, let lies lead the way.
So fire on Judah, Jerusalem’s in flames, Their history’s forgotten, only they’re to blame.
For Israel’s transgressions, for four and more, Sold the righteous, traded the poor, a shameful score.
Dust on the heads of the trampled poor, Justice denied, profaning like never before.
Beside altars they lay, in clothes pledged, Drink wine of the fined, sinning unhedged.
Yet I took down the Amorite tall as the cedars stood, Destroyed them root and fruit, for your own good.
Brought you from Egypt, through wastelands wide, To claim Amorite land, with me as your guide.
Raised prophets and Nazirites from your own tribes, But you gave them wine, silenced their scribes.
"Behold," says Yahweh, "I’ll crush you down, Swift won’t escape, strength won’t be found.
The mighty will fall, no bowman will stand, Even the horse can’t deliver man’s hand.
On that day, the brave will flee away, Stripped bare by truth, naked they’ll stay."
Hear this word that Yahweh speaks, it's true, Against you, Israel, the ones He brought through.
"I chose you alone from the families wide, Now for your sins, you'll face the tide."
Do two stroll together without making a pact? Will a lion roar without its prey intact?
Do young lions shout when they've caught no meat? Can a bird get trapped without a snare beneath its feet?
Does a trumpet blast not bring fear to the town? When trouble strikes, is it Yahweh who's down?
For the Lord reveals to prophets what's concealed, The lion's roared, fear is revealed.
Proclaim in Ashdod, Egypt, rise to see, On Samaria's hills, witness the unrest and plea.
"They don't know to do right," says the Lord, They stash their loot, hoard upon hoard.
So Yahweh declares, "An enemy will invade, Your fortresses fall, your defenses unmade."
"As a shepherd saves from the lion's lair Two legs or an ear, what's left to spare,
So shall Israel be from Samaria's heights, On couches they sit, with silken delights."
"Listen and testify," Yahweh calls, Against Jacob's house, as the judgment falls.
"I'll visit Israel's sins, Bethel's altar's fate, The horns will fall, down they'll break."
Winter and summer houses both meet their demise, Ivory walls crumble, to end all their lies,"
Thus says Yahweh, the Lord of Armies, true, His word against Israel, what will they do?
Listen up now, you Bashan crew, On Samaria's hills, I'm talkin' to you. Oppressing the poor, crushing the weak, "Bring us drinks!" is all you speak.
The Lord's got a word, don't you doubt, "Days are comin', they'll fish you out. Hooks gonna pull you, line by line, Through breaks in the wall, it's a sign."
"Run to Bethel, go on, sin again, Gilgal too, add to your shameful spin. Bring your gifts, brag and boast, 'Cause that's the thing you love the most."
"Teeth are clean, but your plates are bare, Bread's run out, but you don't care. Rain's been scarce, crops don't grow, Yet back to Me, you refuse to go."
"Rain on one, drought on the next, Cities scramble, feeling perplexed. Blight and mildew, locust swarms, Yet still, no return to My arms."
"Plagues like Egypt, smell of decay, Young ones fallen, horses taken away. Burning cities, sticks in fire's blaze, Yet you turn not, in all your ways."
"Prepare, Israel, 'cause here's the call, Gonna meet your God, the Lord of all. Mountains formed, winds He creates, Darkness falls, as judgment waits."
"The God of Armies, His name rings true, And He's got a message just for you."
Hear this word, a lament so deep, Israel's virgin fallen, in her land she'll weep. No one to lift her, no chance to rise, A thousand march out, but a hundred survive.
"Seek Me, live; don't to Bethel roam, Gilgal and Beersheba won't be your home." "Fire in Joseph's house, it'll blaze, If you don't seek Me, no one quells that blaze."
Justice turned to wormwood's bitter taste, Righteousness cast down, all laid to waste. Seek the One who made the stars shine, Turns night to day, calls waters to align.
Destruction on the strong, the fortress falls, They hate the truth in judgment halls. Trample the poor, build homes of stone, But you'll live in them? No, you'll be alone.
Offenses are many, sins are vast, You bribe and ignore the needy cast. Prudent remain silent in times so grim, Evil reigns, but don't let it win.
"Seek good, not evil, so you may live, God of Armies, His presence will give. Hate evil, love good, justice in your courts, Remnant of Joseph, may find Yahweh's support."
Wailing in streets, from farmers to fields, Yahweh's presence, through the middle He yields. "Desire My day? It's darkness, not light, Flee from a lion, into a bear's bite."
"I loathe your feasts, your solemn show, Burnt offerings, peace offerings, I won't know. Noise of your songs, away, I demand, Let justice roll, like rivers through the land."
Sacrifices in the wild for forty years, Idol tents and gods you revered. Captivity beyond Damascus, you'll face, Says Yahweh, God of Armies, in this place.
Woe to the folks chillin' in Zion's ease, Secure on Samaria's heights, taking their peace. Notable men, where Israel flocks, See Calneh, Hamath, Gath—check their blocks.
Are they better than these lands you claim? Is their border broader, or just the same? Pushin' the evil day, bringin' violence near, Lyin' on ivory beds, no fear.
Stretchin' on couches, lambs they devour, Calves from the stalls, feast hour by hour. Strummin' harps, instruments they invent, Drinkin' from bowls, oils for their scent.
But never grieved for Joseph's pain, Their lounging feast will go down the drain. "The Lord Yahweh swears, I hate Jacob's pride, The city's fate? All inside will be fried."
Ten men in a house, death'll be their fate, Relatives carry bodies, silence, don't relate. "Hush, don't mention Yahweh's name," they say, Yahweh commands, the great house breaks away.
Do horses run on rock, do oxen plow the hard? You've turned justice into poison, righteousness marred. Rejoice in nothing, claim strength by your horn, But Yahweh will raise a new nation to scorn.
From Hamath's gate to the Arabah's flow, Yahweh's bringing the affliction, you'll know.
Locusts in the land, formed by His hand, Eatin' the grass, leavin' nothing to stand.
"Forgive, Lord Yahweh, I beg and plea, How can Jacob rise? He's small, you see."
Yahweh relented, "It shall not be," Mercy shown, setting Jacob free.
Then came fire, scorching the ground, "Dried up the deep, devoured all around."
"Stop, Lord Yahweh, spare the land, How can Jacob rise? He's small, understand."
"Again," said Yahweh, "I’ll hold my hand. This too shall not be, I’ll heed your command."
Next, a plumb line in His grip so tight, "Amos, what is it?" "A plumb line, right."
"In Israel's midst, a plumb line I’ll place, Won't pass them by, no more grace."
High places, desolate, sanctuaries laid waste, Against Jeroboam, with sword, I’ll haste.
Amaziah ran to Jeroboam, he cried, "Amos conspires, can't let this slide."
"Jeroboam will fall, Israel's fate is grim, Captivity awaits, future’s lookin' dim."
"Away, you seer, leave Bethel's gate, Prophesy elsewhere, leave the king's estate."
"I’m no prophet," Amos replied, "A herdsman, a farmer, where I abide."
"Yahweh called, from the flock He took, 'Prophesy to Israel,' with a steady look."
"Hear Yahweh’s word, listen and heed, You can't silence truth with your royal decree."
"Your wife, a fate she won’t resist, Sons, daughters fall, land divided, list."
"You’ll die in a place unclean and bare, Israel captive, taken from there."
Yo, the Lord Yahweh showed a scene so true, A basket of summer fruit, I said, "I see it too."
"The end's come for Israel, no more will I pass," Songs of the temple turn to wailing, alas.
Bodies lie everywhere, silence will reign, Those who oppress the poor will bear the pain.
"When's the new moon gone, so we can trade?" Cheating the scales, deceit's been displayed.
Buy the poor for silver, sandals for the needy, Selling the sweepings, oh so greedy.
Yahweh swore by Jacob's pride, "I won't forget, The land will tremble, its people will fret."
Rise like a river, then sink again low, Darkness at noon, the sun won't glow.
Feasts into mourning, songs into cries, Sackcloth and baldness, tears in their eyes.
"A famine's coming," says Yahweh's decree, Not of bread or water, but His word they'll seek.
From sea to sea, they'll wander in vain, Young men and virgins, thirst is their pain.
Those who swear by false gods will fall, And never again will they stand tall.
Standing by the altar, the Lord did say, "Strike those pillars, let them shake and sway.
Break them on the heads, let justice be served, None will escape, none will be preserved.
Dig to Sheol, my hand will bring you back, Climb to heaven, I'll pull you from your track.
Hide on Carmel's peak, I'll find you there, Dive to ocean's depths, the serpent's snare.
Captives before enemies, the sword will call, My eyes set against you, for evil to fall.
The Lord of Armies, with a touch, land melts away, Mournful cries rise like Egypt's river sway.
He builds in the heavens, his vault laid on earth, Calls ocean waters, pouring them forth.
"Like Ethiopians, Israel, to me you belong," Brought you from Egypt, now hear my song.
The Lord's eyes on the kingdom of sin, Destroy, but Jacob's house will begin again.
"I'll sift Israel through the nations' sieve, Not a kernel lost, all who live.
Sinners claiming 'Evil's far away,' The sword will find them, come what may.
In that day, David's tent I'll restore, Patch up the breaches, build it once more.
Possess Edom's remnant, and nations alike, Called by my name, their future bright.
"Days are coming," Yahweh's words resound, Plowman overtakes reaper, on fruitful ground.
Sweet wine dripping, mountains flow, Hills bring abundance, joy will grow.
I'll bring back my people, rebuild the land, Vineyards planted by their own hand.
Cities renewed, gardens bloom in sight, Planted firm, forever in their rightful light."
Yo, Obadiah saw a vision, here's the tale, Yahweh speaks on Edom, no way they prevail. News comes from Yahweh, nations hear the call, "Rise up, get ready, we're gonna watch her fall."
"Behold, you're small in the nation game, Despised and hated, that's your claim to fame. Pride's got you tricked in your rocky high place, Thinking, ‘Who can touch us? Who's got the space?’"
"Fly high like the eagle, nest with the stars, But I'll bring you down, no matter how far," Says Yahweh. "Thieves at night, coming for your gold, Grape pickers show up, won't leave a grape untold."
"Oh, Esau’s treasures, they're all sought out, Your allies ditch you, without a doubt. Friends at your table, they lay a snare, You’re lost in confusion, unaware."
"Wise men of Edom, they won’t stay wise, On the mountain of Esau, wisdom dies." Mighty men of Teman, feel the dismay, Esau’s mountain falls, everyone’s in the fray.
Violence to Jacob brings you shame, Cut off forever, that’s your name. When strangers plundered, you stood aside, Joining in the chaos, you were allied.
"Don't look on Judah in their distress, Don’t speak with pride in their mess. Don’t walk through their gates on that dark day, Don’t take their wealth, just walk away."
"Don’t block the escapees, let them flee, Don’t trap the survivors, let them be. The day of Yahweh’s near, it's coming soon, Your deeds boomerang back, your own tune."
"As you drank on my mountain high, Nations will drink, then say goodbye. But in Zion, some will escape, Jacob's house will take the shape."
"Jacob’s a fire, Joseph's a flame, Esau’s stubble, that's the name. They'll burn and consume, Esau’s no more, Yahweh's word seals the score."
South claims Esau, lowlands take Philistine, Fields and lands, Ephraim and Samaria seen. Benjamin holds Gilead, captives break free, Possessing Negev, claiming destiny.
On Mount Zion, saviors rise, Judging Esau, claiming the prize. Yahweh's kingdom, it will reign, The vision's clear, Yahweh's domain.
Yahweh spoke to Jonah, said, "Get up and go, To Nineveh, preach, let that great city know." But Jonah took flight, ran the opposite way, Down to Joppa he went, found a ship that same day.

Paid his fare, bound for Tarshish, he fled from the Lord, Yet Yahweh sent winds, a storm roared and soared. The sailors, they trembled, each cried to their god, They tossed cargo over, yet Jonah slept odd.
The captain shook Jonah, "Wake up, and plead, Pray to your God, we’re in desperate need!" They cast lots for answers, the lot it found one, It fell upon Jonah, his secret undone.

"Who are you?" they asked, "Why this storm on our seas?" Jonah replied, "I'm Hebrew, and Yahweh I please. The God of the heavens, who made land and sea, It's my flight from Him that caused this decree."

Fear gripped the sailors, "Tell us, what must be done? How to calm this chaos? How to halt this run?" Jonah said, "Throw me over; the storm will cease its roar, For my cause this tempest, my presence you must ignore."

Despite Jonah's plea, they rowed, wouldn't quit, But the sea grew fiercer, they couldn't conquer it. To Yahweh they cried, "Don't blame us, we plea, You've done what you willed, let us not share his decree."

So over went Jonah, into the sea so wild, And the ocean grew calm like a peaceful child. The men feared Yahweh, they sacrificed and vowed, And Yahweh sent a fish that swallowed Jonah, proudly endowed.
Three days, three nights, in the belly Jonah stayed, In the depths of the sea, in the fish he prayed.
In the belly of the beast, Jonah prayed, feeling low, He called out to Yahweh, where else could he go?
"From the depths of my pain, I cried out for aid, And out of the shadows, my cry was relayed.
You tossed me in waters, the heart of the sea, All the waves crashed down, surrounding me.
I thought I was lost, banished from Your sight, Yet I turned to Your temple, hoping for light.
Deep waters rose up, pulling at my soul, With seaweed around me, taking its toll.
Down to the roots, to the mountain's base, The earth held me tight, a relentless embrace.
But You, Yahweh, my God, You lifted my life, From the pit of despair, freeing me from strife.
When my spirit was weak, Your name I recalled, My prayer reached Your temple, my heart enthralled.
Those who chase lies, mercy they leave, But I offer thanks, in You I believe.
With vows I will honor, Your grace I acclaim, For salvation is Yours, forever Your name."
Then Yahweh spoke, the fish set him free, Jonah on dry land, finally released, to be.
God spoke to Jonah, "Hear my call, Head to Nineveh, preach to them all."
Jonah got up, no time to delay, To the great city, made his way.
A city so vast, three days to span, He entered and cried, "Forty days, that's the plan!"
Nineveh listened, believed, and feared, A fast was proclaimed, sackcloth appeared.
From the least to the great, everyone knew, Their king rose up, changed his view.
Off came the robe, on went the sack, Sat down in ashes, no turning back.
Decree went out, through the land it spread, "Don't eat, don't drink," the king said.
"Man and beast, in sackcloth clad, Cry out to God, leave the bad."
"Who knows," he asked, "if God will spare, And turn away His anger's glare?"
God saw their deeds, the change within, He relented, forgave their sin.
Jonah sat seething, frustration on fire, His anger with God rising higher and higher.
He prayed, "Oh Yahweh, wasn’t this my fear, Back home I knew, that's why I'm here.
You're gracious and kind, mercy your trade, Slow to anger, your love never fades.
Now take my life, I beg, let me be, Better to die than live in this plea!"
God asked, "Is it right to rage and burn?" Jonah left the city, hoping to learn.
He built a booth, sat in its shade, Waiting to see what judgement was made.
God grew a vine, shade over his head, Jonah felt joy, his anger fled.
But dawn came, a worm brought doom, The vine withered, sealing its gloom.
The sun beat down, the wind did sway, Jonah wished again for his life to decay.
God asked, "That vine, should anger confine?" Jonah cried, "I'm right, even to die this time."
God said, "You weep for vines you didn't seed, Yet care for a city is not my deed?
A place of thousands, lost in their plight, Shouldn’t I show concern, bring them light?"
Micah got the word, in the days of the kings, For Samaria and Jerusalem, truth it brings.
"Listen, all you people, hear the earth proclaim, Yahweh from His temple, calling out your name."
Look, Yahweh's stepping down from His holy place, Treads on the high mountains, earth shakes in His face.
Mountains melt like wax, valleys split and part, Like water pouring down, nature plays its part.
"For the sins of Jacob, Samaria's the cause, Judah's high places, breaking all My laws."
"Samaria, I'll turn you to rubble and stone, Vines will claim your ground, foundations overthrown."
"Idols crushed to pieces, temple gifts in flame, Prostitution’s wage, returns from whence it came."
So I lament, I wail, stripped and bare, I cry, Howl like jackals, moan as night owls fly.
Her wounds are deep, incurable the pain, From her gates to Judah, trouble's in the lane.
"Don't speak it in Gath, don't shed a tear, In Beth Ophrah, dust rolls with fear."
Shaphir's folks walk in shame, Zaanan won't appear, Beth Ezel's cry rings out, no help is near.
Maroth waits in hope, but evil descends, From Yahweh's gate, Jerusalem it bends.
"Lachish, harness swift steeds, you're the sin's start, Israel's transgressions found, tearing it apart."
"Gifts to Moresheth Gath, deceit in Achzib's place, Mareshah, I’ll send glory, Adullam brace."
"Shave your heads in mourning, hair falls to the floor, Mourn for your children, captive evermore."
Woe to the schemers, plotting evil in bed, When morning comes, they act out what's in their head.
They covet fields, they take what they see, Oppressing a man, his home, and his legacy.
Yahweh speaks: "Behold, disaster's in line, You'll bow your necks in this evil time."
A lament will rise, a doleful cry, "We're ruined! Our fields, taken by and by."
No one to divide the land in Yahweh's space, "Don't prophesy," they say, "no disgrace will we face."
House of Jacob, say it clear: "Is Yahweh angry? Do my words bring fear?"
But my people rise as an enemy, Stripping robes from passersby in their spree.
Driving women from homes, taking blessings from the young, Arise, depart! This land's corruption is sung.
False prophets speak of wine and dreams, They're the voices this people deems.
"I'll gather Jacob, every last one, Like sheep in Bozrah, when the day is done."
The way breaker leads, they break through the gate, Their king before them, with Yahweh innate.
Listen up now, leaders of Jacob's crew, Isn't justice what you're supposed to pursue? But you love what's evil, despise what's right, Tearing off skin, devouring with might.
You eat my people like they're meat for your pot, Break their bones, leave them to rot. You’ll cry to Yahweh, but he’ll turn away, Hide his face, 'cause you led astray.
Prophets lie, lead my people blind, For a bite to eat, they proclaim, "All's fine!" But if you don’t feed them, they’ll wage war, Darkness falls, visions no more.
"The seers are lost, the diviners confused, Lips sealed tight, no answer for the abused." But me, I'm filled with Yahweh’s might, To declare Jacob's sins, and bring truth to light.
Hear this, rulers, who twist the laws, Build Zion with blood, ignoring flaws. Judges take bribes, priests speak for a fee, Prophets lie for cash, claiming, "Safe are we."
But Zion will be plowed, Jerusalem a heap, The temple's mount a forest, dark and deep.
In the days ahead, Yahweh's mountain will rise, Above all peaks, reaching high to the skies.
Nations will say, "Let's climb, let's seek, To God's house we'll go, his wisdom we'll speak."
From Zion the law, from Jerusalem his word, He'll judge the peoples, his voice will be heard.
Swords into plowshares, spears to pruning hooks, No more war, just peace in the books.
Under the vine, under the fig tree they’ll stay, No fear in their hearts, Yahweh’s spoken today.
Others may follow gods of their own, But we'll walk with Yahweh, we're never alone.
"In that day," Yahweh declares with might, "I'll gather the lame, bring them to the light.
Though they were scattered, they’ll come back strong, Yahweh will reign forever, where they belong."
To the tower, the flock, Zion's hill so high, The kingdom will return, as time goes by.
Why do you cry, is your king now gone? Is pain gripping you, like a laboring dawn?
Endure the pain, like birth pangs anew, You'll leave the city, to fields you'll pursue.
In Babylon's land, rescue is near, Yahweh will redeem you from all you fear.
Nations gather, eyes set to defile, But they don't know Yahweh, his plans are worthwhile.
"Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, make haste, With iron horns and bronze hoofs, no time to waste.
Break the nations, their wealth I'll claim, For Yahweh, Lord of earth, in his holy name."
Troops are gathering, the siege is on, Israel's judge gets struck, the battle's begun.
But Bethlehem Ephrathah, you're small but grand, A ruler comes forth, ancient, destined to stand.
He'll leave them till the labor brings forth birth, Then brothers will return, reclaim their worth.
He'll stand and shepherd with Yahweh's might, In His name's majesty, they'll live in the light.
Peace he'll bring when Assyria invades, Seven shepherds rise, eight leaders in spades.
They'll wield the sword in Assyria's lands, Deliverance at the borders, wielding their hands.
Jacob's remnant, like dew on grass, Silent blessings, no need to ask.
Like lions in forests, fierce and bold, Through nations they move, strong and untold.
"Your hand will rise, adversaries fall, Enemies gone, hear Yahweh's call:
'I’ll cut your horses, chariots too, Destroy your cities, all you knew.
No more witchcraft, no soothsayers here, Images and pillars, I’ll make them disappear.
Uproot your poles, tear down your town, Vengeance on nations, my wrath comes down.'"
"Rise up," He says, "take your place, Let mountains and hills hear your case. Listen up, ancient stones and earth, Yahweh's got a word, a rebirth.
People, what have I done to you? How did I burden, what did I do? I took you from Egypt's chains, Through Moses, Aaron, Miriam's reign.
Recall Balak's wicked plot, And Balaam's words, the lesson taught. From Shittim to Gilgal, see, The righteous acts of Yahweh, free.
How should I stand before the Lord? With calves, or gifts I can't afford? Thousands of rams, rivers of oil, Firstborn for sins that spoil?
He's shown what’s good, plain to see, Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly.
Yahweh calls, hear wisdom’s song, "Listen to the rod that keeps you strong. Do you hide treasures cursed and sly? Or measure with scales that lie?
Rich with violence, deceit on their lips, Their words are twisted, truth just slips. So I've struck you down, pain's my tool, Desolation comes, sin's cruel.
You'll eat, but hunger stays, Store up, but it decays. Sow the seeds, but reap won't come, Olives pressed, yet oil's numb.
You follow Omri and Ahab's way, A path to ruin, in dismay. Hissing whispers of disgrace, Bearing reproach, you lose face."
Misery's mine, picking fruit in vain, No grapes on the vine, just empty pain.
The godly vanish, none upright in sight, Hunting each other, they fight through the night.
Hands on evil, bribes rule the land, Rulers conspire, their wicked plans stand.
Best of them's a brier, thorns in their soul, Watchmen's day comes, confusion takes its toll.
"Don't trust your neighbor, don't lean on a friend, Mind your words, even with those you depend."
Sons against fathers, daughters against mothers, Enemies at home, even among brothers.
But as for me, I look to Yahweh above, Wait for salvation, His light and His love.
"Don't gloat, my foe, for I'll rise when I fall, In darkness, Yahweh shines, His light on us all."
I'll bear His wrath, for I've sinned 'neath His view, Till He pleads my case, His justice rings true.
Enemies see, their shame covers their face, Trod like street mire, they fall from their place.
Walls will rise, boundaries extend wide, From Assyria to Egypt, God's people abide.
Lands desolate, fruits of deeds take their toll, Shepherd Your flock, guide each wandering soul.
"As in Egypt's days, My wonders I'll show, Nations will quake, their strength laid low."
Dust they'll lick, serpents bent in dread, Trembling before Yahweh, their fear widespread.
Who pardons like You, passes over our wrong, Loving kindness His delight, His anger not long.
He'll tread sins down, cast them far away, Truth to Jacob, mercy to stay.
Sworn to our fathers, from ancient times heard, Compassion flows, faithful to His word.
Nahum sees a vision, Nineveh in sight, Yahweh’s wrathful, ready for the fight.
God's jealous, takes vengeance with a flame, Anger's slow, yet His power's the same.
Enemies quake, they feel His might, In the storm and whirlwind, He takes flight.
The sea dries up, rivers run no more, Bashan, Carmel, Lebanon, sore.
Mountains quake, hills melt away, Earth trembles where He holds sway.
"Who can stand when anger ignites? Fire pours, rocks break in His sights."
But Yahweh’s good, a refuge strong, He knows His own, where they belong.
An overflowing flood will end the strife, Enemies pursued into the night of life.
"What plot you against the Lord’s plan? Once ended, affliction won’t rise again."
Thorns entangle, they drown in their drink, Consumed like stubble, dry as you think.
One devises evil, wicked in his ways, Yahweh sees him, ends his days.
God says: "Though they’re strong and many, I'll cut them down, no longer any."
"I've afflicted, but no more, Break the yoke, bonds I’ll restore."
"No name will bear on this vile place, Images gone, a grave in disgrace."
See the feet on the mountains bright, Bringing good news, peace in sight.
Judah, keep your vows and feast, The wicked’s gone, forever ceased.
The one who shatters comes right at you, Guard the fort, watch your path—do what you gotta do!
Yahweh lifts Jacob's honor high, Though destroyers tore 'em down, left 'em dry.
Red shields gleam on the warrior's arm, Chariots flash, spears cause alarm.
In the streets, those chariots storm, Like torch-lit lightning, they transform.
Troops are summoned, stumble, and fall, Rushing, they dash, right to the wall.
River gates open, palace dissolves, All is exposed, as mystery evolves.
Nineveh’s pool, long been still, Now folks flee, against their will.
"Stop! Stop!" the cries ring out, But no one turns, without a doubt.
Plunder silver, plunder gold, Endless treasures, stories told.
Empty, void, waste in the air, Hearts melt, knees shake in despair.
Where lions roamed without a care, Now silence reigns where none would dare.
Lions once feasted, caves filled with prey, Now Yahweh speaks, hear what He'll say:
"Behold, I'm against you," Yahweh declares, "Chariots burn, and lions beware.
Your prey cut off, voices fade away, No more messengers, no more sway."
Woe to the city, full of deceit and theft, Prey never leaves, it's all that's left.
Whips crack, wheels clatter loud, Horses prance, chariots proud.
A rider mounts, swords flash bright, Spears gleam, bodies lost to the fight.
Heap of corpses, can't find an end, Stumbling over bodies, around the bend.
Prostitution's charm, witchcraft's might, Nations and families sold in the night.
"Behold, I'm against you," Yahweh declares, "I'll shame your face, strip you bare.
Nations will see, kingdoms will know, I'll make you vile, a spectacle show.
Folks will flee, saying, 'Nineveh's waste, Who'll mourn for her, in such haste?'"
Better than No-Amon, sitting 'midst rivers grand, With waters, the sea was her wall and stand.
Cush and Egypt her strength unbound, Put and Libya her helpers, around.
Yet she was taken, captive she went, Children dashed, her men in torment.
"You'll be drunk, seek strongholds wide, Gates open, fire devours inside."
Troops like women, fortresses like figs, Shaken, they fall, into the eater's digs.
Draw water, strengthen the stronghold's might, Tread the clay, make bricks tight.
Fire will consume, sword will sever, Devour like locusts, now or never.
Merchants like stars, locusts they flee, Guards like swarms, nowhere to see.
Shepherds sleep, nobles lay low, People scatter, mountains they go.
No healing your wound, fatal you be, All clap their hands, acknowledging your cruelty.
Habakkuk's vision hit his eyes like a bomb, "Yahweh, why you silent while violence runs strong? I scream out 'Violence!' but where's your salvation? I see iniquity, a twisted creation.
Destruction, violence, strife everywhere, The law's paralyzed, justice is rare. The wicked surround, the righteous get bent, Justice is twisted, not heaven-sent.
"Look to the nations, watch, be amazed, I'm working a work that'll leave you dazed. Raising the Chaldeans, bitter and fast, Marching the earth, taking lands vast.
Feared and dreaded, their judgment their own, Swifter than leopards, fierce to the bone. Horsemen fly like eagles, ready to feast, They come for violence, a merciless beast.
Kings get mocked, princes are jokes, Laughs at strongholds, at their walls he pokes. Sweeps like the wind, guilty and loud, His strength's his god, his head's unbowed."
"Yahweh, aren't you eternal, my Rock, my Holy One? We won't die, you've set him to punish, it's done. Pure eyes that can't see evil's grime, Why silent while wicked swallow the righteous in time?
Men like fish, creeping things in the sea, Hooked and netted, no ruler, no decree. He catches, rejoices, with fish in his net, Burns incense to dragnets, living without regret.
Will he forever empty his net, Killing nations, no mercy, no debt?"
I stand at my watch, I’m up on the wall, Waiting to hear Yahweh's call. He said, "Write the vision clear for all to see, So even those who run can read and agree.
The vision's set for an appointed time, It’s racing to the end, it’s gonna align. Wait, though it may seem to delay, It’s surely coming, won’t fade away.
Look, the proud soul’s all puffed and wrong, But the righteous live by faith, they stay strong. Wine’s a trap, it makes him roam, Desires as deep as Sheol, never at home.
Nations and peoples he stacks in a heap, But soon they'll rise and make him weep. "Woe to him who steals and takes, How long before his world shakes?"
Your debtors will rise, make you feel small, You’ve plundered nations, now you’ll fall. For the blood and violence you’ve spread around, The land will echo with a vengeful sound.
Woe to those who build with evil gain, High nests crumble, bringing only pain. You’ve brought shame, you’ve cut down souls, The walls will cry, the beams speak of your goals.
"Woe to the city built with blood and sin, Yahweh’s watching, can’t keep it in. The earth will brim with His glory wide, Like waters covering the sea, none can hide.
"Woe to those who pour out drink, To watch their neighbors fall and sink. You’ll feel shame, not glory’s light, Yahweh’s cup will bring the night.
Violence to Lebanon, the beasts and the land, All the bloodshed, they can’t withstand. What’s an idol but a lifeless face? It can’t teach, can’t take Yahweh’s place.
"Woe to him who calls the wood to wake, Or tells the silent stone to shake. Gold and silver can’t give life, No breath within, no end to strife.
But Yahweh’s in His holy place, The earth falls silent before His face!"
Yo, Habakkuk’s in the house, hear the prophet's prayer, "Yahweh, I heard your fame, I know you're there."
In the years renew, make it known, I plea, In your wrath, remember mercy, set the captives free.
God came from Teman, from Paran did He shine, Glory filled the heavens, earth sang with a holy line.
His splendor rose like sunrise, rays from His hand, Where power lay hidden, mighty, grand.
Plague went before Him, pestilence trailed behind, He shook the earth, nations trembled, mountains declined.
Cushan's tents afflicted, Midian shivered with dread, "Was Yahweh mad at rivers?" to the sea He sped.
Uncovered His bow, arrows sworn to fly, Split the earth with rivers, mountains feared the sky.
Waters rose, deep roared, lifted hands on high, Sun and moon stood still, arrows lit the sky.
He marched in wrath, nations felt His ire, For His people's salvation, kindled His holy fire.
Crushed the wicked's head, stripped them bare, Pierced them with their own spears, scattered everywhere.
Trampled the sea with horses, waters churned, I heard, my body trembled, soul burned.
Though the fig tree's barren, no fruit on the vine, Yet in Yahweh I’ll rejoice, His joy is mine.
Yahweh, my strength, makes my feet like a deer, In high places He sets me, drives out fear.
For the music director, stringed instruments play, Praise to Yahweh, the Lord, every single day.
In the days of Josiah, a word from the Lord, To Zephaniah it came, sharp as a sword. "Everything's swept from the earth's face," He declared, "Man and beast, sky and sea, nothing will be spared.
Birds and fish, rubble, and wickedness too, All will be cut off, this warning's for you. Against Judah, My hand will extend, Their idols and priests will meet their end.
Those who worship on rooftops the stars, Who mix My name with Malcam's scars. Turned back from Me, they didn't seek, The day is near; it's not for the meek.
Be still in My presence, the sacred is near, I've prepared a feast, the chosen appear. Princes and kings will face My command, Foreign clothes won't save the land.
Leaping thresholds, with violence and lies, Punishment's coming, drowned in cries. From fish gate to hills, the cry will resound, Canaan's people undone, silver unbound.
I'll search Jerusalem, lamps in hand, Punish the complacent, who've misunderstood My stand. Their houses will rot, wealth turned to dust, Building and planting denied, in their trust.
The day of the Lord is racing near, Mighty men weep, overcome by fear. Wrath, distress, day of gloom and despair, Trumpets sound, fortified walls tear.
Men will stumble, blind by their sin, Blood like dust, flesh discarded in the din. Gold and silver won't buy salvation's release, Fire of jealousy ends the land’s peace."
Gather round, you nation with no shame, Before the day chaffs away, before Yahweh’s flame.
"Seek me now," He calls, "those humble and true, Seek righteousness, seek humility too."
Gaza forsaken, Ashkelon laid bare, Ashdod at noon, Ekron torn in the air.
Woe to the coast, Cherethites hear the sound, Yahweh's word's against you, soon no one around.
Pastures and flocks will claim the sea's edge, Judah's remnant will rest, God will keep his pledge.
He’s heard Moab's scorn, Ammon’s insult loud, Once mighty borders, now nettles in a shroud.
As Sodom was, so Moab shall be, Ammon as Gomorrah, laid waste by decree.
Yahweh’s wrath will famish the gods of the land, All shores will know Him, and bow to His hand.
You Cushites too will face my sword's might, Assyria falls, Nineveh’s night.
Animals rest where cities once stood, Calls echo through windows, in the cedar wood.
The joyous city, once careless and bold, Now desolate and barren, the stories told.
"I am, no other," were her prideful boasts, Now she’s a ruin, with ghosts as her hosts.
Woe to the city, rebellious and stained, Ignored the voice, her soul remained unchained.
Princes like lions, judges like wolves at night, Devouring all, leaving none in sight.
Arrogant prophets, priests defiling law, Injustice reigns without a flaw.
"Fear me," I said, "Receive correction true," But they woke early to corrupt anew.
"Wait for me," says Yahweh, "when I rise to the fight, Gather the nations, pour out my might.
Purify lips, call my name together, People serving me, through stormy weather.
Beyond the rivers, offerings will bring, No more shame in the songs you sing."
The proud removed, the humble will remain, Taking refuge in Yahweh's name.
No more lies, no deceit will be found, Peaceful pastures, fear unbound.
Sing, daughter Zion, shout with all your heart, Yahweh's presence never to depart.
"Don't be afraid," the message is clear, Yahweh's might always near.
He’ll rejoice over you, calm in his embrace, Singing love, removing disgrace.
"I'll deal with your foes, gather the lost, Give them praise, no longer at cost.
I'll restore fortunes, bring you honor and fame," Says Yahweh, with power in his name.
In Darius's year two, month six, day one, Came Yahweh's word, a message begun.
Through Haggai the prophet, to leaders it flew, Zerubbabel and Joshua, what they must do.
Yahweh declared, “These people say, 'Not yet time for my house; we'll delay.'”
But Haggai spoke, words sharp and clear, "Is it time for your homes, while mine's left mere?"
“Consider your ways,” said Yahweh with might, “You've sown, yet little comes to sight.
You eat, not satisfied; you drink, still dry, You clothe yourselves, yet warmth's a lie.
Wages drop through holes, nothing you hold, Consider your ways, hear what I’ve told.
Go to the mountains, bring wood, build anew, I'll take pleasure, glorify what's true.”
"You hoped for much, and it came to small, I blew it away, why?" His voice did call.
“Because my house lies waste, while yours you chase, Thus heavens hold dew, earth withholds its grace.
I called drought on land, grain, and oil, On men, beasts, all hands’ toil.”
Zerubbabel, Joshua, and people in fear, Heard Yahweh's voice, obeyed, drew near.
Then Haggai said, "Yahweh's with you," Spirit stirred in hearts, they knew.
Zerubbabel and Joshua, leaders bold, With the people, built as they were told.
On the twenty-fourth day, in month six’s fame, In year of Darius, they honored His name.
Seventh month, twenty-first day, Yahweh spoke, Haggai the prophet, delivering hope's cloak. "Zerubbabel, Joshua, listen to my call, And to all the people, stand strong and tall.
Who remembers this house in former glory? Now it looks like nothing, just a shadow story. Yet be strong, Zerubbabel," Yahweh repeats, "Be strong, Joshua, stand firm on your feet.
All you people, rise, for I am here, Yahweh of Armies speaks, have no fear. I pledged my word when Egypt was left behind, My Spirit lives with you, peace of mind.
Once more I'll shake earth, sea, and sky, Nations will tremble, as glory draws nigh. Silver and gold, all belong to me, This house will shine, greater it shall be.
On the twenty-fourth day, ninth month rolled, Yahweh's new word, by Haggai was told. "Ask the priests about the sacred law, Does holy meat make other food pure?"
"No," said the priests, "it won't transfer the grace." Haggai replied, "This is Israel's case. Unclean they are, in all they present, Their works defiled, they must repent.
Consider the past, when stones were first laid, Shortfall of harvest, in work they stayed. Blight, mildew, hail, struck all that you grew, Yet back to me you never flew.
From this day forth, mark it clear, Blessings will flow, no more fear. Seed in the barn, fruits yet unshown, From today’s end, blessings I’ll loan.”
Again Yahweh spoke, same day’s light, To Zerubbabel, His promise bright. "Heavens and earth, I'll shake once more, Thrones will crumble, kingdoms will pour.
Chariots, riders, all will fall, Each by the sword of his brother’s call. In that day, Zerubbabel, my chosen seal, As a signet ring, my covenant real."
In the eighth month's glow, second year of Darius' show, Yahweh spoke to Zechariah, words began to flow.
"Yahweh's displeased with your fathers, hear me now," "Return to me," He said, "I'll come to you somehow."
"Don't be like them, who ignored my call," They didn't listen, and they faced the fall.
"Fathers are gone, prophets don't last," But my words remain, standing fast.
They repented, realizing their fate, "Yahweh dealt with us, as our ways relate."
Shebat's eleventh month, the vision's clear, A man on a red horse, standing near.
Among myrtle trees in a ravine's fold, Red, brown, white horses, mysteries to be told.
I asked, "What are these, my Lord?" The angel said, "I'll show, heed my word."
The man among trees spoke, "Yahweh's spies," They roam the earth, under the skies.
Reporting back, "The earth's at peace," But the angel asked, "When will mercy release?"
Yahweh answered with comfort and grace, "I burn with jealousy for Zion's place."
"Angry at nations, too much they've done," "My mercy returns, Jerusalem won."
"My house rebuilt, lines drawn with care," "My cities prosper, Yahweh's there."
I lifted my eyes, four horns I saw, "What are these?" I asked in awe.
"Horns scattered Judah, Israel's plight," Four craftsmen come to set things right.
"To cast down nations, terrify, disband," For Judah's sake, they'll take a stand.
Eyes lifted high, saw a man with a line, "Where you headed?" I asked, in the divine.
He said, "To measure Jerusalem, width and length," An angel stepped out, with heavenly strength.
"Run, tell that young man, hear what I say, Jerusalem's vast, no walls in the way."
"Many will gather with livestock and kin, I'll be a fire, my glory within."
"Come on, flee north, leave Babylon's land, I've scattered you wide, like dust from the hand."
"Zion, escape! The call is loud, Let's move from Babylon, join this crowd."
For Yahweh declares, with armies in tow, "Who touches you, feels my wrath, you know."
"Shake my hand, watch them fall and break, Those who served will plunder for your sake."
"Sing, daughter of Zion, rejoice with me, I'm coming to dwell, you'll see who I'll be."
"Many nations will join, they'll all be mine, I'll dwell among you, everything's fine."
"Judah's my choice, my land, my delight, Jerusalem chosen, shining so bright."
Be silent, all flesh, Yahweh awakes, From His holy place, a move He makes.
I saw Joshua stand before the angel's light, With Satan on his right, ready to fight. God spoke to Satan with a rebuke so bold, “Yahweh rebukes you, Satan, behold!
This is a stick plucked from the fire’s heat," Joshua's garments were filthy, at his feet. Angel said, "Remove those filthy clothes, Your sins are gone, and new robes I bestow.”
“Put a clean turban on his head," was my call, They clothed him fresh, standing tall. Yahweh’s angel spoke, words clear and bright, “Walk in my ways, you'll judge with right.
Keep my courts, you'll have a place to stand, Among these here, in this holy land. Joshua, hear, you and your crew, For I’ll bring the Branch, something new.
Before Joshua, a stone with seven eyes, Yahweh's engraving makes the iniquity fly. In one day, sins will vanish away, Then each neighbor, beneath vine and fig stay.”
Neighbors gathered, peace in sight, Under the fig, in Yahweh’s light.
The angel came back, shook me from my sleep, Woke me up like a man from slumber deep.
"What do you see?" he asked me with a gaze, "I see a gold lamp stand with its seven blaze,
A bowl on top, seven lamps alight, Pipes to each lamp, shining bright.
Two olive trees stand, one left, one right," I asked, "What are these?" in the angel's sight.
"Don't you know?" the angel asked, sincere, I replied, "No, my lord, make it clear."
Then he spoke with Yahweh's word to say, "Not by might or power, but my Spirit's way."
"Who are you, mountain, rising in pride? Before Zerubbabel, you'll be flat and wide.
He'll bring the capstone, with shouts of grace, Calling 'Grace, grace!' in this sacred place."
Yahweh's word came straight to me, "Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation, see?
He'll finish the work, his hands will do, Then you'll know Yahweh sent me to you.
Who despises the day of things so small? These seven shall rejoice, watch the plumb line fall.
Yahweh's eyes, they search the earth, Back and forth, seeing every worth."
I asked again, "What are these olive trees, Side by side with the lamp stand, if you please?"
Twice I asked, "What are these branches of gold, Pouring oil from spouts, so bold?"
He replied, "Don't you know?" once more, I said, "No, my lord, I implore."
"These are the anointed ones," he said to me, "Standing by the Lord of earth, faithfully."
I looked up high, what did I see? A scroll flying by, as plain as can be.
He asked, "What do you see there, my friend?" "A flying scroll," I said, "twenty cubits long end to end."
"This is the curse," he declared with power, "For thieves and liars, their final hour."
"It enters the thief's home, no place to hide, Tearing down walls, swallowing pride."
"Lift your eyes," the angel drew near, "See what appears, don't you fear."
"What is it now?" I asked in awe, "An ephah basket, that's what I saw."
A lead weight lifted, a woman inside, "This is Wickedness," he said, open wide.
He tossed her down, sealed her tight, Locked in the basket, out of sight.
Two women flew with wind in their wings, Stork-like they soared, carrying things.
"Where do they take her?" I asked the guide, "To Shinar," he said, "where she will reside."
