A house to be built, her own domain, In the land of Shinar, she'll remain.
I lifted my eyes, and what did I see? Four chariots rolling between bronze peaks, wild and free.
The first had red horses, fierce and bold, In the second, black horses, dark as coal.
The third rode in with steeds of white, And the fourth, dappled, a powerful sight.
I asked the angel, "My lord, what’s the deal?" He said, "These are the four winds, heaven's seal."
The black horses charge to the north land, The white behind, as if hand in hand.
The dappled head south, spreading wide, While strong ones roam the earth with pride.
He spoke, "Go, walk the earth, roam and track!" So they moved, forth and back.
Then he called, "Those in the north, They've quieted my spirit from henceforth."
Yahweh’s word came, bold and clear, "Gather from captivity, bring them near.
Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, come today, To Josiah’s house, where they from Babylon stay.
Take silver, take gold, craft a crown, Place it on Joshua, the high priest renowned.
Tell him, 'Yahweh of Armies declares, The Branch will rise, building temple stairs.
Yes, he will build, he’ll bear the glory, He’ll sit on the throne, that's the story.
He'll rule and priest, in peace unite, The counsel of peace shall be their light.
Crowns for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, Hen, A memorial in Yahweh’s temple, amen.
From afar, they’ll come to build Yahweh’s place, You'll know Yahweh sent me in this grace.
It’ll happen if you heed and hear, Yahweh’s voice, loud and clear."
In the fourth year of Darius, the scene was set, Yahweh's word to Zechariah, on the date you won't forget.
From Bethel they came, Sharezer and Regem Melech too, Seeking Yahweh's favor, wondering what to do.
"Should we weep in the fifth month, again this year, As we've done in the past, shedding many a tear?"
Then Yahweh's word came, strong and clear, "Speak to the people, let all the priests hear.
When you fasted and mourned, was it for me? Or was it for yourselves, can't you see?
When you eat and drink, isn't it self-driven? Aren't these the words by prophets once given?
Back when Jerusalem was bustling with life, And around her, cities free from strife."
Then Yahweh spoke again, with a message profound, "True judgment, kindness, let them abound.
Don't oppress the widow, the fatherless, or the poor, Show compassion, keep evil from your core."
But they turned away, refused to hear the call, Hardened their hearts, unyielding as a wall.
Yahweh’s wrath was stirred, from neglect and defiance, He called, they ignored, now they face the consequence.
"Just as they ignored, and turned from my voice, I'll scatter them far, they've left me no choice.
A whirlwind will take them to lands unknown, For the desolate land is what they have sown."
Thus the scene is set, the message is clear, Actions have consequences, heed what you hear.
The word of Yahweh came, strong and true, "Jealous for Zion, with a wrathful hue."
"I’ve returned to Zion, where truth shall reign, In Jerusalem's heart, my presence will remain.
Old men, old women, strolling the street, Boys and girls playing where laughter meets.
If it’s marvelous to you, why not to me?" Yahweh of Armies declares with decree.
"From east and west, my people I'll save, In Jerusalem they'll dwell, as I pave the way.
Be strong, hear this from prophets of old, When no wages were paid, nor peace up for hold.
I won't be as I was in the days gone past, The seed and the vine, their fruit will last.
Once a curse, now a blessing you'll be, So fear not, let your hands work free.
I thought of wrath when your fathers strayed, But now I plan good, so don't be afraid.
Speak truth to your neighbor, let peace preside, Avoid false oaths, let no evil reside.
The word of Yahweh comes once more, Fasts turn to feasts, joy to the core.
Many will come from cities and lands, Seeking Yahweh's favor, in united bands.
In those days, ten will hold fast To the skirt of a Jew, for God is with you, at last."
Yo, listen up, Yahweh's word's gonna fly, Against Hadrach's land and Damascus sky.
The tribes of Israel, their eyes on the Lord, Hamath's next, as they sharpen the sword.
Tyre, she stacked silver like dust in the air, But the Lord's gonna strike, fire everywhere.
Ashkelon sees it, feelin' that fear, Gaza's in pain, Ekron sheds a tear.
Kings will fall, the throne's gonna shake, Ashkelon empty, pride will break.
Foreigners in Ashdod, Philistine pride's gone, "I'll cut it off, no oppressor will go on."
"Blood from his mouth, abominations too, He'll join Judah, be one of you."
"I'll camp 'round my house, armies stay away, No more oppression, I've seen it today."
Zion, daughter, rejoice and shout, Your King is coming, no doubt.
Lowly, yet righteous, salvation he brings, On a donkey's colt, the King of Kings.
Chariots cut off, no more war cries, Peace to nations, from sea to sky.
Prisoners freed, from the pit of despair, "Return with hope, I'm there to care."
Judah's my bow, Ephraim the string, Zion's sons rise, hear the battle ring.
Yahweh's seen, lightning's his arrow, Trumpet sounds, whirlwinds follow.
Yahweh defends, sling stones fly, Drunk with victory, they roar high.
Saved by God, like jewels in a crown, Lifted up, never coming down.
Oh, his goodness, beauty so great, Grain and new wine, it's time to celebrate.
"Ask Yahweh for rain in spring's embrace, He makes storm clouds, showers fall to grace.
Teraphim's lies, diviners deceive, False dreams they spin, but no reprieve.
Sheep wander lost, no shepherd's care, Oppressed they roam, burdened by despair.
"My wrath's for shepherds, goats I’ll scold, Yahweh's flock will be bold.
From Judah comes the stone, the nail, the bow, Mighty rulers, together they grow.
Tread down the streets, mud under their feet, Fight with Yahweh, their victory's sweet.
"I'll strengthen Judah, Joseph I'll save, In mercy's light, they'll leave the grave.
"I am Yahweh, their God who hears, Ephraim rejoices, sheds no tears.
Children see joy like wine's delight, In Yahweh's name, hearts take flight.
"I'll signal, gather, redeem anew, Increase their number, as they once grew.
Scattered afar, they'll remember my name, With children return, they'll never be the same.
"From Egypt's grip, from Assyria's hand, I'll lead them to Gilead, Lebanon's land.
"Through seas of trouble, I'll make a way, Nile's depths dry, pride will sway.
Strength in Yahweh, they'll walk in his fame, Up and down, in his holy name," says Yahweh.
Open up, Lebanon, let the fire consume your trees, Cypress and cedar fall to their knees.
Oaks of Bashan, hear the cries in the wood, The strong have fallen, their pride misunderstood.
Hear the shepherds wail, their glory's gone, Lions roar, the Jordan's pride is withdrawn.
Yahweh declares, "Feed the destined flock, Buyers kill with impunity, stock by stock."
"Shepherds sell and count their gold, No pity shown, just stories told."
"I won't spare the people," declares Yahweh strong, "Men turn on each other, right or wrong."
I fed the destined, the oppressed in their plight, Held two staffs close, called 'Favor' and 'Union' tight.
Three shepherds cut off, in a month, they were done, Weary of them, their loathing for me begun.
I said, "I won't feed, let the dying die, And those left consume, no need to ask why."
Broke Favor's staff, covenant shattered wide, The flock knew Yahweh's word couldn't hide.
"If you deem it right, give me my pay, If not, then keep it," I did say.
They counted out thirty silver coins, my due, Yahweh said, "To the potter, throw them, untrue."
In Yahweh’s house, to the potter, went the price, Union's staff broke, end of brotherhood's ties.
Yahweh spoke, "Take the foolish shepherd's gear, A new shepherd rises, one who won't care."
"Won't mend the broken, nor tend the flock, He'll feast on the fat, tear apart the stock."
"Woe to the shepherd who deserts his post, Sword on his arm, his eye's vision lost."
Yahweh speaks, listen clear, hear His call, He stretched the heavens wide, made earth stand tall. Inside man, His spirit He formed with care, Now His words to Israel, hear them declare:
"Jerusalem a cup all nations will drain, Judah too, feeling the siege's strain. On that day, Jerusalem's weight they'll meet, All who touch it will suffer defeat.
Horses in terror, riders losing their minds, My eyes on Judah, sightless foes left behind. Chieftains whisper, 'Inhabitants strong,' Their strength in Yahweh, where they belong.
On that day, Judah's leaders like flames, Devouring nations, spreading their names. Jerusalem's place, secure and tight, "Yahweh saves," Judah's future bright.
Feeble as David, defense is sure, Like Yahweh’s angel, steadfast and pure. Nations gathered, but destined to fall, Jerusalem's foes, Yahweh will call.
Grace like rain, pouring down, On David's house, grace profound. They'll look to Me, pierced with grief's sting, Mourning deep, a bitter cry they sing.
In that day, mourning fills the air, Like Megiddon's tears, the valley's despair. Each family, separate in their pain, David, Nathan, Levi—mourning's refrain.
Apart they stand, wives and kin, In solitude, their mourning begins. Every family, each their part, Tears and sorrow, heavy on the heart."
In that day, a spring will flow, David's house will know, A cleansing for sin, Jerusalem's glow.
Yahweh of Armies speaks with might, "Idols' names gone, lost from sight."
Prophets and impure spirits, out they'll go, “The land will be pure, just so you know.”
If a prophet dares to rise and lie, Parents will say, "For this, you must die."
No hairy cloaks to deceive and pretend, "I’m no prophet, just a farmer, my friend."
"What are these wounds?" someone will ask, "In my friends' house, they gave me this task."
"Awake, sword, strike my shepherd," Yahweh cries, Sheep will scatter, as confusion flies.
Two parts gone, but one remains, In the fire, I'll purify, break the chains.
Silver refined, gold tested, strong, They'll call Me, I'll listen, where they belong.
"It is my people," Yahweh will declare, "We are His, in His constant care."
A day of Yahweh's wrath, the nations drawn near, Jerusalem's plunder divided, instilling fear.
The city falls, homes rifled, women in tears, Half the folks in chains, but some remain here.
"Yahweh fights," a battle like days of old, Mount Olives splits, a mighty tale to be told.
Flee through the valley, like an earthquake's flight, Yahweh comes with His holy ones, a powerful sight.
No light or frost, uniqueness in the air, Evening brings light, His presence everywhere.
Living waters flow, from Jerusalem they stream, East and west they go, like a vivid dream.
Yahweh reigns as King, earth under His sway, On that day, His name alone we will say.
Land like Arabah, the heights raised high, Jerusalem dwells safe, peace in the sky.
A plague strikes down those who dared to fight, Flesh, eyes, tongue consume, a terrible sight.
Panic spreads, neighbors turn hand on hand, Judah fights bravely, wealth in the land.
Gold, silver, cloth, the nations' riches stored, Animals stricken too, by Yahweh’s word.
Survivors each year will come and kneel, Worship the King, Yahweh, whose power is real.
No rain for those who refuse the feast, Egypt and others, punished like the least.
On horses' bells, "HOLY TO YAHWEH" rings wide, Every pot made holy, Yahweh’s pride.
No Canaanite found in Yahweh’s sacred place, His house purified, full of grace.

Yahweh speaks to Israel, a word through Malachi's pen, "I've loved you," He declares, "How?" you question again. "Esau and Jacob were brothers, remember the tale? I loved Jacob, but Esau's land I made a barren vale."

Edom boasts, "We'll rise, rebuild from the ground," But Yahweh says, "They'll build, yet I'll tear it down. Men will call them 'The Wicked Land,' forever under my frown." Your eyes will see it, and you'll proclaim, "Yahweh is renowned!"

"A son honors his dad, a servant his boss, right? Where's my honor, my respect? You priests, you slight. You ask how you've despised my name, it's plain, Polluted bread you offer on my altar, again and again."

"When you bring the blind for sacrifice, ain't that wrong? The lame and sick you offer, you think that's strong? Would your governor take it, be pleased with such things?" Yahweh asks, "Show me the respect that royalty brings."

"Entreat God's favor, seek His grace," Yahweh suggests, "Would He accept you now, after all this mess?" "If just one would close the doors, stop this hollow flame, I take no joy in you," Yahweh of Armies proclaims.

"From day's first light to its final fall, My name's revered among nations, pure offerings all. But you profane it, call my table a burden to bear, Bring what's beaten, lame, and sick, yet think I'd care?"
"Cursed be the deceiver with a male in his fold, Who vows a good gift, but offers what's cold. For I am a great King," Yahweh's voice rings, "My name is awesome among all earthly things."
Listen up, priests, this command is laid for you, If you won’t listen, hear my truth, it’s due.
"Glorify my name," Yahweh speaks forth, Or curses will rain, blessings lost, henceforth.
Your lineage rebuked, dung on your face, From feasts you uphold, in disgrace.
"You’ll know I sent this word anew, My covenant with Levi, it stands true."
"Life and peace I gave, that reverence be found, He honored my name, with awe profound.
Truth on his lips, no wrong in his stride, Walked in peace, led many to my side."
A priest’s lips hold knowledge, they seek my way, Messenger of Yahweh, in truth they stay.
But you've strayed, caused many to fall, Corrupted Levi’s vow, hear my call.
Contemptible, wicked, the people see, For you’ve twisted my law, shown partiality.
One Father we have, one God made us all, Why betray each other, make the covenant fall?
Judah's betrayal, an unholy affair, With foreign gods, they lay bare.
Yahweh cuts off those who stray, From Jacob’s tents, they’ll fade away.
You cover altars with tears and sighs, But no more is your offering prized.
"Why?" you ask, Yahweh bears witness true, Against your youth’s wife, you've been untrue.
One he made, with Spirit’s breath, For godly offspring, not treacherous death.
"Hate and divorce," Yahweh shouts loud, "Violence you wear, like a shroud.
Pay heed to your spirit, stay faithful, stay right, Unfaithful hearts weary me, in the dead of night."
You weary Yahweh with words you speak, "How weary?" you ask, confused and weak.
Claiming evil is good in Yahweh's sight, Demanding justice, as darkness turns to light.
"Behold, the messenger's on his way, Prepping the road, clearing the fray. The Lord you seek will hit the scene, In His temple, quick and keen.
"Can you stand the day He arrives? Like fire and soap, refining lives. He'll purify Levi's sons with ease, Offerings in righteousness, aiming to please.
Judah, Jerusalem, bringing the past back, Offerings now pleasant, no more slack. A swift witness, I'll come near, Against injustice, let it be clear.
"I, Yahweh, never change, Sons of Jacob, don't rearrange. You've strayed, turned from My call, Return to Me, and I'll restore all."
"How do we return?" you cry, "Robbing God," you deny. Tithes and offerings you've withheld, Cursed the nation, truth be upheld.
Bring tithes, fill My storehouse's space, Test Me, I'll pour blessings, fill the place. Rebuke the devourer, fields shall thrive, Nations call you blessed, see you alive.
"Your words against Me, hard, you say, Serving's vain, you question the way. The proud seem happy, wicked rise, Tempt God, escape, no surprise."
But those who fear, together they stand, Yahweh listens, a book in His hand. "They're My own, they'll be spared, As a son who's loved, deeply cared."
Return, discern, the good and the bad, Who serves God, and who's been had.
A day is coming, hot as a furnace blaze, Proud hearts and wicked ways, they'll go up in flames. "Not a root or a branch will remain," Yahweh declares, Fire will consume them, leaving only air.

But those who fear my name, rise with healing light, "Leaping like the calves, you'll dance out of night." You'll tread down the wicked, ashes under your feet, On the day I act, feel the heat of my beat.
"Remember Moses' law, given in Horeb's sight, Statutes and ordinances, keep them in your life." Elijah's coming, before that great day, Turning hearts around, in a brand new way.
Fathers to children, children to their dads, Or else I'll strike the earth—no time for feeling sad. Yahweh of Armies speaks, His word prevails, From the furnace to the healing, His truth never fails.
From Abraham to Jesus, the line's divine, A heritage of kings, a sacred sign.
Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Judah's crew, Judah and Tamar brought Perez and Zerah too.
Hezron and Ram, lineage maintained, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon named.
By Rahab, Salmon fathered Boaz bold, Boaz and Ruth, their story told.
Obed to Jesse, then David the king, From David to Solomon, history would sing.
Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa's reign, Jehoshaphat, Joram, in the line they remain.
Uzziah and Jotham, Ahaz, the call, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, stand tall.
Josiah, Jechoniah at Babylon's door, Exile came, but the line restored.
From Shealtiel to Zerubbabel's might, Abiud to Azor, the torch passed right.
Zadok, Achim, Eliud stand, Eleazar, Matthan, a destined band.
Jacob and Joseph, to Mary betrothed, From her, Jesus, prophecy clothed.
Fourteen from Abraham to David's throne, Fourteen to exile, then Jesus shown.
Mary, engaged but blessed by the Spirit's power, Joseph, righteous, faced a challenging hour.
"Joseph, son of David," the angel proclaimed, "Fear not, take Mary, don't be ashamed.
She'll bear a son, name him Jesus, the call, He'll save the people, redeem them all."
Prophets spoke of a virgin's child, "Immanuel," God's presence compiled.
Joseph woke, did as told, obeyed the command, Took Mary, awaited the promised land.
He knew her not till the birth was done, And named him Jesus, the awaited one.
Born in Bethlehem, under Herod's reign, Wise men from the east made their claim.
"Where's the King of the Jews?" they said, "We saw his star, it led ahead."
Herod heard and felt the fear, All Jerusalem knew something was near.
Chief priests, scribes, gathered, sought, "In Bethlehem," prophecy taught.
Herod, in secret, called the wise, "Find the child, report back," he devised.
The star led on, guiding bright, Till it stopped, shining its light.
Joy overflowed, the wise men knelt, Mary with the child, the wonder felt.
Gifts of gold, frankincense, myrrh they gave, In worship profound, their hearts did rave.
Warned in a dream, they took a new track, Avoided Herod, never went back.
An angel to Joseph, in dreams did say, "Rise, take the child, to Egypt away."
By night they fled, under the stars, Till Herod's time passed, till all was ours.
Herod's wrath, rage unchecked, Children of Bethlehem faced his wreck.
Prophecy spoke of Rachel's tears, Weeping echoed through those years.
When Herod died, Joseph dreamt again, "Return to Israel, free from pain."
Back they went, but cautious, aware, To Galilee, Nazareth's care.
Fulfillment came as prophets had seen, The child called Nazarene, where he’d been.
In those days, John hit the scene, wild and free, Preaching in Judea, "Repent! The kingdom's near, you see!"
He was the voice Isaiah foretold, In the wilderness, making paths bold.
John rocked camel's hair with a leather belt, Locusts and honey, his meals, heartfelt.
Crowds from all around came to see, Baptized in the Jordan, setting spirits free.
But Pharisees and Sadducees came with a plan, John wasn't impressed, he called out their clan.
"You brood of vipers! Who gave you the tip-off? Produce worthy fruit, or face the cut-off."
"Don't lean on Abraham, thinking you're grand, God could raise children from stones in this land."
"The ax is ready to chop the bad roots, Trees without good fruit get the boot!"
"I baptize with water, but one greater will rise, With the Holy Spirit, fire in his eyes."
"He'll winnow and cleanse, gather the wheat, But burn the chaff with fire oh so neat."
Then Jesus from Galilee stepped into the scene, To be baptized by John in waters so clean.
John hesitated, "I need your touch, Yet you come to me? This is too much!"
Jesus replied, "Let it be so now, To fulfill righteousness, we'll take this vow."
In the water, Jesus rose, heaven's gate swung wide, The Spirit, like a dove, came to abide.
A voice from the heavens thundered strong, "This is my beloved Son, in Him I belong."

Out in the wilderness, the Spirit led him fast, Forty days, forty nights, hunger hit at last. The devil stepped up, said, "Son, make bread from stone," But Jesus replied, “Man ain't fed on bread alone."
Took him to the temple high, said, "Son, take a leap, Angels got your back, your feet won't meet the street." Jesus answered, “It's said, don’t test the Lord, God's in control, heed his holy word."
On a mountain peak, the world spread wide, Devil said, "Bow to me, kingdoms'll be your pride." Jesus shot back, “Get behind me, Satan, Worship only God, his word I’m statin’."
Devil left him be, angels came to serve, Jesus stood firm, never lost his nerve. He heard John's been caught, so he moved on to Galilee, Left Nazareth, Capernaum by the sea.

Fulfilled Isaiah's words, in darkness light was seen, "Repent," he preached, "Heaven's kingdom's keen." Saw brothers by the sea, casting nets with might, "Come after me, fishers of men you'll be tonight."
Left their nets, followed him without delay, Called more brothers, they came, no words to say. Jesus traveled Galilee, preaching Kingdom's news, Healing every sickness, no one did he refuse.
From Galilee to Judea, the crowds they grew, The sick, the possessed, he healed them too. Great multitudes followed, from lands far and wide, His light and love spread, couldn't be denied.
Crowds gathered, mountains climbed, He took a seat, Disciples gathered 'round, ready for the treat.
"Blessed are the poor in spirit, Kingdom of Heaven's theirs, Blessed are the mournful, comfort erases cares.
Blessed are the gentle, they'll inherit the earth, Those hungry for righteousness? They'll find worth.
Blessed are the merciful, mercy they'll obtain, Pure hearts will see God, His presence they'll gain.
Peacemakers are God's kids, known far and wide, Persecuted for righteousness? Kingdom's on their side.
Reproached and persecuted for my name, don't be sad, Rejoice, be glad, rewards in Heaven ain't half bad.
You're the salt of the earth, don't lose your taste, Saltless cast out, trodden, a waste.
You're the light of the world, city on a hill can't hide, Light the lamp on a stand, let it shine with pride.
Let your light shine, show good works to men, Glorify your Father in Heaven, again and again.
Don't think I came to destroy the law, no, I fulfill, Not one letter will pass, 'til all's accomplished, still.
Break the least command? Least in Heaven, I say, Do and teach them all? Great you'll stay.
Unless righteousness surpasses scribes' and Pharisees' call, No entry to the Kingdom, for you at all.
You've heard it said, 'Don't murder, face the law's might,' But anger without cause brings judgment's light.
Say 'Raca' to a brother? Council's near, Call him 'fool'? Fire of Gehenna, fear.
If at the altar, you recall a brother's pain, Make peace first, then offer again.
Agree with adversaries, quickly settle the score, Lest prison holds you, freedom no more.
You've heard it said, 'Adultery, don't commit,' But lust in your heart? Guilty of it.
If your eye offends, pluck it, better to lose a part, Than whole body's plunge into Gehenna's dark.
Hand causing sin? Cut it, throw it away, Better one piece gone than all astray.
Divorce with a decree, it's that you’ve heard, But I say immorality makes the word.
False vows to ancient ones were said, But don't swear at all, keep your head.
Heaven's God's throne, earth His footstool, Jerusalem's the King's city, keep it cool.
Let your 'Yes' be 'Yes,' 'No' be 'No,' Anything else comes from the evil's flow.
'An eye for an eye,' they say, justice tight, But turn the other cheek, don't fight.
Give your cloak if sued for your coat, Go two miles when forced, that's the note.
Give to those who ask, don't turn away, Borrowers receive, come what may.
Love your neighbor, hate your enemy’s the tale, But love, bless, and pray, that's the trail.
Sun rises and rain falls on good and bad, Love those who love you, reward's just a tad.
Tax collectors greet friends, what's your chore? Be perfect as your Father, just that and more."
When you give to the poor, keep it on the down low, Don't blast trumpets, let the good deeds quietly show.
Hypocrites in the streets, seeking glory from men, They got their reward, but it's empty in the end.
When you give, let your left hand be blind, Your Father sees in secret, His rewards you'll find.
When you pray, don’t be like those who seek attention, In the corners, in the synagogues, craving man's mention.
Go to your room, close the door tight, Pray to your Father who sees without sight.
No endless babble, God's got you, He knows, Before you even ask, His wisdom flows.
Pray like this: “Our Father in the sky, Keep Your name holy, Your Kingdom nearby.
Your will be done, here as up there, Give us today what we need to share.
Forgive our debts as we forgive too, Keep us from evil, in everything we do.
For Yours is the Kingdom, power and glory, Forever and ever, that's the story.”
Forgive others' wrongs, then you'll be free, Your Father'll forgive you, that's His decree.
When you fast, don't show it with a gloomy face, Act normal, clean, full of His grace.
Your Father sees the secret, He’ll give reward, Not the men who watch, with their own accord.
Don't store treasures where moth and rust decay, In heaven, they last, they're there to stay.
Where your treasure is, there’s your heart, So choose wisely, play your part.
The body's lamp is the eye, let it shine bright, If it's evil, you'll be lost in the night.
No man can serve two kings on the throne, Loving one, hating the other, you'll be torn.
Don’t stress about life, what you’ll eat or wear, Life's more than these, so don’t despair.
Look at the birds, they don’t worry or sow, Yet your Father feeds them, don’t you know?
Worry can’t add a moment to your day, So trust in faith, let anxiety sway.
Lilies in the fields, they grow without toil, Yet even Solomon can't match their royal.
If God clothes the grass, here today, gone tomorrow, Won't He clothe you, dispel your sorrow?
Seek first His Kingdom, righteousness in sight, Everything you need, He’ll provide in the light.
Don't worry 'bout tomorrow, let it be, Each day has enough for you and me.
"Don't judge others, or you'll be judged the same, With the measure you use, you'll play your own game.
See the speck in your brother's eye? It's plain, But miss the beam in yours—that's insane.
"Remove your own block," He said with a sigh, "Then help your brother, now clear in your eye."
"Don't toss what's holy to dogs, don't be giving, Your pearls to pigs who'll trample and leave you grieving.
Ask, and it's given, seek, and you'll find, Knock, and that door will open in kind.
If your child needs bread, would you hand him a stone? If fish is his wish, would a serpent be thrown?
If you, flawed beings, give gifts that are good, How much more will God, as a Father should.
"Treat others the way you want to be treated, This is the law, the prophets completed.
Enter the narrow gate, it's tight but it's right, The wide path leads to darkness, not light.
Beware of false prophets, in disguise they may be, A wolf in sheep's clothing is not what you see.
By their fruits, you'll know what they yield, Good trees bring life, corrupt trees are killed.
Not everyone crying 'Lord' gets through heaven's gate, Only those who do God's will, their fate is great.
On that day, many will plead, But I'll say, 'I never knew you, leave indeed.'
"Those who hear and act are wise, like rock they stand, The floods, the winds won't move their land.
But those who hear and don’t act, like sand, they fall, The storm takes them down, their ruin was the call."
When Jesus spoke, the crowds were amazed, For He taught with authority, unlike scribes' old ways.
He stepped off the mountain, crowds at his back, A leper knelt, "Lord, please heal the track." Jesus reached out, "I want to make you clean," Touched him, and leprosy was nowhere to be seen.
"Tell no one, show the priest, offer your gift right," As a testimony, let them see the light. In Capernaum, a centurion came in need, "My servant's in pain, can you perform the deed?"
Jesus said, "I'll come and heal him now," The centurion replied, "Just speak, make that vow. I'm under command, I know how it rolls, I say 'go' and they move, just like the scrolls."
Jesus marveled, "Such faith, not found in this land, Many will come, but some will be banned." To the centurion, "Go, your faith made it true," And the servant was healed, all fresh and new.
At Peter's house, his wife’s mother lay still, He touched her hand, and fever had no will. She rose up quickly, served him on the spot, At night, many came, needing healing they sought.
Demons cast out, sickness healed with his word, Fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy that they heard. Seeing the crowds, he said, "We must depart," A scribe approached, "Teacher, I’ll follow your heart."
"The foxes have holes, birds nests to rest, But the Son of Man roams with no place to nest." Another said, "Let me bury my dead." "Follow me," Jesus said, "Let the dead bury the dead."
They set sail, the sea roared loud and high, But Jesus slept, while the storm passed by. "Save us, Lord," they cried, in fear's embrace, "Why such little faith?" He rebuked the waves' race.
The storm calmed, leaving marveled men in awe, "Even the wind and sea obey his law." In Gergesenes, two fierce souls met, Possessed by demons, a challenge they set.
"What do you want, Son of God, at this hour?" The demons begged, "Send us to that swine tower." "Go!" he commanded, and into pigs they fled, Rushed down the cliff, where the waters spread.
Witnesses ran, told the town all they'd seen, The city came out, begged Jesus to leave the scene.

Stepped in a boat, crossed the sea, hit his city, Paralyzed man brought, friends showed faith gritty. “Son, cheer up! Sins forgiven,” Jesus declared, Scribes whispered "blasphemy," but Jesus wasn't scared.
He read their minds, asked, "Why doubt in your heart? Is it easier to say sins forgiven or make this man start?" Then he turned to the man, “Get up and walk, Take your mat, go home,” no more talk.
Crowds marveled, glorifying God's power, Authority on Earth was the talk of the hour. Jesus saw Matthew, at the tax booth he sat, “Follow me,” he said, Matthew was down with that.

At dinner with sinners, Pharisees complained, "Why eat with these folks?" they disdainfully exclaimed. Jesus replied, “Healthy need no doctor, just the sick, Learn mercy, not sacrifice, that's my pick.”
John’s crew questioned, “Why don’t your guys fast?” “Bridegroom's here now, but this won't last. New cloth on old, new wine in fresh skin, Both are preserved, no bursting within.”
A ruler approached, “My daughter just died, But your touch will revive her,” he cried. On his way with disciples, a woman snuck around, Touched his clothes, her healing was profound.
“Daughter, cheer up! Your faith made you whole,” In that moment, sickness lost control. At the ruler’s house, musicians made a noise, “She's just asleep,” he said, dismissing the ploys.
Crowd laughed, but Jesus took her hand, The girl arose, spread news across the land. Two blind men followed, “Son of David, hear our plea!” “Believe I can do this?” asked He.
“Yes, Lord,” they answered, their faith was true, Touched their eyes, vision renewed. “Don't spread the word,” his command tight, But they shared his fame, couldn't keep it light.

Eight days later, up the mountain they went, Peter, John, and James, in prayer they were bent.

All amazed, yet he spoke again, "Son of Man will be in men's hands then."
They argued on who was the greatest one, He brought a child, "See what must be done.

To Jerusalem he set his face, Samaritans refused to give him place.
"Call down fire?" the disciples asked, "No destruction, saving's my task."
On the road, a man pledged to follow, "Foxes have holes, but no place I can borrow."

Another wished to bid farewell at home, "No looking back, you're Kingdom-bound to roam."
Seventy sent, in pairs they roam, Into each city, where He’d soon make His home. "The harvest is great, but workers are few, Pray to the Lord, He’ll send laborers through."
"Go as lambs where wolves might reside, Carry no purse, let My peace be your guide. Enter a house, say, 'Peace to this place,' If peace finds a home, let it embrace."
"Stay in that house, eat what they share, The worker's due pay, be fair and square. Heal the sick, say, 'God’s Kingdom's near,' If you’re not received, then make it clear."
Shake off the dust, leave it behind, "The Kingdom's come, though you were blind." For some, judgment's harsh, Sodom's fate will pale, "More tolerable for them if you fail."
"Woe to Chorazin, Bethsaida too! Miracles ignored, what will you do? Capernaum raised, but soon you'll fall, Rejecting My messengers, you reject all."
Seventy returned, filled with delight, "Even demons flee at Your name, what a sight!" "Satan fell like lightning," He replied, "You’ve power over all, with Me as your guide."
"Rejoice not in spirits that heed, But that heaven records your deed." Jesus thanked His Father above, For revealing truth with childlike love.
To disciples He turned, words He did impart, "Blessed are your eyes, seeing what others cannot. Prophets and kings longed for this view, But you see and hear—you're the chosen few."
A lawyer stood, seeking to test, "How to find life that's truly blessed?" "Love God fully, your neighbor as dear," "Correct," said Jesus, "Do this without fear."

"Martha, Martha, you're troubled, it's clear, One thing is needed—Mary chose it here. What she’s found won't be taken away, Sit at my feet, take time to stay."
In a quiet place, his prayer was done, A disciple asked, "Teach us to pray, like John."
"When you pray, say this," Jesus began, "Our Father in heaven, holy be your name, man.
May your Kingdom come, your will be done, On earth as in heaven, let it be won.

He went on, "Imagine at midnight's hour, You knock on a friend's door, with no power.
'Friend, lend me loaves, three for me to share, A pal's come to visit, and my cupboard's bare.'
Though he might say, 'I'm tucked in, door's sealed,' Persistence will get you the bread he'll yield.
So ask, it'll be given, seek and you'll find, Knock and the door will open, keep that in mind.
If your kid asks for bread, will you give a stone? Or a snake for a fish, leave him alone?
If you, though flawed, know gifts for your kin, How much more will God give the Spirit within?"
Casting out demons, a man mute now spoke, Crowds marveled, while some others did poke.
"He casts by Beelzebul," they did say, Testing him, seeking a sign that day.
But Jesus, aware of their inner divide, Said, "A kingdom split falls, it cannot abide.
If Satan fights Satan, how can he stand? But if by God's finger, demons leave this land,
Then the Kingdom of God is here with you. The strong man guards, but a stronger breaks through.
Who isn't with me, surely stands against, Who doesn't gather, scatters by chance.
An unclean spirit, when it leaves a man, Seeks rest, finds none, returns with a plan.
Seven more join, more wicked than before, The man's state worsens, evil comes through the door."
A woman shouted, "Blessed is your birth!" But he replied, "Blessed are those who hear God's worth."
"This generation seeks a sign, But no sign shall be given, except Jonah's line.
As Jonah was to Nineveh, a sign they knew, So the Son of Man is a sign to you.
The Queen of the South came for Solomon's fame, One greater than Solomon stands here, no shame.
Nineveh repented, Jonah's words they heeded, One greater than Jonah is here, unneeded is greed."
A lamp on a stand shines bright, Not hidden but seen, giving light.
The eye's the lamp, see well and be bright, If darkness clouds, your whole body's night.
With him, a Pharisee sat to dine, He marveled Jesus skipped the wash line.
"Outside you clean, but inside you're grim, Didn't the maker of both make them akin?
Give from within, and you'll be clean, But woe to you for bypassing God's love unseen.
Best seats and greetings you do adore, But justice and mercy you ignore.
Woe to you, hidden graves so cold, Men walk unaware of your stories untold."
A lawyer spoke, "Teacher, you insult our lot," Jesus replied, "Woe to you, burdening a lot.
You don't help, but weigh others down, You build prophets' tombs, while they frown.
This generation will answer for the blood, From Abel to Zachariah, in a flood.
You took the key of knowledge away, You hinder others, blocked the way."
The scribes and Pharisees, angry they grew, Waiting to trap him, with accusations new.
Thousands gathered, a crowd so tight, He told his disciples, "Stay clear of the blight, The yeast of the Pharisees, hypocrisy's game, What’s hidden in shadows will burst into flame.

Five little sparrows, worth just two coins, Yet not one is forgotten in God’s vast designs. Your hairs, they’re counted, so don’t be dismayed, You’re worth more than sparrows, so don’t be afraid.
"Confess me to men, and I’ll speak your name, Deny me, and the angels won’t know your fame. Blaspheme the Spirit, no forgiveness in sight, But speak against me, and you’re alright.

But he answered, "Man, who made me decide? Beware of greed, let it not guide. Life’s not in treasures, possessions you keep, A rich fool’s story echoes, his harvest so deep.

"Don't fret for your life, food, or attire, Life’s more than clothing, more than your desire. Look at the ravens, they don’t sow or reap, Yet God feeds them, as you rest or sleep.

Yet the crowd clung tight, to every word He spoke, In the temple, wisdom awoke.

Down to Troas, where Paul saw a vision clear, A Macedonian man pleading, “Come over here.”
They set sail, knowing their mission was true, To Macedonia, preaching the news, breaking through.
In Philippi, a Roman colony, they stayed, On Sabbath, by the river, women gathered and prayed.
Lydia, a merchant in purple, heard Paul's part, The Lord opened her ears, touched her heart.
Baptized with her house, she begged them, pleading, "If I've been faithful, come stay, I'm needing."
As they went to prayer, a girl with a spirit came by, Crying, "These men show salvation on high!"
Days of this, till Paul, annoyed, turned around, "In Jesus' name, come out!" And the spirit unbound.
Her masters saw profit vanish in the air, Seized Paul and Silas, dragged them in despair.
Before the rulers, accusations loud and clear, "These Jews disturb our city, customs we won't adhere."
Crowd in fury, magistrates stripped them down, Beaten with rods, tossed in jail, in the center of town.
In the stocks, they prayed and sang through night’s dark, An earthquake hit, breaking chains, making its mark.
The jailer woke, saw doors open wide, Drew his sword, ready to die, terrified inside.
But Paul shouted, "Don’t harm, we’re all here!" Lights called, he trembled, feeling fear.
"What must I do to be saved?" he cried, broken, "Believe in Jesus, and salvation’s awoken."
They shared the Lord’s word with him and his kin, He washed their wounds, baptized, free from sin.
Rejoicing in faith, he set food at the table, Morning came, and the jailer was able.
The magistrates sent, "Let those men go free," But Paul said, "Not secretly, come set us free!"
Hearing they were Romans, the rulers were in fright, Came and begged them, asking them to take flight.
Released from prison, they went to Lydia’s place, Encouraged the brothers, then left with grace.
Through cities and towns, Paul and crew, Thessalonica's the spot, a synagogue in view.
Paul's custom was clear, three Sabbaths he'd preach, From Scriptures, the Christ's story he'd teach.
"This Jesus, the Christ," he proclaimed, Some believed, their hearts were inflamed.
But some Jews, unpersuaded, they stirred up a scene, Grabbed some rough men, made the city mean.
Jason's house was stormed, chaos did roar, "These world-turners are here!" they swore.
"Jason's harboring them, Caesar's rules they defy, Claiming Jesus king, not a Roman lie."
The city quaked, rulers troubled in mind, Jason posted bail, left woes behind.
Paul and Silas, brothers sent them away, To Beroea by night, not to delay.
Beroeans noble, searching words with zeal, Many believed, with fervor they'd feel.
But Thessalonian Jews, upon hearing the word, Stirred more trouble, their anger stirred.
Brothers sent Paul off, to the sea he'd fly, Silas and Tim stayed, not saying goodbye.
Paul reached Athens, idols all around, Spirit provoked, he spoke with sound.
Jews in the synagogue, market chats too, Epicureans and Stoics asked, "What's new?"
"What's this babbler want to say?" "Foreign gods?" they wondered that day.
To the Areopagus they took him, "New teachings? Let us begin."
All Athenians loved a brand-new tale, Paul stood ready, without fail.
"You men of Athens, religious you seem, 'Unknown God' altars in your worship scheme.
This God I proclaim, who made earth and sky, "Not in temples," was his reply.
Life and breath he gives, in him we move, From one blood he made nations groove.
Seek him, find him, he's never far, In him we live, he's our guiding star.
God isn't gold, or stone, or art, He's the living God, in our heart.
"Repent," he calls, "a judgment, a day, By the man he raised, he will have his say."
Resurrection talk, some mocked with glee, Others said, "Again, we want to see."
Paul departed, yet some believed, Dionysius, Damaris, their hearts relieved.
Paul left Athens, arrived in Corinth's heat, Met Aquila and Priscilla, where trade and faith meet.
Tent makers they were, so Paul joined in the work, In synagogues he preached, his words never shirked.
Silas and Timothy arrived, and Paul's zeal ignited, To the Jews, "Jesus is Christ," his message recited.
Opposition came, slander loud and fierce, Paul shook his clothes, "From you I now pierce."
"I'll turn to Gentiles, your blood's not on me," He left for Justus' house, next door, you see.
Crispus believed, the synagogue chief, With all of his house, they turned to belief.
In a vision God spoke, "Fear not, speak out, No harm will come; I've got folks about."
For a year and a half, Paul taught, God’s word he spread, But trouble stirred when Gallio took the seat ahead.
The Jews rose up, with Paul they took issue, But Gallio dismissed, "This I won't pursue."
He drove them out, their cries left behind, Sosthenes beaten, Gallio paid no mind.
Paul stayed longer, then set sail for Syria, With Priscilla and Aquila, from Corinth's area.
At Cenchreae, a vow, shaved head he bore, To Ephesus he came, reasoned once more.
Invited to stay, yet onward he pressed, "To Jerusalem I must go, if God wills, I'll rest."
From Caesarea to Antioch, his journey was grand, Then through Galatia, Phrygia, strengthening the band.
Apollos appeared, eloquent and bold, Knew only John’s baptism, yet his spirit cold.
Priscilla and Aquila taught him anew, More accurately now, in Christ he grew.
To Achaia he went, the brothers him sent, Refuted the Jews, with Scripture's consent.
Paul hit Ephesus, disciples he found, "Did the Spirit come when belief was around?" "We haven't heard of the Holy Ghost," Paul asked, "In which baptism do you boast?"
"John's," they answered, "that's what we know," Paul said, "John spoke of the one who'd show. Baptized in Jesus, now you're in, Holy Spirit coming, let Him begin."
Hands laid, Spirit flowed, tongues and prophecy, Twelve men strong, now hear and see. Paul hit the synagogue, three months strong, Bold words of the Kingdom, where they belong.
Some hearts hardened, speaking ill of the Way, Paul took the disciples, taught every day. Two years gone, in Asia all heard, Jews and Greeks received the Word.
Miracles flew from Paul's hand, Healing the sick across the land. Some exorcists tried to imitate, Called Jesus' name, but met their fate.
"Jesus I know, Paul too, But who are you?" the spirit threw. They fled wounded, story spread wide, Fear and reverence on every side.
Believers came, confessing deeds, Burned their books, destroyed their creeds. Fifty thousand silver's worth gone, The Lord's Word mighty, shone like dawn.
Paul planned, Spirit-led, to roam, “Macedonia, Jerusalem, then to Rome.” Timothy and Erastus sent ahead, Paul stayed back, Asia's work not dead.
A stir rose up, Demetrius' concern, Silver shrines, a trade they yearn. "Paul's turned people from our hand-made gods, Artemis' temple, her majesty nods."
Ephesus angered, shouts of praise, "Great is Artemis," in a roaring blaze. City in a frenzy, theater's call, Gaius, Aristarchus, caught in the brawl.
Paul held back, friends' plea made, Assembly wild in the theater's shade. Confusion reigned, no clear track, Alexander tried, but crowd fought back.
Two-hour chant, a deafening cry, "Great is Artemis," filled the sky. Town clerk calmed, "Ephesus knows, Keeper of Artemis, image from Zeus shows."
"Quiet down, don't act in haste, These men have no temple waste. Courts are open, seek your due, Don't create a riot without a clue."
Dismissed the crowd, with peace in sight, Ephesus calmed, from their riotous night.
After the uproar ceased, Paul gathered his crew, Gave them a hug, said "Farewell," and off he flew. Through Macedonia, encouraging them all, Then into Greece, where he answered the call.
Three months he spent, but trouble was near, The Jews plotted hard, so he steered clear. Back through Macedonia, he chose his way, With Sopater, Aristarchus, and others on display.
They went ahead, waiting for us at Troas, We sailed from Philippi, fast as we could pass. Five days on the sea, then seven days at rest, Paul spoke his heart out, giving them his best.
In the upper room, the lights were bright, Eutychus in the window, caught in the night. Sleep took him down from the third-floor height, Paul embraced him, "He's alive!" he said outright.
Up they went, breaking bread and talking 'til dawn, The boy was alive, their sorrow all gone. We sailed to Assos to meet Paul on the way, Then onward to Mitylene, sailing day by day.
Past Ephesus, Paul was on a mission, Jerusalem called him, with a Pentecost vision. He summoned the elders, from Ephesus they came, He spoke of his journey, in the Lord's holy name.
"From the first day I set foot on this ground, With humility and tears, my faith did resound. I taught you the truth, both in public and home, To Jews and Greeks, God's grace I've shown.
Bound in the Spirit, Jerusalem’s my aim, The Spirit warns me, bonds and trials the same. But I won't stop, I’ll finish my race, Testify to the Good News of God’s grace."
"You'll see my face no more, this is my parting word, But I've spoken the truth, the whole counsel you've heard. Guard the flock, for wolves will come, From your own ranks, they’ll try to numb.
For three years straight, with tears I taught, Now to God’s word of grace, you’re brought. I sought no treasure, my hands met the need, Remember, it's more blessed to give than to greed."
He knelt down and prayed, tears flowed like rain, They hugged and wept, feeling the pain. Sorrowful most for words that were said, They'd see him no more, as Paul turned ahead.
Set sail from Cos, next stop was Rhodes, Then Patara called with her shiploads.
To Phoenicia, we made our way, Cyprus on the left, didn't delay.
Tyre's shores, where the cargo unloads, Met disciples, stayed on the roads.
They warned Paul, "Don't go to Jerusalem," Through the Spirit, the message was solemn.
Days passed, we journeyed anew, Families joined, prayers on the beach, it's true.
Boarded the ship, waves our last sight, They went home, as we took flight.
Ptolemais greeted, one day we stayed, To Caesarea next, where we prayed.
Philip's house, with daughters who prophesy, Agabus came with a prophetic tie.
Bound himself with Paul's own belt, "Says the Spirit, Jerusalem will be felt."
Begged him not to go, hearts in pain, Paul stood firm, ready for chain.
He said, "Your tears, why break my heart? For Jesus, I'm ready to take any part."
Couldn't change his mind, with a sigh, "The Lord's will be done," was our cry.
Baggage packed, to Jerusalem we went, Mnason of Cyprus, with us he was sent.
Brothers received us with joy and grace, Paul met James, elders in place.
Gentile ministry, Paul reported it well, Glorified God, their praises did swell.
But rumors about Paul had spread, Jews among Gentiles, misled.
Assembly called, to clear the air, Four men with vows, Paul to share.
Purify together, expenses paid, Show the truth, let rumors fade.
Only Gentiles, rules to heed, From idols and immorality, take heed.
Paul purified, temple he entered, Seven days until his offering rendered.
Jews from Asia, stirred the crowd, "Against our law," they shouted loud.
Dragged Paul out, the temple doors closed, Jerusalem's uproar was exposed.
Commander came, soldiers in tow, The beating stopped, the crowd's anger slow.
Bound with chains, seeking truth in the noise, Paul taken away, amidst the uproar's voice.
Crowd's cries, "Away with him!" they shout, Soldiers held Paul, as they moved out.
Paul spoke, "Can I address, a word to you?" The officer asked, "Do you speak Greek too?"
Not an Egyptian, Paul made it clear, "I'm a Jew from Tarsus, hear me, dear."
Permission granted, Paul stood tall, On the stairs with silence over all.
In Hebrew he spoke, with hand held high, And the crowd listened, as Paul let his words fly.
Brothers, fathers, lean in close, hear my defense I'm 'bout to disclose. Speaking Hebrew, the crowd fell still, listening to my tale with quiet thrill.
"A Jew from Tarsus, I was raised here, under Gamaliel's watchful sphere. Zealous for God, like you today, I pursued this path, come what may.
I hunted followers of the Way, binding them up, night and day. High priest and elders all know my deeds, letters in hand for Damascus' needs.
On my journey near Damascus noon, a blazing light turned day from gloom. I hit the ground and heard Him call, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute at all?'
'Who are you, Lord?' I asked in fright. He said, 'I'm Jesus, in your sight.' My companions saw the light's glare, but His voice they didn't share.
I asked, 'What should I do, my Lord?' He replied, 'To Damascus, walk forward.' Blind from the light that shone so bright, led by hand, I reached the city's height.
Ananias, devout and true, met me there, knew what to do. 'Brother Saul, receive your sight,' he said, restoring my vision right.
God chose me for this role, to hear and see, deep in my soul. 'Witness to all, do not delay, rise up baptized, wash sin away.'
Back in Jerusalem, in prayer's deep trance, He warned, 'Flee, no second chance. They won't heed your testimony, so depart for lands unknown, my homie.'
'But Lord,' I pleaded, 'they know my crime, Stephen's blood, my consent at the time.' 'Go,' He commanded, 'to the Gentiles, you're sent.'
They listened keen til that last line was spent. Then rage ignited, voices soared, 'Rid the earth of this man,' they roared.
Dust filled the air, they cast cloaks aside, officer grabbed me, to scourge and decide. But I spoke up, 'A Roman am I, no lawful scourge you can apply.'
The centurion paused, went to his boss, 'Careful, this man's Roman, not a loss.' The commander asked, 'Is this true?' 'Yes,' I replied, my words drew.
'A costly buy,' he said of his claim, 'But I was born Roman,' I declared my name. Fear struck them all, they stepped away, not daring to touch me another day.
Next day came, seeking truth profound, freed from bonds, before council, I was bound."
Paul faced the council, standing tall and true, "Brothers, my conscience is clear before God and you." Ananias ordered a strike on Paul's face, Paul shot back, "God'll hit you in disgrace!"
"Whitewashed wall, do you judge by the law's might, Yet command a strike that ain't right?" "Do you speak against the high priest?" they cried, Paul replied, "I didn't know, I abide.
For it is written, 'Speak no ill of the chief, That's the word, no room for disbelief.'" Paul saw the divide, Pharisees from Sadducees, He shouted out, "On resurrection, judge me, please!"
A clash arose, the crowd was torn, Pharisees believed, but Sadducees scorned. Scribes of the Pharisees stood to say, "Let him be, if an angel showed the way."
Commotion stirred, the officer feared, Paul might be harmed; he intervened and steered. In the barracks, Paul found peace that night, The Lord said, "Cheer up, you'll testify in Rome's light."
By day, a plot thickened, forty men swore, Not to eat or drink till Paul's no more. They planned with leaders, a deadly snare, "We'll strike him down, with no time to spare."
Paul's nephew heard and ran to the cell, Told Paul the plot, told him well. Paul called a centurion, "Take this lad, He's got something urgent, and it's bad."
The officer listened, hand in hand, "What's your news? Help me understand." "They're lying in wait, more than forty, Don't trust their words, they're ready to be naughty."
Officer warned, "Don't spill a word, Keep this secret, let nothing be heard." He called for soldiers, two hundred strong, With horsemen and spears, to move Paul along.
To Felix, he'd write, the truth set to sail, "Paul's a Roman, saved him from their wail." Soldiers moved by night with skill, To Antipatris, they climbed the hill.
Caesarea reached, the letter was shown, Felix read, and his tone was grown. "What province?" he asked, from Cilicia you hail, "When accusers come, your case will prevail."
Paul was held in Herod's halls, Awaiting justice, within those walls.
After five days, Ananias came with his crew, Elders and Tertullus, they'd something to do.
Informing the governor, with Paul in their sights, Tertullus spoke, setting the stage for the fights.
"By your great foresight, peace we embrace, Prosperity flows, thanks to your grace."
"But let's not delay, hear what we say, This man’s a plague, incites in a big way."
A ringleader of Nazarenes, causing much dread, He tried to profane the temple, that's what he said.
The Jews joined the attack, confirming the charge, Paul stood up, ready to barge.
"Felix, for years you've judged this land, I make my defense, with confidence at hand."
"Twelve days since I went to Jerusalem's heart, No disputes, no crowds, I played no part."
"They’ve got no proof, just empty claims, But I follow the Way, with no shame."
"Believing the law and prophets, I confess, Hope in resurrection, the just and unjust, I profess."
"My conscience is clear, before God, before men, Gifts for the needy, that’s where I've been."
"They found me purified, without a riot, Those from Asia should speak, if they stay quiet."
"Unless it’s this, the resurrection theme, For that, I’m judged, it seems."
Felix knew the Way, but pushed pause, "Wait for Lysias, then decide on the cause."
Paul kept in custody but had his space, Friends could visit, he wasn't erased.
Felix with Drusilla, called Paul near, He spoke of faith, Felix quaked in fear.
"Not now, Paul, I'll call you in time," Hoping for money, his thoughts not in line.
Two years later, Felix stepped away, Festus took over, but Paul stayed.
Festus rolled in, just three days new, from Caesarea to Jerusalem, he flew. Chief priests and top folks, with a plan so grim, begged Festus to summon Paul, aiming to dim him.
"Keep Paul here," Festus said, "he's at Caesarea, If he's guilty, come with me, and we'll see ya."
Ten days in the city, then off to the seat, Paul brought in, to face charges he couldn’t defeat.
Jews circled round with tales full of strife, But lacked any proof, couldn't take Paul's life.
Paul stood firm, saying, "I've broken no law, Not the temple, not Caesar, no sin to gnaw."
Festus sought favor, asked Paul, "Will you go? To Jerusalem's judgment, is that a yes or a no?"
Paul replied, "I'm here, right where I need, To Caesar's court, for Caesar's creed.
If guilty, I'll face what's coming to me, But if not, then you can't make me flee.
I appeal to Caesar!" the words echoed out, Festus conferred, had no doubt.
"You've appealed to Caesar, to Caesar you'll ride," Days later, Agrippa with Bernice by his side.
Festus laid it out, "Prisoner left by Felix, Jews want him judged, but Rome has its tricks.
Face-to-face, that's the Roman way, Accusers meet accused, no delay."
Charges laid, but not as expected, Just talk of Jesus, dead but resurrected.
Paul's appeal sent him to a higher throne, Festus needed clarity, not left alone.
Agrippa wanted to hear the tale, "Tomorrow," Festus said, "with detail."
Next day came, with pomp and flair, Paul brought in before all who cared.
Festus spoke, "King Agrippa, and all, Here's the man, the Jews want to fall.
But guilty of death, he's not, so I write, To Caesar he goes, for justice bright.
Seems absurd to send him, without a clear vice, So listen and help, in this legal slice."
Paul faced Agrippa, ready to defend, His hand stretched out, the truth to send.
"Happy to speak, O King, to you today, Concerning accusations the Jews relay.
You know their customs, you know their lore, So hear me patiently, it's you I implore.
From youth in Jerusalem, my path I walked, A Pharisee's life, where devotion stalked.
Now judged for hope, the promise divine, Our twelve tribes have sought it, through time.
Why doubt God can raise the dead? With proof and promise being widespread.
I fought the name of Jesus with zeal, Persecuted believers with misguided deal.
In synagogues, I pushed them to blaspheme, Chased them to cities, rage in my scheme.
On Damascus road, with power and might, A heavenly light blazed, brighter than bright.
We fell down, sky's voice did awake, 'Saul, Saul, why this path you take?'
'Who are you, Lord?' I inquired, 'I'm Jesus, whom you've conspired.
But rise, stand strong, my message be clear, To witness to all, from far and near.
Gentiles and kin, open their eyes, From darkness to light, let them rise.
I obeyed, King, that vision so grand, Declared repentance, throughout the land.
For this, the Jews seized me in fury, But God's help steadied my jury.
Prophets and Moses, I preach their claim, Christ's suffering, resurrection, the flame.
Festus called me mad, bold with disdain, 'Not crazy,' I said, 'truth remains plain.
King knows these truths, not from the dark, Publicly spoken, all left a mark.
Do you believe, O King, the prophets true? I know you do, their words come through.'
Agrippa queried, 'Trying to convert with might?' Paul wished all were like him, but without chains tight.
The king rose, with Bernice and crew, Decided Paul did nothing death could ensue.
Agrippa to Festus, with a sigh so deep, 'If not for Caesar, this man we'd release to keep.'"
We're set to sail to Italy, Paul's in the mix, Julius the centurion, in charge of the fix.
On a ship from Adramyttium, off we glide, With Aristarchus by Paul's side.
We dock in Sidon, Julius gives Paul a break, To see his friends, for refreshment's sake.
From there we move, 'neath Cyprus we cruise, The winds against us, we gotta choose.
We hit Myra, switch ships, head to Italy's land, But slow winds hold us, and it's hard to stand.
Paul warns, “This journey's bound for disaster, Cargo, ship, and lives may go faster.”
The centurion listens to the ship's guide, Thinking Crete's Phoenix is a safer ride.
South winds whisper, they think they're on track, But Euroclydon storms, wind at our back.
We struggle and strain, the ship's tossed wild, With ropes, anchors, and fears compiled.
Days without sun, stars, or hope in sight, Paul stands up, speaks of an angel's light.
“Fear not, we'll lose this ship, not lives,” Paul said, “God’s got a plan, no need to dread.”
Fourteen nights of rocking and rolling, Soundings say land, hope now controlling.
Sailors plot an escape, but Paul declares, “Stay in the ship, God’s promise he shares.”
They cut the ropes, trust is renewed, Paul urges, “Eat, keep up your mood.”
Morning breaks, a bay comes in view, Anchors cut, sails raised, they pursue.
The boat hits ground where seas collide, The stern breaks, but Paul’s hope abides.
Soldiers plan to kill, but Julius saves, Paul’s life cherished, his faith engraves.
Some swim, some float on planks and boards, All make it to land, safe with the Lord's accord.
We landed on Malta, the island's name we learned, The locals showed kindness, as the fire burned. Paul gathered sticks, laid them on the flame, A viper struck his hand, but he stayed the same.
The natives whispered, "This man must be cursed, Escaped the sea, but Justice will do its worst." Paul shook the snake off into the blazing fire, He felt no harm, watching eyes filled with desire.
They thought he'd swell, maybe drop down dead, But when nothing happened, "He's a god," they said. Nearby lands owned by Publius, the chief so grand, Welcomed us warmly, in his house we did stand.
Publius's father lay sick, fever gripping tight, Paul prayed, laid hands, and restored his light. Then all the sick came, and Paul healed each one, They honored us well for the good deeds done.
After three months, we sailed on from that shore, In Alexandria's ship, known by "The Twin Brothers" lore. Touched Syracuse, stayed for three days, Circled to Rhegium, where the south wind plays.

Reached Puteoli, found brothers, stayed seven days, Then onward to Rome, where courage found its ways. Brothers greeted us at the Appian Market's call, Paul thanked God, heart strengthened, standing tall.
In Rome, handed to the guard, the prisoners were, But Paul stayed with a soldier, no chains to deter. Three days later, the Jewish leaders he called, Explained his case, how to Caesar he was hauled.
"No letters against you," the leaders said, "But we want to hear about this sect so widespread." Paul testified from morning to night, Some believed, some left, their minds in a fight.

"The Spirit spoke through Isaiah," Paul declared, "Hearing but not understanding, hearts hardly cared. God's salvation is sent, to nations they'll receive, They will listen, their hearts won't deceive."
Two years Paul stayed, in his rented place, Preaching boldly of Christ, sharing grace. God's Kingdom proclaimed, with no restraint, Paul's courage unwavering, a steadfast saint.
Paul’s on the scene, called to preach the Word, God's Good News, the best you ever heard. Prophets spoke it, Scriptures defined, About God's Son, from David's line.
Declared the Son with power, he rose from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord, the one who led. Grace and apostleship through Him we receive, Faith across nations, in His name, believe.
In Rome, you're called, beloved and known, "Grace and peace," from God’s own throne. I thank God for you, your faith worldwide, Unceasing in prayer, with you side by side.
I long to see you, gifts spiritual to share, Together encouraged, each other’s faith there. Often I planned, but hindered I was, Fruit among you, the reason, the cause.
To Greeks and foreigners, my debt is wide, Wise and foolish, I'm on that ride. Eager to preach, with strength and might, Not ashamed, it's the power and light.
Reveals God's righteousness, faith to faith declared, "The righteous shall live by faith," prepared. God’s wrath from heaven on ungodliness shown, Suppressing truth, unrighteousness grown.
Invisible things, since creation, are clear, Everlasting power, divine, near. Though knowing God, they failed to praise, Became vain, their hearts in a daze.
Claimed wisdom, but fool's crown embraced, God's glory for images, disgrace. So God gave them to lusts and shame, Honored the creature, forgot His name.
Vile passions took hold, against nature they turned, Men and women, in lust they burned. God gave them a mind that strayed, Unrighteous acts, they displayed.
Filled with immorality, malice, and strife, Envy, murder, deceit filled their life. Arrogant, boastful, haters of God, Unmerciful and unkind, they trod.
Knowing God’s law, ignoring His call, Approved those who sinned, led them to fall.
Without excuse, man, you judge, you condemn, You do the same, can't hide from them.
God's truth judges all who act this way, Think you'll escape? Well, no, not today.
Despise God's riches, patience, and grace? Don't you know His goodness leads to a new place?
Your hard heart's storing up wrath on that day, Judgment's coming, can't keep it at bay.
"To each by their works," God will repay, Persevere in good, eternal life's your stay.
But self-seeking hearts, who stray from truth, Wrath, indignation, that's the proof.
Anguish on evil, whether Jew or Greek, But glory and peace for those who seek.
God shows no partiality, it's true, Law or no law, judge or be judged too.
Not hearers, but doers justified before God, Even Gentiles with law in their hearts, it's odd.
Secrets revealed on that judgment day, By Jesus Christ, no time to play.
You call yourself Jew, rest on the law, Guide the blind, but what do you draw?
Preach don't steal, but do you take? Don't commit adultery, but do you fake?
Glory in law, yet dishonor God, Gentiles blaspheme, ain't that odd?
Circumcision counts if you do the right, Transgress and it loses all its might.
Uncircumcised keeping law, will they not? Judge you who break it, got you caught.
True Jew's inward, not just the flesh, Heart's circumcision, spirit refresh.
Praise from God, not from men, That's the truth, again and again.
What's the deal, what's the Jew's gain, what's circumcision's claim? Plenty in every way, they got God's truth to proclaim.
If some folks lack belief, does it cancel God's stand? "No way!" God's always true, while man's truths turn to sand.
"If our wrong highlights God's right, should He still bring wrath?" "No way! God judges the world, guiding all on His path."
If my lie shows God's glory, why am I called to pay? "Let’s do evil for good"—those folks are led astray.
So who's better—us or them? Not one stands without sin, All are under its power, no one's righteous within.
Scripture tells it straight, "None seeks, none does good, Like graves with open mouths, deceitful tongues understood."
“Their mouths curse, their feet rush to blood and strife, No peace, no fear of God, this is their life.”
The law speaks to all, stops mouths in their tracks, No flesh justified by works; law shows sin’s cracks.
But now, without the law, God's righteousness shines, Faith in Jesus, no difference, for those in His lines.
All have sinned and missed God's glorious light, Yet through grace in Jesus, He makes wrongs right.
God sent His Son, blood spilled to show, His righteousness shines now, for those who believe and know.
Where’s the boasting now? It’s gone, no doubt, Not by works, but by faith that we shout.
God’s not just for Jews, He's for Gentiles, too, Justifying all by faith, making all things new.
Do we nullify law with faith's embrace? Never! We uphold it, in God's righteous space.
What did Abraham find, our ancient kin? Just by his flesh, could he win?
If works could justify, he'd boast for sure, But not with God, there's more to explore.
Scripture says, "He believed, it was right," Faith was his key, not strength or might.
A worker's reward is what he's owed, But faith gives grace, it's not a loan.
David spoke of blessing, so clear, "Blessed are they with sins covered here."
Sins forgiven, God won't charge, Faith not works, in Abraham's barge.
